Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّ حَّ م َّذٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
«كُّل ُّ مَّ اءٍ طَّ اهِز إ ِلأ َّ مَّ ا عَّلِمْ ث َّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّذ ِر .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"All water is pure except for that which you know to be impure."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 133 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 7

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «إَّلْمَّاء ُّي ُّطَّ هِّ زُّ وَّ لأَّ ي ُّطَّ ه َّز .
ق مي ى وج ذب ماء ولم ي علم ق ي ه ن ح اسه ق ي وص ا من ه وإس زب ، وإ ن وج ذب ق ي ه ما ي ن ح سه ق لا ي ي وص ا من ه ولأ ي س زب إ لأ ق ى
جال إلأص طزإر ق ي س زب من ه ولأ ي ي وص ا من ه وي ي مم إ لأ إ ن ي كون إلماء كزإ ق لا ن ا س ن ا ن ي ي وص ا من ه وي س زب ، وق غ ق ي ه س ى إ و
لم ي ق غ، ما لم ي ي ع ي ز ري ح إلماء، ق ا ن ي ع ي ز ق لا ي س ،زن ه ولأ ي ي وض من ه. وإلكز ما ي كون ي لاي ه إ س ن ار طولأ، ق ى عزض ي لاي ه إ س ن ار
ق ى عمق ي لاي ه إ س ن ار. ون الور ن إ لف ومان ي ا رطل ن المذن ى
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Water purifies, but is not purified itself”.
commentary:
So when you find water and are unsure of its impurity, you may perform ablution from
it and drink. However, if you find something (within it) that contaminates it, do not
perform ablution or drink from it unless in a state of necessity.
In that case, you may drink from it but not perform ablution, but instead perform
Tayammum unless the water is abundant, in which case it is permissible to both
perform ablution and drink from it - regardless if something has fallen into it or not, as
long as the smell of the water has not changed.
If it has changed, do not drink from it or perform ablution with it.
Measure of one Kurr is three spans long, three spans wide, and three spans deep. It is
weighing one thousand two hundred Ratl in Madina terms.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 570 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 1 • Al- Ash'athiyat, Part 1, p. 11 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 215 • Al-Wadar (Lil-Rawandi) Vol. 1, p. 39 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 21 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 17 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 133 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p.

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ «إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ إَّلْمَّاءُّ ق َّذْ رَّ ق ُّل َّي َّي ْن ِ لَّمْ ي ُّن َّح ِّ سْ هُّ س َّ ى ْ ء وَّ إَّلْق ُّل َّي َّان ِ ج َّ ز َّي َّان .
ولأ ن ا س ن الوص وء وإلع سل من إلح ن ان ه وإلأسي ي اك ن ماء إلورذ وإلماء إلذ ى ي سح ن ه إلس مس لأ ي ي وص ا ن ه، ولأ ي ع ي سل ن ه من
إلح ن ان ه ، ولأ ي عح ن ن ه لأ ن ه ي ورب إلن زض. ولأ ن ا س ن ا ن ي ي وص ا إلزج ل ن الماء إلحمي م إلحار.
ولأ ي ق سذ إلماء إ لأ ما كان ث له ن ق س
سان له . وكل ما وق غ ق ى إلماء مما لي س له ذم ق لا ن ا س ن اسي عماله وإلوص وء من ه ماب ق ي ه إ و لم ي مث . ق ا ن كان معك إ ن اءإن
ق وق غ ق ى إ جذهما ما ي ن ح س إلماء ولم ي علم ق ى إ ي هما وق غ ق ا هزق هما ج مي عا وي ي مم. ولو إ ن مي ز إن ي ن سالأ: مي ز إب ن ول ومي ز إب
م.اء ق اج ي لطا ي م إ صاب ي ون ك من ه لم ي كن ن ه ن ا س
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said:
"If the water is the amount of two qullas, nothing can make it impure, and two qullas
are (equal to) two jars”.
commentary:
There is no harm in performing ablution, washing after major impurity (ghusl), or using
rose water for cleansing. However, do not use water heated by the sun for ablution,
washing after major impurity, or kneading dough, as it is said to cause leprosy. There
is no harm in performing ablution with hot water. Water is only corrupted (rendered
impure) by substances that have a flowing soul (i.e., those that bleed). Any object that
falls into water and does not have blood may still be used for ablution and other uses,
regardless of whether it died in the water or not.
If you have two containers and something that makes water impure falls into one of
them, but you do not know which, pour out both and perform tayammum (dry
ablution). If water from two drainpipes flows down, one with urine and the other with
pure water, and they mix and get on your clothes, there is no harm.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 7 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 33 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 166

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ هِس َّ امُّ ن ْن ُّسَّ الِمٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ عَّن ِ إَّلس َّ طْ حِ ي ُّن َّالُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّي ُّصِ ي ن ُّهُّ إَّلس َّ مَّاءُّ ق َّي َّكِف ُّ ق َّي ُّصِ ي ث ُّ إَّلي َّوْ ب
ُّق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِهِ مَّ ا إ َّصَّ ان َّهُّ مِن َّ إَّلْمَّاءِ إ َّكْي َّزُّ مِن ْه .
english_text:
Hisham ibn Salim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
urinating on a roof, then rain falls on it causing water to drip onto clothes.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it as long as the water that hits it is more than the
urine”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: عَّن ْ طِ ي ن ِ إَّلْمَّطَّ زِ ي ُّصِ ي ث ُّ إَّلي َّوْ ب َّ ق ِي هِ إَّلْن َّوْ لُّ وَّ إَّلْعَّذ ِرَّة ُّ وَّ إَّلذ َّمُّ ق َّق َّال
ُّ«طِ ي ن ُّ إَّلْمَّطَّ زِ لأَّ ي ُّن َّح ِّ س .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about rain-soaked mud that
gets on clothes, which may contain urine, feces, and blood.
Imam {a.s} said: "Rain-soaked mud does not make (the clothes) impure”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 47

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّز ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم ِ : عَّن ِ إَّلْن َّي ْث ِ ي ُّن َّالُّ عَّلَّى ط َّ هْ زِةِ وَّ ي ُّع ْ ي َّسَّ لُّ مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّان َّه
ْ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّصِ ي ن ُّهُّ إَّلْمَّطَّ زُّ إ َّ ي ُّو ْ ج َّ ذ ُّ مِن ِمَّ ان ِهِ ق َّي ُّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّ ن ِهِ لِلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ زَّى ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother, Imam Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a roof where people
urinate and perform ritual washing after major impurity (ghusl), and then it rains.
He asked: "Can the water that flows from it be used for ablution (wudu) for prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If it flows, there is no harm in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 177 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p.

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّمُّز ُّ ق ِى مَّ اءِ إَّلْمَّطَّ زِ وَّ ق َّذْ صُّ ث َّ ق ِي هِ ج َّ مْ ز ق َّا َّصَّ اب َّ ي َّوْ ن َّهُّ هَّلْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِي هِ ق َّن ْلَّ إ َّن ْ ي َّع ْ سِ لَّهُّ ق َّق َّال
ِ«لأَّ ي َّع ْ سِ لُّ ي َّوْ ن َّهُّ وَّ لأَّ رِج ْ لَّهُّ وَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِي هِ وَّ لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about a man
who walks through rainwater into which wine has been poured in and it gets on his
clothes. Should he wash it before praying in those clothes?
Imam {a.s} said: "He does not need to wash his clothes or his feet, and he may pray in
them, and there is no harm in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 191 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p.

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text: وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّم َّار ْ إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْق َّى ْ ءِ ي ُّصِ ي ث ُّ إَّلي َّوْ ب َّ ق َّلاَّ ي ُّع ْ سَّ لُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ِسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about vomit that
gets on clothing and is not washed off.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 423 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 235

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوق َّال
ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
«كُّل ُّ س َّ ى ْ ءٍ ي َّح ْ ي َّز ُّ ق َّسُّ و ْ رُّةُّ جَّ لاَّل وَّ لُّعَّان ُّهُّ جَّ لاَّل .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws}, said:
"Everything that chews the cud - its leftover water and saliva are permissible."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 228 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 75 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 232 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 414

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
وإ َّي َّى
ِإ َّهْلُّ إَّلْن َّاذِي َّه ِ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق َّق َّالُّوإ ي َّا رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ إ ِن َّ جِ ي َّاص َّ ن َّا هَّذ ِة َّ ي َّزِذُّهَّا إَّلسِّ ن َّاعُّ و
َّإَّلْكِلاَّب ُّ وَّ إَّلْن َّهَّان ِمُّ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهُّمْ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ «لَّهَّا مَّ ا إ َّج َّ ذ َّب ْ إ َّق ْو َّ إهُّهَّا وَّ لَّكُّمْ سَّ ان ِزُّ ذ َّلِك .
وإ ن س زب من إلماء ذإن ه إ و جمار إ و ن ع ل إ و س اة إ و ن ق زة إ و ن عي ز ق لا ن ا س ن اسي عماله وإلوص وء من ه. ق ا ن وق غ
ور ع ق ى إ ن اء ق ي ه ماء إ هزي ق ذ لك إلماء.
: وإ ن ولغ ق ي ه كلث إ و س زب من ه إ هزي ق إلماء وع سل إلأ ن اء ي لاب مزإب
مزة ن الي زإب ومزي ي ن ن الماء ي م ي ح ق ف. وإ ما إلماء إلأ ج ن ق ي ح ث إلي ن ز ة عن ه إ لأ إ ن ي كون لأ ي وج ذ ع ي زة.
ولأ ن ا س
.ن الوص وء ن ماء ي س زب من ه إلسن ور، ولأ ن ا س ن س زن ه
english_text:
The people of the desert came to the Messenger of Allah {saws} and said:
"O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, our water reservoirs are frequented by wild animals, dogs,
and livestock."
He {saws} said: "What they take with their mouths is for them, and rest is for you”.
commentary:
If a beast, donkey, mule, sheep, cow, or camel drinks from water, there is no harm in
using it and performing ablution with it. However, if a lizard falls into a vessel of water,
the water should be poured out. If a dog licks the vessel or drinks from it, the water
should be poured out, and the vessel washed three times: once with earth and twice
with water, then dried.
As for stagnant water with an unpleasant odor, it is best to avoid it, unless no other
water is available. There is no harm in performing ablution with water from which a cat
has drunk, and there is no harm in drinking it.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 414 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 28 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 161

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوق َّال
ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«إ ِن ِّى لأَّ إ َّمْ ي َّن ِغُّ مِن ْ طَّ عَّامٍ طَّ عِمَّ مِن ْهُّ إَّلسِّ ن َّوْ رُّ وَّ لأَّ مِن ْ س َّ زَّإب ٍ س َّ زِب َّ مِن ْه .
ولأ ي ح ور إلوص وء ن سو ر إلي هوذى وإلن صزإن ى وولذ إلز ن ا وإلمس زك وكل من ج الف إلأسلام، وإ س ذ من ذ لك سو ر
إلن اصث . وماء إلحمام سن ي له سن ي ل إلماء إلح ارى إ ذ إ كان ث له ماذة .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"I do not refrain from food that a cat has tasted, nor from drink that it has sipped."
commentary:
It is not permissible to perform ablution with the leftover water of a Jew, a Christian,
someone born out of wedlock, a polytheist, or anyone who opposes Islam. Even more
prohibited is the leftover water of a nasibi (one hostile to the family of the Prophet).
The water of a public bath is treated like flowing water if it has a continuous source.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 228

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّق ِى إَّلْمَّاءِ إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّن ُّولُّ ق ِي هِ إَّلذ َّوَّ إب ُّ وَّ ي َّلَّغ ُّ ق ِي هِ إَّلْكِلاَّب ُّ وَّ ي َّع ْ ي َّسِ لُّ ق ِي هِ إَّلْح ُّ ن ُّث ُّ «إ ِن َّه
إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ ق َّذْ رَّ كُّزٍّ لَّمْ ي ُّن َّح ِّ سْ هُّ س َّ ى ْ ء .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "Regarding water into which
animals urinate, dogs drink, or someone performs ghusl (ritual washing after major
impurity): "If it reaches the amount of a kurr (a specific measure), then nothing can
make it impure”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«كَّان َّ ن َّن ُّو إ ِسْ زَّإن ِي لَّ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّصَّ اب َّ إ َّجَّ ذَّهُّمْ ق َّطْ زَّة ُّ ن َّوْ لٍ ق َّزَّص ُّ وإ لُّحُّ ومَّ هُّمْ ن ِالْمَّق َّارِي ض ِ و
َّق َّذْ وَّ س َّ غَّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ عَّلَّي ْكُّمْ ن ِا َّوْ سَّ غِ مَّ ا ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلس َّ مَّاءِ وَّ إَّلْأ َّرْ ض ِ وَّ ج َّ عَّلَّ لَّكُّمُّ إَّلْمَّاءَّ ط ْ هُّورإً ق َّان ْط ُّ زُّوإ كَّي َّ ف َّ ي َّكُّون ُّون .
ق ا ن ذج لث جي ه ق ى جث ماء وج زج ث من ه صث من إلماء ي لاب إ كف ، و إسي عمل إلن اق ى ، وق لي له وكي ي زة ن من ز له وإجذة.
ولأ

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The Children of Israel, if a drop of urine touched them, they would cut away the
affected flesh with scissors. But Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Exalted, has granted you vast
leniency - wider than the space between the heavens and the earth - and has made
water purifying for you. So, consider how you conduct yourselves (at removing
impurities)”.
commentary:
If a snake enters a water container and then exits, pour out three handfuls of the water
and use the rest; a small or large amount of water is treated the same.
There is also no harm in drawing water with a rope made from pig hair.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 356 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 16 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 133

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about the use of pig skin to
make a bucket for drawing water.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about the skins of dead
animals used to hold milk, water, or clarified butter.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in putting whatever you like in them - water, milk, or
clarified butter - and using it for ablution and drinking. However, do not pray in it (i.e.,
in clothes made from it)”.
commentary:
It is permissible to perform ablution with the leftover water of someone in a state of
major impurity (junub) or a menstruating woman, if no other water is available. If a man
performs ablution or washing with impure water or washes his clothes with it, he must
repeat the ablution, washing, prayer, and the washing of the clothes, as well as any
vessel into which the water was poured. If someone enters a public bath without a
clean scoop and his hands are impure, he may dip his hand in the water while saying,
"In the name of Allah {SWT}."
This aligns with what Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Exalted, says: "And He has not placed
upon you in the religion any hardship" (Surah Al Hajj 22:78).
Similarly, if a person in a state of major impurity (junub) reaches a small amount of
water on the road without a clean container to draw it and has impure hands, he
should do the same.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 19, p. 104 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 463

english_text:
Ameerul Momineen Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} was asked: "Is it better to perform
ablution from the leftover water of a group of Muslims, or from a covered white jug?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, rather from the leftover water of the group of Muslims, for the most
beloved aspect of your religion to Allah
{SWT} is the tolerant and agreeable
monotheism."
commentary:
If a Muslim and a dhimmi (non-Muslim under protection) are together in a public bath,
the Muslim should wash from the pool before the dhimmi.
It is not permissible to purify with leftover water of the public bath, as it includes the
washings of Jews, Zoroastrians, Christians, and those who harbor enmity toward the
family of Muhammad {a.s}, the last of whom are the worst of them.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 69 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 210

Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about the collected
water in a public bath from people’s washings, which may get onto clothes.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it”.
commentary:
There is also no harm in performing ablution with used water. When The Prophet {saws}
performed ablution, people would take the leftover water from his ablution to perform
their own. If a person performs ablution in a clean vessel, it is no harm if someone else
using that water for ablution.
However, water used to wash clothes, to wash after major impurity (ghusl), or to
remove impurities should not be used for ablution.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 15 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 379 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 51 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 213

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about water from which a
chicken had drunk.
Imam {a.s} said: "If there is known dirt on its beak, do not perform ablution with it or drink
from it. But if there is no known dirt on its beak, you may perform ablution with it and
drink from it."
commentary:
Any animal whose meat is lawful to eat does not render water impure by drinking from
it, so ablution and drinking from it are permitted. Ablution with water from which a
hawk, falcon, or eagle has drunk is also permissible, provided there is no visible blood
on its beak. If blood is seen on its beak, do not use the water for ablution or drinking.
If a person has a nosebleed, and a few small drops of blood fall into their container
without visibly affecting the water, ablution from it is allowed. However, if the blood is
clearly noticeable in the water, it is not permissible to use it for ablution.
If a chicken, bird, or similar animal steps on dung and then enters water, ablution with
that water is not allowed unless it is a large quantity (kurr).
If a dead mouse, rat, or small bird falls into a water container and decays, it is not
permitted to drink from or use that water for ablution. If the animal has not decayed,
there is no harm in drinking from or using the water for ablution; simply remove the
dead animal if it is still fresh. This applies to containers like jars, water pitchers, or
skins.
If a mouse or similar animal falls into a well and dies, and bread is kneaded with that
well’s water, it is permissible to eat the bread if it has been baked in fire.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 153 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 231

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The fire consumes what is within it."
commentary:
If a mouse falls into a container of solidified fat, oil, or honey, remove the mouse along
with some of the surrounding substance, and the rest can be used and eaten. The
same applies if a mouse falls into flour or similar substances. However, if a mouse
falls into liquid oil, it is permissible to use that oil as a fuel for lighting. If a mouse falls
into a container of oil but is removed before it dies, it is permissible to use that oil for
anointing or to sell it to a Muslim.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 156

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a well from which
water was drawn for ablution, washing clothes, and kneading dough, and then it was
discovered that there was a dead animal in it.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm, and the clothes do not need to be washed again, nor
does the prayer need to be repeated”.
commentary:
If a mouse or dog has eaten or sniffed a piece of bread, set aside the part that was
sniffed or eaten and consume the rest. There is no harm in performing ablution with
water from reservoirs in which urine has been introduced if the color of the water
overpowers the urine. However, if the urine overpowers the water, it should not be
used for ablution. It is not permissible to perform ablution with milk, as ablution
should be done with water or clean earth (tayammum).
It is permissible to perform ablution with nabidh (a drink), as The Prophet {saws}
performed ablution with it. This was water in which a few dates were soaked, leaving
a clear liquid on top. If the dates change the color of the water, it should not be used
for ablution. The type of nabidh allowed for ablution and drinking is one in which dates
are soaked in the morning and drunk in the evening, or soaked in the evening and drunk
in the morning. If a person performs ghusl (ritual washing) in a low area and fears that
water will flow back into the area from which they are washing, they should pour one
handful of water in front of them, one to their right, one to their left, and one behind
them, then proceed with the washing.
If water splashes onto a person’s clothes or body from the water used for cleansing
(istinja), there is no harm (for ablution). If water splashes from one’s hand into a
container or spills onto the ground and then falls into the container, there is no harm.
The same applies during ghusl from major impurity.
If a dead animal falls into flowing water, there is no harm in performing ablution from
the side of the water that is free of the dead animal.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Part 1, p. 201

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمَّاء ُّ إَّلس َّ اكِن ِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِي هِ إَّلْح ِ ي ق َّه ُّ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ ان ِث ِ إَّلْأ ج َّ زِ وَّ لأَّ ي ُّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا
ِ مِن ْ ج َّ ان ِث ِ إَّلْح ِ ي ق َّه .
english_text:
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about stagnant water that contains a dead animal.
Imam {a.s} said: "Perform ablution from the other side and not from the side of the dead
animal".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 161

english_text:
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a pond with a dead animal in it.
Imam {a.s} said: "If the water overpowers it so that no odor is detectable, then perform
ablution and ghusl with it”.
commentary:
If one becomes ritually impure (junub) while traveling and only has snow, it is
permissible to perform ghusl with it, as well as ablution by rubbing it on the skin. It is
also permissible for a person in a state of major impurity to scoop water from a
container with his hand.
If he performs ghusl and water splashes from the ground into a container, or runs from
his body into a container, there is no harm in it.
It is also permissible for a man and woman to perform ghusl from the same container,
but She should use his leftover water, and he should not use hers.
The most significant impurity that may fall into a well is a human who dies in it,
requiring seventy buckets of water to be drawn. The smallest is a small bird, requiring
one bucket. For other cases, the amount depends on the item:
If a mouse falls in and does not decay, draw one bucket; if decayed, draw seven (and
discard).
If a donkey falls in, draw a kurr (large quantity) of water (and discard).
If a dog falls in, draw thirty to forty buckets (and discard).
If a cat falls in, draw seven buckets (and discard).
If a chicken or pigeon falls in, draw seven buckets (and discard).
If a camel, cow, or wine is poured in, the entire well’s water must be drawn out (and
discard).
If a few drops of blood fall in, a few buckets are sufficient (and discard).
If a man urinates in the well, forty buckets should be drawn (and discard).
If a child who has eaten solid food urinates, draw three buckets; if an infant, draw one
bucket.
If a basket of fresh or dry feces or manure falls in, there is no harm in using the well for
ablution, provided no contents spilled into the water. If feces fall in directly, draw ten
buckets ; if it dissolves, draw forty to fifty buckets needs to be drawn from it.
If a well is near a cesspit, the minimum distance of the well should be five arm-lengths
if the ground is solid. If the ground is soft, then it will be minimum distance of seven
arm-lengths.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«لَّي ْ سَّ ي ُّكْزَّةُّ مِن ْ ق ُّزْب ٍ وَّ لأَّ ن ُّعْ ذِ ن ِن ْز ي ُّع ْ ي َّسَّ لُّ مِن ْهَّا وَّ ي ُّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّي َّع َّي َّزِ إَّلْمَّاء .
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} said:
"A well from which water is used for ghusl (ritual washing) and ablution is not disliked,
whether it is near or far, as long as the water does not change (in smell, color, or
taste)”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
It was narrated from Abu Basir that Imam {a.s} said:
"We stayed in a house with a well beside a drain, with only about two arm-lengths
between them. The people refrained from performing ablution from it, which caused
them difficulty. So we went to Abu Abdullah {a.s} and informed him.
Imam {a.s} said: 'Perform ablution from it, for that drain has channels that flow into a
valley, which leads to the sea.'".
commentary:
If something falls into a well and changes the smell of the water, all the water must be
drawn out. If the amount is large and difficult to draw, it is obligatory to hire four men
to draw from it in turns from morning until evening.
As for water from sulfur springs, The Prophet {saws} forbade using it for medicinal
purposes but did not prohibit ablution with it. These are hot waters found in the
mountains that have a sulfur smell.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 98 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 199

َّوَّ ق َّال ِعَّلَّي ْ ه َّإَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «إ ِن َّهَّا مِن ْ ق َّي ْ حِ ج َّ هَّن َّم . »
. وإ ن ق طز ج مز إ و ن ن ي ذ ق ى عح ي ن ق ق ذ ق سذ ق لا ن ا س ن ن ي عه من إلي هوذ وإلن صارى ن عذ إ ن ي ن ي ن لهم وإلق ق اع مي ل ذ لك
english_text: Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: ""Indeed, it (hot water) is from the heat of Hell."
commentary:
If wine or nabidh (fermented drink) falls into dough, it becomes impure and spoiled.
However, it is permissible to sell it to Jews and Christians after informing them of the
impurity. The same rule applies to fuqqa‘ (a type of fermented drink).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
a man who finds a dead mouse in his container after having used it multiple times for
ablution, ghusl (ritual washing), or washing his clothes, and it was already decayed.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he saw it in the container before performing ablution, ghusl, or
washing his clothes, and still used the water afterward, then he must wash his clothes,
wash everything that came into contact with that water, and repeat his ablution and
prayer.
However, if he only noticed the mouse after he had finished, then he should avoid
using the water, but he is not required to repeat anything, as he does not know when it
fell into the container."
Imam {a.s} said: "It is possible that it only fell into the container at the moment he saw
it."

َّإ َّن ْ ي َّق ُّومَّ ق ِى إَّلْمَّطَّ زِ جَّ ي َّى ي ُّع ْ سَّ لَّ رَّإ ْسُّ هُّ وَّ ج َّ سَّ ذُّةُّ وَّ هُّوَّ ي َّق ْذِرُّ عَّلَّى مَّ اءٍ سِ وَّ ى ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ع َّس ِلَّهُّ إِع ْ ي ِسَّ الَّهُّ ن ِالْمَّاء
َّ إ َّج ْ ز َّإ َّةُّ ذ َّلِك.
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man in a state
of major ritual impurity (junub) : Would it suffice for him to stand in the rain until his
head and body are washed, if he also has access to other water?
Imam {a.s} said: "If the rain washes him completely as it would with water for ghusl, then
that suffices."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 348

ُّإَّلْق َّا ْرَّة ِ إ ِذ َّإ س َّ زِن َّث ْ مِن َّ إَّلْأ ِن َّاءِ إ َّن ْ ي َّس ْ زَّب َّ مِن ْهُّ إ َّوْ ي َّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّ مِن ْه.
.وإلور ع ه إ ذ وق عث ق ى إلن ن ز ن ز ح من ها ي لاب ذلأء
وإ ذ إ ذ ن ح رج ل طي زإ مي ل ذج اج ه إ و جمامه ق وق غ ن ذمه ق ى إلن ن ز ن ز ح من ها
.ذلأء
english_text:
Ishaq ibn Ammar reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} used to say:
"There is no harm in using the leftover water from which a mouse has drunk, for
drinking or performing ablution."
commentary:
If a lizard falls into a well, three buckets should be drawn from it.
If a man slaughters a bird, such as a chicken or a pigeon, and its blood falls into a well,
a few buckets should be drawn from the well (and discarded).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 419 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 26 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 4, p. 53 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 76 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 239

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّوسَّ ى ُّن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم ِعَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ ذ َّن َّحَّ س َّ اة ً ق َّاص ْ طَّ زَّن َّث ْ ق َّوَّ ق َّعَّث ْ ق ِى ن ِن ْز
َّمَّ اءٍ وَّ إ َّوْ ذَّإج ُّ هَّا ي َّس ْ ح ُّ ث ُّ ذَّماً هَّلْ ي ُّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ مِن ْ ي ِلْك َّ إَّلْن ِن ْزِ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّن ْز َّحُّ مِن ْهَّا مَّ ا ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّلاَّي ِي ن َّ ذ َّ لْوإً إ ِلَّى إ َّرْن َّعِي ن َّ ذَّلْوإً ي ُّم
ي َّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ مِن ْهَّا .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man who
slaughtered a sheep, which then convulsed and fell into a well while its veins were still
bleeding. He asked if one could perform ablution from that well.
Imam {a.s} said: "Between thirty and forty buckets should be drawn from it, and then it
may be used for ablution."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 203 • Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 179

ق َّق َّالَّ «لَّي ْسَّ ن ِس َّ ى ْ ءٍ لِأ َّن َّ إَّلْوَّ ر َّع َّ رُّن َّمَّا طَّ زَّحَّ ج ِ لْذَّةُّ إ ِن َّمَّا ي َّكْق ِي ك َّ مِن ْ ذ َّلِك َّ ذَّلْو وَّ إجِ ذ .
english_text:
Ya'qub ibn 'Uthaym asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a well
of water that had a smell, and pieces of skin were coming out of it.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is nothing (to worry about) because a lizard may sometimes shed its
skin. Drawing one bucket is sufficient for that."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 6 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 419 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 86 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 189

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ج َّ ان ِزُّ ن ْن ُّ ي َّز ِي ذَّ إَّلْح ُّ عْ ق ِى ُّ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ ه ِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلس َّ امِّ إ َّن ْزَّضَّ ي َّق َّغُّ ق ِى إَّلْن ِن ْزِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لَّي ْسَّ ن ِس َّ ى ْ ءٍ جَّ زِّك
ِإَّلْمَّاءَّ ن ِالذ َّلْو .
english_text:
Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi about a gecko falling into a well.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is nothing (to worry about); stir the water with a bucket."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 5 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 86

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ ي َّعْ ق ُّوب ُّ ن ْن ُّ عُّي َّي ْمٍ عَّن ْ سَّ امِّ إ َّن ْزَّض َّ وَّ ج َّ ذْ ن َّاةُّ ق ِى إَّلْن ِن ْزِ ق َّذْ ي َّق َّس َّ ح َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن َّمَّا عَّلَّي ْك َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّن ْز َّحَّ مِن ْهَّا سَّ ن ْعَّه

.وإلعط اي ه إ ذ إ وق عث ق ى إللن ن جزم إللن ن وي ق ال: إ ن ق ي ها إلسم
وإ ن وق عث س اة وما إ س ن هها ق ى ن ن ز ي ن ز ح من ها ي سعه ذلأء إ لى
.عس زة ذلأء
english_text:
Yaqub ibn Uthaym asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a gecko
that was found decayed in a well.
Imam {a.s} said: "You only need to draw seven buckets from it."
Ya'qub then asked: "Our clothes that we prayed in - do we need to wash them and
repeat the prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
commentary:
If a lizard falls into milk, the milk becomes forbidden to consume, as it is said to
contain poison. If a sheep or a similar animal falls into a well, nine to ten buckets
should be drawn (to discard).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«كَّان َّث ْ ق ِى إَّلْمَّذِي ن َّه ِ ن ِن ْز ق ِى وَّ سَّ ظِ مَّ ز ْن َّلَّه ٍ ق َّكَّان َّث ِ إَّلزِّي حُّ ي َّهُّث ُّ ق َّي ُّلْق ِى ق ِي هَّا إَّلْق َّذ َّرَّ و
كَّان َّ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ي َّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ مِن ْهَّا .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"There was a well in Medina in the middle of a garbage dump. The wind would blow
filth into it, yet The Prophet {saws} used to perform ablution from it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 41 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 176

Chapter Title: WATER; ITS PURITY AND IMPURITY
arabic_text:
ْ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ مُّ حَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّ سْ لِمٍ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْن ِن ْزِ ي َّق َّغُّ ق ِي هَّا إَّلْمَّي ْي َّه ُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن كَّان َّ لَّهَّا رِي ح ن ُّز ِحَّ مِن ْهَّا
ًعِ س ْ زُّون َّ ذَّلْوإ.
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a
dead animal that falls into a well.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it has an odor, twenty buckets should be drawn from it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

. ولأ ي ح ور إ ن ي ن ول إلزج ل ق ى ماء رإكذ، ق ا ما إلماء إلح ارى ق لا ن ا س إ ن ي ن ول ق ي ه ولكن ي ي ح وف علي ه من إلس ي طان
وق ذ روى " إ ن إلن ول ق ى إلماء إلزإكذ ي ورب إلن سي ان .
english_text:
Kurdawiyah al-Hamdani asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim
{a.s} about a well into which water from the road flows, containing urine, feces, animal
urine and droppings, and dog excrement.
Imam {a.s} said: "Thirty buckets should be drawn from it, especially if it has a bad odor”.
commentary:
It is not permissible for a man to urinate in stagnant water. However, there is no harm
in urinating in flowing water, though it is advised to be cautious of potential harm from
the devil.
It is also narrated that urinating in stagnant water causes forgetfulness.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS
arabic_text:
ب اب- ارت ي اد المكان للجدب والسن ة ف ي دخ ولة والآ داب ف ي ة ا لي الج روج من ة
ُّق َّالَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
«كَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ َّس َّ ذ َّ إَّلن َّاسِ ي َّوَّ ق ِّي اً لِلْن َّوْ لِ جَّ ي َّى إ َّن َّهُّ كَّان َّ إ ِذ َّإ
ِإ َّرَّإذَّ إَّلْن َّوْ لَّ عَّمَّذَّ إ ِلَّى مَّ كَّان ٍ مُّ زْ ي َّق ِغٍ مِن َّ إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ إ َّوْ مَّ كَّان ٍ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِي هِ إَّلي ُّزَّإب ُّ إَّلْكَّي ِي زُّ كَّزَّإه َّ ي َّه ُّإ َّن ْ ي ُّن ْص َّ حَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلْن َّوْ ل .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} was the most cautious of people regarding urine, to the
extent that when he intended to relieve himself, he would go to an elevated spot of
land or a place with abundant soil to avoid any splashing of urine onto himself."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 278 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 33 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 105 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 338 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 168

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS
arabic_text:
وَّ كَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّرَّإذَّ ذُّج ُّ ولَّ إَّلْمُّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ِ ق َّالَّ « إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ ِن ِّى ِإ َّعُّوذ ُّ ن ِك َّ مِن َّ إَّلزِّج ْ سِ إَّلن ِّح ْ س
َّ إَّلْح َّ ن ِي ث ِ إَّلْمُّح ْ ن ِث ِ إَّلس َّ ي ْطَّ ان ِ إَّلز َّج ِ ي مِ إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ َّمِث ْ عَّن ِّى إَّلْأ َّذ َّى وَّ إ » ِعِ ذ ْ ن ِى مِن َّ إَّلس َّ ي ْطَّ ان ِ إَّلز َّج ِ ي م
ُّوَّ إ ِذ َّإ إِسْ ي َّوَّ ى ج َّ الِساً لِلْوُّص ُّ وءِ ق َّالَّ « إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ َّذ ْ هِث ْ عَّن ِّى إَّلْق َّذ َّى وَّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّى وَّ إِج ْ عَّلْن ِى مِن َّ إَّلْم َّي َّطَّ هِّ زِي ن َّ » وَّ إ ِذ َّإ ي َّز َّج َّ زَّ ق َّال
ٍ « إَّلل َّهُّم َّ كَّمَّا إ َّطْ عَّمْ ي َّن ِي هِ طَّ ي ِّن اً ق ِى عَّاق ِي َّه ٍ ق َّا َّج ْ زِج ْ هُّ مِن ِّى ج َّ ن ِي ي اً ق ِى عَّاق ِي َّه.
english_text:
When the Messenger of Allah {saws} intended to enter the place of ablution
(lavatory), He would say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, I seek refuge in You from the unclean, impure, evil, defiling devil, the
accursed. O’ Allah {SWT}, remove harm from me and protect me from the accursed
devil."
When He {saws} would sit down to perform ablution, He {saws} would say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, remove from me impurities and harm, and make me among those who
are purified"
And when He {saws} strained to relieve himself, He {saws} would say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, as You provided this to me as pure sustenance and in good health, so
allow it to leave me as impurity in good health."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 307

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
ِوَّ كَّان َّ عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ ه َّ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّق ُّولُّ: «مَّ ا مِن ْ عَّن ْذٍ إ ِلأ َّ وَّ ن ِهِ مَّ لَّك مُّوَّ ك َّل ي ُّلَّوِّ ى عُّن ُّق َّهُّ جَّ ي َّى ي َّن ْط ُّ زَّ إ ِلَّى جَّ ذَّ ي ِهِ ي ُّم ُّي َّق ُّول
ِلَّهُّ إَّلْمَّلَّك ُّ ي َّا إِن ْن َّ إ ذَّمَّ هَّذ َّإ رِر ْق ُّك َّ ق َّان ْط ُّ زْ مِن ْ إ َّي ْن َّ إ َّج َّ ذ ْ ي َّهُّ وَّ إ ِلَّى مَّ ا صَّ ارَّ ق َّي َّن ْن َّع ِى لِلْعَّن ْذ عِ ن ْذَّ ذ َّلِك َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّق ُّولَّ: إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إُّرْر ُّق ْن ِى
َّإَّلْحَّ لاَّلَّ وَّ ج َّ ن ِّن ْن ِى إَّلْحَّ زَّإم.
.ولم ي ز للن ن ى صلى إلله علي ه وإ له ق ظ ن ح و لأن إلله ي ن ارك وي عالى وكل إلأ رض ن ان ي لاع ما ي ح زح من ه
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} used to say:
"There is no servant (of Allah {SWT}) except that there is an angel appointed to turn his
head to look at his excrement, and then the angel says to him:
'O’ child of Adam, this is your provision, so reflect from where you took it and what it
has turned.'
It is appropriate for the servant at that moment to say:
‘O’ Allah {SWT}, grant me lawful provision and keep me away from the unlawful.'"
commentary:
It is also narrated that The Prophet {saws} never left excrement, as Allah {SWT}, the Blessed
and Exalted, commanded the earth to absorb whatever left his body.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Majmu’at Warram, Part 2, p. 26 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 333 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 164

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ كَّان َّ إ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّرَّإذَّ إَّلْحَّ اج َّ ه َّ وَّ ق َّف َّ عَّلَّى ن َّاب ِ إَّلْمَّذ ْ هَّث ِ ي ُّم َّ إِلْي َّق ِث َّ عَّن ْ ي َّمِي ن ِهِ وَّ عَّن ْ ي َّسَّ ارِة
إ ِلَّى مَّ لَّكَّي ْ هِ ق َّي َّق ُّولُّ «إ َّمِي طَّ ا عَّن ِّى ق َّلَّكُّمَّا
إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّى َّ إ َّن ْ لأَّ إ ُّجَّ ذِّب َّ ن ِلِسَّ ان ِى س َّ ي ْن اً جَّ ي َّى إ َّج ْ زُّح َّ إ ِلَّي ْكُّمَّا .
english_text:
And when The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} intended to
relieve himself, He would stand at the entrance to the restroom, then turn to his right
and left toward his two angels, saying:
"Step aside from me, and I vow before Allah {SWT} that I will not speak with my tongue
until I return to you."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Majmu’at Warram, Part 2, p. 26

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ كَّان َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِذ َّإ ذَّج َّ لَّ إَّلْح َّ لاَّءَّ ي َّق ُّولُّ: « إَّلْحَّ مْ ذُّ لِل َّهِ إَّلْحَّ اق ِظ ِ إَّلْمُّو َّ ذِّى » ق َّا ِذ َّإ ج َّ زَّح ُّ مَّ سَّ حَّ ن َّطْ ن َّه َّوَّ ق َّال -
إَّلْحَّ مْ ذُّ لِل َّهِ إَّل َّذ ِى إ َّج ْ زَّح َّ عَّن ِّى إ َّذ َّإةُّ وَّ إ َّن ْق َّى ق ِى َّ ق ُّو َّ ي َّهُّ ق َّي َّا لَّهَّا مِن ْ ن ِعْ مَّه ٍ لأَّ ي َّق ْذِرُّ إَّلْق َّا
ذِرُّون َّ ق َّذْ رَّهَّا .
english_text:
When Imam Ali {a.s} would enter the restroom, he would say:
"Praise be to Allah {SWT}, the Preserver and the One who brings all matters to their
fulfilment."
Upon exiting, he would wipe his abdomen and say:
"Praise be to Allah {SWT}, who has removed harm from me and left within me strength.
What a blessing it is, one whose value cannot be fully appreciated by any capable of
appreciation.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Majmu’at Warram, Part 2, p. 26 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 308

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ كَّان َّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِذ َّإ ذَّج َّ لَّ إَّلْح َّ لاَّء ُّي ُّق َّن ِّغُّ رَّإ ْسَّ هُّ وَّ ي َّق ُّولُّ ق ِى ن َّق ْسِ هِ : « ن ِسْ مِ إَّلل َّهِ وَّ ن ِالل َّهِ وَّ لأَّ إ ِلَّهَّ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلل َّه
َّ رَّب ِّ إ َّج ْ زِح ْ عَّن ِّى إَّلْأ َّذ َّى سَّ زْجاً ن ِع َّي ْ زِ جِ سَّ اب ٍ وَّ إِج ْ عَّلْن ِى لَّك َّ مِن َّ إَّلس َّ اكِزِي ن َّ ق ِي مَّا ي َّصْ زِق ُّهُّ عَّن ِّى مِن َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّى وَّ إَّلْع َّمِّ إ ل َّذ ِى
لَّوْ جَّ ن َّسْ ي َّهُّ عَّن ِّى هَّلَّكْث ُّ لَّك َّ إَّلْحَّ مْ ذُّ إِعْ صِ مْ ن ِى مِن ْ س َّ زِّ مَّ ا ق ِى هَّذ ِةِ إَّلْن ُّق ْعَّه ِ وَّ إ َّج ْ زِج ْ ن ِى مِن ْهَّا سَّ ا َّ لِماً وَّ جُّ لْ ن َّي ْن ِى وَّ ن َّي ْ ن
ِطَّ اعَّه ِ إَّلس َّ ي ْطَّ ان ِ إَّلز َّج ِ ي م.
وي ن ن ع ى للزج ل إ ذ إ ذج ل إلح لاء إ ن ي ع طى رإ سه إ ق زإرإ ن ا ن ه ع ي ز من زء ن ق سه من إلعي وب ، وي ذج ل رج له إلي سزى ق ن ل إلي من ى
ق زق ا ن ي ن ذج ول إلح لاء وذج ول إلمسح ذ، وي ي عوذ ن الله من إلس ي طان إلزج ي م، لأن إلس ي طان إ كي ز ما ي هم ن الأن سان إ ذ إ كان
.وجذة، وإ ذ إ ج زح من إلح لاء إ ج زح رج له إلي من ى ق ن ل إلي سزى
english_text:
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} would enter the restroom, and would cover his head and say
privately:
"In the name of Allah {SWT} and by Allah {SWT}. There is no god but Allah {SWT}. O’ Lord {AZJ},
remove harm from me completely without difficulty, and make me among those who
are grateful for the relief You grant me from harm and distress, which, if You withheld,
would cause my destruction. Praise be to You. Protect me from the evil of what may
be in this place, and let me leave safely. Place a barrier between me and obedience to
the accursed devil."
commentary:
It is recommended that a person cover his head when entering the restroom as an
acknowledgment of his own imperfections, and enter with the left foot before the right
to distinguish between entering the restroom and entering the mosque. He should
seek refuge in Allah {SWT} from the accursed devil, as the devil is most likely to trouble a
person when they are alone. Upon leaving the restroom, he should step out with his
right foot before his left.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 308

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ وَّ ج َّ ذْ ب ُّ ن ِح َّ ظِّ سَّ عْ ذِ ن ْن ِ عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ جَّ ذِي ي اً إ َّسْ ن َّذَّةُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «م ن ْ كَّي ُّزَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ هْ وُّ ق ِى
َّإَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّلْي َّق ُّلْ إ ِذ َّإ ذَّج َّ ل ِ إَّلْح َّ لاَّءَّ: ن ِسْ مِ إَّلل َّهِ وَّ ن ِالل َّهِ إ َّعُّوذ ُّ ن ِالل َّهِ مِن َّ إَّلزِّج ْ سِ إَّلن ِّح ْ سِ إَّلْح َّ ن ِي ث ِ إَّلْمُّح ْ ن ِث ِ إَّلس َّ ي ْطَّ ان
ِإَّلز َّج ِ ي م.
english_text:
I found in the handwriting of Sa’d ibn Abdullah a narration attributed to Imam
Al-Sadiq {a.s}, in which He said:
"Whoever experiences frequent forgetfulness in prayer should say, upon entering the
restroom:
'In the name of Allah {SWT} and by Allah {SWT}. I seek refuge in Allah {SWT} from the unclean,
impure, evil, defiling devil, the accursed.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Masbah (Lalkafami) Vol. 1, p. 199 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 119 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 308

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"When one of you uncovers himself to urinate or for any other reason, let him say, 'In
the name of Allah {SWT},' for then the devil will lower his gaze from him until he is
finished."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Thawāb al-Aʿmāl wa ʿIqāb al-Aʿmāl, Part 1, p. 15 • Al- Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 119 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 308 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 60, p. 201 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 176

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّ رَّج ُّ ل لِعَّلِى ِّ ن ْن ِ إَّلْحُّ سَّ ي ْن ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّي ْن َّ ي َّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ إَّلْع ُّزَّن َّاءُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي َّي َّق ُّون َّ س ُّ طُّ وطَّ إَّلْأ َّن ْهَّارِ وَّ إَّلط ُّ زُّق َّ إَّلن َّاق ِذ َّة
ُّ وَّ ي َّحْ ث َّ إَّلْأ َّس ْ ح َّ ارِ إَّلْمُّي ْمِزَّة ِ وَّ مَّ وَّ إص ِ غَّ إَّلل َّعْ ن ِ » ق َّق ِي لَّ لَّهُّ وَّ إ َّي ْن َّ مَّ وَّ إص ِ غُّ إَّلل َّعْ ن ِ ق َّالَّ « إ َّن ْوَّ إب
ِإَّلذ ُّور .
english_text:
A man asked Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain {a.s}: "Where should strangers relieve
themself?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They should avoid the banks of rivers, public pathways, under fruit-
bearing trees, and places of cursing (where excreta will cause agitation to people)’.
He was then asked: "What are places of cursing? (that cause agitation)”
Imam {a.s} said: ‘The entrances of houses’.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 15 • Ma’ani al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 368 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 30 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 106 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 324 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 171

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق ِى ج َّ ن َّزٍ إ ج َّ زَّ: «لَّعَّن َّ إَّلل َّهُّ إَّلْمُّي َّع َّوِّ طَّ ق ِى ط ِ لِّ إَّلن ُّز َّلِ وَّ إَّلْمَّان ِغَّ إَّلْمَّاءَّ إَّلْمُّن ْي َّاب َّ و َّ إَّلس َّ اذ َّ إَّلط َّ زِي ق َّ إَّلْمَّسْ لُّوك .
english_text:
In another report, it states that "May Allah {SWT} curse the one who defecates in
the shade of a resting place, the one who prevents access to flowing water, and the
one who obstructs a frequently used pathway”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
english_text:
In a narration, it states: "Whoever blocks a pathway, Allah {SWT} will cut short his
life."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ُّ ن ْن ُّ عَّلِى ٍّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ مَّ ا جَّ ذ ُّ إَّلْع َّان ِظِ ق َّالَّ «لأ َّي َّسْ ي َّق ْن ِلِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّسْ ي َّذْ ن ِزْهَّا وَّ لأَّ ي َّسْ ي َّق ْن ِلِ إَّلزِّي ح
وَّ لأَّ ي َّسْ ي َّذْ ن ِزْهَّا .
english_text:
Imam Hasan ibn Ali {a.s} was asked about the proper etiquette for relieving
oneself.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not face the Qibla (direction of prayer) or turn your back to it, and
do not face the wind or turn your back to it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 326

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
:َّوَّ ق ِى ج َّ ن َّزٍ إ ج َّ ز ُّ«لأَّ ي َّسْ ي َّق ْ ن ِلِ إَّلْهِلاَّلَّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّسْ ي َّذْ ن ِزْة .
.ومن إسي ق ن ل إلق ن له ق ى ن ول إ و ع ان ظ ي م ذ كز ق ي حزف عن ها إ ج لالأ للق ن له لم ي ق م من موص عه جي ى ي ع ق ز إلله له
english_text:
In another narration, it is stated:
"Do not face the crescent moon, nor turn your back to it (whilst relieving oneself)."
commentary:
Furthermore, if someone does face the Qibla while urinating or relieving themselves
and then remembers, they should shift away from it out of respect for the Qibla. They
will not rise from that position until Allah {SWT} forgives them.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ذَّج َّ لَّ إ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إَّلْن َّاق ِزُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إَّلْح َّ لاَّءَّ ق َّوَّ ج َّ ذَّ لُّق ْمَّه َّ ج ُّ ن ْز ٍ ق ِى إَّلْق َّذ َّرِ ق َّا َّج َّ ذ َّهَّا و ع َّسَّ لَّهَّا وَّ ذَّق َّعَّهَّا إ ِلَّى ٍ مَّ مْ لُّوك
ْ كَّان َّ مَّ عَّهُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي َّكُّون ُّ مَّ عَّك َّ لأ ِكُّلَّهَّا إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ زَّج ْ ث ُّ » ق َّلَّم َّا ج َّ زَّح َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ لِلْمَّمْ لُّوك ِ «إ َّي ن َّ إَّلل ُّق ْ مَّه ُّ» ق َّالَّ إ َّكَّلْي ُّهَّا ي َّا
ِ إِن ْن َّ رَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ ' ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن َّهَّا مَّ ا إِسْ ي َّق َّز َّب ْ ق ِى ج َّ وْ ف ِ إ َّجَّ ذٍ إ ْ لأ َّ وَّ ج َّ ن َّث ْ لَّهُّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّه ُّ ' ق َّاذ ْ هَّث ْ ق َّا َّن ْث َّ جُّ ز ق َّا ِن ِّى إ َّكْزَّةُّ إ َّن
ِ إ َّسْ ي َّح ْ ذِمَّ رَّج ُّ لاً مِن ْ إ َّهْلِ إَّلْح َّ ن َّه.
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} entered the restroom and found a piece
of bread in the filth. He took it, washed (purified) it, and handed it to a servant who was
with Him, saying: 'Keep it with you for me, to eat when I come out.'
When he emerged, he asked the servant: 'Where is the piece of bread?'
(The Servant) replied: "I have eaten it, O’ son of the Messenger of Allah {saws}."
Imam {a.s} said: "It has not settled in the stomach of anyone except that Paradise is
obligatory for him. Go, for you are free, as I dislike to employ a man from the people of
Paradise”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 2, p. 188 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 19, p. 273 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 361 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 23, p. 53

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text: َّ وَّ ن َّهَّى رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّطَّ مِّحَّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ن ِن َّوْ لِهِ ق ِى إَّلْهَّوَّ إءِ مِن ِإَّلس َّ طْ حِ إ َّوْ مِن َّ إَّلس َّ ى ْ ءِ إَّلْمُّزْ ي َّق ِغ.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} prohibited a man from directing his urine into the
air from a rooftop or any elevated place.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 352

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «إَّلْن َّوْ لُّ ق َّان ِماً مِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ عِ ل َّه ٍ مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ ق َّاءِ وَّ إَّلأِسْ ي ِن ْح َّ اءُّ ن ِالْي َّمِي ن ِ مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ ق ِاء .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said:
"Urinating while standing without a reason is from rudeness, and using the right hand
for cleansing is also from rudeness."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Khasal, Part 1, p. 54 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 322 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 174 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 201

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
english_text:
It has been narrated: "There is no harm if the left hand is incapacitated (or
missing)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 321

Hisham ibn Salim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} saying:
"Is it permissible for me to perform ghusl (ritual washing) from major impurity (junub)
and other reasons in a restroom where people urinate, while wearing Sindhi sandals?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If the water flowing from your body reaches the soles of your feet, then
do not wash the soles of your feet”.
commentary:
Similarly, if a man performs ghusl in a pit and the water flows beneath his feet, he
should not wash his feet.
However, if his feet are submerged in the water, he should wash them.

Omar ibn Yazid asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the
recitation of supplications in the restroom and reading the Qur'an.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is not permitted to recite more than the Ayat al-Kursi or to praise
Allah {SWT} (by saying) 'All praise is due to Allah {SWT}, the Lord {AZJ} of the worlds' while in
the restroom."
commentary:
And whoever hears the call to prayer (adhan) should respond as the caller does and
should not refrain from making supplications and praising Allah {SWT} just because he
is in the restroom, for remembering Allah {SWT} is commendable in every situation.

When Allah {SWT} spoke to Musa ibn Imran {a.s}, Musa {a.s} asked:
"O’ Lord {AZJ}, are You far from me that I call to You, or are You near that I may converse
with You?"
Allah {SWT}, Glorious and Exalted, revealed to him: "I am with the one who remembers
Me"
Musa {a.s} then said: "O’ Lord {AZJ}, there are circumstances in which I hold You in such
reverence that I would not mention You."
Allah {SWT} said: "O’ Musa, remember Me in all circumstances."
commentary:
And it is not permissible for a man to enter the restroom with a ring bearing the name
of Allah {SWT} or with a Qur'an. If he enters while wearing a ring with Allah’s {SWT} name,
he should switch it to his left hand when he wants to perform istinja (cleaning oneself).
Similarly, if the ring is made of Zamzam stone, he should remove it while performing
istinja. Once a man has finished relieving himself, he should say, "Praise be to Allah
{SWT}, who has removed harm from me and provided me with sustenance and granted
me relief from affliction."
Istinja should be done with three stones and then with water ; if one uses only water,
that suffices.
It is not permissible to use dung or bones for istinja, as the delegation of jinn came to
the Messenger of Allah {saws} and requested sustenance, and he gave them dung and
bones.
Therefore, it is inappropriate to use these for istinja.

english_text:
People used to perform istinja (cleaning after relieving oneself) with stones, and
a man from the Ansar ate some food, which upset his stomach. He then performed
istinja with water. Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: "Indeed, Allah {SWT} loves
those who repent and loves those who purify themselves." (Surah Al Baqarah 2:222).
The Messenger of Allah {saws} called him, and the man feared that something negative
had been revealed about him. When he entered, the Prophet asked him, "Have you
done anything today?"
He replied: "Yes, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, I ate some food, which upset my
stomach, so I performed istinja with water."
The Prophet then said:
"Rejoice! For Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, has revealed concerning you: 'Indeed,
Allah {SWT} loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves.' You are
among the first to repent and among the first to purify themselves."
commentary:
It is said that this man was Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari.
Furthermore, when one wishes to perform istinja, he should wipe from the area of the
anus to the testicles three times, then shake the private part three times. When
pouring water over his hand for istinja, he should say, "Praise be to Allah {SWT}, who
made water purifying and did not make it impure." He should pour on his private part
twice the amount of water that was on it from urine; this is the minimum required. Then
he should perform istinja for feces and wash until clean. The person performing istinja
should pour water when the flow of urine has stopped.
If someone prays and remembers afterward that he did not wash his private part, he
must wash it and repeat his ablution and prayer. However, if he forgets to perform
istinja after relieving himself and prays, he does not need to repeat the prayer.
For feces, it is sufficient to perform istinja with stones, pottery, or soil (apart from
water).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 129 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 354

fulfilled”.

: ولأ ي ح ور إلي ع وط ق ى ق ي ى إلن ز إل وي حث إلأ س ح ار إلمي مزة ، وإلعله ق ى ذ لك
english_text:
The Prophet, said to some of his wives:
"Tell the believing women to perform istinja with water and to be thorough in it, for it is
a means of purification for the private parts and helps prevent hemorrhoids."
commentary:
It is not permissible to relieve oneself in shaded areas or under fruit-bearing trees. The
reasoning for this is: (continues to next Hadith)
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

وَّ لَّوْ لأَّ إ َّن َّ مَّ عَّهَّا مَّ ن ْ ي َّمْ ن َّعُّهَّا
َّلَّأ َّكَّلَّي ْه
ا إَّلسِّ ن َّاعُّ وَّ هَّوَّ إم ُّ إَّلْأ َّرْ ض ِ إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ ق ِي هَّا ي َّمَّزَّي ُّهَّا .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Indeed, Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, has appointed angels to protect the
vegetation of the earth, including trees and palm trees. There is no tree or palm except
that there is an angel with it from Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, who guards it. If it
were not for the presence of those angels to protect them, wild animals and pests
would consume their fruits."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 56, p. 239

Chapter Title: SEEKING PLACE TO RELIEVE ONESELF AND MANNERS OF ENTER AND EXIT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ إ ِن َّمَّا ن َّهَّى رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ َّن ْ ي َّص ْ زِب َّ إ َّجَّ ذ مِن َّ إَّلْمُّسْ لِمِي ن َّ ج َّ لاَّءَّة ْي َّحْ ث َّ س َّ ح َّ زَّة ٍ إ َّوْ ن َّح ْ لَّه ٍ ق َّذ

ُّي َّحْ ص ُّ زُّة .
ومن لأ ي ن ق طغ ن وله وي ع لن ه ق الله . إ ولى ن العذ ر ق لي ي ق علي ه ما إسي طاع ولي ي ح ذ ج زي طه
ومن ن ال ولم ي ي ع وط ق لي س علي ه إلأسي ن ح اء وإ ن ما علي ه ع سل ذ كزة، ومن ي ع وط ولم ي ن ل ق لي س علي ه إ ن ي ع سل ذ كزة وإ ن ما
. علي ه إ ن ي سي ن ح ى
.ومن ي وص ا ي م ج زج ث من ه ري ح ق لي س علي ه إلأسي ن ح اء وإ ن ما علي ه إ عاذة إلوص وء
english_text:
(Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} ) has narrated: "The Messenger of Allah
{saws} prohibited any Muslim from relieving himself under a tree or palm that has borne
fruit due to the presence of the angels assigned to them. Imam {a.s} said:
'That is why trees and palms seem luster when they bear fruit, for the angels are
present there.'".
commentary:
For one who suffers from a continual inability to control their urine, Allah {SWT} is more
deserving of the excuse. They should take precautions as much as they can and
should use a cloth (to protect themselves). (means to prevent urine from spreading).
If someone urinates but does not defecate, they are not required to perform istinja;
they only need to wash their private part. If someone defecates but does not urinate,
they are not required to wash their private part, but they must perform istinja.
If someone performs ablution and then passes gas, they are not required to perform
istinja; they only need to repeat their ablution.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 327

arabic_text:

مِن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ سَّ م َّاةُّ «ن َّلَّع َّن ِى إ َّن َّهُّ إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ زَّج َّ ث ْ مِن ْهُّ رِي ح إِسْ ي َّن ْح َّ ى .
english_text:
It was narrated that Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} would awaken
from his sleep, perform ablution, and not perform istinja.
He expressed astonishment at a man whom he referred to, saying, "I have heard that
when he passes gas, he performs istinja."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 44 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 135 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 345

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The prayer consists of three parts: one-third is for purification, one-third is for bowing
(ruku), and one-third is for prostration (sujud) "

arabic_text:

english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"When the time for prayer enters, purification (ablution) and the prayer become
obligatory, and there is no prayer without purification."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 140 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 43 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 372 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 203

ُّ«إِق ْي ِي َّاحُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءُّ وَّ ي َّحْ زِي مُّهَّا إَّلي َّكْن ِي زُّ وَّ ي َّحْ لِي لُّهَّا إَّلي َّسْ لِي م .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}, said:
"The initiation of prayer is purification (ablution), its prohibition is the takbir (saying
'Allahu Akbar'), and its permissibility is the Tasleem (saying 'Assalamu Alaikum')."
commentary:
The obligations of Salat are seven: timing, purification, attention, facing the Qibla,
bowing (Rukuh), prostration (Sujood) and supplication.

ب اب-
مق دار الماء للوض وء والغ سل

صَّ ل َّى ُّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ج َّ مْ سَّ ه ُّ إ َّمْ ذَّإذٍ وَّ إَّلْمُّذ ُّ وَّ ر ْن ُّ مِان َّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ ي َّمَّان ِي ن َّ ذِرْهَّماً وَّ إَّلذِّرْهَّمُّ سِ ي َّه
ِّ ذَّوَّ إن ِي ق َّ وَّ إَّلذ َّإن ِق ُّ وَّ ر ْن ُّ سِ ث
ِجَّ ن َّاب ٍ وَّ إَّلْحَّ ن َّه ُّ وَّ ر ْن ُّ جَّ ن َّي َّي ْن ِ مِن ْ س َّ عِي زٍ مِن ْ إ َّوْ سَّ اطِ إَّلْحَّ ث ِّ لأَّ مِن ْ ص ِع َّارِةِ وَّ لأَّ مِن ْ كِن َّارِة .
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} said:
"For ghusl (ritual washing), a saa' of water is required, and for wudu (ablution), a mud
of water is sufficient.
The saa' of The Prophet {saws} is five amdad (measures), and the mud weighs two
hundred and eighty dirhams. One dirham is six danaq (small units), and one danaq
weighs six grains.
The grain should be from medium-quality barley, not from the small or large types”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Ma’ani al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 249 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 135 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 121 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 314 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 481 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 350

arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:

ِق َّا ُّولَّن ِك َّ عَّلَّى ج ِ لاَّف ِ سُّ ن َّي ِى وَّ إَّلي َّان ِث ُّ عَّلَّى سُّ ن َّي ِى مَّ عِى ق ِى جَّ ط ِ ي زَّة ِ إَّلْق ُّذْ س .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"Ablution (wudu) is a mud (a specific measure), and ghusl (ritual washing) is a saa' (a
larger measure). There will come people after me who will underestimate these
amounts, and those will be contrary to my Sunnah.
The one who adheres to my Sunnah will be with me in the enclosure of holiness
(Paradise)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Ash'athiyat, Part 1, p. 16 • Al-Wadar (Lil-Rawandi) Vol. 1, p. 44 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 313 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 483 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Part 1, p. 347

مِي ْلُّ ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّاس ْ ي َّزَّي ْث ُّ وَّ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ْب ُّ وَّ مَّ ا ي َّسُّ وو ُّن ِى ن ِذ َّلِك َّ مَّ ال كَّي ِي ز .
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} was asked about a man who
needed to perform wudu for prayer but could not find water, except for a quantity of
water worth a hundred dirhams. Should he buy it to perform wudu or should he
perform tayammum (dry ablution)?
Imam {a.s} said: ""Rather, he should buy it. I have experienced a similar situation, and I
bought it and performed wudu and I would not mind having that money”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 370 • Muskkin al-Fu’ād, Part 1, p. 141 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 523 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 243 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 356

english_text:
Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} and his wife performed ghusl using five amdad from one
container."
Zurarah then asked how it was done.
Imam {a.s} said: "He started by immersing his hand in the water before hers and
cleansed his private part. Then She did the same and cleansed her private part. After
that, he poured water over himself, and She poured water over herself until they were
finished. The amount that the Prophet used for ghusl was three amdad, while She used
two muds. This was sufficient for both of them because they shared the same water.
However, for someone who performs ghusl alone, they must use a saa'."
commentary:
For wudu, three handfuls of water are required: one for the face and two for the arms.
If someone can only manage one handful of water, they should divide it into three
parts.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"A man may worship Allah {SWT} for forty years but does not truly obey Him in wudu
(ablution) because he washes what Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him
to wipe."

english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Shall I not describe the ablution of the Messenger of Allah {saws} to you?"
They replied: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} then called for a bowl containing some water and placed it in front of him.
He rolled up his sleeves, dipped his right hand into the water, and said: "This is if the
hand is pure."
Imam {a.s} then scooped a full handful of water, placed it on his forehead, "In the name
of Allah {SWT}," allowing the water to flow over the edges of his beard.
Then Imam {a.s} passed his hand over his face and the front of his temples once.
Imam {a.s} dipped his left hand into the water, scooped a full handful, and placed it on
his right elbow, running his hand along his forearm until the water flowed over the tips
of his fingers.
Imam {a.s} then scooped with his right hand again and placed it on his left elbow,
running his hand along his forearm until the water flowed over the tips of his fingers.
He then wiped front of his head and the tops of his feet with the leftover moisture from
the water.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE DESCRIPTION OF THE ABLUTION OF THE MESSENGER OF ALLAH {saws}
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} performed wudu and then wiped over his sandals.
Al-Mughirah said to him: "Did you forget, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}?"
He {saws} replied: "No, rather it is you who has forgotten. This is how my Lord {AZJ}
commanded me."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 286 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 460

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"By Allah {SWT}, the ablution of the Messenger of Allah {saws} was performed only once for
each part, and The Prophet {saws} performed wudu once for each action."
Imam {a.s} said: "This is an ablution that Allah {SWT} does not accept the prayer without
it”.
commentary:
As for the reports that have been narrated about performing wudu twice for each
action: (continues to next hadith)
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 318 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 438

english_text:
In a broken chain of narration, Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal recounts from those who
narrated from Abu Abdullah {a.s} who said: "Allah {SWT} made ablution (wudu) obligatory
once for each action, but the Messenger of Allah {saws} prescribed it twice for the
people”.
commentary:
The chain of narration is disconnected, and this is in the form of denial (that Prophet
‘exceeded’ the limit of Allah {SWT}), and not informing (of the limit being exceeded).
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} recalled this report is in the context to refute it, and not to ‘report’
it.
This is stated in a manner of condemnation, rather than mere reporting, as if He {a.s} is
saying: ‘Allah {SWT} has set a limit, and the Messenger of Allah {saws} has ‘exceeded’ it?
(How can this be?) when Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, has said: "And whoever transgresses
the limits of Allah {SWT} has certainly wronged himself."’ (Surah At Talaq 65:1)
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 318 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 439

It has been narrated (by Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} ) that:
"Ablution is a limit set by Allah {SWT} so that He may know who obeys Him and who
disobeys Him. And a believer is not made impure by anything ; rather, something like
oil is sufficient for him”.

"Whoever exceeds the prescribed limits in his ablution (wudu) is like one who nullifies
it”.

english_text:
In another narration with a broken chain, Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam said: "I was
informed by someone who heard Abu Abdullah {a.s} say: 'I am amazed at those who
prefer to perform wudu twice, while the Messenger of Allah {saws} performed it twice.
The Prophet {saws} would renew his ablution for each obligatory prayer and each
prayer.'"
commentary:
The meaning of this narration is that I am astonished at those who neglect to renew
their ablution when the Prophet did so. The report that states "Whoever exceeds twice
will not be rewarded" supports what I have mentioned. It means that renewing wudu
after it has already been done does not carry a reward, similar to the call to prayer
(adhan). For instance, one who prays Dhuhr and Asr with one adhan and two iqamah
suffices, and it is better to call the adhan for Asr as well. The third call to prayer is an
innovation with no reward. The reports indicating that twice is better imply the renewal
of wudu, and those mentioning two times indicate its thoroughness (i.e., performing it
well).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text: َّو ِرُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّ ي َّح ْ ذِي ذَّ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءِ لِصَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْعِس َّ اءِ ي َّمْ حُّ و لأَّ وَّ إَّلل َّهِ وَّ ن َّلَّى وَّ إَّلل َّه.

(Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} ) narrated that:
"Renewing wudu for the Isha prayer erases sins, by Allah {SWT}, indeed it does, by Allah
{SWT}."

english_text:
(Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} ) narrated in another report that:
"Ablution (wudu) upon wudu is light upon light, and whoever renews their wudu
without having incurred a new state of impurity, Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, renews
their repentance without requiring further forgiveness."
commentary:
Allah {SWT} Almighty has entrusted the Prophet {saws} with matters of religion, but He did
not entrust him with transgressing the established boundaries set by divine law.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 367

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} has narrated;
"Whoever performs wudu twice will not be rewarded."
commentary:
This means that by performing wudu in a manner different from what has been
prescribed, one does not earn the reward that was promised for proper adherence to
the ritual. The comparison is made to a worker who does not perform the task they
were hired for; they would not receive payment for not fulfilling the terms of their
agreement.

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"One day, The Commander of the Faithful {a.s} was sitting with Muhammad ibn al-
Hanafiyyah when He said to him: 'O’ Muhammad, bring me a container of water so I
can perform wudu for prayer.'
Muhammad brought him water.
Imam {a.s} poured it with his right hand onto his left hand, then said:
'In the name of Allah {SWT} and by Allah {SWT}, and all praise is due to Allah {SWT} who made
water purifying and did not make it impure.'
He then performed istinja and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, protect my private part and keep it chaste; cover my private areas and
forbid me from the Fire.'.
Then He rinsed his mouth and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, grant me the ability to present my arguments on the Day I meet You, and
loosen my tongue to remember You and to thank You.'.
He then sniffed water and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, do not make me forbidden from the fragrance of Paradise, and make me
among those who can smell its scent and enjoy its sweetness.'.
He washed his face and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, make my face white on the Day when faces are darkened, and do not
make my face dark on the Day when faces are made luminous.'.
He then washed his right hand and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, grant me my book in my right hand and grant me eternity in Paradise with
my left hand, and hold me accountable with an easy account.'
He then washed his left hand and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, do not grant me my book in my left hand, and do not make it tied around
my neck. I seek refuge in You, O’ my Lord {AZJ}, from the torments of the Fire.'
He then wiped his head and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, envelop me in Your mercy, blessings, and forgiveness.'
He then wiped his feet and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, keep me steadfast on the Straight Path on the Day when the feet may
slip, and make my efforts pleasing to You, O’ Lord {AZJ} of Glory and Honor.'
He then raised his head and looked at Muhammad and said:
'O’ Muhammad, whoever performs wudu like my wudu and recites like my recitations,
Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, will create an angel from every drop [of water] that
purifies him, and that angel will glorify and praise Allah {SWT}, and Allah {SWT}, Mighty and
Majestic, will record the reward for him until the Day of Resurrection.'".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 16 • Al- Amali (by Al-Saduq) Vol. 1, p. 554 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 53 • Al-Waezin School, Vol. 2, p. 305 • Falah Al-Sael, Part 1, p. 52 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 28 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 401 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 318

english_text:
It was noted that The Commander of the Faithful {a.s} would not allow anyone to
pour water on him while performing wudu.
When he was asked: "O’ Commander of the Faithful, why do you not let them pour
water on you?"
Imam {a.s} said: "I do not like to share my prayer with anyone”.
He also recited the verse of Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted:
"And whoever expects to meet his Lord {AZJ}, let him do righteous work and not associate
anyone in the worship of his Lord {AZJ}." (Surah Al Kahf 18:110).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 330 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 477

ِإَّلذ ُّعَّاء .
english_text:
It is narrated that Commander of the Faithful {a.s}, when performing wudu, would
say:
"In the name of Allah {SWT} and by Allah {SWT}, and the best names for Allah {SWT} and the
greatest names for Allah {SWT}, who is the Dominant over those in the heavens and the
Dominant over those on the earth. All praise is due to Allah {SWT}, who has made from
water every living thing and has revived my heart with faith. O’ Allah {SWT}, accept my
repentance and purify me. Grant me goodness and show me all I love, and open for
me the avenues of good from You, O’ Hearer of Supplication."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 328 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 424

english_text:
Zurarah bin A'yan said to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}:
"Inform me about the limits of the face that one should wash, as mentioned by Allah
{SWT}, Mighty and Majestic."
Imam {a.s} said: "The face that Allah {SWT} has commanded to be washed is that which no
one should add to or subtract from. If someone adds to it, they will not be rewarded,
and if they subtract from it, they will sin. The area includes from the hairline of the head
to the chin, and what is encompassed by the thumbs (when making a circle with the
fingers) is considered part of the face. Anything outside of that is not considered part
of the face”.
Zurarah asked: "What about the temples?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
Zurarah then said: "What if it is surrounded by hair?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Whatever is surrounded by hair is not required for the servants to seek
or look for; however, water should flow over it."
commentary:
Regarding the washing of the hands, it extends from the elbows to the tips of the
fingers. The limit for wiping the head is to wipe with three joined fingers from the front
of the head. The limit for wiping the feet is to place your hands at the tips of your toes
and extend them to the ankles, starting with the right foot before the left, and this
should be done with what remains of moisture on the hands without renewing the
water. There should be no hair returned during the washing of the hands or the wiping
of the head and feet.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

ْ«ي َّان ِغْ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءِ كَّمَّا ق َّالَّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ إِن ْذَّإ ْ ن ِالْوَّ ج ْ هِ ي ُّم َّ ن ِالْي َّذَّ ي ْن ِ ي ُّم َّ إِمْ سَّ ح

ْن ِالْوَّ ج ْ هِ وَّ إ َّعِ ذْ عَّلَّى إَّلذ ِّرَّإعِ وَّ إ ِن ْ مَّ سَّ حْ ث َّ إَّلزِّج ْ لَّ ق َّن ْلَّ إَّلز َّإ ْسِ ق َّامْ سَّ حْ عَّلَّى إَّلز َّإ ْسِ ي ُّم َّ إ َّعِ ذ

ِإَّلل َّهُّ ن ِه.
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Follow the sequence of wudu as Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded.
Start with the face, then the hands, then wipe the head and the feet. Do not precede
anything before what you are commanded.
If you wash the arm before the face, start with the face and then repeat on the arm. If
you wipe the foot before the head, then wipe the head and then repeat on the foot.
Begin with what Allah {SWT} has started with."
Similarly, in the adhan to Salat and the iqamah, start with the first (shahada) and then
the second (shahada) and so forth.
If you say: ‘Hasten to prayer (Hayya allas’Salat)’ before the testimonies, then you will
again start with the testimonies and then repeat ‘Hasten to prayer.’"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 34 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 97 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 73 • Fiqh al-Qur'ān, Part 1, p. 28 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 2, p. 197 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 343 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 448 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 362 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p.

english_text:
It has been narrated in another report: "In the case of someone who starts
washing their left arm before their right, they should wash their right arm again and
then wash their left arm again”.
It has also been reported, "that they should wash their left arm again”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 344 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 453

ً«إِع ْ سِ لْ ي َّذَّك َّ مِن َّ إَّلْن َّوْ لِ مَّ ز َّة ً وَّ مِن َّ إَّلْع َّان ِظِ مَّ ز َّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّان َّه ِ ي َّلاَّي ا .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "Wash your hand after urine once,
after defecation twice, and after janabah (ritual impurity) three times."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 332 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 428

ً «إِع ْ سِ لْ ي َّذَّك َّ مِن َّ إَّلن َّوْ مِ مَّ ز َّة .
ومن كان وص و وة من إلن وم ون سى [إ ن ي ع سل ي ذة] ق ا ذج ل ي ذة إلماء ق ن ل إ ن ي ع سلها ق علي ه إ ن ي صث ذ لك إلماء ولأ ي سي عمله
.ق ا ن إ ذج لها ق ى إلماء من جذب إلن ول وإلع ان ظ ق ن ل إ ن ي ع سلها ن اسي ا ق لا ن ا س ن ه. إ لأ إ ن ي كون ق ى ي ذة ق ذ ر ي ن ح س إلماء
وإلوص وء مزة مزة ، ومن ي وص ا مزي ي ن لم ي و ج ز ومن ي وص ا ي لاي ا ق ق ذ إ ن ذع، ومن مسح ن اطن ق ذمي ه ق ق ذ ي ن غ وسوإس
. إلس ي طان
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"When you wake up from your sleep, wash your hands once”.
commentary:
He added that if someone performed wudu after sleeping and forgot to wash their
hand before putting it in the water, they must pour that water out and not use it for
ablution.
However, if they put their hand in the water after using the bathroom (urine or
defecation) before washing it while forgetting, it is permissible. This is unless there is
something impure on their hand that would make the water impure.
Furthermore, wudu should be performed once for each action, and whoever performs
it twice will not be rewarded. If someone performs wudu three times, they have
innovated, and whoever wipes the soles of their feet is following the whispers of Satan.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 332 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 428

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD

َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
