ومن كان ن ه ق ى إلموإص غ إلي ى ي ح ث علي ها إلوص وء ق زجه إ و ج زإجه إ و ذمامي ل ولم ي و ذ ة جلها، ق لي حلها ولي ع سلها، وإ ن إ ص ز
.ن ه جلها، ق لي مسح ي ذة على إلح ن ان ز وإلق زوح ولأ ي حلها ولأ ي عن ث ن ح زإجي ه
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"If I had not seen the Messenger of Allah {saws} wiping over the tops of his feet, I would
have thought that the soles of the feet should be wiped instead of the tops”.
commentary:
If someone has sores, wounds, or boils in the places where wudu is required, and
removing them does not harm them, they should remove them and wash the affected
areas.
If removing them would cause harm, they should wipe over the bandages and sores
without removing them or tampering with their wounds.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 292 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 416

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD

- وَّ ق َّذْ رُّوِى َّ: ق ِى إَّلْح َّ ن َّان ِزِ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ «ي َّع ْ سِ لُّ مَّ ا جَّ وْ لَّهَّا .
ولأ ي ح ور إلمسح على إلعمامه ولأ على إلق لن سوة ولأ على إلح ق ي ن وإلح ورن ي ن إ لأ ق ى جال إلي ق ي ه وإلح ي ق ه من إلعذو إ و ق ى
.ي لح ي ح اف ق ي ه على إلزج لي ن ، ي ق ام إلح ق ان مق ام إلح ن ان ز ق ي مسح علي هما
english_text:
It has been narrated about bandages from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s}:
Imam {a.s} said: "Wash that which is around them."
commentary:
It is not permissible to wipe over a turban (Amamah), a cap (qalansuwah), or leather
socks (khuffs) and stockings (jawrab) except in cases of necessity, such as during fear
of an enemy or in snow where there is a risk to the feet.
The leather socks can be treated like bandages, and one can wipe over them.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 464

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلْعَّالِمُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِّ «ي َّلاَّي َّه لأَّ إ َّي َّق ِى ق ِي هَّا إ َّجَّ ذإً س ُّ زْب ُّ إَّلْمُّسْ كِزِ وَّ إَّلْمَّسْ حُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْح ُّ ق َّي ْن ِ وَّ مُّي ْعَّه ُّ إَّلْحَّ ح .
english_text:
The scholar, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said:
"There are three things in which I do not fear anyone (taqiyya): drinking intoxicants,
wiping over the leather socks (khuffs), and the Hajj Tamattu'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 292

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
arabic_text:
َّو َّ رَّوَّ ب ْ عَّان ِس َّ ه ُّ عَّن ِ إَّلن َّن ِى ِّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ َّس َّ ذ ُّ إَّلن َّاسِ جَّ سْ زَّة ً ي َّوْ مَّ إَّلْق ِي ُّامَّ ه ِ مَّ ن ْ رَّإ َّى وُّص ُّ وءَّة
ِعَّلَّى ج ِ لْذِ ع َّي ْ زِة.
english_text:
Aisha narrated from the Prophet {saws}, that He said:
"The people with the most regret on the Day of Resurrection will be those who sees his
wudu (ablution) on the skin of someone else”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 306 • Tafsir al-Safi, Part 2, p. 15 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 461 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 10, p. 399 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 31, p. 37 • Tafsir Kanz al-Daqa’iq, Part 4, p. 50

ولم ي عزف للن ن ى صلى إلله علي ه وإ له ج ف إ لأ ج ق ا إ هذإة له إلن ح اس ى ، وكان موص غ ط هز إلق ذمي ن من ه مس ق وق ا، ق مسح إلن ن ى
صلى إلله علي ه وإ له على رج لي ه وعلي ه ج ق اة، ق ق ال إلن اس: إ ن ه مسح على ج ق ي ه على إ ن إلحذي ث ق ى ذ لك ع ي ز صحي ح
إلأسن اذ.
english_text:
It was narrated from Aisha that The Prophet {saws} narrated:
"I would prefer to wipe over the back of a donkey in the wilderness than to wipe over
my leather socks (khuffs)."
commentary:
It is noted that the Prophet Muhammad {saws} did not possess any leather socks except
for a pair that was gifted to him by the Negus (the king of Abyssinia). These socks had
a split in the area covering the tops of the feet.
The Prophet wiped over his feet while wearing these socks.
When people saw this, they said he had wiped over his leather socks (but he had not).
However, the authenticity of this narration is not confirmed.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 31, p. 38

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
english_text:
Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about a man whose leather socks
(khuffs) are torn, and he puts his hand in and wipes over the tops of his feet. Is this
sufficient?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

ٍوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إ َّن ُّو إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّز ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم ُّ: عَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ ق ُّطِ عَّث ْ ي َّذُّةُّ مِن َّ إَّلْمِزْق َّق ِ كَّي ْف َّ ي َّي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ُّ ق َّالَّ «ي َّع ْ سِ ل
ِمَّ ا ن َّق ِى َّ مِن ْ عَّص ُّ ذِة.
وَّ كَّذ َّلِك َّ رُّوِى َّ: ق ِى ق َّطْ غِ إَّلزِّج ْ لِ «وَّ إ ِذ َّإ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّب ِ ، إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ُّ إ َّلْق َّث ْ ق ِن َّاعَّهَّا عَّن ْ مَّ وْ ص ِ غِ مَّ سْ حِ رَّإ ْسِ هَّا
َّق ِى صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْع َّذَّإة ِ وَّ إَّلْمَّع ْ زِب ِ وَّ ي َّمْ سَّ حُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ ي ُّح ْ ز ِي هَّا ق ِى سَّ ان ِزِ إَّلص َّ لَّوَّ إب ِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّذْ ج ِ لَّ إ ِصْ ن َّعَّه ْ ا ق َّي َّمْ سَّ حَّ عَّلَّى رَّإ ْسِ هَّا مِن

english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}, was asked about a man
whose hand was cut off at the elbow. How should he perform wudu?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should wash what remains of his forearm."
And similarly, it was narrated regarding the amputation of the leg.
When a woman performs wudu, She should remove her head covering (niqab) from
the area where She wipes her head during the Fajr and Maghrib prayers, and She can
wipe over it. In all other prayers, She may insert her finger to wipe over her head without
having to remove her head covering.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 208 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 29 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 360 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 363 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 479

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD

ِإَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ن ِط َّ اهِزِ إَّلذ ِّرَّإع .
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} said: "Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, has
prescribed for people in wudu that a woman should begin with the inner part of her
arm, while a man should begin with the outer part of his arm”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 467

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«مَّ ن ْ ذ َّكَّزَّ إِسْ مَّ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّى وُّص ُّ ون ِهِ ق َّكَّا َّن َّمَّا إِع ْ ي َّسَّ ل .
english_text:
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: 'Whoever mentions the name of Allah {SWT} while
performing wudu (ablution) is as if they have taken a full bath (ghusl).'".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Thawāb al-Aʿmāl wa ʿIqāb al-Aʿmāl, Part 1, p. 15 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 358 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 67 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 327 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 423 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 425 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 315

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّ مَّ ن ْ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّ ق َّذ َّكَّزَّ إِسْ مَّ إَّلل َّهِ طَّ هُّزَّ ج َّ مِي غُّ ج َّ سَّ ذِةِ وَّ كَّان َّ إَّلْوُّ ص ُّ وءُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءِ كَّق َّ ارَّة ً لِمَّا ن َّي ْن َّهُّمَّا مِن
ْ إَّلذ ُّن ُّوب ِ وَّ مَّ ن ْ لَّمْ ي ُّسَّ مِّ لَّمْ ي َّطْ هُّزْ مِن ُّج َّ سَّ ذِةِ إ ِلأ َّ مَّ ا إ َّصَّ ان َّهُّ إَّلْمَّاء .
english_text:
It is narrated: 'Whoever performs ablution and mentions the name of Allah {SWT},
all of his body becomes pure, and the ablution performed between two ablutions
serves as atonement for the sins committed between them.
And whoever does not mention [the name of Allah {SWT}] will not purify his body except
for what the water touches.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Thawāb al-Aʿmāl wa ʿIqāb al-Aʿmāl, Part 1, p. 15 • Ilal al- Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 289 • Rawdat al-Wa’izin, Vol. 2, p. 306 • Jami’ al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 63 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 328 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 425 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 314

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
arabic_text:

َّذ ُّن ُّون ِهِ ق ِى ن َّهَّارِةِ مَّ ا ج َّ لاَّ إَّلْكَّن َّان ِزَّ وَّ مَّ ن ْ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّ لِصَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلص ُّ ن ْحِ كَّان َّ وُّ ص ُّ وو ُّةُّ ذ َّلِك َّ كَّق َّارَّة ً لِم ِا مَّ ص َّ ى مِن ْ ذ ُّن ُّون ِهِ ق ِى لَّي ْلَّي ِه
ْإ ِلأ َّ إَّل َّكَّن َّان ِز.
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} said:
'Whoever performs ablution for the Maghrib prayer, his ablution serves as atonement
for the sins he committed during the day, except for the major sins.
And whoever performs ablution for the Fajr prayer, his ablution serves as atonement
for the sins he committed during the night, except for the major sins.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 70 • Thawāb al-Aʿmāl wa ʿIqāb al- Aʿmāl, Part 1, p. 17 • Rawdat al-Wa’izin, Vol. 2, p. 306 • Jami’ al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 64 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 366 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 376 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 231

Chapter Title: THE LIMITS OF ABLUTION, ITS ORDER AND REWARD
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ و ِإ لِه:
َّ«إِق ْي َّحُّ وإ عُّي ُّون َّكُّمْ عِ ن ْذَّ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءِ لَّعَّل َّهَّا لأَّ ي َّزَّى ن َّارَّ ج َّ هَّن َّم .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"'Open your eyes during ablution, so that they may not see the fire of Hell.'".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Thawāb al-Aʿmāl wa ʿIqāb al-Aʿmāl, Part 1, p. 17 • Ilal al- Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 280 • Jami’ al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 64 • Miftāḥ al-Falāḥ, Part 1, p. 24 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 334 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 486 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 336 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 346 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 3, p. 270

.ماء
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
'Whoever performs ablution and wipes himself (with a towel) will have a good deed
written for him. And whoever performs ablution and does not wipe himself until his
ablution dries, Allah {SWT} will write for him thirty good deeds.'.
commentary:
And it is permissible for a man to pray with one ablution for all the prayers of the night
and day as long as he does not break his ablution, and the same applies to a single
tayammum (dry ablution) as long as he does not break it or find water.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Rawdat al-Wa’izin, Vol. 2, p. 306

.ق ا ذ إ كان مغ إلزج ل ج اي م ق لي ذورة ق ى إلوص وء، وي حوله عن ذ إلع سل
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"'When a man performs ablution, let him splash his face with water, for if he is drowsy,
it will awaken him, and if it is cold, he will not feel the cold.'".
commentary:
If a man has a ring, he should rotate it during ablution and remove it during a wash
(ghusl).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 281 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 357 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 68 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 333 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 434 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 337

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"And if you forget (to rotate your ring in ablution) until you stand in Salat, then I do not
command you to repeat it (Salat)."
commentary:
And if a man wakes up from his sleep and has not relieved himself, he should not put
his hand in the vessel until he washes it, for he does not know where his hand has been
during the night.
The supplication of ablution is for the person performing it to say: supplication of
ablution is for the one performing it to say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, I ask You for the completion of my ablution, the completion of my prayer,
Your pleasure, and Paradise.'
This is the supplication of ablution.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 281

ْ «مَّ ا ر َّإلَّ ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي ُّوصِ ي ن ِى ن ِالسِّ وَّ إك ِ جَّ ي َّى ج َّ س ِ ي ث ُّ إ َّن
َّإ ُّجْ ق ِى َّ إ َّوْ إ َّذْ رَّذَّ وَّ مَّ ا ر َّإلَّ ي ُّوصِ ي ن ِى ن ِالْح َّ ارِ جَّ ي َّى ط َّ ن َّن ْث ُّ إ َّن َّهُّ سَّ ي ُّوَّ رِّي ُّهُّ وَّ مَّ ا ر َّإلَّ ي ُّوصِ ي ن ِى ن ِالْم ُّمْ لُّوك ِ جَّ ي َّى ط َّ ن َّن ْث ُّ إ َّن َّه
ُّ سَّ ي َّص ْ زِب ِلَّهُّ إ َّج َّ لاً ي ُّعْ ي َّق ُّ ق ِي ه. وَّ ق ِى ج َّ ن َّزٍ إ ج َّ زَّ: «وَّ مَّ ا ر َّإلَّ ي ُّوصِ ي ن ِى ن ِالْمَّزْإ َّة ِ جَّ ي َّى ط َّ ن َّن ْث ُّ إ َّن َّهُّ لأَّ ي َّن ْن َّع ِى طَّ لاَّق ُّهَّا .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said: "Archangel Jibril {a.s} kept advising me about
the miswak until I feared I might wear down my teeth or make them fall out.
And Archangel Jibril {a.s} continued to advise me about the neighbor until I thought he
would make him an heir.
And Archangel Jibril {a.s} continued to advise me about servants until I thought he would
set a term for them to be freed."
In another report, "And Archangel Jibril {a.s} continued to advise me about women until
I thought that divorce would not be appropriate for them."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 48 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 7 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 5, p. 515

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ«ن َّز َّلَّ ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ن ِالسِّ وَّ إك ِ وَّ إَّلْحِ ح َّ امَّ ه ِ وَّ إَّلْح ِ لاَّل .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: 'Archangel Jibril {a.s} brought down
the practices of using the miswak, cupping (hijama), and flossing (khilal).'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 558 • Al-Ādāb al-Dīniyyah, Part 1, p. 71 • Al-Ādāb al-Dīniyyah, Part 1, p. 89 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 51 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 677 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 59, p. 117 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 63, p. 439 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 130 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 138

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ٍمُّوسَّ ى ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّز ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم ُّ : «إ َّكْلُّ إَّلْأ ُّس ْ ن َّان ِ ي ُّذ ِي ث ُّ إَّلْن َّذَّن َّ وَّ إَّلي َّذَّل ُّك ُّ ن ِالْح َّ ز َّف ِ ي ُّن ْلِى إَّلْح َّ سَّ ذَّ وَّ إَّلسِّ وَّ إك
َّق ِى إَّلْح َّ لاَّءِ ي ُّورِب ُّ إَّلْن َّح َّ ز .
english_text:
Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} said:
"Consuming ushnan (a type of cleansing herb) melts the body, scrubbing with pottery
wears out the body, and using a siwak in the bathroom causes bad breath”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 32 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 48 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 51 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 122 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 337 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 135 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 138

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«إ َّرْن َّغ مِن ْ سُّ ن َّن ِ إَّلْمُّزْسَّ لِي ن َّ إَّلي َّعَّط ُّ زُّ وَّ إَّلسِّ وَّ إك ُّ وَّ إَّلن ِّسَّ اءُّ وَّ إَّلْحِ ن َّاء .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Four practices are from the traditions of the messengers: applying fragrance, using
siwak (toothstick), having relations with women, and using henna."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 677 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 10 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 135

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ «إ ِن َّ إ َّق ْوَّ إهَّكُّمْ طُّ زُّق ُّ إَّلْق ُّزْإ ن ِ ق َّطَّ هِّ زُّوهَّا ن ِالسِّ وَّ إك .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"Your mouths are the pathways of the Quran, so purify them with siwak (toothstick)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Majmu’at Warram, Part 1, p. 7 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 676 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 23

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق ِى وَّ صِ ي َّي ِهِ لِعَّلِى ٍّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِّ«ي َّا عَّلِى ُّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ ن ِالسِّ وَّ إك ِ عِ ن ْذَّ وُّص ُّ وءِ كُّل
ٍ صَّ لاَّة .
english_text:
The Prophet {saws}, said in his will to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}:
"O’ Ali {a.s}, make sure to use siwak (toothstick) before wudu (ablution) for every prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 17

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said: "Siwak (tooth cleaning) is half of wudu
(ablution)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 49 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 676 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 17 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 136 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 343 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 346 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Part 1, p. 364

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ً«لَّم َّا ذَّج َّ لَّ إَّلن َّاسُّ ق ِى إَّلذِّ ي ن ِ إ َّق ْوَّ إج اً إ َّي َّي ْهُّمُّ إَّلْأ َّر ْذُّ إ َّرَّق َّهَّا ق ُّلُّون اً وَّ إ َّعْ ذ َّن َّهَّا إ َّق ْوَّ إها
ق َّق ِي لَّ ي َّا رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ ، هَّذ َّإ إ َّرَّق ُّهَّا ق ُّلُّون اً عَّزَّق ْن َّاةُّ ق َّلِمَّ صَّ ارَّب ْ إ َّعْ ذ َّن َّهَّا إ َّق ْوَّ إهاً ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن َّهَّا ْكَّان َّث ْ ي َّس ِ ي َّاك ُّ ق ِى إَّلْح َّ اهِلِي َّه .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said :
"When people entered the religion in large numbers, the tribe of Azd came among
them with the softest hearts and the sweetest mouths.
It was asked: 'O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, we understand why they have the softest
hearts, but why do they have the sweetest mouths?'
He {saws} said: 'They used to use siwak (toothstick) even in the pre-Islamic period.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 676 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 10 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 22, p. 312 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 136

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «لِكُّلِّ س َّ ى ْ ءٍ طَّ هُّور وَّ طَّ هُّورُّ إَّلْق َّمِ إَّلسِّ وَّ إك .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Everything has a means of purification, and the means of purification for the mouth is
the siwak (tooth cleaning)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 49 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 677 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 10 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 22, p. 312 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 136

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«إ ِن َّ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ كَّان َّ ي ُّكْي ِزُّ إَّلسِّ وَّ إك َّ وَّ لَّي ْسَّ ن ِوَّ إج ِ ث ٍ ق َّلا
ِي َّص ُّ ز ُّك َّ ي َّزْكُّهُّ ق ِى ق َّزْطِ إَّلْأ َّي َّام .
ولأ ن ا س إ ن ي سي اك إلصان م ق ى س هز رمص ان إ ى إلن هار س اء. ولأ ن ا س ن السوإك للمحزم، وي كزة إلسوإك ق ى إلحمام لأ ن ه ي ورب
ون اء إلأ سن ان ، وإلسوإك من إلحن ي ق ي ه وهى عس ز سن ن : ج مس ق ى ، إلزإ س وج مس ق ى إلح سذ، ق ا ما إلي ى ق ى إلزإ س ق المص مص ه
وإلأسي ن س اق ، و إلسوإك ، وق ض إلس ارب وإلق زق لمن طول س عز رإ سه، ومن لم ي ق زق س عز رإ سه ق زق ه إلله ي وم إلق ي امه ن من س ار
.من ن ار
. وإ ما إلي ى ق ى إلح سذ: ق الأسي ن ح اء، وإلح ي ان ، وجلق إلعان ه ، وق ض إلأ ط ق ار ون ي ف إلأ ن طي ن
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Indeed, the Messenger of Allah {saws} frequently used siwak (tooth cleaning), but it is
not obligatory, so it will not harm you if you leave it for a few days”.
commentary:
is permissible for a fasting person to use siwak at any time of the day in Month of
Ramadan, and for someone in a state of ihram (pilgrim's state) to use siwak. However,
using siwak in the bathhouse is discouraged, as it is believed to harm the teeth.
The siwak is part of the Hanifye Ibraheem sunnah, which consists of ten Sunnahs: five
for the head and five for the body.
As for those related to the head, they are; rinsing the mouth, cleaning the nose, using
siwak, trimming the mustache, and parting the hair. Those who do not part their hair
will have it parted by a saw of fire on the Day of Judgment.
As for those related to the body, they are; Cleansing after relieving oneself (istinja),
circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, clipping the nails, and plucking the armpit hair.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 563 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 677 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 11 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 134

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلْن َّاق ِزُّ وَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ٍ «صَّ لاَّة ُّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ن ِسِ وَّ إك ٍ إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ مِن ْ سَّ ن ْعِي ن َّ رَّكْعَّه ً ن ِع َّي ْ زِ سِ وَّ إك .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} and Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} said: "Two units of prayer performed with siwak (tooth cleaning) are better than
seventy units of prayer without siwak."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Ādāb al-Dīniyyah, Part 1, p. 72 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 50 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 137

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إَّلْن َّاق ِزُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ً ق ِى إَّلسِّ وَّ إك ِ «لأَّ ي َّذَّعْ هُّ ق ِى كُّلِّ ي َّلاَّي َّه ِ إ َّي َّامٍ وَّ لَّوْ إ َّن ْ ي ُّمِز َّةُّ مَّ ز َّة ً وَّ إجِ ذَّة .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said about the siwak:
"Do not neglect it for more than three days, even if you use it just once."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 50 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 137

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ً«إِكْي َّحِ لُّوإ وَّ ي ْزإً وَّ إِسْ ي َّاكُّوإ عَّزْص ا .
english_text:
The Prophet {saws} said: "Apply kohl in an odd number of strokes and use siwak
(tooth cleaning) across the width of the mouth”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Ādāb al-Dīniyyah, Part 1, p. 80 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 678 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 23 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 101

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
english_text:
It is reported that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} stopped using siwak
two years before he passed away, as his teeth had weakened.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 678 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 25 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 127

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّ وسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّز ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم ِ : عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّسْ ي َّاك ُّ مَّ ز َّة ً ن ِي َّذِةِ إ ِذ َّإ ق َّامَّ إ ِلَّى صَّ لاَّة
ِإَّلل َّي ْلِ وَّ هُّوَّ ي َّق ْذِرُّ عَّلَّى إَّلسِّ وَّ إك ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ اف َّ إَّلص ُّ ن ْحَّ ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} bout a man
who uses his hand to clean his teeth when he gets up for the night prayer (Salat Al Layl),
even though he has access to siwak.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he fears that dawn is approaching, there is no harm in doing so."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 250 • Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 207 • Makarim Al-Akhlaq, vol. 1, p. 50 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 127 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 341 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 84, p. 207

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ٍ «لَّوْ لأَّ إ َّن ْ إ َّس ُّ ق َّ عَّلَّى إ ُّم َّي ِى لَّأ َّمَّ زْ ي ُّهُّمْ ن ِالسِّ وَّ إك ِ عِ ن ْذَّ وُّ ص ُّ وءِ كُّلِّ صَّ لاَّة .
english_text:
The Prophet {saws} said: "If it were not burdensome for my community, I would
have commanded them to use siwak (tooth cleaning) with each wudu (ablution) before
every prayer."

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF SIWAK

with them in their bedding at night."

arabic_text:

english_text:
It is narrated: "The Kaaba complained to Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, about
the distress it suffered from the breaths of the polytheists.
Allah {SWT}, Exalted be He, revealed to it: 'Calm yourself, O’ Kaaba, for I will replace them
with a people who purify themselves with branches of trees.'
When Allah {SWT} sent His Prophet Muhammad {saws}, the Trustworthy Spirit, Archangel
Jibril {a.s}, descended upon him with the siwak (toothstick)."

ِ«ق ِى إَّلسِّ وَّ إك ِ إِي ْن َّي َّا عَّس ْ زَّة َّ ج َّ صْ لَّه ً هُّوَّ مِن َّ إَّلس ُّ ن َّه ِ وَّ مَّ طْ هَّزَّة لِلْق َّمِ وَّ مَّ ح ْ لاَّة لِلْن َّصَّ ز

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Siwak (tooth cleaning) has twelve benefits: it is part of the Sunnah (tradition), purifies
the mouth, improves vision, pleases the Merciful, whitens the teeth, removes decay,
strengthens the gums, increases appetite, removes phlegm, enhances memory,
multiplies good deeds, and brings joy to the angels."

english_text:
A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah {saws} and asked Him about
various matters. Among the questions they asked was: ‘Tell us, O’ Muhammad, why
these four parts are washed in ablution when they are the cleanest parts of the body?'
The Prophet {saws} replied: "When Satan whispered to Adam {a.s}, he approached the tree
and looked at it, and thus he lost the brightness of his face. Then he walked towards it
- this was the first step taken towards wrongdoing.
He reached out with his hand to take from it, and he ate. Consequently, the ornaments
and coverings left his body, and he placed his hands on his head and wept.
When Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic, accepted his repentance, He made it obligatory
upon him and his descendants to purify these four parts.
Thus, Allah {SWT} commanded the washing of the face because he had looked at the
tree, the washing of the hands up to the elbows because he had used them to take
from it, the wiping of the head because he had placed his hand on his head, and the
wiping of the feet because he had walked with them towards the wrongdoing
(khatee'ah)."

english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ar-Ridha {a.s} wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in response
to his questions: "The reason for wudu (ablution), for which it has become obligatory
for a servant to wash the face and arms, and to wipe the head and feet, is to prepare
to stand before Allah {SWT} Almighty, to face Him with one’s visible limbs, and to
encounter the noble recording angels with them.
The face is washed for the act of prostration and submission. The hands are washed
so that one may turn them over in prayer, supplicating with them, expressing hope and
reverence, and focusing in worship. The head and feet are wiped because they are
exposed, facing all conditions, and do not possess the same level of humility and
dedication as the face and arms."
commentary:
My father wrote in his letter: "If you finish part of your wudu and the water runs out
before you complete it, then when you bring water to continue, complete your wudu if
the parts you previously washed are still wet. But if they have dried, start your wudu
over. If some parts of your wudu dry before you complete it, but water is still available
to you, simply wash the remaining parts, whether the earlier parts have dried or not."

َّن ِا َّن َّك َّ صَّ ل َّي ْ ث َّ ي َّوْ ماً ن ِع َّي ْ زِ وُّ ص ُّ وءٍ وَّ مَّ زَّرْب َّ عَّلَّى ص َّ عِي ف ٍ ق َّلَّمْ ي َّن ْصُّ زْةُّ ق َّح َّ لَّذُّوةُّ ج َّ لْذَّة ً مِن ْ عَّذ َّإب ِ إ ُّلل َّهِ ي َّعَّالَّى ق َّامْ ي َّلَّا َّ ق َّن ْزُّة
ًن َّارإ.
english_text:
(Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} ) narrated:
"A certain man from among the scholars was placed in his grave, and it was said to
him:
'We will strike you with one hundred lashes from the punishment of Allah {SWT}, Mighty
and Majestic.' He replied: 'I cannot bear it.'
They continued to reduce the punishment, until it was brought down to one lash.
(Still) He said: 'I still cannot bear it.'
They replied: 'It is unavoidable.'
He asked: 'Why will you lash me?'
They said: 'We will lash you because one day you prayed without wudu (ablution), and
because you passed by a weak person and did not help him.'
So they lashed him once with a punishment from Allah {SWT}, and his grave was filled
with fire."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 43

Chapter Title: ON THOSE WHO OMIT WUDU OR PART OF IT, OR DOUBTS IN ITS COMPLETION
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
َّ«ي َّمَّان ِي َّه لأَّ ي َّق ْ ن َّلُّ إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّمْ صَّ لاَّة ً إَّلْعَّن ْذُّ إَّلْأ ن ِق ُّ جَّ ي َّى ي َّزْج ِ غَّ إ ِلَّى مَّ وْ لأَّةُّ و
َّإَّلن َّاس ِ ز ُّ عَّن ْ ر َّوْ ج ِ هَّا وَّ هُّوَّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا سَّ اج ِ ظ وَّ مَّ ان ِغُّ إَّلز َّكَّاة ِ وَّ إ ِمَّ امُّ ق َّوْ مٍ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ن ِهِمْ وَّ هُّمْ لَّهُّ ك ْارِهُّون َّ وَّ ي َّارِك ُّ إَّل َّوُّص ُّ وءِ و
َّإَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ُّ إَّلْمُّذْ رِكَّه ُّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ن ِع َّي ْ زِ ج ِ مَّارٍ وَّ إَّلز ِّن ِّي ن ُّ وَّ هُّوَّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي ُّذَّإق ِغُّ إَّلْن َّوْ لَّ وَّ إَّلْع َّان ِظَّ و
ُّ إَّلس َّ كْزَّإن .
. وي ارك إلوص وء ن اسي ا مي ى ذ كز ق علي ه إ ن ي ي وص ا وي عي ذ إلصلاة
english_text:
The Prophet, said:
"Allah {SWT} does not accept the prayer of eight types of people:
The runaway servant until he returns to his master,
The rebellious wife whose husband is displeased with her,
The one who withholds zakat,
The Imam whom people dislike to pray behind,
The one who neglects wudu,
The mature (of age) woman who prays without a head covering,
The one who prays while suppressing the urge to urinate or defecate (Zabeen),
And the one who is intoxicated."
commentary:
If someone forgets to perform wudu and remembers later, they must perform wudu
and repeat the prayer.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 44 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 8, p. 348

Chapter Title: ON THOSE WHO OMIT WUDU OR PART OF IT, OR DOUBTS IN ITS COMPLETION
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
«وُّص ِ غَّ عَّن ْ إ ُّم َّي ِى ي ِسْ عَّه ُّ إ َّس ْ ي َّاءَّ إَّلس َّ هْ وُّ وَّ إَّلْح َّ طَّ ا ُّ وَّ إَّلن ِّسْ ي َّان ُّ وَّ مَّ ا إ ُّكْزِهُّوإ
َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ مَّ ا لأَّ ي َّعْ لَّمُّون َّ وَّ مَّ ا لأَّ ي ُّطِ ي ق ُّون َّ وَّ إَّلطِّ ي َّزَّة ُّ وَّ إَّلْحَّ سَّ ذُّ وَّ إَّلي َّق َّك ُّزُّ ق ِى إَّلْوَّ سْ وَّ سَّ ه ِ ق ِى إ َّلْح َّ لْق ِ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّن ْطِ ق ِ إ ُّ لْأ ِن ْسَّ ان
ٍ ن ِس َّ ق َّه.
english_text:
The Prophet {saws} said:
"Nine things have been lifted from my community: mistakes, errors, forgetfulness,
what they are compelled to do, what they do not know, what they cannot endure,
superstitions, envy (if not acted upon), and thoughts of doubt in creation as long as a
person does not express them verbally."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 5, p. 1085 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 7, p. 293 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 8, p. 249 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 1, p. 637

Chapter Title: ON THOSE WHO OMIT WUDU OR PART OF IT, OR DOUBTS IN ITS COMPLETION
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إ َّن ُّو إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّز ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم ُّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّن ْق َّى مِن ْ وَّ ج ْ هِهِ إ ِذ َّإ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّ مَّ وْ ص ِ غ لَّمْ ي ُّصِ ن ْه
ِإَّلْمَّاءُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي ُّح ْ ز ِي هِ إ َّن ْ ي َّن ُّل َّهُّ مِن ْ ن َّعْ ض ِ ج َّ سَّ ذِة .
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about a man who,
while performing wudu, misses a small area on his face that the water does not reach.
Imam {a.s} said: "It suffices for him to moisten it with water from another part of his
body."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 352 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 472

Chapter Title: ON THOSE WHO OMIT WUDU OR PART OF IT, OR DOUBTS IN ITS COMPLETION
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ْ«إ ِن ْ ن َّسِ ي ث َّ مَّ سْ حَّ رَّإ ْسِ ك َّ ق َّامْ سَّ حْ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ عَّلَّى رِج ْ لَّي ْك َّ مِن ْ ن ِل َّه ِ وَّ ص ُّ ون ِك َّ ق َّا ِن ْ لَّم
َّ ي َّكُّن ْ ن َّق ِى َّ ق ِى ي َّذِك َّ مِن ْ ن َّذَّإوَّ ة ِ وَّ ص ُّ ون ِك َّ س َّ ى ْ ء ق َّح ُّ ذ ْ مِم َّا ن َّق ِى َّ مِن ْهُّ ق ِى لِحْ ي َّي ِك َّ وَّ إِمْ سَّ حْ ن ِهِ رَّإ ْسَّ ك
ْوَّ رِج ْ لَّي ْ ك َّ وَّ إ ِن ْ لَّم
ْ ي َّكُّن ْ لَّك َّ لِحْ ي َّه ق َّح ُّ ذ ْ مِن ْ جَّ اج ِ ن َّي ْك َّ وَّ إ َّس ْ ق َّارِ عَّي ْن َّي ْ ك َّ وَّ إِمْ سَّ حْ ن ِهِ رَّإ ْسَّ ك َّ وَّ رِج ْ لَّي ْك َّ وَّ إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّن ق َّ مِن ْ ن ِل َّه ِ وَّ ص ُّ ون ِك َّ س َّ ى ْ ء
َّإ َّعَّذْ ب َّ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وء .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"If you forget to wipe your head, then wipe it and your feet with the remaining moisture
from your wudu.
If there is no moisture left in your hands from the wudu, then take what remains in your
beard and wipe your head and feet with it.
If you do not have a beard, then take from your eyebrows and the lashes of your eyes
and wipe your head and feet with that.
If there is no moisture left from your wudu, then repeat the wudu."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 351 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 409

Chapter Title: ON THOSE WHO OMIT WUDU OR PART OF IT, OR DOUBTS IN ITS COMPLETION
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي زٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّق ِى رَّج ُّ لٍ ن َّسِ ى َّ مَّ سْ حَّ رَّإ ْسِ هِ ق َّالَّ «ق َّلْي َّمْ سَّ حْ » ق َّالَّ لَّمْ ي َّذ ْ كُّزْ ة
ِجَّ ي َّى ذَّج َّ لَّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّالَّ «ق َّلْي َّمْ سَّ حْ رَّإ ْسَّ هُّ مِن ْ ن َّلَّلِ لِحْ ي َّي ِه .
english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} regarding a
man who forgets to wipe his head during wudu.
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him wipe it."
Abu Basir asked: "What if he does not remember until he has started the prayer?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Then let him wipe his head with the moisture from his beard”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 352 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 410

Chapter Title: ON THOSE WHO OMIT WUDU OR PART OF IT, OR DOUBTS IN ITS COMPLETION
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ ر َّي ْ ذٍ إَّلس َّ ح َّ امِ وَّ إَّلْمُّق َّص َّ لِ ن ْن ِ صَّ الِحٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ْ ق ِى رَّج ُّ لٍ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا َّ ق َّن َّسِ ى َّ إ َّن
َّ ي َّمْ سَّ حَّ عَّلَّى رَّإ ْسِ هِ جَّ ي َّى ق َّامَّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّالَّ «ق َّلْي َّن ْصَّ زِف ْ ق َّلْي َّمْ سَّ حْ ن ِزَّإ ْسِ هِ وَّ لْي ُّعِذِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة.
ومن س ك ق ى س ى من وص ون ه وهو ق اعذ على جال إلوص وء ق لي عذ، ومن ق ام عن مكان ه ي م س ك ق ى س ى من وص ون ه ق لا
ي لي ق ث إ لى إلس ك إ لأ إ ن ي سي ي ق ن ، ومن س ك ق ى إلوص وء وهو على ي ق ي ن من إلحذب ق لي ي وص ا ، ومن س ك ق ى إلحذب وكان
على ي ق ي ن من إلوص وء ق لا ي ن ق ض إلي ق ي ن ن الس ك إ لأ إ ن ي سي ي ق ن ، ومن كا ن على ي ق ي ن من إلوص وء وإلحذب ولأ ي ذرى إ ي هما
إ سن ق ق لي ي وص ا.
english_text:
In the narration of Zayd al-Shahham and al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, narrated from
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, concerning a man who performs wudu but
forgets to wipe his head until he has started the prayer,
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him leave, wipe his head, and repeat the prayer."
commentary:
For anyone who doubts something in their wudu while still seated in the place of wudu,
they should redo it. However, if they have already left the place and then doubt
something about the wudu, they should disregard the doubt unless they are certain. If
a person is certain of a state of ritual impurity (hadath) but doubts whether they
performed wudu, they should perform wudu. Conversely, if one is certain of wudu but
doubts an act that would invalidate it, they should not negate their certainty due to
doubt unless they are certain. If one is sure of both wudu and impurity but does not
know which came first, they should perform wudu.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 352 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 371

Chapter Title: WHAT NULLIFIES ABLUTION
arabic_text:
ب اب-
ما ت ن ق ض الوض وء
ُّسَّ ا َّلَّ ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ ن ْن ُّ إ َّعْ ي َّن َّ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ وَّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ عَّم َّا ي َّن ْق ُّض ُّ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءَّ ق َّق َّالأَّ «مَّ ا ج َّ زَّح َّ مِن ْ طَّ زَّق َّي ْك
ْإَّلْأ َّسْ ق َّلَّي ْن ِ إَّلذ َّكَّزِ وَّ إَّلذ ُّن ُّزِ مِن ْ ع َّان ِظٍ إ َّوْ ن َّوْ لٍ إ َّوْ مَّ ن ِى ٍّ إ َّوْ رِي حٍ وَّ إَّلن َّوْ مُّ جَّ ي َّى ي ُّذ ْ هِث َّ إَّل َّعَّق ْل .
ولأ ي ن ق ض إلوص وء
ما سوى ذ لك من إلق ى وإلق لس وإلزعاف
وإلحح امه وإلذمامي ل وإلح زوح وإلق زوح، ولأ ي وج ث إلأسي ن ح اء .
english_text:
Zurarah ibn A'yan asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} and Imam Jafar
ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about what nullifies wudu (ablution).
They said: "Anything that exits from your two lower openings, the front (urethra) and
the back (anus), such as excrement, urine, semen, or wind, as well as sleep that
causes a loss of consciousness, invalidates wudu”.
commentary:
And the ablution is not invalidated by anything other, such as; vomiting, regurgitation,
nosebleeds, cupping, abscesses, wounds, and sores, do not nullify ablution nor
necessitate istinja (cleansing of private parts).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT NULLIFIES ABLUTION
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
.» ِ«لَّي ْسَّ ق ِى جَّ ث ِّ إَّلْق َّزْعِ وَّ إَّلذِّ ي ذَّإن ِ إَّلصِّ ع َّارِ وُّص ُّ وء إ ِن َّمَّا هُّوَّ ن ِمَّن ْز ِلَّه ِ إَّلْق َّمْ ل
.وهذ إ إ ذ إ لم ي كن ق ي ه ي ق ل، ق ا ذ إ كان ق ي ه ي ق ل ق ق ي ه إلأسي ن ح اء وإلوص وء
وكلما ج زح من إلطزق ي ن من ذم وق ي ح ومذ ى ووذ ى وع ي ز ذ لك ق لا وص وء ق ي ه ولأ إسي ن ح اء ما لم ي ح زح ن ول إ و ع ان ظ إ و
ري ح إ و من ى.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"There is no ablution required in the instance of taenia worms (or ticks and small
worms), they are regarded like lice, and this applies if they do not have any waste
matter, However, if there is waste matter, then istinja (cleansing of the private parts)
and ablution are required.”
commentary:
Anything that exits from the two lower openings (other than stool, urine, wind, or
semen) such as blood, pus, pre-seminal fluid, or other discharges does not require
ablution or istinja, unless it is urine, stool, wind, or semen.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 36 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 12 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 82 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 248 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 258

Chapter Title: WHAT NULLIFIES ABLUTION
arabic_text:

ْ إ َّج ِ ذُّ إَّلزِّي حَّ ق ِى ن َّطْ ن ِى جَّ ي َّى إ َّط ُّ ن َّ إ َّن َّهَّا ق َّذْ ج َّ زَّج َّ ث

Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah asked Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
'I feel wind in my stomach to the extent that I think it has exited.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'You do not need to perform ablution unless you hear a sound or
perceive the smell.'
Imam {a.s} then added:
'Indeed, Satan sits between a man's buttocks and causes him to think he has passed
wind to make him doubt.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 246

Zurarah asked Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who trims his nails, clips his
mustache, and cuts some of the hair from his beard and head. Does that nullify his
ablution?
Imam {a.s} said: 'O’ Zurarah, all of this is Sunnah (recommended practice), while
ablution is an obligation (fardh). None of the Sunnah practices invalidate an
obligation. In fact, such practices increase one's purity.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 346 • Al-Istibsar, P 1, p. 95 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 252 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 287 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 105 • Al-Fusul al- Muhimmah, P 2, p. 17

Ismail ibn Jaber asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
who trims his nails and mustache: should he wipe them with water afterward?
Imam {a.s} said: 'No, he is already pure.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text: َّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ عَّن ْ إ ِن ْس َّ اذِ إَّلس ِّ عْ زِ هَّلْ ي َّن ْق ُّض ُّ إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءَّ ق َّق َّالَّ لأ .

(Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}) was asked whether reciting poetry nullifies ablution?
Imam {a.s} said: 'No.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Sama'a ibn Mehran asked Imam {a.s} about a man who nods off while standing
or bowing in prayer. Imam {a.s} said: 'He does not need to perform ablution.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 255

Chapter Title: WHAT NULLIFIES ABLUTION

english_text:
Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about a man who falls asleep
while sitting: does he need to perform ablution?
Imam {a.s} said: 'He does not need to perform ablution as long as he remains seated
and does not slump over.' (overcome with sleep whereby he loses awareness)
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
'There is no need for ablution after kissing, touching intimately, or touching the private
parts.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 37 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 21 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 87 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 268 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 270

english_text:
Hariz narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
'If a man has a condition where urine or blood drips from him, then at the time of
prayer, he should use a pouch filled with cotton, attach it, and place his private part
inside it.
Then he should pray, combining the Dhuhr and Asr prayers by delaying Dhuhr and
advancing Asr with one call to prayer (adhan) and two calls to commence (iqamah).
Similarly, he should delay Maghrib and advance Isha with one adhan and two iqamah.
He should do the same for Fajr.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 348 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 26 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 143 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 297

Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man who urinates, performs ablution, then stands for prayer and finds wetness.
Imam {a.s} said: 'There is nothing upon him, and he does not need to perform ablution
again.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Another narration (by Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} ) states: In the
case of a man who urinates, performs istinja (cleansing of private parts), and then
notices wetness afterward: 'If he, after urinating, presses the area between the anus
and the testicles three times and massages it, then performs istinja, he need not worry
even if wetness flows down to his thighs.'.
commentary:
If a man touches the inner part of his anus or the inner part of his urethra, he must
repeat his ablution; if he does so during prayer, he should interrupt the prayer, perform
ablution, and repeat the prayer. Additionally, if he opens his urethra, he must redo his
ablution and prayer.
However, if someone uses an enema or carries something impure [such as filth], he is
not required to redo his ablution even if it exits from him, unless it is mixed with feces,
in which case he must perform istinja (cleaning the private parts) and redo the
ablution.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} did not consider the
pre-seminal fluid (madhi) to invalidate ablution or require ritual wash, nor did he deem
it necessary to wash clothing that had been affected by it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 177 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 281

وإلمذ ى ما
ي ح زح ق ن ل إلمن ى وإلوذ ى ما ي ح زح ن عذ إلمن ى على إ ي زة، وإلوذى ما ي ح زح على إ ي ز إلن ول، لأ ي ح ث ق ى س ى من ذ لك

english_text:
It has been narrated that pre-seminal fluid (madhi) and post-urinal fluid
(wadhi) are akin to saliva and mucus, so neither the garment nor the private parts need
to be washed because of them.
commentary:
These are four things: Semen (mani), pre-seminal fluid (madhi), post-seminal
discharge (wadhi), and a fluid discharged after urination (wudi).
Semen is a thick, gushing fluid that necessitates a full ritual bath (ghusl janabah).
Madhi is what comes out before semen, wadhi is what comes out after semen, and
wudi is what is discharged after urination. None of these, except semen, require a
ritual ghusl), nor ablution (wudu), nor the washing of clothing, nor the washing of
anything that comes into contact with the body.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 177

Abdullah ibn Bakir asked Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who wears a
garment with janabah (ritual impurity from sexual activity) and sweats in it.
Imam {a.s} said: 'The garment does not make the man ritually impure.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 52 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 268 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 185 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 170 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 182 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 267 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 445

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
english_text:
In another narration: 'A garment does not make a man ritually impure, nor does
a man make a garment ritually impure.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ر َّي ْذ إَّلس َّ ح َّ امُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ عَّن ِ إَّلي َّوْ ب ِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِي هِ إَّلْح َّ ن َّان َّه ُّ وَّ ي ُّصِ ي ن ُّن ِى إَّلس َّ مَّاءُّ جَّ ي َّى ي َّن ْي َّل
ِعَّلَّى َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
وإ ذ إ ن ام إلزج ل على ق زإس ق ذ إ صان ه من ى ق عزق ق ي ه ق لا ن ا س ن ه.
ومي ى عزق ق ى ي ون ه وهو ج ن ث ق لي ي ن س ف ق ي ه إ ذ إ إع ي سل
، وإ ن كان ث إلح ن ان ه من جلال ق حلال إلصلاة ق ي ه، وإ ن كان ث من جزإم ق حزإم إلصلاة ق ي ه، وإ ذ إ عزق ث إلحان ض ق ى ي وب ق لا
.ن ا س ن الصلاة ق ي ه
english_text:
Zayd al-Shahham asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
garment that has janabah (ritual impurity due to seminal discharge) and is then rained
on, causing it to become wet while he is wearing it.
Imam {a.s} said: 'There is no harm in it.'
commentary:
If a man sleeps on a bed that has been affected by semen and then sweats on it, there
is no issue with that either.
If a person sweats in their garment while in a state of janabah, they may dry themselves
with it after performing the ritual bath (ghusl). If the janabah occurred through
permissible means, it is permissible to pray in that garment; if it was from
impermissible (forbidden) means, then it is impermissible to pray in it. If a
menstruating woman sweats in a garment, there is no issue with praying in that
garment.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ لِن َّعْ ض ِ ن ِسَّ ان ِهِ «ن َّاوِلِي ن ِى إَّلْح ُّ مْ زَّة َّ» ق َّق َّالَّث ْ لَّهُّ إ َّن َّا جَّ ان ِض
َّ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهَّا «إ
ِ جَّ ي ْص ُّ ك ِ ق ِى ي َّذِك .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said to one of his wives: "Hand me the khumrah (a
small prayer mat)." She replied: "I am menstruating"
He {saws} said: 'Is your menstruation in your hand?'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 489 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 357

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
english_text:
Muhammad Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man who becomes junub (ritually impure due to seminal discharge) while wearing a
garment and has no other garment to wear.
Imam {a.s} said: 'He should pray in it, and when he finds water, he should wash it.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق ِى ج َّ ن َّزٍ إ ج َّ زَّ: و َّ إ َّعَّاذَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة.
وإلي وب إ ذ إ إ صان ه إلن ول ع سل ق ى ماء ج ار مزة ، وإ ن ع سل ق ى ماء رإكذ ق مزي ي ن ي م ي عصز ، وإ ن كان ن ول إلع لام إلزص ي غ
.صث علي ه إلماء صن ا، وإ ن كان ق ذ إ كل إلطعام ع سل، وإلع لام وإلح اري ه ق ى هذ إ سوإء
english_text: In another narration: 'And he should repeat the prayer.'.
commentary:
Regarding a garment that is affected by urine, it should be washed once in running
water, and if it is washed in stagnant water, it should be washed twice, then wrung out.
If it is the urine of a nursing boy, it should be poured over with water; if he has begun
eating solid food, it should be washed. In this regard, the ruling for a boy and a girl is
the same."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
english_text:
It has been narrated from The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib
{a.s}:
'The milk and urine of a baby girl must be washed from clothing before She starts
eating solid food because her milk is considered to come from her mother’s bladder.
However, the milk and urine of a baby boy do not need to be washed from clothing
before he starts eating solid food because his milk is considered to come from his
shoulders and arms.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Fiqh al-Reza {a.s}, vol. 1, p. 95 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 294 • Al-Ash'athiyat, Part 1, p. 12 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 250 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 173 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 142 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 398 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 101 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 116

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ جَّ كَّمُّ ن ْن ُّ جُّ كَّي ْمٍ إِن ْن ُّ إ َّج ِ ى ج َّ لا َّذٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ُّولُّ ق َّلاَّ إ ُّصِ ي ث ُّ إَّلْمَّاءَّ وَّ ق َّذْ إ َّصَّ اب
َّي َّذِى س َّ ى ْ ء مِن َّ إَّلْن َّوْ لِ ق َّا َّمْ سَّ حُّ هُّ ن ِالْحَّ ان ِظِ وَّ ن ِالي ُّزَّإب ِ ي ُّم َّ ي َّعْ زَّق ُّ ي َّذِى ق َّا َّمَّ س ُّ وَّ ج ْ هِى إ َّوْ ن َّعْ ض َّ ج َّ س ذِى إ َّوْ ي ُّصِ ي ث ُّ ي َّوْ ن ِى
ِق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Hakam ibn al-Hakim Akhi Khallad asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s}, saying to him:
'I urinate and do not find water, and some urine gets on my hand. I then wipe it on the
wall or with dust. Later, my hand sweats, and I touch my face or some part of my body,
or it touches my clothing.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'There is no harm in it.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مُّ ن ْن ُّ إ َّن ِى مَّ حْ مُّوذٍ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلطِّ ن ْق ِسَّ ه ِ وَّ إَّلْق ِزَّإس ِ ي ُّصِ ي ن ُّهُّمَّا إَّلْن َّوْ لُّ كَّي ْف َّ ي ُّصْ ن َّغُّ و
ِهُّوَّ ي َّح ِ ي ن كَّي ِي زُّ إَّلْحَّ س ْ وِ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي ُّع ْ سَّ لُّ مِن ْهُّ مَّ ا ط َّ هَّزَّ ق ِى وَّ ج ْ هِه .
english_text:
Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmoud asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} about rug (al
tanfasah) or mattress (al firash) that is affected by urine, especially if it is thick and
heavily padded.
Imam {a.s} said: 'You should wash the surface that is visible.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ جَّ ن َّان ُّ ن ْن ُّ سَّ ذِي زٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّق َّال-
َّ إ ِن ِّى رُّن َّمَّا ن ُّلْث ُّ ق َّلاَّ إ َّق ْذِرُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْمَّاءِ وَّ ي َّس ْ ي َّذ ُّ ذ َّلِك
َّ عَّلَّى َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ن ُّلْث َّ وَّ ي َّمَّس َّ حْ ث َّ ق َّامْ سَّ حْ ذ َّكَّزَّك َّ ن ِزِي ق ِك َّ ق َّا ِن ْ وَّ ج َّ ذْ ب َّ س َّ ي ْ ن اً ق َّق ُّلْ هَّذ َّإ مِن ْ ذ َّإك .
english_text:
Hanan ibn Sudair asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} saying:
'Sometimes I urinate and cannot find water, and it becomes difficult for me.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'If you urinate and dry yourself, then wipe your private part with your
saliva. If you notice anything afterward, say (assume), "This is from that."'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: عَّن ِ إِمْ زَّإ َّة ٍ لَّي ْسَّ لَّهَّا إ ِلأ َّ ق َّمِي ض وَّ إجِ ذ وَّ لَّهَّا مَّ وْ لُّوذ ق َّي َّن ُّولُّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا ك ُّي ْف َّ ي َّصْ ن َّغُّ ق َّالَّ «ي َّع ْ سِ ل
» ً إَّلْق َّمِي ضَّ ق ِى إَّلْي َّوْ مِ مَّ ز َّة
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a woman who has
only one shirt and a child who urinates on her. What should She do?
Imam {a.s} said: 'She should wash the shirt once a day.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 141

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّمُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلن ُّعْ مَّان ِ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
إ َّج ْ زُّح ُّ مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ لاَّءِ ق َّا َّسْ ي َّن ْح ِ ى ن ِالْمَّاءِ ق َّي َّق َّغُّ ي َّوْ ن ِى ق ِى
ذ َّلِك َّ إَّلْمَّاءِ إَّل َّذ ِى إِسْ ي َّن ْح َّ ي ْث ُّ ن ِهِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِهِ وَّ لَّي ْسَّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ س َّ ى ْ ء .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
'I leave the restroom and perform istinja (cleansing) with water, and my clothing falls
into the water used for istinja. Is there anything upon me?'
Imam {a.s} said: 'There is no harm in it, and it does not affect you.'".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ٍإ َّن ُّو إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّز ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم َّ : ق ِى طِ ي ن ِ إَّلْمَّطَّ زِ «إ ِن َّهُّ لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِهِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصِ ي ث َّ إَّلي َّوْ ب َّ ي َّلاَّي َّه
ُّإ َّي َّامٍ إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّعْ لَّمَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّذْ ن َّح َّ سَّ ه ُّس َّ ى ْ ء ن َّعْ ذَّ إَّلْمَّطَّ زِ ق َّا ِن ْ إ َّصَّ ان َّهُّ ن َّعْ ذَّ ي َّلاَّي َّه ِ إ َّي َّامٍ ع َّسَّ لَّهُّ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ طَّ زِي ق اً ن َّط ِ ي ق اً لَّمْ ي َّع ْ سِ لْه .
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} said regarding rain-soaked
mud: 'There is no harm if it comes into contact with clothing for three days, unless it is
known that it has become contaminated with something impure after the rain. If it
comes into contact after three days, it should be washed. However, if it is a clean path,
there is no need to wash it.'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 13 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 267 • Al-Saraer, Part 3, p. 613 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 46 • Wasa’il Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 522 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 125

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إ َّن ُّو إَّلْأ َّعَّز ِّ إَّلن َّح َّ اسُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّق َّالَّ: إ ِن ِّى إ ُّعَّالِح ُّ إَّلذ َّوَّ إب َّ ق ْزُّن َّمَّا ج َّ زَّج ْ ث ُّ ن ِالل َّي ْلِ وَّ ق َّذ
ن َّالَّث ْ وَّ رَّإي َّث ْ ق َّي َّص ْ زِب ُّ إ ِجْ ذَّإهَّا ن ِي َّذِهَّا إ َّوْ ن ِزِج ْ لِهَّا ق َّي ُّن ْص َّ حُّ عَّلَّى ي َّوْ ن ِى ِق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
ولأ ن ا س ن ح زء إلذج اج ه وإلحمامه ي صي ث إلي وب ، ولأ ن ا س ن ح زء ما طار ون وله، ولأ ن ا س ن ن ول كل س ى إ كل لحمه ق ي صي ث
إلي وب ، ولأ ن ا س ن لن ن إلمزإ ة إلمزص عه ي صي ث ق مي صها ق ي كي ز وي ي ن س.
english_text:
Abu Al-Agharr al-Nakhkhas asked Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}, saying:
‘I tend to the riding animals, and sometimes I go out at night and they have urinated or
defecated, so one of them strikes with its leg or hand [1causing it to splash on my
clothing.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'There is no harm in it.'
commentary:
There is also no harm if chicken or pigeon droppings come into contact with clothing.
Likewise, there is no issue with the droppings or urine of flying creatures or the urine
of any animal whose meat is lawful to eat coming into contact with clothing. There is
also no issue if the milk of a nursing woman touches her shirt, even in large amounts,
once it dries.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT DEFILES CLOTHING AND THE BODY
arabic_text:
وَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إَّلزِّص َّ ا ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:

ِإَّلس ُّ ق َّاق َّ إ َّي َّز إ َّسْ وَّ ذُّ مِم َّا وَّ طِ ن َّهُّ مِن َّ إَّلْق َّذ َّرِ وَّ ق َّذْ ع َّسَّ لَّهُّ كَّي ْف َّ ي َّصْ ن َّغُّ ن ِهِ وَّ ن ِزِج ْ لِهِ إَّل َّي ِى وَّ ط ُّ ى َّ ن ِهَّا إ َّ ي ُّح ْ ز ِي هِ إَّلْع َّسْ لُّ إ َّمْ ي ُّح َّ لِّل
ْ [إ َّط ْ ق َّارَّةُّ] ن ِا َّط ْ ق َّارِةِ وَّ ي َّسْ ي َّن ْح ِ ى ق َّي َّح ِ ذُّ إَّلزِّي حَّ مِن ْ إ َّط ْ ق َّارِةِ وَّ لأَّ ي َّزَّى س َّ ي ْن اً ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ س َّ ى ْ ءَّ عَّلَّي ِ هِ مِن َّ إَّلزِّي حِ وَّ إَّلس ُّ ق َّاق
ِن َّعْ ذَّ ع َّسْ لِه .

english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} as asked about a man who steps in a public
bath with cracked feet and steps on urine and lime, causing a black residue to enter
the cracks. If he washes it, how should he treat it, and what about his foot that stepped
on it? Is washing sufficient, or should he also scrape under his nails? And he washes
himself, only to then find smell emanating from his nails even when there is nothing?
Imam {a.s} said: ‘There is nothing on him from the smell or the residue in the cracks after
washing’
commentary:
It is permissible for a person to rub themselves in the bath with flour, bran, or other
beneficial substances, as there is no excessiveness in what benefits the body;
extravagance applies to what wastes water or harms the body.
Regarding blood that stains clothing: there is no issue with praying in it if the amount
is not greater than a dirham in size. The "dirham-sized" measure weighs approximately
one and one-third dirhams. If the blood is less than a full dirham, washing is preferred
but not obligatory for prayer. However, if the blood is less than the size of a chickpea,
there is no obligation to wash it unless it is menstrual blood. Menstrual blood, urine,
and semen, regardless of quantity, must be washed from the clothing, and prayers
must be repeated if performed without realizing its presence.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
It is narrated regarding semen that if a man is junub (ritually impure due to
seminal discharge) and gets up, looks, and finds nothing, then there is nothing upon
him. However, if he does not look and does not check, he must wash himself and
repeat his prayer.
commentary:
There is no issue with the blood of fish on clothing, whether a small or large amount,
when praying. If semen, urine, blood, or feces touch a man's cap, turban, waistband,
socks, or shoes, there is no harm in praying in them, because prayer is not complete
when performed solely in any of these items.
If one's clothing touches a dead donkey, there is no need to wash it, and there is no
issue with praying in it.
There is no harm in touching the bone of a deceased person after a year has passed,
and there is no issue with using a deceased person’s tooth as a replacement for one’s
own.
If a dry dog touches one’s clothing and it is not a hunting dog, it suffices to sprinkle
water on it. If it is wet, it must be washed. For a hunting dog, if it is dry, there is nothing
upon the person ; if it is wet, it suffices to sprinkle water. There is no issue with praying
in a garment that has come into contact with alcohol because Allah {SWT}, the Exalted,
has prohibited its consumption but has not prohibited praying in a garment affected
by it. However, praying in a place where alcohol is present is not permissible.
If a person urinates and a spot of urine touches their thigh, then prays and later
remembers that they did not wash it, they must wash it and repeat the prayer.
If a mouse falls into water, exits, and then walks on clothing, one should wash the area
where traces of it are seen and sprinkle water on the rest of the area.
If a man has a bleeding wound that soils his clothing, there is no need to wash it until
the wound heals or the bleeding stops.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 478

english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about a eunuch
who experiences difficulty with urination and notices wetness repeatedly.
Imam {a.s} replied: 'He should perform ablution and sprinkle his clothing with water
once during the day.'.

english_text:
A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah {saws}, and the most learned
among them asked him several questions.
Amongst them, one (Jew) asked: 'Why did Allah {SWT} command ghusl (ritual bathing)
after janabah (ritual impurity due to sexual discharge) but did not command ghusl after
defecation and urination?'
The Messenger of Allah {saws} replied:
'When Adam ate from the tree, it coursed through his veins, hair, and skin.
So when a man engages in intercourse, the fluid (semen) is released from every vein
and hair in his body.
Therefore, Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, has commanded his descendants to perform ghusl
after janabah until the Day of Resurrection.
On the other hand, urine is expelled as the excess from the drink consumed by
humans, and feces is the excess from the food consumed.
Thus, for those acts, wudu (ablution) is required.'
The Jewish scholar said: 'You have spoken the truth, O’ Muhammad.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 282 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 537 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 179 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 599 • Tafsir Kanz al-Daqa’iq, Part 4, p. 55

english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in response to
his questions:
'The reason for the ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah (ritual impurity from sexual discharge)
is for cleanliness, to purify a person from what has affected them and to cleanse their
entire body, because janabah involves the whole body. Therefore, it is necessary to
purify the entire body. The reason for the lightening (of obligation) in the case of urine
and feces is because they occur more frequently and continuously compared to
janabah, so it is sufficient to perform wudu (ablution) due to their frequency, difficulty,
and the fact that they occur without intentional desire or pleasure. Janabah occurs
only through enjoyment or intentional acts involving themselves.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 281 • Al-Manaqib, Vol. 4, p. 355 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 538 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 178 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 2

ي َّع ْ ي َّسِ لَّ وَّ ي َّق ْص ِ ى َّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ وَّ ع ُّسْ لُّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّان َّه ِ ق َّزِي ص َّ ه.

Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
'There are seventeen occasions for ghusl (ritual bathing):
On the night of the 17th of the month of Ramadan, the night of the 19th, the night of
the 21st, and the night of the 23rd - on which Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree) is
hoped for.
Also, ghusl on the two Eid’s (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha),
Also, upon entering the two holy sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina),
Also, on the day of putting on the ihram (for pilgrimage), the day of visiting (the sacred
sites), the day of entering the House (the Kaaba), the day of Tarwiyah (the 8th of Dhu
al-Hijjah), the day of Arafah (the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah),
Also, after washing a deceased person and shrouding them, or if you touch the
deceased after their body has cooled.
There is also ghusl for Jumu’ah, for a solar eclipse if the entire disc of the sun is
obscured, and if you wake up and have not prayed, then you must perform ghusl and
make up the prayer. Ghusl for janabah (ritual impurity from sexual discharge) is
obligatory.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 382 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 304

english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the
Jumu'ah wash (ghusl).
Imam {a.s} said: 'It is obligatory for both travel and residency, except that it has been
permitted for women to forgo it during travel due to a shortage of water.
The ghusl of janabah (ritual impurity due to sexual discharge) is obligatory, as is the
ghusl of menstruation, and the ghusl for a woman experiencing istihadah (irregular
bleeding). If She uses a cotton cloth to absorb the blood and the blood exceeds the
cloth, She must perform ghusl for every two prayers, and for Fajr, She must perform
ghusl as well. If the blood does not pass the cotton, She must perform wudu for each
prayer.
The ghusl for postnatal bleeding (nifas) is obligatory,
The ghusl for a newborn (is obligatory),
The ghusl for washing a deceased person (is obligatory),
The ghusl for one who has washed a deceased person (is obligatory),
The ghusl for entering the state of ihram (pilgrimage attire) is obligatory,
The ghusl on the day of Arafah (is obligatory),
The ghusl for visitation of Kaaba (is obligatory), except for one with a valid excuse.
The ghusl for entering the Kaaba is obligatory,
The ghusl for entering the sacred sanctuary (haram). It is recommended for one not to
enter it without performing ghusl.
The ghusl for the Mubahalah (mutual prayer for truth) is obligatory,
The ghusl for seeking rain (istisqa) is obligatory.
The ghusl for the 1st night of Ramadan is recommended, as is the ghusl for the night of
the 21st, which is a Sunnah, and the ghusl for the night of the 23rd should not be
neglected, as one of these nights is hoped to be Laylat al-Qadr.
The ghusl for the day of Eid al-Fitr and the day of Eid al-Adha should not be omitted,
The ghusl for seeking divine guidance (istikhara) is recommended."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 104 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 3, p. 303

english_text:
(From Mas'adah ibn Ziyad) A man said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s}:
'I have neighbors who have female maidservant singers who sing and play the lute.
Sometimes I go to the restroom and prolong my stay to listen to them.'
Al-Sadiq {a.s} replied: 'Do not do that.'
The man said: 'By Allah {SWT}, I do not approach them with my feet; it is only that I listen
with my ears.'
Al-Sadiq {a.s} responded: 'By Allah {SWT}, have you not heard Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, say:
"Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - all of those will be questioned."' [Surah
Al-Isra 17:36]
The man said: 'It is as though I had never heard this verse from the Book of Allah {SWT},
the Exalted, from an Arab or a non-Arab. Certainly, I will abandon it and seek Allah’s
{SWT} forgiveness.'
Al-Sadiq {a.s} said to him, 'Arise, perform ghusl (ritual bathing), and pray as much as you
like, for you were persisting in a grave matter. How terrible would your state have been
had you died in that condition! Seek Allah’s {SWT} forgiveness and ask Him for
repentance from everything He dislikes, for He dislikes only the repugnant things, and
leave repugnant things to their people, for everything has its people.'
commentary:
All ghusls (ritual baths) are Sunnah except for the ghusl of janabah (sexual impurity),
and ghusl for janabah suffices in place of wudu (ablution), as both are obligations, and
the greater one covers the lesser. If one performs ghusl for reasons other than
janabah, they should begin with wudu and then perform ghusl, as ghusl does not
replace wudu, since ghusl is Sunnah and wudu is an obligation, and a Sunnah does
not replace an obligation.
"My father wrote to me in his letter: 'When you intend to perform ghusl for janabah
(ritual impurity due to sexual discharge), strive to urinate first so that any remaining
semen in your urethra is expelled. Then wash your hands three times before placing
them in the water container, even if there is no impurity on them.
If you place them in the container while they are impure, then discard the water. If
there is no impurity, there is no harm. If any semen has touched your body, wash it off.
Then perform istinja (cleansing of the private parts) and thoroughly wash your genitals.
Pour three handfuls of water over your head and separate the hair with your fingers so
that the water reaches the roots of all your hair.
Take the container in your hand and pour water over your head and body twice and rub
your body thoroughly. Insert your fingers into your ears and ensure water reaches all
parts. Every part that the water touches becomes purified, so ensure that no hair on
your head or beard remains without water reaching beneath it. If someone deliberately
leaves any hair unwashed during ghusl for janabah, they will be in the Fire.
If someone fails to urinate after janabah or suspects that residual moisture may
remain within them, it may lead to an incurable disease. If one wishes to rinse the
mouth and nose during ghusl for janabah, it is permissible but not obligatory, as ghusl
pertains to what is external, not internal. However, if a person wants to eat or drink
before performing ghusl, they must wash their hands, rinse their mouth, and clean
their nose first. If they eat or drink before doing so, it is feared they may develop
leprosy.'”
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 116 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, vol. 3, p. 535 Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi said:
‘Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked whether it is appropriate for a man
to sleep while in a state of janabah (ritual impurity from sexual discharge).’
Imam {a.s} replied: 'It is disliked (makruh) to do so without first performing wudu
(ablution).'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 423 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 1, p. 382 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 227

In another narration, Imam {a.s} said:

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} narrates from his father, Imam
Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}:
'If a man is in a state of janabah (ritual impurity due to sexual discharge), he should not
eat or drink until he performs wudu (ablution).'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 418 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 219

Chapter Title: METHOD OF GHUSL FOR JANABAH (RITUAL BATH FOR SEXUAL IMPURITY)
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said: "'I dislike being in a state of janabah (ritual impurity) when the
sun turns yellow (at sunset) and when it rises while it is yellow (sunrise)."

Al-Halabi said: I asked him about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bathing)
without a covering (loincloth) when no one can see him.
Imam {a.s} said: 'There is no harm in it.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 515

Al-Halabi said: ‘Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who engages in
sexual relations with a woman but does not ejaculate. Is ghusl (ritual bathing) required
for him?
Imam {a.s} said: 'Imam Ali {a.s} used to say, "If the circumcised part touches the
circumcised part, ghusl becomes obligatory."'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: METHOD OF GHUSL FOR JANABAH (RITUAL BATH FOR SEXUAL IMPURITY)
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} would say: 'How can ghusl (ritual bathing) not be
obligatory when the Hadd (prescribed punishment) is applicable in such a case (if it is
adultery)?".
Imam {a.s} said: 'The dowry and ghusl become obligatory upon him’
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

woman without intercourse, and he ejaculates but She does not. Is ghusl (ritual
bathing) required for her?
Imam {a.s} said: 'She is not required to perform ghusl. If he does not ejaculate, then he
is also not required to perform ghusl.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 124 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 111 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 408 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 199

Chapter Title: METHOD OF GHUSL FOR JANABAH (RITUAL BATH FOR SEXUAL IMPURITY)
english_text:
Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi narrates that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} was asked about a man who performs ghusl (ritual bathing) and then later finds
wetness, having urinated before performing the ghusl.
Imam {a.s} said: 'He should perform wudu (ablution). But if he had not urinated before
performing the ghusl, he should repeat the ghusl.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 415

english_text:
Al-Halabi narrates that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked
about a man who sleeps, then wakes up and touches his private part, finding wetness,
but did not see anything in his dream. Should he perform ghusl (ritual bathing)?
Imam {a.s} said: 'No, ghusl is only required for major discharge (al-māʾ al-akbar, i.e.,
semen).'.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 403 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, vol. 2, p. 250

sees in her dream what a man sees (i.e., a sexual dream).

english_text:
Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi said:
"I was told by someone who heard Imam {a.s} say:
'If a person in a state of janabah (ritual impurity due to sexual discharge) immerses
themselves in water all at once, that suffices for their ghusl (ritual bath).'.
commentary:
If a person becomes junub (ritually impure) multiple times during a day or night, one
ghusl is sufficient unless they become junub again after performing ghusl or
experience a wet dream. If they have a wet dream, they should not engage in
intercourse until they perform ghusl for the wet dream.
There is no issue for a person in a state of janabah to recite the entire Quran, except
for the verses of prostration, which are found in Surah Luqman, Surah Ha-Mim As-
Sajdah (Surah Fussilat), Surah An-Najm, and Surah Al-‘Alaq
A person who is junub or without wudu should not touch the Quran, but it is
permissible for them to touch the paper (not the Quranic text) or to have someone else
turn its pages, and they may read and mention the names of Allah {SWT}.
A menstruating woman and a person in a state of janabah should not enter the
mosque except when passing through it, and they may take something from it, but they
should not leave anything in it, as they are able to leave it in other places.
If a woman wishes to perform ghusl from janabah but begins menstruating, She should
delay the ghusl until her menstruation ends. Then, She should perform one ghusl that
covers both janabah and menstruation.
There is no issue for a person in a state of janabah to dye their hair, become junub
while their hair is dyed, undergo cupping, remember Allah {SWT}, use depilatory agents,
slaughter animals, wear a ring, sleep in a mosque, pass through it, or become junub
at the beginning of the night and sleep until the end of it. If a person becomes junub in
a place where there is only frozen water and they cannot reach clean soil, they should
perform tayammum (dry ablution) and pray, then avoid returning to a place where their
faith may be jeopardized.
My father, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, wrote to me: 'There is no issue with
dividing the ghusl. Wash your hands, private parts, and head, and delay washing the
rest of your body until the time of prayer, at which point you wash your body. However,
if you have any hadath (ritual impurity, such as urination or defecation) after washing
your head but before washing your body, repeat the ghusl from the beginning. If you
begin washing your body before your head, repeat the ghusl for your body after
washing your head.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 43 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 148 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 125 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 521 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 521 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 232 • Wasa’il Al-Shia, vol. 2, p. 233 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Part 1, p. 470 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Part 1, p.

english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
'Menstruation is a form of impurity that Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, has afflicted women
with.
In the time of Noah {a.s}, women would menstruate only once a year until a group of
seven hundred women went out of their homes, wore brightly colored garments,
adorned themselves with jewelry, and used perfume. They then spread out among the
lands, sat with men, attended festivals, and sat in their gatherings.
Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, then afflicted these women with monthly menstruation due to
this behavior, so their blood began to flow, and they were separated from men. Thus,
they would menstruate every month, and Allah {SWT} kept them occupied with
menstruation and reduced their desires.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Other women who did not engage in such behavior would only
menstruate once a year.'
Imam {a.s} continued, 'The descendants of those who menstruated every month
married the daughters of those who menstruated once a year, and their offspring
intermingled. Consequently, their daughters menstruated monthly, leading to an
increase in the children of those who menstruated monthly due to regular
menstruation, while the children of those who menstruated yearly were fewer due to
the corruption of their blood.'
Imam {a.s} concluded, 'Thus, the offspring of those who menstruated monthly
increased, while the offspring of those who menstruated yearly decreased.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 433 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 11, p. 326 • Qisas al-Anbiya’ (li’l-Jaza’iri) Vol. 1, p. 77

The Prophet {saws} said:
‘Indeed, Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A} is not like any of you; She does not experience
menstrual blood nor postnatal bleeding, like the heavenly maidens.'

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about the saying of Allah
{SWT}, the Exalted: 'They will have therein purified spouses.' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:25)
Imam {a.s} said: 'The purified spouses are those who do not menstruate and do not
experience postnatal bleeding.'
commentary:
My father, wrote to me in his letter: 'Know that the minimum days of menstruation are
three days, and the maximum is ten days. If a woman sees blood for three days or
more, up to ten days, it is considered menstruation, and She must refrain from prayer
and not enter the mosque except while passing through. It is obligatory for her to
perform wudu (ablution) before each prayer, sit facing the Qiblah, and remember Allah
{SWT} for the duration of her daily prayer.
If She sees blood for one or two days, it is not considered menstruation unless She
sees blood for three consecutive days. She must make up the prayers that She missed
during those one or two days. If She sees blood for more than ten days, She should
refrain from prayer for ten days, then perform ghusl (ritual bath) on the eleventh day
and use a cotton pad (Kersaf). If the blood does not soak through the pad, She can
perform her prayers with wudu. If the blood soaks through the pad but does not flow,
She prays the Salat Al Layl prayer and the Fajr prayer with ghusl, and the other prayers
with wudu. If the blood flows, She prays the Salat Al Layl prayer and the Fajr prayer
with ghusl, and the Dhuhr and Asr prayers with ghusl, delaying the Dhuhr prayer
slightly and hastening the Asr prayer, and She prays the Maghrib and Isha prayers with
one ghusl, delaying the Maghrib prayer slightly and hastening the Isha prayer until her
menstruation days arrive, at which point She refrains from prayer.
Once She has performed ghusl as described, it becomes permissible for her husband
to approach her. The minimum period of purity (tuhr) is ten days, and there is no
maximum limit. A menstruating woman should use nine ratls of water for ghusl,
measured by the Medinian Ratl. If a woman sees yellowish discharge during her
menstruation days, it is considered part of her menstruation. If She sees it during her
purification days, it is considered a sign of purity.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1
