وذ كز س ي ح ن ا محمذ ن ن إلحسن -
ق ى ج امعه ق ى إلح اري ه ي موب مغ إلزج ال ق ى إلسق ز ق ال: إ ذ إ كان ث إن ن ه إ كي ز من ج مس
. سن ي ن إ و سث ذق ن ث ولم ي ع سل، وإ ذ إ كان ث إن ن ه إ ق ل من ج مس سن ي ن ع سلث ، وذ كز عن إلحلن ى جذي ي ا ق ى معن اة عن إلصاذق
english_text:
Abu al-Numeir, the freed slave of al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, asked Imam Al-
Sadiq {a.s}: "Tell me about the age up to which a child can be washed by women."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Up to three years old."
commentary:
Our Shaykh Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan mentioned in his book, ‘Al Jamiah’, a girl who
dies among men during travel. If She is older than five or six years, She should be
buried without washing. If She is younger than five years, She can be washed.
He mentioned a related narration from Al-Halabi attributed to Imam Al-Sadiq.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
english_text:
Mansour ibn Hazim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man traveling with his wife, and She dies. Should he wash her?
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, as well as his mother, sister, and similar relatives. He should
cover her private parts with a cloth and then perform the washing."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ سَّ مَّاعَّه ُّ ن ْن ُّ مِهْ زَّإن:
ُّ عَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ مَّ اب َّ وَّ لَّي ْ سَّ مَّ عَّهُّ إ ِلأ َّ ن ِسَّ اء ق َّق َّالَّ «ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّهُّ إِمْ زَّإ َّة ذ َّإب ُّ مَّ حْ زَّمٍ مِن ْهُّ وَّ ي َّصُّ ث
ِإَّلن ِّسَّ اءُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلْمَّاءَّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّح ْ لَّغُّ ي َّوْ ن َّهُّ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّث ِ إِمْ زَّإ َّة مَّ اي َّث ْ مَّ غَّ رِج َّ الٍ وَّ لَّي ْ سَّ مَّ عَّهُّمُّ إ َّمْ زَّإ َّة وَّ لأ
ْ مَّ حْ زَّم لَّهَّا ق َّلْي ُّذْ ق َّن
كَّمَّا هِى َّ ق ِى ي ِي َّان ِهَّا وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ مَّ عَّهَّا ذ ُّو مَّ حْ زَّمٍ لَّهَّا ع َّس َّ لَّهَّا مِن ْ ق َّوْ ق ِ ي ِي َّان ِهَّا .
english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man who dies and is only accompanied by women.
Imam {a.s} replied: "A woman who is his mahram (close relative) should wash him, and
the other women should pour water over him without removing his clothes. If it is a
woman who dies among men, with no women or mahram present, She should be
buried as she is in her clothing. If a mahram is present, he may wash her from over her
clothes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 155 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 444 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 204 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 306 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 519

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ عَّم َّار إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى:
ِعَّن ِ إَّلص َّ ن ِي َّه ِ لأَّ ي ُّصَّ اب ُّ إِمْ زَّإ َّة ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّهَّا ق َّالَّ «ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّهَّا إ َّوْ لَّى إَّلن َّاسِ ن ِهَّا مِن َّ إَّلزِّج َّ ال .
english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a young
girl for whom no woman is available to wash her.
Imam {a.s} replied: "The one most closely related to her among men should wash her."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 155 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 519

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ: عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ إَّلْمُّسْ لِمِ ي َّمُّوب ُّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ وَّ لَّي ْ سَّ مَّ عَّهُّ رَّج ُّ ل مُّسْ لِم وَّ مَّ عَّهُّ رِج َّ ال ن َّصَّ ارَّى ُّوَّ عَّم َّي ُّهُّ وَّ ج َّ الَّي ُّه
َّمُّسْ لِمَّي َّان ِ كَّي ْف َّ ي ُّصْ ن َّغُّ ق ِى ع ُّسْ لِهِ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّهُّ عَّم َّي ُّهُّ وَّ ج َّ الَّي ُّهُّ ق ِى ق َّمِي صِ هِ وَّ لأ
ُّ ي َّق ْ زَّن ُّهُّ إَّلن َّصَّ ارَّى » وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ ي َّمُّوب
ِ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ وَّ لَّي ْسَّ مَّ عَّهَّا إِمْ زَّإ َّة مُّ سْ لِمَّه وَّ مَّ عَّهَّا ن ِسَّ اء ن َّصَّ ارَّى وَّ مَّ عَّهَّا عَّم ُّهَّا وَّ ج َّ الُّهَّا مُّسْ لِمَّان َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي ُّع َّسِّ لاَّن ِهَّا وَّ لأ
ْ ي َّق ْ زَّن ُّهَّا إَّلن َّصْ زَّإن ِي َّه ُّ ع َّي ِزَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ي َّكُّون ُّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا ذِرْع ق َّي ُّصَّ ث ُّ إَّلْمَّاءُّ مِن ْ ق َّوْ ق ِ إَّلذِّرْع .
english_text:
The Imam was asked about a Muslim man who dies while traveling, with no
other Muslim men present but with a group of Christian men and two Muslim women
(his paternal aunt and maternal aunt). How should his washing be performed?
Imam {a.s} replied: "His paternal aunt and maternal aunt should wash him while he is in
his shirt, and the Christian men should not approach him”.
Similarly, he was asked about a Muslim woman who dies while traveling, with no
Muslim women present but accompanied by Christian women, along with her Muslim
paternal uncle and maternal uncle.
The Imam said: "Her uncles should wash her, but the Christian women should not
approach her. She should wear a protective garment, and water should be poured over
the garment."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 155 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 517

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّه:
َّ عَّن ِ إَّلن َّصْ زَّإن ِى ِّ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ وَّ هُّوَّ مَّ غَّ إَّلْمُّسْ لِمِي ن َّ ق َّي َّمُّوب ُّ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّهُّ مُّسْ لِم وَّ لأَّ ي َّذْ ق ِن ُّهُّ وَّ لأ
ُّكَّزَّإمَّ ه َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّق ُّومُّ عَّلَّى ق َّن ْزِةِ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ إ َّن َّاة.
english_text:
Imam was asked about a Christian who dies while traveling among Muslims.
Imam {a.s} said: "A Muslim should not wash him, nor bury him, nor give him any honor,
and should not stand by his grave, even if he was his father."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 155 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 335 • Sulwat al- Hazin, Part 1, p. 256 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 514 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 204

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
english_text:
Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar asked Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}: "May I be your ransom, what
is your ruling about a woman who dies while traveling with men, none of whom are her
mahram (close relatives), and no women are present? What should be done with her?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Only those parts that Allah {SWT} has required for tayammum (dry
ablution) should be washed, and She should not be touched or any of her private
features, which Allah {SWT} has commanded to be covered, uncovered."
He then asked: "How should it be done?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Her inner palms should be washed first, then her face, followed by
washing the backs of her hands”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 156 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 342 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 1, p. 442 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 200 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 202 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 522

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ عَّم َّارُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّوسَّ ى إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى:
عَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ مَّ اب َّ وَّ لَّي ْسَّ مَّ عَّهُّ رَّج ُّ ل مُّسْ لِم وَّ لأَّ إِمْ زَّإ َّة مُّسْ لِمَّه مِن ْ ذ َّوِى

ُّإ َّ ص ْ طُّ ز .
english_text:
Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
about a man who dies and is accompanied by no Muslim men or female Muslim
relatives. Instead, there are Christian men and Muslim women unrelated to him.
The Imam said: "The Christian man should first perform ghusl (ritual washing for
himself), then wash the deceased, as it is a case of necessity”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED

ن َّصْ زَّإن ِي َّه وَّ رِج َّ ال مُّسْ لِمُّون َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي َّع ْ ي َّسِ لُّ إَّلن َّصْ زَّإن ِي َّه ُّ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّهَّا .
وج مسه ي ن ي ط ز ن هم ي لاي ه إ ي ام إ لأ إ ن
ي ي ع ي زوإ:
إلع زي ق ، وإلمصعوق ، وإلمن طون ، وإلمهذوم، وإلمذج ن. وإلمح ذور
إ ذ إ ماب ي صي ث
علي ه إلماء صن ا إ ذ إ ج ي ف إ ن ي سق ظ من ج لذة س ى عن ذ إلمس وكذ لك إلكسي ز وإلمحي زق وإلذ ى ن ه إلق زوح.
english_text:
The Imam was asked about a Muslim woman who dies and is accompanied by
no Muslim women or male Muslim relatives, but there is Christian woman and Muslim
men present.
Imam {a.s} replied: "The Christian woman should first perform ghusl (ritual washing for
herself), and then She should wash the deceased."
commentary:
And five categories of deceased individuals can be kept for three days before burial
unless their bodies begin to decompose : hose who have drowned, those struck by
lightning, those who died of stomach-related ailments, buried under rubble, and those
who died from smoke inhalation.
For someone who has died of smallpox (or similar contagious diseases), water should
be poured over the body without touching it if there is a fear that touching would cause
the skin to detach. The same applies to individuals with broken limbs, burns, or severe
sores.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ«إ ِذ َّإ مَّ اب َّ إَّلْمَّي ِّث ُّ ق ِى إَّلْن َّحْ زِ ع ُّسِّ لَّ وَّ جُّ ن ِّظَّ وَّ كُّق ِّن َّ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّوي َّق ُّ ق ِى رِج ْ لِه
ِجَّ ح َّ ز وَّ ي ُّزْمَّ ى ن ِهِ ق ِى إَّلْمَّاء .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said: "When a person
dies at sea, they are washed, anointed (with Hunut), and shrouded. Then a stone
should be tied to their leg, and they should be cast into the water."
references: Qurb al-Isnād, Part 1, p. 138 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 157 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 339 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 538 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 206 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 2

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
ِوَّ ق َّذْ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّهُّ ي ُّح ْ عَّلُّ ق ِى ج َّ ان ِي َّه ٍ وَّ ي ُّوكَّى رَّإ ْسُّ هَّا وَّ ي ُّزْمَّ ى ن ِهَّا ق ِى إَّلْمَّاء .
هذ إ
كله إ ذ إ لم ي ق ذر على إلس ظ.
english_text:
It has been narrated that a deceased person should be placed in a large jar
(khabiyah), which is then sealed, and the jar is thrown into the water.
commentary: This applies when it is not possible to reach the shore.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ «إَّلْمَّزْج ُّ ومُّ وَّ إَّلْمَّزْج ُّ ومَّ ه ُّ ي ُّع َّس َّ لاَّن ِ وَّ ي ُّحَّ ن َّطَّ ان ِ وَّ ي ُّلْن َّسَّ ان ِ إَّلْكَّق َّن َّ ق َّن ْلَّ ذ َّلِك
ْي ُّم َّ ي ُّزْج َّ مَّان ِ وَّ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا وَّ إَّلْمُّق ْي َّض ُّ مِن ْهُّ ن ِمَّن ْز ِلَّه ِ ذ َّلِك َّ ي ُّع َّس َّ لُّ وَّ ي ُّحَّ ن َّظُّ وَّ ي ُّلْن َّسُّ إَّل َّكَّق َّن َّ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّق َّاذُّ وَّ ي ُّص ِل َّى عَّلَّي ْ ه .
ق ا ذ إ كان إلمي ث مصلون ا إ ن ز ل عن إلح س ن ه ن عذ ي لاي ه إ ي ام وع سل وكق ن وذق ن ولأ ي ح ور صلن ه إ كي ز من ي لاي ه إ ي ام .
english_text:
Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said : "The man and
woman sentenced to stoning should be washed, embalmed, and dressed in shrouds
before being stoned, then they are to be stoned and prayers are to be offered for them
(Salat Al Janazah). The person subject to retaliation (Qisas) is treated similarly: they
should be washed, embalmed, and dressed in shrouds before the execution, and
funeral prayers should be offered for them (Salat Al Janazah).
commentary:
If the deceased was crucified, they should be taken down after three days, washed,
shrouded, and buried. It is not permissible for crucifixion to last more than three days.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 214 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 157 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 334 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 350 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 513

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man
who has been devoured by a wild animal or birds, leaving only his bones without flesh.
He asked what should be done in such a case.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should be washed, shrouded, funeral prayers should be offered
for him, and he should be buried”.
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, P 1, p. 349 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 158 • Wasail Al-Shia, P 3, p. 134

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED

وَّ ذَّق َّن َّهُّمَّا
ق ِى ي ِي َّان ِهِمَّا ن ِذِمَّ ان ِهِمَّا وَّ لَّمْ ي ُّصَّ لِّ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا .
. هكذ إ روى، لكن إلأ صل إ ن لأ ي ي زك إ جذ من إلأ مه إ ذ إ ماب ن ع ي ز صلاة
english_text:
In another report, "Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}, did not wash Ammar ibn Yasir and
Hashim ibn Utbah (known as al-Mirqal). He buried them in their clothing with their
blood and did not offer funeral prayers for them”.
commentary:
This is how it was narrated, it is understood that no member of the community should
be left without a funeral prayer upon their death.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 331 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 332 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 6, p. 168 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 214 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 469 • Al- Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 482 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 507

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ َّن ُّو مَّ زْ ي َّمَّ إَّلْأ َّن ْصَّ ارِى ُّ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّال -
َّ«إَّلس َّ هِي ذُّ إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ ن ِهِ رَّمَّ ق ع ُّسِّ لَّ وَّ كُّق ِّن َّ و
ِجُّ ن ِّظَّ وَّ صُّ لِّى َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّكُّن ْ ن ِهِ رَّمَّ ق كُّق ِّن َّ ق ِى إ َّي ْوَّ إن ِه .
english_text:
Abu Mariam Al-Ansari narrated that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
said:
"If a martyr has a remaining breath (sign of life), then he should be washed, shrouded,
embalmed, and funeral prayers should be offered for him. But if there is no remaining
breath, he should be shrouded in his own clothes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 211 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 331 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 214 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 348 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 506

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
english_text:
Aban ibn Taghlib asked Him about a man who is killed in the path of Allah {SWT}:
Should he be washed, shrouded, and embalmed (with Hunut)?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should be buried as he is, in his clothing with his blood, unless
there is a sign of life remaining. If he has a sign of life and then dies, he should be
washed, shrouded, embalmed, and the funeral prayer should be offered for him. This
is because the Messenger of Allah {saws} prayed over Hamza, shrouded him, and
embalmed him because he had been stripped (of his clothing)”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
ِوَّ إُّسْ ي ُّس ْ هِذَّ جَّ ن ْط َّ لَّه ُّ ن ْن ُّ إ َّن ِى عَّامِزٍ إَّلز َّإهِث ُّ ن ِا ُّجُّ ذٍ ق َّلَّمْ ي َّا ْمُّ زِ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ ل ِهِ ن ِع ُّسْ لِه َّوَّ ق َّال ُّ «رَّإ َّي ْ ث
ُّ إَّلْمَّلاَّن ِكَّه َّ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلس َّ مَّاءِ وَّ إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ ي ُّع َّسِّ لُّ، جَّ ن ْط َّ لَّه َّ ن ِمَّاءِ إَّلْمُّز ْن ِ ق ِى صِ حَّ اف ٍ مِن ْ ق ِص َّ ه ٍ وَّ كَّان َّ ي ِ سَّ م َّى ع َّسِ ي لَّ إَّلْمَّلاَّن ِكَّه .
english_text:
Hanzalah ibn Abu 'Amir, known as " Rahib," was martyred at the Battle of Uhud.
The Prophet Muhammad {saws} did not command that he be washed, saying: "I saw the
angels washing Hanzalah with water from the clouds, using silver vessels."
Because of this, he was given the title "Ghasil al-Malaika" (The One Washed by the
Angels).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 159 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 349 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 506 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 20, p. 47

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«ي ُّن ْز َّعُّ عَّن ِ إَّلس َّ هِي ذِ إَّلْق َّزْوُّ وَّ إَّلْح ُّ ف ُّ وَّ إَّلْق َّلَّن ْسُّ وَّ ة ُّ وَّ إَّلْعِمَّامَّ ه ُّ وَّ إَّلْمِن ْطَّ ق َّه ُّ و
َّ إَّلس َّ زَّإوِي لُّ إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّكُّون َّ إ َّصَّ ان َّهُّ ذَّم ق َّا ِن ْ إ َّصَّ ان َّهُّ ذَّم ي ُّزِك َّ وَّ لأَّ ي ُّي ْزَّك ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ س َّ ى ْ ء مَّ عْ ق ُّوذ إ ِلأ َّ جُّ ل .
وإلمحزم إ ذ إ ماب ع سل وكق ن وذق ن وعمل ن ه ما ي عمل ن المحل إ لأ إ ن ه لأ ي ق زن ه إلكاق ور. وق ي ي ل إلمعزكه ق ى ع ي ز طاعه إلله
. عز وج ل ي ع سل كما ي ع سل إلمي ث ، وي ص م (رإ سه إ لى عن ق ه، وي ع سل مغ إلن ذن
وإ ذ إ ماي ث إلمزإ ة وهى جامل وولذها ي ي حزك
ق ى ن طن ها س ق ن طن ها من إلح ان ث إلأ ي سز وإ ج زح إلولذ ، وإ ن ماب إلولذ ق ى ج وق ها ولم ي ح زح وهى جي ه إ ذج ل إ ن سان ي ذة
ق ى ق زج ها وق طغ إلولذ ن ي ذة وإ ج زج ه.
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"From a martyr, the fur, shoes, cap, turban, belt, and trousers should be removed,
unless they have been stained with blood ; if they are stained with blood, they are to
be left on. No tied item should remain on the body; it must be untied."
commentary:
Regarding a person in a state of ihram (ritual consecration during Hajj or Umrah) who
dies, they should be washed, shrouded, and buried with all the rites performed for
someone not in ihram, except that camphor should not be used.
A person killed in battle not in obedience to Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, should be washed
like any deceased person, and if their head has been severed, it should be joined to
the body and washed together.
In the case of a woman who dies while pregnant, if the fetus is moving in her womb,
the left side of her abdomen should be opened, and the child removed. If the child dies
inside her and does not come out while She is alive, a person should reach in through
the birth canal, cut the child into pieces, and extract it.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 211 • Da‘ā’im al-Islām, Part 1, p. 229 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 159 • Al-Khisal, Part 1, p. 333 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 332 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 349 • Wasail Al- Shia, Part 2, p. 510 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 2 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 2, p. 179

ِوَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّهُّ لَّم َّا ق ُّن ِض َّ إ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إَّلْن َّاق ِزُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ لَّمْ ي َّز َّلْ إ َّن ُّو عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ ه إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّا ْمُّ زُّ ن ِالسِّ زَّإح ِ ق ِى

.ومن كان ج ن ن ا وإ رإذ إ ن ي ع سل إلمي ث ق لي ي وص ا وص وء إلصلاة ي م ي ع سله
ومن إ رإذ إلح ماع ن عذ ع سله للمي ث ق لي ي وص ا ي م ي ح امغ .
وإ ن ع سل مي ث ق ح زح من ه ذم كي ي ز لأ ي ن ق طغ ق ا ن ه ي ح عل علي ه إلطي ن إلحز
.ق ا ن ه ي ن ق طغ
english_text:
It has been narrated that when Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} passed
away, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} continued to have a lamp lit in the room
where Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} lived, until Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} also passed
away.
Then Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} also instructed to do the same
in the room of Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} to remain lit until He was taken
to Iraq, after which it is unknown what happened”.
commentary:
Regarding a person in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) who wishes to wash a
deceased person, they should perform ablution (wudu) as for prayer before washing
the body.
If someone wishes to engage in marital relations after washing the deceased, they
should perform ablution before doing so.
If a deceased person is washed and a significant amount of blood continues to flow
from the body without stopping, then clean clay should be applied, as it will stop the
bleeding.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
english_text:
Sulayman ibn Khalid asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"Does one who washes the deceased need to perform ghusl (ritual purification)?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes."
He then asked: "What about someone who places the deceased in the grave?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "No, because he only touches the clothing."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CHAPTER ON TOUCHING THE DECEASED
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"When (my son) Ismail died, I ordered that his body, while covered, be uncovered so
that I could kiss his forehead, chin, and neck.
Then, I had him covered again and later ordered that he be uncovered a second time,
and I kissed his forehead, chin, and neck once more. Then, I had him covered again.
After that, I instructed that he be washed. When the washing was completed, I entered
while he was being shrouded and said: 'Uncover his face,' and I kissed his forehead,
chin, and neck and then recited protective supplications over him.
I then said: 'Wrap him.'
Someone asked: 'With what did you offer the protective supplication?'
Imam {a.s} replied: 'With the Qur'an.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Kamal Al-Din, Part 1, p. 71 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 565 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 298 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 47, p. 247 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 16 • Awalim al- Ulum, Vol. 20, p. 912

ُّ«إ ِن َّ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق َّن َّلَّ، عُّي ْمَّان َّ ن ْن َّ مَّ ط ْ عُّون ٍ رَّص ِ ى َّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّن ْه
ِن َّعْ ذَّ مَّ وْ ي ِه .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} kissed ‘Uthman ibn Maz'un after his death."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 161 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 161 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 430 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 100 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 4, p. 38 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 564 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 298 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 22, p. 264 • Mustadrak Al- Wasail, Vol. 2, p. 493

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
ب اب-
الصلاه علي المي ت
ُّق َّالَّ إ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ٍ«مَّ ن ْ ي َّن ِغَّ ج َّ ن َّار َّة ً كَّي َّث َّ إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّ إ َّرْن َّعَّه َّ ق َّزَّإرِي ظَّ ق ِي زَّإطٍ لأِي ِّن َّاعِ هِ إ ِي َّاهَّا وَّ ق ِي زَّإط
ِ لِلص َّ لاَّة ِ عَّلَّي ْهَّا وَّ ق ِي زَّإطٍ لِلاِن ْي ِط َّ ارِ جَّ ي َّى ي َّق ْ زُّع َّ مِن ْ ذَّق ْن ِهَّا وَّ ق ِي زَّإطٍ لِلي َّعْ ز ِي َّه .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"Whoever follows a funeral procession, Allah {SWT} will record four qirats for them : one
qirat for following the procession, one qirat for offering the funeral prayer, one qirat for
waiting until the burial is completed, and one qirat for offering condolences."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 161 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 401

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم :
«مَّ ن ْ مَّ س َّ ى مَّ غَّ ج َّ ن َّار َّة ٍ جَّ ي َّى ي ُّصَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْهَّا ي ُّم َّ رَّج َّ غَّ كَّان َّ لَّهُّ ق ِي زَّإط وَّ إ ِذ َّإ مَّ س َّ ى
ٍمَّ عَّهَّا جَّ ي َّى ي ُّذْ ق َّن َّ كَّان َّ لَّهُّ ق ِي زَّإطَّ ان ِ وَّ إَّلْق ِي زَّإطُّ مِي ْلُّ ج َّ ن َّلِ إ ُّجُّ ذ .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Whoever walks with a funeral procession until the funeral prayer is offered and then
returns will receive one qirat (measure of reward). If they continue walking with it until
the deceased is buried, they will receive two qirats, and one qirat is like the size of
Mount Uhud."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 173 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 455 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 400 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 145

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ٍعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «مَّ ن ْ ي َّن ِغَّ ج َّ ن َّار َّة َّ إِمْ زِى ٍ مُّ سْ لِم َّإ ُّعْ طِ ى َّ ي َّوْ مَّ إَّلْق ِي َّامَّ ه ِ إ َّرْن َّغَّ س َّ ق َّاعَّاب ٍ وَّ لَّمْ ي َّق ُّلْ س َّ ي ْ ن اً إ ِلأ َّ ق َّال
َّ لَّهُّ إَّلْمَّلَّك ُّ وَّ لَّك َّ مِي ْلُّ ذ َّلِك .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said: "Whoever follows the funeral procession of a Muslim will be
granted four intercessions on the Day of Judgment. Whatever supplication or
statement they make, the angel will say to them, 'And for you is the same.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Amali (by Al-Saduq) Vol. 1, p. 217 • Al-Wa'ezin, Vol. 2, p. 494 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 257

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ً «مَّ ن ْ إ َّج َّ ذ َّ ن ِح َّ وَّ إن ِث ِ إَّلس َّ زِي زِ إَّلْأ َّرْن َّعَّه ِ ع َّق َّزَّ إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّ إ َّرْن َّعِي ن َّ كَّن ِي زَّة .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "Whoever takes hold of the four
sides of the bier (funeral bier) will have forty major sins forgiven by Allah {SWT}."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, V3, p.174 • Al-Wafi, V 24, p. 396 • Wasail Al-Shia, P3, p. 154

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «مَّ ن ْ س َّ ي َّغَّ ج َّ ن َّار َّة َّ مُّو ْ مِن ٍ جَّ ي َّى ي ُّذْ ق َّن َّ ق ِى ق َّن ْزِةِ وَّ ك َّلَّ إَّلل َّهُّ ن ِه َّ سَّ ن ْعِي ن َّ مَّ لَّكاً مِن َّ إَّلْمُّس َّ ي ِّعِي ن
ِ ي ُّس َّ ي ِّعُّون َّهُّ وَّ ي َّسْ ي َّع ْ ق ِزُّون َّ لَّهُّ إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ زَّح َّ مِن ْ ق َّن ْزِةِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْمَّوْ ق ِف .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said: "Whoever accompanies the funeral of a believer until they are
buried in their grave, Allah {SWT} will assign seventy angels to accompany and seek
forgiveness for that person when they rise from their grave to stand at the gathering
(on the Day of Judgment)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 173 • Al-Amali (by Al-Saduq) Vol. 1, p. 217 • Rawdat al-Wa'izin, Vol. 2, p. 488 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 400 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 145 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 257

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said:
"The first gift given to a believer in their grave is the forgiveness granted to those who
followed their funeral procession."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Muʾmin, Part 1, p. 65 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 173 • Al- Khasal, Part 1, p. 24 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 455 • Sulwat al-Hazin, Part 1, p. 262 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 399 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 143 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 258

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"When a believer enters their grave, it is proclaimed: 'Behold, your first gift is Paradise!
And the first gift for those who followed your funeral procession is forgiveness.'"
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 172 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 162 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 399 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 142

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ً «مَّ ن ْ جَّ مَّلَّ إ َّج َّ اةُّ إَّلْمَّي ِّث َّ ن ِح َّ وَّ إن ِث ِ إَّلس َّ زِي زِ إَّلْأ َّرْن َّعَّه ِ مَّ حَّ ا إَّلل َّهُّ عَّن ْهُّ إ َّرْن َّعِي ن َّ كَّن ِي زَّة
ِمِن َّ إَّلْكَّن َّان ِز.
.وإلسن ه إ ن ي حمل إلسزي ز من ج وإن ن ه إلأ رن عه وما كان ن عذ ذ لك ق هو ي طوع
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}, said: “Whoever carries their deceased
brother on all four sides of the bier, Allah {SWT} will erase forty major sins from them."
commentary:
The Sunnah (recommended practice) is to carry the bier from its four sides, and any
additional carrying (from other angles) after that is considered voluntary.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 162 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 395

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ «مَّ ن ْ إ َّج َّ ذ َّ ن ِق َّوَّ إن ِمِ إَّلس َّ زِي زِ ع َّق َّزَّ إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّ ج َّ مْ ساً وَّ عِ س ْ زِي ن َّ كَّن ِي زَّة ً وَّ إ ِذ َّإ رَّن َّغَّ ج َّ زَّح
ِ مِن َّ إَّلذ ُّن ُّوب .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "Whoever takes hold of the
handles of the bier, Allah {SWT} will forgive twenty-five major sins for them. And if they
carry it on all four sides, they will be cleansed of their sins."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 174 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 162 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 196 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 395 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 154 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 155 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 263

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم لِأ ِسْ حَّ اق َّ ن ْن ِ عَّم َّارٍ إ ِذ َّإ جَّ مَّلْث َّ ج َّ وَّ إن ِث َّ إَّلس َّ زِي زِ سَّ زِي زِ إَّلْمَّي ِّث ِ ج َّ زَّج ْ ث َّ مِن َّ إَّلذ ُّن ُّوب ِ كَّمَّا
َّ وَّ لَّذَّي ْك َّ إ ُّم ُّك .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said to Ishaq ibn Ammar:
"When you carry the sides of the bier of the deceased, you will be cleansed of your sins
as if you were just born from your mother."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
english_text:
Abu Ja'far, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}, said:
"Walking behind the funeral procession is better than walking in front of it, but there is
no harm if you walk in front."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
ِوَّ كَّي َّث َّ إَّلْحُّ سَّ ي ْن ُّ ن ْن ُّ سَّ عِي ذٍ إ ِلَّى إ َّن ِى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّسْ ا َّلُّهُّ: عَّن ْ سَّ زِي ز إَّلْمَّي ِّث ِ ي ُّحْ مَّلُّ إ َّ لَّهُّ ج َّ ان ِث
ِ ي ُّن ْذَّإ ُّ ن ِهِ ق ِى إَّلْحَّ مْ لِ مِن ْ ج َّ وَّ إن ِن ِهِ إَّلْأ َّرْن َّعَّه ِ إ َّوْ مَّ ا ج َّ ف َّ عَّلَّى إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّحْ مِلُّ مِن ْ إ َّى ِّ إَّلْح َّ وَّ إن ِث ُّ س َّ اءَّ ق َّكَّي َّث َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم
َّ«مِن ْ إ َّي ِّهَّا س َّ اء .
english_text:
Hussein ibn Saeed wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s},
asking about the bier of the deceased: Is there a specific side that should be carried
first from among its four sides, or can one carry it from any side that is easiest?
Imam {a.s} replied: "From whichever side he wishes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 162 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 398 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 155

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلْح َّ ن َّار َّة ِ ي ُّح ْ زَّح ُّ مَّ عَّهَّا ن ِالن َّارِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن َّ إِن ْن َّه َّ رَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ و
ُّإ لِهِ إ ُّج ْ زِح َّ ن ِهَّا لَّي ْلاً وَّ مَّ عَّهَّا مَّ صَّ ان ِي ح .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a funeral procession
in which fire (torches or lamps) is carried.
Imam {a.s} replied: "The daughter of the Messenger of Allah {saws} was taken out at night,
and lamps accompanied her."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 162 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 406 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 159

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّجَّ ذِهِمَّا عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّال-
سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمَّس ْ ى ِ مَّ غَّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّار َّة ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّذَّي ْ هَّا
وَّ عَّن ْ ي َّمِي ن ِهَّا وَّ عَّن ْ س ِ مَّالِهَّا وَّ ج َّ لْق ِهَّا .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of them (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali
Al-Baqir {a.s} or Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} ) that he asked about walking
with the funeral procession.
Imam {a.s} replied: "In front of it, on its right side, on its left side, and behind it."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 169 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 163 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 403 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 149

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ سِ ن َّان ٍ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّال-
ِ «لَّم َّا مَّ اب َّ إ ذَّمُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّن َّلَّغ َّ إ ِلَّى إَّلص َّ لاَّة
َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّالَّ هِن َّه ُّ إَّلل َّهِ لِح َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّق َّذ َّمْ ي َّا رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ ق َّصَّ لِّ عَّلَّى ن َّن ِى ِّ إَّلل َّ هِ ق َّق َّالَّ ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِن

َّ إَّلص َّ لَّوَّ إب ِ إَّل َّي ِى ق َّزَّص َّ هَّا إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّعَّالَّى عَّلَّى إ ُّم َّ ه ِ مُّحَّ م َّذٍ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ وَّ هِى َّ إَّلس ُّ ن ِه ُّ إَّلْح َّ ارِي َّه ُّ ق ِى وُّلْذِةِ إ ِلَّى ي َّوْ م
ِ إَّلْق ِي َّامَّ ه.
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said:
"When Adam {a.s} passed away and it was time to perform the prayer for him, the son of
Adam, Hibatullah (Seth), said to Archangel Jibril {a.s}:
'Advance, O’ Messenger (intermediary) of Allah {SWT}, and lead the prayer over the
Prophet of Allah {SWT}.'
Archangel Jibril {a.s} replied: 'Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, commanded us to prostrate to your
father, and we do not go ahead of the best of his progeny. You are among the most
righteous of them, so you should lead.'
Hibatullah advanced and performed five takbirs over him, corresponding to the
number of prayers that Allah {SWT} made obligatory for the Ummah of Muhammad
(peace and blessings be upon
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 163 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 330 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 416 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 76 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 11, p. 260

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:

english_text:
When the Messenger of Allah {saws} offered the funeral prayer over a deceased
person, he would recite the first takbir and then recite the testimony of faith (shahada).
He would then recite the second takbir, send blessings upon the Prophet and his
family, and make supplications.
Upon the third takbir, he would pray for the believing men and women.
After the fourth takbir, he would supplicate for the deceased,
And then conclude with a fifth takbir before leaving.
When Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, forbade him from praying over the hypocrites,
he recited the first takbir, recited the shahada,
then recited the second takbir, sent blessings upon the Prophet and his family,
recited the third takbir, and prayed for the believing men and women.
Upon the fourth takbir, he did not offer any supplication for the deceased and then
concluded.
commentary:
When someone offers the funeral prayer over a deceased person, they should stand
at the head of the body so that if the wind lifts their garment, it will touch the funeral
bier. After each takbir, they should make the following supplications:
They should say the first Takbir and declare (Testimony of Faith):
"I bear witness that there is no god but Allah {SWT}, alone with no partner, and I bear
witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, sent with truth as a bearer of
glad tidings and a warner before the Hour."
Then they should say the second takbir and say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, have
mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the
family of Muhammad, just as You blessed, had mercy upon, and honored Ibrahim and
the family of Ibrahim. Truly, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."
Then they should say the third takbir and say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, forgive the believing men and women, the Muslim men and women, the
living and the dead."
Then they should say the fourth takbir and say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, this is Your servant, the child of Your servant and the child of Your
maidservant. They have returned to You, and You are the best to return to. O’ Allah {SWT},
we know nothing of them except good, but You know them better than we do. If they
were a doer of good, increase their goodness; if they committed wrong, forgive and
overlook their misdeeds. O’ Allah {SWT}, place them among the highest ranks of the
elevated ones and grant mercy upon them with Your mercy, O’ Most Merciful of the
merciful."
Then they should say the takbir for the fifth time, and conclude. The one offering the
prayer should not leave their position until they see the body being carried away by the
men.
The reason for reciting five takbirs in the funeral prayer is because Allah {SWT}, the
Exalted, has imposed five obligations upon the people: prayer (Salat), almsgiving
(Zakat), fasting (Saum), pilgrimage (Hajj), and leadership (Wilayah).
Thus, Allah {SWT} has designated one takbir for each obligation for the deceased.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 181 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 163 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 189 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 437 • Tafsir al-Safi, Part 2, p. 365 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 60 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 2, p. 249 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 5, p. 512

It has been narrated that the reason behind this practice is that Allah {SWT}, the
Exalted, has prescribed five obligatory prayers for people, and thus, one takbir is
designated for the deceased from each of these obligatory prayers.
commentary:
When offering the funeral prayer for a woman, one should stand near her chest. There
is no Tasleem (final salutatory phrase) in the funeral prayer except in cases of taqiyya
(precautionary dissimulation to protect oneself).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 164 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 76

english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said: "The Commander of the Faithful
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} used to recite takbirs five at a time over the deceased. When
people would arrive late and say, 'O’ Commander of the Faithful, we did not catch the
prayer over Sahl ibn Hunayf,' he would place the bier down and recite five takbirs over
him again, repeating this process until he reached the grave, doing so five times”.
commentary:
If someone recites one or two takbirs over a funeral and then another bier is brought
to join the first, they may, if they wish, continue with five takbirs over both, or they can
finish the first funeral prayer and then start anew for the second.
If a person offers the funeral prayer over a deceased individual who is positioned
incorrectly, they should correct the position and repeat the prayer.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"If a person catches one or two takbirs of the funeral prayer over the deceased, they
should complete the remaining takbirs consecutively."

english_text:
Omar ibn Yazid narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, that He
said: "If a believer passes away and forty men from among the believers attend their
funeral and say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, we do not know of anything but good from this person, and You know him
better than we do,'
Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, responds, 'I have accepted your testimony and
forgiven him for what I know that you do not.'"

Al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik asked Imam {a.s}: "Is it permissible to perform the
funeral prayer for the deceased in the mosque?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Abu Basir asked Imam {a.s} about who has the most right to perform the funeral
prayer for a woman who has passed away.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Her husband."
Abu Basir then asked: "Does the husband have more right than her father, son, or
brother?"
The Imam said: "Yes, and he may also wash her."
commentary:
My father wrote in his message to me:
"Know, my son, that the person with the most right to lead the funeral prayer for the
deceased is whoever is designated by the deceased's guardian (Wali).
If there is a man from the Banu Hashim among the people, he has priority for leading
the prayer if designated by the guardian of the deceased.
If someone leads without being appointed by the deceased’s guardian, then they are
usurping that right."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 177 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 205 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 486 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 417 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 115

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"If you miss the funeral prayer for the deceased until they are buried, there is no
problem in performing the prayer for them after they have been buried”.

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إَّلْي َّسَّ غُّ ن ْن ُّ عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ إَّلْق ُّمِّى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى عَّلَّى إَّلْح ِ ن َّار َّة ِ وَّ جْ ذَّةُّ ق َّال
ِ «ن َّعَّمْ » ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّاي ْن َّان ِ ي ُّصَّ لِّي َّان ِ عَّلَّي ْهَّا ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ وَّ لَّكِن ْ ي َّق ُّومُّ إَّلْأ ج َّ زُّ ج َّ لْف َّ إَّلْأ ج َّ زِ وَّ لأَّ ي َّق ُّومُّ ن ِح َّ ن ْن ِه .
english_text:
Al-Yasa' ibn Abdullah al-Qummi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} about a man praying over a funeral alone.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, he may do so."
I then asked: "What if there are two people praying?"
The Imam said: "Yes, but one should stand behind the other, not next to him."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 176 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 166 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 319 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 424 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 120

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِج َّ ان ِز ق َّالَّ إ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ «إ ِذ َّإ لَّمْ ي َّحْ ص ُّ زِ إَّلزِّج َّ الُّ إَّلْمَّي ِّث َّ ي َّق َّذ َّمَّ ث ِ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ُّ وَّ سَّ طَّ هُّن َّ وَّ ق َّامَّ إَّلن ِّسْ وَّ ة
ِ عَّن ْ ي َّمِي ن ِهَّا وَّ س ِ مَّالِهَّا وَّ هِى َّ وَّ سَّ طُّ هُّن َّ ي ُّكَّن ِّزُّ جَّ ي َّى ي َّق ْ زُّع َّ مِن َّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة.
english_text:
Jabir said : Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"If no men are present for the deceased, a woman should step forward and stand in
the middle, with the other women positioned on her right and left, and She should lead
by reciting the takbirs until the prayer is completed."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 179 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 166 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 326 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 425 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 118 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 337

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ُّ ن ْن ُّ ر ِي َّاذٍ إَّلص َّ ي ْق َّل:
ْ سُّ ن ِلَّ إ َّن ُّو عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ كَّي ْف َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إَّلن ِّسَّ اءُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْح َّ ن َّان ِز ِ إ ِذ َّإ لَّمْ ي َّكُّن
مَّ عَّهُّن َّ رَّج ُّ ل ق َّق َّالَّ «ي َّق ُّمْ ن َّ ج َّ مِي عاً ق ِى صَّ ف ٍّ وَّ إجِ ذٍ وَّ لأَّ ي َّي َّق َّذ َّمُّهُّن َّ إِمْ زَّإ َّة » ق ِي لَّ ق َّق ِى صَّ لاَّة ٍ مَّ كْي ُّو ُّ ن َّه ٍ إ َّ ي َّو ُّم ً ن َّعْ ص ُّ هُّن َّ ن َّعْ ص ا
ْق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّم .
english_text:
Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal reported that Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} was asked
about how women should perform the funeral prayer if no men are present.
Imam {a.s} replied: "They should all stand together in a single row, and no woman should
step forward as a leader."
He was then asked if, during the obligatory (written) prayers, one woman may lead
another.
The Imam said: "Yes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 166 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 117

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
َّ«صَّ ل ُّوإ عَّلَّى إَّلْمَّزْج ُّ ومِ مِن ْ إ ُّم َّ ي ِى وَّ عَّلَّى إَّلْق َّاي ِلِ ن َّق ْسَّ هُّ مِن ْ إ ُّم َّي ِى وَّ لأ
ٍ ي َّذَّعُّوإ إ َّجَّ ذإً مِن ْ إ ُّم َّي ِى ن ِلاَّ صَّ لاَّة .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"Offer the funeral prayer for the stoned (person) from my Ummah and for the one who
takes their own life from my Ummah, and do not leave anyone from my Ummah
without the funeral prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 166 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 328 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 468 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 481 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 133 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 41

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ هِس َّ امُّ ن ْن ُّ سَّ الِمٍ إ َّن َّا ُّعَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
عَّن ْ س َّ ارِب ِ إَّلْح َّ مْ زِ وَّ إَّلز َّإن ِى وَّ إَّلس َّ ارِق ِ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْهِمْ إ ِذ َّإ
ْمَّ اي ُّوإ ق َّق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّم .
english_text:
Hisham ibn Salim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
whether the funeral prayer should be offered for one who drinks alcohol, commits
adultery (zina), or steals if they pass away.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 166 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 328 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 468 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 481 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 132

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّ عَّم َّارُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّوسَّ ى إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى:
ْق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ مَّ ا ي َّق ُّولُّ ق ِى ق َّوْ مٍ كَّان ُّوإ ق ِى سَّ ق َّزٍ لَّهُّم
َّي َّمْ س ُّ ون َّ عَّلَّى سَّ اجِ لِ إَّلْن َّحْ زِ ق َّا ِذ َّإ هُّمْ ن ِزَّج ُّ لٍ مَّ ي ِّث ٍ عُّزْ ي َّان ٍ ق َّذْ لَّق َّط َّ هُّ إَّلْن َّحْ زُّ وَّ هُّمْ عُّزَّإة لَّي ْسَّ م َّ عَّهُّمْ إ ِلأ َّ إ ِر َّإر ق َّكَّي ْ ف
ِ ي ُّصَّ ل ُّون َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ هُّوَّ عُّزْ ي َّان وَّ لَّي ْسَّ مَّ عَّهُّمْ ق َّص ْ لُّ ي َّوْ ب ٍ ي ُّكَّق ِّن ُّون َّهُّ ن ِهِ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّحْ ق َّزُّ لَّهُّ وَّ ي ُّوص َّ غُّ ق ُّ ى لَّحْ ذِةِ وَّ ي ُّوص َّ غُّ إَّلل َّن ِن
ُّ عَّلَّى عَّوْ رَّي ِهِ » لِي ُّسْ ي َّزَّ عَّوْ رَّي ُّهُّ ن ِالل َّن ِن ِ وَّ ن ِالْحَّ ح َّ زِ وَّ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْ هِ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّ ذْ ق َّن .
english_text:
Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati said:
"I asked Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a group of people who were traveling along the
seashore and came across a dead man who was naked and had been cast ashore by
the sea. They themselves were also without sufficient clothing, having only a single
garment. How should they perform the funeral prayer for him since he was naked and
they did not have an extra cloth to shroud him?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "A grave should be dug, and he should be placed in his burial niche,
with bricks placed over his private parts to cover them. Then, the funeral prayer should
be offered over him, and he should be buried."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 214 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 166 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 179 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 327 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 487 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 131

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ ِسْ حَّ اق ُّ ن ْن ُّ عَّم َّارٍ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِي هِ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ْ «إ َّن َّ عَّلِي اً صَّ لَّوَّ إب ُّ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ ج َّ ذَّ ق ِطَّ عاً مِن
ْ مَّ ي ِّث ٍ ق َّح ُّ مِعَّث ْ ي ُّم َّ صَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْهَّا ي ُّم َّ ذُّق ِن َّث.
english_text:
Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, and
him from his father, Imam al-Baqir: that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}, once found
scattered parts of a deceased person. He gathered them together, performed the
funeral prayer over them, and then they were buried.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 167 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 337 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 3, p. 329 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 492 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 135

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
وَّ رَّوَّ ى ُّإَّلْق َّص ْ لُّ ن ْن ُّ عُّي ْمَّان َّ إَّلْأ َّعْ وَّ رُّ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِي هِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّق ِى إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّق ْي َّلُّ ق َّي ُّوج َّ ذ
َّرَّإ ْسُّ هُّ ق ِى ق َّن ِي لَّه ٍ وَّ وَّ سَّ طُّ هُّ وَّ صَّ ذْ رُّةُّ وَّ ي َّذَّإةُّ ق ِى ق َّن ِي لَّه ٍ وَّ إَّلْن َّاق ِى مِن ْهُّ ق ِى ق َّن ِي لَّه ٍ ق َّالَّ «ذِي َّي ُّهُّ ع ِلَّى مَّ ن ْ وُّج ِ ذَّ ق ِى ق َّن ِي لَّي ِه
ِصَّ ذْ رُّةُّ وَّ ي َّذَّإةُّ وَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه .
english_text:
Al-Fadl ibn 'Uthman al-A'war narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-
Sadiq {a.s} and him from his father, Imam al-Baqir, regarding a man who is killed and his
head is found in one tribe, his torso and hands in another tribe, and the rest of his body
in a different tribe.
The Imam said: "The responsibility for his blood money (diyah) is upon the tribe where
his torso and hands are found, and the funeral prayer should be performed over those
parts”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 167 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 4, p. 166 • Al- Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 491 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 135

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«إ ِذ َّإ وُّج ِ ذَّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ق َّي ِي لاً ق َّا ِن ْ وُّج ِ ذَّ لَّهُّ عُّص ْ و مِن ْ إ َّعْ ص َّ ان ِهِ ي َّام اً صُّ لِّى َّ عَّلَّى ذ َّلِك َّ و
َّ ذُّق ِن َّ وَّ إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي ُّوج َّ ذْ لَّهُّ عُّص ْ و ي َّام لَّمْ ي ُّصَّ ل َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ ذُّق ِن .
وإ ذ إ وسظ إلزج ل ن ن صق ي ن صلى على إلن صف إلذ ى ق ي ه إلق لث ، وإ ن لم ي وج ذ من ه إ لأ إلزإ س لم ي صل علي ه.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
“If a man is found killed and one of his limbs is found intact, a funeral prayer should
be offered over it, and it should be buried. If no complete limb is found, no funeral
prayer is offered, but it should still be buried”.
commentary:
And if a man is cut in half, he should pray funeral prayer over the half that contains the
heart; if only the head remains, he should not pray funeral prayer over it.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 212 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 167 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 337 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 490 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 137 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 8

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ وَّ عُّن َّي ْ ذ ُّإَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ عَّلِى ٍّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِّ إ َّن َّهُّ سُّ ن ِلَّ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ عَّلَّى إَّلص َّ ن ِى
ْ مَّ ي َّى ي ُّصَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ عَّق َّلَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ» ق َّق ُّلْث ُّ مَّ ي َّى ي َّح ِ ث ُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ إِن ُّن َّ سِ ث ِّ سِ ن ِي ن َّ وَّ إَّلصِّ ي َّام
ُّإ ِذ َّإ إ َّطَّ اق َّه.
ومن جص ز مغ ق وم ي صلون على طق ل ق لي ق ل: " إللهم إج عله لأ ن وي ه ولن ا ق زطا.
english_text:
Zurarah and Ubaidullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He was asked about when the funeral prayer should be
offered for a child.
Imam {a.s} replied: "When the child understands the concept of prayer."
I asked: "At what age does prayer become obligatory for the child?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "When the child reaches six years old, and fasting becomes
obligatory when they are capable of it."
commentary:
And if someone attends the funeral prayer for a child, they should say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, make this child a precursor (one who goes ahead) for their parents and
for us”.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 206 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 167 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 198 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 479 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 495 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 95

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:
َّوَّ صَّ ل َّى إ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّلَّى إِن ْن ٍ لَّهُّ صَّ ن ِى ٍّ صَّ ع ِي زٍ لَّهُّ ي َّلاَّب ُّ سِ ن ِي ن َّ ي ُّم َّ ق َّال -
َّ «لَّوْ لأَّ إ َّن َّ إَّلن َّاسَّ ي َّق ُّولُّون
ِإ ِن َّ ن َّن ِى هَّاس ِ مٍ لأَّ ي ُّصَّ ل ُّون َّ عَّلَّى إَّلصِّ ع َّارِ مِن ْ إ َّوْ لأَّذِهِمْ مَّ ا صَّ ل َّي ْث ُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} offered the funeral prayer for a young son
of his who was three years old.
Imam {a.s} then said: "If it were not for the fact that people might say that the Banu
Hashim do not offer funeral prayers for their young children, I would not have prayed
over him”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 498 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 101

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)

english_text:
He was asked : "When does the funeral prayer become obligatory for a child?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "When the child understands the concept of prayer and is six years
old."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)

مغ من إ جن ث .
english_text:
Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s}:
"Prayers over the oppressed (Al-Mustadh'afin) and those who are unversed of their
beliefs will be: first send salawat for the Prophet his family, and then make
supplications for the believing men and women, and then do supplication saying:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, forgive those who have repented and followed Your path, and protect
them from the punishment of Hellfire.'"
commentary:
It is said in the Salat Al Mayyat prayer for someone whose sect is unknown:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, this soul You have given life to and You have caused to die, O’ Allah {SWT},
grant it what it has turned to, And gather it with those it loved."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 168 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 459

» َّ ي ُّعَّاذِى إ َّوْ لِي َّاءَّك َّ وَّ ي ُّن ْع ِض ُّ إ َّهْلَّ ن َّي ْث ِ ن َّن ِي ِّك .
english_text:
It was narrated by Safwan ibn Mehran al-Jammal from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"A man from the hypocrites passed away, and Imam al-Hussain ibn Ali {a.s} went out
walking. Imam {a.s} encountered a servant of his, and asked: 'Where are you going?'
The servant said: 'I am avoiding the funeral of this hypocrite so that I do not have to
pray over him.'
Imam al-Hussain {a.s} replied: 'Come stand by my side, and whatever you hear me say,
you should say as well.' Imam {a.s} then raised his hands and said:
"'O’ Allah {SWT}, disgrace Your servant among Your servants and in Your lands. O’ Allah
{SWT}, make him taste the intensity of Your fire. O’ Allah {SWT}, make him feel the heat of
Your punishment, for he was loyal to Your enemies, hostile to Your allies, and had
hatred for the family of Your Prophet.'"
references: Al-Kafi, V.3, p. 189 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 168 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 70

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)

. ِ إَّلْمُّسْ ي َّص ْ عَّف ُّ مِن ْك َّ ن ِسَّ ن ِي لٍ ق َّاسْ ي َّع ْ ق ِزْ لَّهُّ عَّلَّى وَّ ج ْ هِ إَّلس َّ ق َّاعَّه ِ مِن ْك َّ لأَّ عَّلَّى وَّ ج ْ هِ إَّلْوَّ لأَّي َّه
english_text:
It was narrated by Ubaidullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"If you perform the funeral prayer for an enemy of Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, we know of him only that he was an enemy to You and Your Messenger.
O’ Allah {SWT}, fill his grave with fire, fill his innermost with fire, and hasten him toward
the fire, for he was loyal to Your enemies, hostile to Your allies, and had hatred for the
family of Your Prophet. O’ Allah {SWT}, make his grave tight upon him.'"
And when his coffin bier is raised, say: "O’ Allah {SWT}, do not raise him up or purify him."
And if he However, if he is considered weak (Mustadh’af), say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, forgive those who repent, follow Your way, and protect them from the
torment of Hell."
If you are unaware of his condition, then say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, if he loved good and its people, forgive him, have mercy upon him, and
overlook him."
And If the Mustadh’af has a connection to you, seek forgiveness for him as an
intercession but not as an expression of loyalty."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:

َّ إَّلْحُّ زِّ ق َّذ َّمَّ إَّلْعَّن ْذَّ وَّ إ َّج َّ زَّ إَّلْحُّ ز َّ وَّ إ ِذ َّإ صَّ ل َّى عَّلَّى إَّلْكَّن ِي زِ وَّ إَّلص َّ ع ِي زِ ق َّذ َّمَّ إَّلص َّ ع ِي زَّ وَّ إ َّج َّ زَّ إَّلْكَّن ِي ز .
english_text:
When Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} performed the funeral prayer for a man and a
woman together, he would place the woman in front and the man behind.
When praying for a slave and a free person, he would place the slave in front and the
free person behind. When praying for an elder and a child, he would place the child in
front and the elder behind.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 175 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 169 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 322 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 471 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 430 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 126

english_text:
Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said: "There is no harm in placing the man in front and the woman behind or in
placing the woman in front and the man behind"
commentary:
This is referring to the arrangement of the funeral prayer for the deceased.
The preferred position in the funeral prayer is the last row, and the reason for this is
that women used to mix with men during the funeral prayer.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text: The Prophet, said: "The best place in the funeral prayer is the last row."
commentary:
Therefore, people should move back to the last row, as its merit remains as the
Prophet {a.s} described.
Furthermore, if a man is invited to both a feast (walimah) and a funeral, he should
attend the funeral, as it reminds him of the hereafter, and leave the feast, as it reminds
him of worldly matters.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Tahdhib, Volume 1, p. 343 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 176

english_text:
The Prophet, said:
"If you are invited to funerals, hasten to attend, but if you are invited to weddings, take
your time."
commentary:
My father wrote in his letter to me:
Do not offer the funeral prayer while wearing a sandal with an elevated heel, and do
not rush with two deceased people together on one bier. He also said: When two
people are praying over a deceased person, one should stand behind the Imam, not
next to him. If a man, a woman, a boy, and a slave are all part of the funeral, position
the woman closest to the Qibla, followed by the slave, then the boy, and then the man
nearest to the Imam. The Imam stands behind the man and prays over them all with a
single prayer.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 169 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 402 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 451 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 32

english_text:
Yunus ibn Ya'qub asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
performing the funeral prayer without being in a state of ritual ablution (wudu).
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, it is permissible, for it is comprised of takbir (saying 'Allahu
Akbar'), tasbih (glorification of Allah {SWT}), tahmid (praise of Allah {SWT}), and tahlil
(declaration of 'La ilaha illa Allah {SWT}'), just as you say them in your home."
commentary:
In another narration, it is mentioned: "One may perform tayammum (dry ablution) if
they wish."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}:
"A menstruating woman may participate in the funeral prayer but does not stand in the
rows with the rest of the congregation."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 170 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 24, p. 421

english_text:
In a narration of Sama’a ibn Mehran from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"A menstruating woman who is present at a funeral should perform tayammum (dry
ablution) and pray for the deceased, standing apart and separate from the row."
commentary:
This means that She stands to the side and does not mix with the men.
Similarly, a person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) should also perform
tayammum and then offer the funeral prayer.
When the deceased is carried to the grave, it should not be rushed or hurriedly placed
into the grave, as the grave is a place with immense awe and trials.
The one carrying the body should seek refuge in Allah {SWT} from the difficulties of the
grave.
The deceased should be placed near the edge of the grave for a moment to prepare
and then moved closer gradually.
The person authorized by the guardian of the deceased may place the body in the
grave, either with two people (in pairs) or one at a time. At the sight of the grave, one
should say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, make it a garden from the gardens of Paradise and not a pit from the pits
of Hellfire".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "The depth of the grave is to the
collarbone (clavicle)."
commentary:
Some have said it is to the chest, while others have said it should be as deep as the
height of a man, so that the shroud can cover the head of the deceased in the grave.
As for the niche (luhd), it should be wide enough to allow for the deceased to sit up.
It is narrated from Imam al-Hadi {a.s} that it is permissible for the grave to be lined with
wooden boards and covered with them over the deceased.
Each thing has its place, and the entrance to the grave is at the feet of the deceased.
When burying a woman, She should be lowered into the grave from the side, with her
husband standing where he can support her hip, while a man is lowered from his feet
and slid in gently.
My father wrote in his letter to me:
When you enter the grave, recite the Surah Al-Fatiha, the two chapters of seeking
refuge (Surah Al-Falaq & Surah An-Nas), and the Ayatul Kursi (2:255).
When you receive the deceased, say: "In the name of Allah {SWT}, and by Allah {SWT}, and
in the religion of the Messenger of Allah {saws} and his family."
Place the deceased on their right side, facing the Qibla, untie the shroud, place their
cheek on the earth, and say: "O’ Allah {SWT}, make the earth gentle on their sides, raise
their soul to You, and grant them Your pleasure."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Salim ibn Mukram narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said: "A pillow of earth should be placed for the deceased, and a clump of soil
behind their back to prevent them from lying flat. The knots of their shroud should be
untied, their face uncovered, and supplications should be made:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, this is Your servant, the child of Your servant and maidservant. They have
returned to You, and You are the best to receive.
O’ Allah {SWT}, expand their grave for them, teach them their proof, and join them with
their Prophet. Protect them from the trial of Munkar and Nakir.'"
Then, place your right hand under their right shoulder and your left hand on their left
shoulder, and shake them firmly while saying:
"O’ [name of the deceased], child of [father’s name], Allah {SWT} is your Lord {AZJ},
Muhammad is your Prophet, Islam is your religion, Ali is your guardian and Imam" -
Name each of the Imams, ending with: 'Your Imams are the guides and the righteous.'
Then repeat the talqeen (prompting of faith) once more.
And when you put earth over him or when placing bricks over the grave, say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, have mercy on their loneliness, connect their solitude, comfort their
fear, and fill them with Your mercy so that they need no mercy from anyone other than
You. Unite them with those they loved."
When visiting their grave, recite this supplication facing the Qibla, with hands on the
grave.
Upon exiting the grave, while brushing the dirt off your hands, say:
"Indeed, we belong to Allah {SWT}, and indeed, to Him we shall return."
Throw dirt onto the grave with the backs of your hands three times, saying:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, we believe in You and affirm Your Book. This is what You and Your
Messenger have promised, and Allah {SWT} and His Messenger have spoken the truth."
Whoever performs this and says these words will earn a reward for every particle of
soil.
Once the grave is made/leveled, pour water over it, beginning at the head and circling
around all four sides, returning to the head without breaking the flow of water. If any
water remains, pour it in the middle of the grave.
Place your hand on the grave, supplicate for the deceased, and seek forgiveness for
them.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 172 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 521 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 179

Chapter Title: THE FUNERAL PRAYER (SALAT AL-JANAZAH)
arabic_text:

ن ِهِ ق َّي َّص َّ غَّ ق َّاةُّ عَّلَّى رَّإ ْسِ هِ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّن َّاذِى َّ ن ِا َّعْ لَّى صَّ وْ ي ِهِ : ي َّا ق ُّلاَّن َّ ن ْن َّ ق ُّلاَّن ٍ إ َّوْ ي َّا ق ُّلاَّن َّه َّ ن ِن ْث َّ ق ُّل اَّن َّه َّ هَّلْ إ َّن ْث َّ عَّلَّى إَّلْعَّهْ ذِ إَّل َّذ ِى
ْق َّارَّق ْن َّاك َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ مِن ْ س َّ هَّاذَّة ِ إ َّن ْ لأَّ إ ِلَّهَّ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلل َّهُّ وَّ ج ُّذَّةُّ لأَّ س َّ زِي ك َّ لَّهُّ وَّ إ َّن َّ مُّحَّ م َّذإً صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ عَّن ْذُّةُّ وَّ رَّسُّ ولُّه
سَّ ي ِّذُّ إَّلن َّن ِي ِّي ن َّ وَّ إ َّن َّ عَّلِي اً إ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ وَّ سَّ ي ِّذُّ إَّلْوَّ صِ ي ِّي ن َّ وَّ إ َّن َّ مَّ ا ج َّ اءَّ ن ِهِ مُّحَّ م َّذ ِصَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه َّ جَّ ق وَّ إ َّن
ْإَّلْمَّوْ ب َّ جَّ ق وَّ إَّلْن َّعْ ث َّ جَّ ق «وَّ إ َّن َّ إَّلسّٰ اعَّه َّ إ ي ِي َّه لأٰ رَّي ْث َّ ق ِي هٰ ا وَّ إ َّن َّ إَّللّٰهَّ ي َّن ْعَّث ُّ مَّ ن ْ ق ِى إَّل»ِق ُّن ُّور
ق َّا ِذ َّإ ق َّالَّ ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّالَّ مُّن ْكَّز
لِن َّكِي زٍ إِن ْصَّ زِف ْ ن ِن َّا عَّن ْ هَّذ َّإ ق َّق َّذْ لُّق ِّن َّ ن ِهَّا ُّجُّ ح َّ ي َّه .
english_text:
Yahya ibn Abdullah narrates from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"There is no harm for the family of the deceased among you to help the deceased
prepare for the encounter with Munkar and Nakir (the questioning angels).” I asked:
“How should we do that?”
Imam {a.s} said: “When the deceased is placed in the grave, the closest person to them
should remain by their side, place their mouth near the head of the deceased, and call
out in a loud voice:
"O’ [name of the deceased], child of [father’s name], are you still on the covenant upon
which we left you - the testimony that there is no god but Allah {SWT}, alone without
partner, and that Muhammad {saws} is His servant and Messenger, the Master of the
Prophets; that Ali is The Commander of the Faithful, the Master of the Successors; that
what Muhammad {saws} brought is the truth; that death is real, resurrection is real, and
that the Hour is coming without a doubt, and that Allah {SWT} will raise those who are in
the graves?"
If this is said: Munkar will turn to Nakir and say:
“Let us leave, for he has been properly instructed (given Talqeen)."
commentary:
The term "ma'tam” originally referred to a gathering of men and women for either
sorrowful or joyful occasions. Over time, it became specifically associated with
gatherings of women during times of mourning for the deceased.
It has also been said to apply particularly to young women in mourning (Al-Nihaya).
Additionally, the term "matam" can also refer to food that is prepared for the deceased
("Fi").
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 201 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 173 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 1, p. 321 • Sulwat al-Hazin, Part 1, p. 270 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 531 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 200

"Whoever consoles a grieving person will be clothed in a robe of honor on the Day of
Standing (the Day of Judgment), which will bring them joy (and honor)."

It was narrated from Hisham ibn al-Hakam that He said:
"I saw Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} offering condolences both before and after
the burial."

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The obligatory act of offering condolences is after the burial."

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"It is sufficient as a form of condolence for the bereaved to see you."

english_text:
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} visited a group of people who had experienced a loss and
said:
"May Allah {SWT} strengthen you in your weakness, grant you beautiful patience, and
have mercy on your deceased." Then Imam {a.s} departed (from the funeral).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 174 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 555 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 218

إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ َّ لِهِ ق َّلَّن ْ ي َّق ُّوي َّهُّ وَّ إجِ ذَّة مِن ْهُّن َّ إ ِن ْ س َّ اءَّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل .
english_text:
The truthful one, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, offered condolences
to a man who had lost his son and said to him: "Allah {SWT} is better for your son than
you are, and the reward from Allah {SWT} is better for you than your son."
Later, when the Imam heard of the man's continued grief, he returned to him and said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} also passed away; do you not take him as an example?"
The man said that his son was on the verge of maturity (approaching adulthood).
The Imam then said (consoling him): "There are three things ahead of him: the
testimony that there is no god but Allah {SWT}, Allah’s {SWT} mercy, and the intercession
of the Messenger of Allah {saws}. He will not miss out on any of these, if Allah {SWT} the
Almighty wills."

ٍق ِى ق َّمِي ضٍ جَّ ي َّى ي ُّعْ زَّف َّ وَّ ي َّن ْن َّع ِى لِح ِ ي زَّإن ِهِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّطْ عِمُّوإ عَّن ْهُّ ي َّلاَّي َّه َّ إ َّي َّام .
english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"It is proper for the person responsible for the funeral (i.e., the chief mourner) not to
wear an outer cloak (ridā') and to remain in a shirt (Qamis) so that they are recognized
(as grieving). It is also proper for the neighbors to provide food on their behalf for three
days.”
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال ِعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «مَّ لْعُّون مَّ لْعُّون مَّ ن ْ وَّ ص َّ غَّ رِذَّإءَّةُّ ق ِى مُّصِ ي ن َّه ِ ع َّي ْ زِة.
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said: "Cursed!, cursed is the one who puts down (removes) their
cloak (rida') in the misfortune of someone else."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 174 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 1, p. 307 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 554 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 441 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 71

english_text:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} placed his cloak down during the funeral of Sa'd
ibn Mu'adh (may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him). When asked about this, Prophet {saws}
said:
"I saw the angels had placed their cloaks down, so I placed mine as well."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 175 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 554 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 2, p. 442 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 269

Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "If patience had not been created before trials, the
believer would have shattered like an egg striking a rock."
references: Al-Kafi Volume 2, p. 92 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 175 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 4, p. 338 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 566 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 257 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 68, p. 82

َّو
» َّ مَّ ن ْ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّصَّ اب َّ ج َّ ي ْ زإً ق َّالَّ «إَّلْحَّ مْ ذُّ لِلّٰهِ رَّب ِّ إَّلْعٰ الَّمِي ن

ِإ َّسْ ي َّع ْ ق ِزُّ إَّلل َّهَّ وَّ إ َّي ُّوب ُّ إ ِلَّي ْ ه.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said: "There are four qualities; whoever possesses
them will be in the greatest light of Allah {SWT}, the Exalted and Glorious:"
One whose protection is in the testimony that there is no god but Allah {SWT} and that I
am the Messenger of Allah {saws},
And one who, when afflicted with a calamity, says:
"Indeed, we belong to Allah {SWT} and to Him we will return"
And one who, when blessed with goodness, says:
"All praise is due to Allah {SWT}, the Lord {AZJ} of the worlds"
And one who, when committing a sin, says:
"I seek forgiveness from Allah {SWT} and repent to Him."
references: Al Mahasin, Part 1, p. 7 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 175 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 165 • Al-Khisal, Part 1, p. 222 • Tahaf al-Uqool, Part 1, p. 40 • Mishkat Al-Anwar, Part 1, p. 148 • Muskkin al-Fu’ād, Part 1, p. 110 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 568 • Tafsir al-Safi, Part 1, p. 205 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 248

ُّ«مَّ ا مِن ْ مُّو ْ مِن ٍ ي ُّصَّ اب ُّ ن ِمُّصِ ي ن َّه ٍ ق ِى إَّلذ ُّن ْي َّا ق َّي َّسْ ي َّزْج ِ غُّ عِ ن ْذَّ مُّصِ ي ن َّي ِهِ وَّ ي َّصْ ن ِز
َّجِ ي ن َّ ي َّق ْ ح َّ ا ُّةُّ إَّلْمُّصِ ي ن َّه ُّ إ ِلأ َّ ع َّق َّزَّ إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّ مَّ ا مَّ ص َّ ى مِن ْ ذ ُّن ُّون ِهِ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلْكَّن َّان ِزَّ إَّل َّي ِى إ َّوْ ج َّ ث َّ إ َّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ عَّلَّي ْه ا إَّلن َّارَّ وَّ كُّل َّمَّا
َّ ذ َّكَّزَّ مُّصِ ي ن َّي َّهُّ ق ِي مَّا ي َّسْ ي َّق ْن ِلُّ مِن ْ عُّمُّزِةِ ق َّاسْ ي َّزْج َّ غَّ عِ ن ْذَّهَّا وَّ جَّ مِذَّ إَّلل َّهَّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ عِ ن ْذَّهَّا، ع َّق ُّزَّ إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّ كُّل َّ ذ َّن ْث ٍ إِكْي َّسَّ ن َّه
َّ ق ِي مَّا ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلأِسْ ي ِزْج َّ اعِ إَّلْأ َّو َّ لِ إ ِلَّى إَّلأِسْ ي ِزْج ِ اعِ إَّلْأ َّج ِ ي زِ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلْكَّن َّان ِزَّ مِن َّ إَّلذ ُّن ُّوب .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Whenever a believer is afflicted with a calamity in this world and responds by reciting
the phrase of 'istirja' (saying 'Indeed, we belong to Allah {SWT} and to Him we will return')
at the moment of calamity and exhibits patience, Allah {SWT} forgives their past sins,
except for major sins for which Allah {SWT} has decreed Hellfire.
Additionally, each time the believer remembers that calamity in the future, recites
'istirja' again, and praises Allah {SWT}, Allah {SWT} forgives all sins committed between the
first instance of istirja' and the next, except for major sins."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 175 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 567 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 249

ٍ إ َّجَّ ذ ن ِعَّي ْ س .
english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There is an angel assigned to the cemeteries.
When the family of the deceased returns home after the funeral, this angel takes a
handful of soil and throws it after them, saying, 'Forget what you have seen.'
Were it not for this, no one would find any benefit (joy) in living."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 175 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 560 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 278

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever is afflicted with a calamity, whether they express intense grief over it or not,
whether they exercise patience or not, their reward from Allah {SWT}, the Exalted and
Glorious, is Paradise."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 176 • Muskkin al-Fu’ād, Part 1, p. 21 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 567 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 116

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The reward for a believer whose child dies is Paradise, whether they exhibit patience
or not”.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 219 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 176 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 284 • Muskkin al-Fu’ād, Part 1, p. 20 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 547 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 244 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 69, p. 332 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 116

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever loses a child (before their own passing), it is better for them than leaving
behind seventy children after them, all of whom rode horses and fought in the way of
Allah {SWT}, the Exalted and Glorious."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 176 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 245

english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"No one will enter Paradise unless they have a farat (one who goes ahead)."
A man who had no children and had not lost any asked:
"O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, does everyone among us have a farat?"
The Prophet replied: "Yes, among the farat of a believer is their brother in faith who
preceded them (in death) for the sake of Allah {SWT}, the Exalted and Glorious."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 176 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 548

english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said to Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A} when Ja'far
ibn Abi Talib was martyred:
"Do not supplicate with (expressions of) humiliation, loss, or desolation. Whatever you
have said about him is true."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 176 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 105

ن ْي َّا .
english_text:
it was narrated from Mehran ibn Muhammad that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad
Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"When a person dies, Allah {SWT}, the Exalted and Glorious, sends an angel to the one
among their family who is most deeply affected by the loss. The angel touches their
heart and alleviates the intensity of grief. If it were not for this, the world would not be
able to continue”.

ِق َّي َّق ُّولُّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ إِن ْن ُّوإ لَّهُّ ن َّي ْي اً ق ِى إَّلْح َّ ن َّه ِ ' وَّ سَّ م ُّوةُّ ن َّي ْث َّ إَّلْحَّ مْ ذ .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said: "When the child of a believer passes away,
Allah {SWT} – knowing best what His servant has said – asks the angels: 'Have you taken
the child of My believing servant?' They reply: 'Yes, our Lord {AZJ}.'
Allah {SWT} then asks: 'What did My servant say?'
They say: "He praised You and said: "Indeed, we belong to Allah {SWT} and to Him we will
return"
Then Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, says: "'Build for My servant a house in Paradise and name
it the House of Praise (Bayt al-Hamd).'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
When Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain {a.s}, saw a funeral procession, He would say:
'Praise be to Allah {SWT} who did not make me from among those whose lives were
abruptly taken'".

ُّ«لَّم َّا مَّ اب َّ إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مُّ ن ْن ُّ رَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق َّالَّ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّه
َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ «جَّ ز ِن َّا عَّلَّي ْك َّ ي َّا إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مُّ وَّ إ ِن َّا لَّصَّ ان ِزُّون َّ ي َّحْ ز َّن ُّ إَّلْق َّلْث ُّ وَّ ي َّذْ مَّ غُّ إَّلْعَّي ْن ُّ وَّ لأ ن َّق ُّولُّ مَّ ا
» َّ ي ُّسْ ح ِ ظُّ إَّلز َّب .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"When Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of Allah {saws} passed away, the Prophet said:
'We are grieved by your departure, O’ Ibrahim, and we are patient. The heart is
sorrowful, and the eyes shed tears, but we do not say that which displeases the Lord
{AZJ}.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 177 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 571 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 280 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 4, p. 283 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 10, p. 398

ر َّي ْذِ ن ْن ِ جَّ ارِي َّه َّ كَّان َّ إ ِذ َّإ ذَّج َّ لَّ ن َّي ْي َّهُّ كَّي ُّزَّ ن ُّكَّاو ُّةُّ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا ج ِ ذ إً وَّ ي َّق ُّولُّ «كَّان َّا»ًي ُّحَّ ذِّ ي َّان ِى وَّ ي ُّو َّ إن ِسَّ ان ِى ق َّذ َّهَّن َّا ج َّ مِي عا .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"When The Prophet {saws} received news of the deaths of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib {a.s} and Zayd
ibn Harithah, he would weep intensely when he entered his house and would say,
'They used to converse with me and bring me comfort, and now they are both gone.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 177 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 571 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 280 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 21, p. 55

ي َّسْ ي َّن ِق َّان ِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْكَّاق ِزِ ق َّي َّا ْي ِي هِ إَّلْن َّلاَّءُّ وَّ هُّوَّ ج َّ ز ُّوع .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Indeed, trials and patience race toward the believer, so when trials reach him, he is
patient. But panic and trials race toward the disbeliever, so when trials reach him, he
panics."
references: Al-Muʾmin, Part 1, p. 63 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 223 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 177 • Muskkin al-Fu’ād, Part 1, p. 51 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 25, p. 566 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 256 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 68, p. 95 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 142 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 2, p. 65
