ٍس َّ ى ْ ء
ً هَّذ َّإ إَّلْمَّوْ ص ِ غُّ ق َّالَّ ي َّا مُّحَّ م َّذُّ هَّذ ِةِ كُّوق َّان ُّ وَّ هَّذ َّإ مَّ سْ ح ِ ذُّهَّا إ َّم َّا إ َّن َّا ق َّق َّذْ رَّإ َّي ْي ُّهَّا عِ س ْ زِي ن َّ مَّ ز َّة
ًج َّ زَّإن اً وَّ عِ س ْ زِي ن َّ مَّ ز َّة ً عُّمْ زَّإن ا
ٍ ن َّي ْن َّ كُّلِّ مَّ ز َّي َّي ْن ِ ج َّ مْ سُّ مِان َّه ِ سَّ ن َّه .
english_text:
The Prophet, said: "When I was taken on the Night Journey (Isra'), I passed by
the site of the Mosque of Kufa while I was on al-Buraq, with Archangel Jibril {a.s}
accompanying me.
Archangel Jibril {a.s} said to me, 'O’ Muhammad, descend and pray at this place.'
So, I descended and prayed. Then I asked: 'O’ Archangel Jibril {a.s}, what is this place?'
Archangel Jibril {a.s} said: 'O’ Muhammad, this is Kufa, and this is its mosque. As for me,
I have seen it twenty times in a state of ruin and twenty times in a state of prosperity,
with five hundred years between each state.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 231 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 14, p. 1447

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْأ َّصْ ن َّغ ِ ن ْن ِ ن ُّن َّاي َّه َّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: ن َّي ْن َّا ن َّحْ ن ُّ ذ َّإب ِي َّوْ مٍ جَّ وْ لَّ إ َّمِي زِ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق ِى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذ
َّ إَّلْكُّوق َّه ِ إ ِذ ْ ق َّالَّ «ي َّا إ َّهْلَّ إَّلْكُّوق َّه ِ لَّق َّذْ جَّ ن َّاكُّمُّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ ن ِمَّا لَّمْ ي َّحْ ث ُّ ن ِهِ إ َّجَّ ذإً مِن ْ ق ِ ص ْ لِ مُّصَّ لا َّكُّمْ ن َّي ْث ِ إ ذَّمَّ وَّ ن َّي ْ ث
ِ ن ُّوحٍ وَّ ن َّي ْث ِ إ ِ ذْ رِي سَّ وَّ مُّصَّ ل َّى إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مَّ إَّلْح َّ لِي لِ وَّ مُّصَّ ل َّى إ َّج ِ ى إَّلْح َّ ص ِ زِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ وَّ مُّصَّ لا َّى َّ وَّ إ ِن َّ مَّ سْ ح ذَّكُّمْ هَّذ َّإ
ْلَّأ َّجَّ ذُّ إَّلْأ َّرْن َّعَّه ِ إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ إَّل َّي ِى إِج ْ ي َّارَّهَّا إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ لِأ َّهْلِهَّا وَّ كَّا َّن ِّى ن ِهِ ق َّذ ِ إ ُّي ِى َّ ن ِهِ ي َّوْ مَّ إَّلْق ِي َّامَّ ه ِ ق ِى ي َّوْ ن َّي ْن ِ إ َّن ْي َّص َّ ي ْن
َّ ي َّي َّس َّ ن َّهُّ ن ِالْمُّحْ زِمِ وَّ ي َّس ْ ق َّغُّ لِأ َّهْلِهِ وَّ لِمَّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِي هِ ق َّلاَّ ي ُّزَّذ ُّ س َّ ق َّاعَّي ُّهُّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّذ ْ هَّث ُّ إَّلْأ َّي ُّامُّ وَّ إَّلل َّي َّالِى جَّ ي َّى ي ُّن ْصَّ ث َّ إَّلْحَّ ح َّ ز
َّإَّلْأ َّسْ وَّ ذُّ ق ِي هِ وَّ ل ْي َّا ْي ِي َّن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ر َّمَّ ان ي َّكُّون ُّ مُّصَّ ل َّى إَّلْمَّهْ ذِى ِّ مِن ْ وُّلْذِى وَّ مُّصَّ ل َّى كُّلِّ مُّو ْ مِن ٍ وَّ لأَّ ي َّن ْق َّى عَّلَّى إَّل أ َّرْض ِ مُّو ْ مِن
إ ِلأ َّ كَّان َّ ن ِهِ إ َّوْ جَّ ن َّ ق َّلْن ُّهُّ إ ِلَّي ْ هِ ق َّلاَّ ي َّهْ ح ُّ زُّوةُّ وَّ ي َّق َّز َّن ُّوإ إ ِلَّى إَّلل َّهِ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ ن ِال ْص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِي هِ وَّ إِرْع َّن ُّوإ إ ِلَّي ْ هِ ق ِى ق َّص َّ اءِ جَّ وَّ إن ِح ِ كُّم
ِ ق َّلَّوْ ي َّعْ لَّمُّ إَّلن َّاسُّ مَّ ا ق ِي هِ مِن َّ إَّلْن َّزَّكَّه ِ لَّأ َّي َّوْ ةُّ مِن ْ إ َّق ْطَّ ارِ إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ وَّ لَّوْ جَّ ن ْوإً عَّلَّى إَّلي َّلْح .
english_text:
It has been reported from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata that He said:
One day while we were with Amir al-Mu'minin {a.s} in the Mosque of Kufa, Imam {a.s} said:
"O’ people of Kufa, Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, has blessed you with something
no one else has been blessed with - the virtue of your place of prayer, which was the
house of Adam, the house of Noah, the house of Idris, the place of prayer of Ibrahim
{a.s} the Friend (Khalil), the place of prayer of my brother al-Khidr {a.s}, and my place of
prayer.
This mosque of yours is one of the four mosques chosen by Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic, for its people.
I can see it on the Day of Judgment, coming in two white garments, resembling a
pilgrim in ihram, and it will intercede for its people and for those who pray in it; its
intercession will not be rejected. The days and nights will not pass until the Black
Stone is placed in it. A time will come when it will be the place of prayer for the Mahdi
from my descendants and the place of prayer for every believer. No believer will
remain on the earth without either being there or having their heart yearn toward it.
So, do not abandon it. Seek nearness to Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, by praying
in it, and turn to Him to fulfil your needs in it.
If people knew the blessings it contains, they would come to it from all corners of the
earth, even if they had to crawl on ice."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 231 • Al-Wafi, V. 14, p. 1447 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 5, p.

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ إ َّم َّا مَّ سْ ح ِ ذُّ إَّلس َّ هْ لَّه ِ ق َّق َّذْ ق َّالَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «لَّوِ إِسْ ي َّح َّ ارَّ عَّمِّى ر َّي ْ ذ ن ِهِ لَّأ َّج َّ ارَّة ُّ إَّلل َّهُّ سَّ ن َّه ً ذ َّلِك َّ مَّ وْ ص ِ غ
ن َّي ْث ِ إ ِذْ رِي سَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إَّل َّذ ِى كَّان َّ ي َّح ِ ي ظُّ ق ِي هِ وَّ هُّوَّ إَّلْمَّوْ ص ِ غُّ إَّل َّذ ِى ِ ج َّ زَّح َّ مِن ْهُّ إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْعَّمَّالِق َّه
ِّوَّ هُّوَّ إَّلْمَّوْ ص ِ غُّ إَّل َّذ ِى ج َّ زَّح َّ مِن ْهُّ ذَّإوُّذُّ إ ِلَّى ج َّ الُّوب َّ وَّ ي َّحْ ي َّهُّ صَّ ح ْ زَّة ج َّ ص ْ زَّإءُّ ق ِي هَّا صُّ ورَّة ُّ وَّ ج ْ هِ كُّل
َّن َّن ِى ٍّ ج َّ لَّق َّهُّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ و
ِ ج َّ ل َّ وَّ مِن ْ ي َّحْ ي ِهِ إ ُّج ِ ذ َّب ْ طِ ي ن َّه ُّ كُّلِّ ن َّن ِى ٍّ وَّ هُّوَّ مَّ وْ ص ِ غُّ إَّلز َّإكِث ِ » ق َّق ِي لَّ لَّهُّ وَّ مَّ ا إَّلز َّإكِث ُّ ق َّالَّ « إَّلْح َّ ص ِ زُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم.
. وإ ما مسح ذ ن زإي ا ن ن ع ذإذ ق صلى ق ي ه إ مي ز إلمو من ي ن علي ه إلسلام لما رج غ من ق ي ال إ هل إلن هزوإن
english_text:
As for the Mosque of Al-Sahla, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"If my uncle Zayd had sought refuge in it, Allah {SWT} would have protected him for a year.
This is the location of the house of Idris {a.s}, where he used to sew, and it is the place
from which Ibrahim {a.s} departed to the Amalekites.
It is also the place from which David {a.s} set out to confront Goliath. Beneath it lies a
green stone that contains the image of the face of every prophet created by Allah {SWT},
the Mighty and Majestic. From beneath it, the clay (substance) of every prophet was
taken. It is also the place of the Rider."
He was asked: "And who is the Rider?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Al-Khidr {a.s}."
commentary:
As for the Mosque of Baratha in Baghdad, Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi
Talib {a.s} prayed there when he returned from the battle against the people of
Nahrawan.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 232 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 14, p. 1452

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
- وَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ ج َّ ان ِزِ ن ْن ِ عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ إَّلْأ َّن ْصَّ ارِى ِّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: صَّ ل َّى ن ِن َّا عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ن ِن َّزَّإ ِي َّا ن َّعْ ذَّ رُّج ُّ وعِ هِ مِن ْ ق ِي َّال
إَّلس ُّ زَّإة ِ وَّ ن َّحْ ن ُّ ر ُّهَّاءُّ مِان َّه ِ إ َّلْف ِ رَّج ُّ لٍ ق َّن َّز َّلَّ ن َّصْ زَّإن ِى مِن ْ صَّ وْ مَّ عَّي ِهِ ق َّق َّا ِلَّ مَّ ن ْ عَّمِي ذُّ هَّذ َّإ إَّلْح َّ ي ْس ِ ق َّق ُّلْن َّا هَّذ َّإ ق َّا َّق ْن َّلَّ إ ِلَّي ْ ه
َّ ق َّسَّ ل َّمَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّق َّالَّ ي َّا سَّ ي ِّذِى إ َّن ْث َّ ن َّن ِى ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ سَّ ي ِّذِى ق َّذْ مَّ اب َّ » ق َّالَّ ق َّا َّن ْث َّ وَّ صِ ى ُّ ن » ْن ِى ٍّ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّم
َّ ي ُّم َّ ق َّالَّ لَّهُّ «إِج ْ لِسْ كَّي ْف ُّ سَّ ا َّلْث َّ عَّن ْ هَّذ َّإ» ق َّالَّ إ َّن َّا ن َّن َّي ْث ُّ هَّذ ِةِ إَّلص َّ وْ مَّ عَّه َّ مِن ْ إ َّج ْ لِ هَّذ َّإ إَّلْمَّوْ ص ِ غِ وَّ هُّوَّ ن َّزَّإي َّا وَّ ق َّزَّإ ْب
ِ ق ِى إَّلْكُّي ُّث ِ إَّلْمُّن ْز َّلَّه ِ إ َّن َّهُّ لأَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى هَّذ َّإ إَّلْمَّوْ ص ِ غِ ن ِهَّذ َّإ إَّلْح َّ مْ غِ إ ِلأ َّ ن َّن ِى إ َّوْ وَّ صِ ى ُّ ن َّن َّى ٍّ و َّ ق َّذْ ج ِ ن ْث ُّ إ ُّسْ لِمُّ ق َّا َّسْ لَّمَّ وَّ ج َّ زَّح
َّ مَّ عَّن َّا إ ِلَّى إَّلْكُّوق َّه ِ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهُّ عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «ق َّمَّن ْ صَّ ل َّى هَّاهُّن َّا» ق َّالَّ صَّ ل َّى عِ ي سَّ ى إِن ْن ُّ مَّ زْ ي ُّمَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ وَّ إ ُّم ُّه
ِ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهُّ عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «إ َّ ق َّا ُّج ْ ن ُّزُّك َّ مَّ ن ْ صَّ ل َّى هَّاهُّن َّا» ق َّالَّ ن َّعَّمْ ق َّالَّ « إَّلْح َّ لِي لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم.
english_text:
It was narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari that He said:
"Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} led us in prayer at Baratha after returning from the battle
with the Khawarij, and we were about one hundred thousand men.
A Christian descended from his monastery and asked: "Who is the leader of this
army?"
We said: "This man (referring to Imam Ali {a.s})."
He approached him, greeted him, and said: "O’ my master, are you a prophet?"
Imam Ali {a.s} replied: "No, the Prophet, my master, has passed away."
The man asked: "Then you are the successor of a prophet?"
Imam Ali {a.s} said: "Yes."
Imam Ali {a.s} then asked him, "Sit down; why do you ask this?"
The man replied: "I built this monastery because of this place, which is Baratha, and I
have read in the revealed books that no one will pray here with such a large gathering
except for a prophet or the successor of a prophet. So, I have come to accept Islam."
He then embraced Islam and accompanied us to Kufa.
Imam Ali {a.s} asked him, "Who else has prayed here?"
The man replied: "Jesus, the son of Mary {a.s}, and his mother."
Ali said to him, "Shall I inform you of who else has prayed here?"
The man said: "Yes."
Imam Ali {a.s} said: "Ibrahim {a.s}."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 232 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 287 • Madīnat Maʿājiz al-Aʾimma ʿAlayhim al-Salām, Part 1, p. 491

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«مَّ ن ْ ي َّن َّح َّ مَّ ق ِى إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ ي ُّم َّ رَّذ َّهَّا ق ِى ج َّ وْ ق ِهِ لَّمْ ي َّمُّز َّ ن ِذَّإءٍ إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْزَّإ َّي ْه.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever clears his throat in the mosque and then swallows it back, no disease will
pass through them without it curing them."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 233 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 18 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 256 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 442 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 500 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 223 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 13

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
َّ «مَّ ن ْ كَّن َّسَّ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذَّ ي َّوْ مَّ إَّلْح َّ مِي سِ وَّ لَّي ْلَّه َّ إَّلْح ُّ مُّعَّه ِ ق َّا َّج ْ زَّح َّ مِن ْهُّ مِن
ُّإَّلي ُّزَّإب ِ مَّ ا ي ُّذ َّر ُّ ق ِى إَّلْعَّي ْن ِ ع َّق َّزَّ إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّعَّالَّى لَّه.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"Whoever sweeps the mosque on Thursday and the night of Jumu’ah (Thursday night)
and removes from it even the dust that could irritate the eye, Allah {SWT}, the Exalted,
will forgive them."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 233 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 254 • Rawdat al- Wa’izin, Vol. 2, p. 336 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 509 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 238 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p.

arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«مَّ ن ْ مَّ س َّ ى إ ِلَّى إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ لَّمْ ي َّص َّ غْ رِج ْ لَّي ْ هِ عَّلَّى رَّطْ ث ٍ وَّ لأَّ ي َّان ِسٍ إ ِلأ َّ ي ُّسَّ ن ِّحُّ لَّه
ِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْأ َّرَّص ِ ي ن َّ إَّلس َّ ان ِعَّه .
.وق ذ إ ج زج ث هذ ة إلأ ج ن ار مسن ذة وما روي ث ق ى معن اها ق ى كي اب ق ص ل إلمساج ذ وجزمي ها وما ج اء ق ي ها
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever walks to the mosque, every step they take - whether it falls upon something
moist or dry - glorifies Allah {SWT} for them down to the seventh earth”.
commentary:
These reports have been narrated with their chain of transmission, and what has been
narrated in their meaning can be found in the book of the virtues and sanctity of the
mosques and what has been mentioned therein.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال عَّلِى ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«صَّ لاَّة ق ِى ن َّي ْث ِ إَّلْمَّق ْذِسِ ي َّعْ ذِلُّ إ َّلْف َّ صَّ لاَّة ٍ وَّ صَّ لاَّة ق ِى إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ إَّلْأ َّعْ ط َّ مِ ي َّعْ ذِل
َّمِان َّه َّ إ َّلْف ِ صَّ لاَّة ٍ وَّ صَّ لاَّة ق ِى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذِ إَّلْق َّن ِي لَّه ِ ي َّعْ ذِلُّ ج َّ مْ ساً وَّ عِ س ْ زِي ن َّ صَّ لاَّة ً وَّ صَّ لاَّة ق ِى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذِ إ َّ لس ُّ وق ِ ، ي َّعْ ذِلُّ إِي ْن ْ ي َّى
ً عَّس ْ زَّة َّ صَّ لاَّة ً وَّ صَّ لاَّة ُّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ق ِى ن َّي ْي ِهِ ي َّعْ ذِلُّ صَّ لاَّة ً وَّ إجِ ذَّة .
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said :
"A prayer in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) is equivalent to one thousand prayers. A prayer
in the Great Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) is equivalent to one hundred thousand prayers.
A prayer in the Mosque of the Tribe (Masjid al-Qabilah) is equivalent to twenty-five
prayers. A prayer in the market mosque is equivalent to twelve prayers. A man's prayer
in his home is equivalent to one prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 233 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 30 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 253 • Al-Wa'ezin School, Vol. 2, p. 338 • Jami’ al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 70 • Falah Al-Sael, Part 1, p. 91 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 513 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 289 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 15 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 9, p. 270

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ «مَّ ن ْ ن َّن َّى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذإً كَّمَّق ْ حَّ ضِ ق َّطَّ اة ٍ ن َّن َّى إَّلل َّهُّ لَّهُّ ن َّي ْي اً ق ِى إَّلْح َّ ن َّه.
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said: "Whoever builds a mosque as small
as a sandgrouse’s nest, Allah {SWT} will build for them a house in Paradise."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 235 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 2, p. 30 • Al-Masbah (Lalkafami) Vol. 1, p. 13 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 4 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 3, p. 366

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
english_text:
Abu Ubaidah Al-Hadha’ said: "Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} passed
by me while I was between Makkah and Madinah placing stones. I asked: 'Is this from
that?'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Yes.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عُّن َّي ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ عَّلِى ٍّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ إَّلْمُّط َّ ل َّلَّه ِ ي ُّكْزَّةُّ إَّلْق ِي َّامُّ ق ِي هَّا ق َّال
«ن َّعَّمْ وَّ لَّكِن ْ لأَّ ي َّص ُّ ز ُّكُّمُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ ق ِي هَّا.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ً«إ َّو َّلُّ مَّ ا ي َّن ْذَّإ ُّ ن ِهِ ق َّان ِمُّن َّا سُّ ق ُّوف ُّ إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ ق َّي ُّكَّسِّ زُّهَّا وَّ ي َّا ْمُّ زُّ ن ِهَّا ق َّي ُّح ْ عَّلُّ عَّزِي س ا
كَّعَّزِي س ِ مُّوسَّ ى .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"The first thing our Qa'im (the awaited savior Imam Muhammad ibn Hassan Al-Mahdi
{a.s} ) will do is to break the roofs of the mosques and order them to be made as an open
canopy (like the canopy of Musa {a.s})”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 236 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 491 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 207 • Ithbāt al-Hudāt, Part 5, p. 65

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text: َّوَّ كَّان َّ عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِذ َّإ رَّإ َّى إَّلْمَّحَّ ارِي ث َّ ق ِى إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ كَّس َّ زَّهَّا و ِي َّق ُّولُّ «كَّا َّن َّهَّا مَّ ذ َّإن ِحُّ إَّلْي َّهُّوذ .
english_text:
When Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} saw the niches (mihrabs) in mosques, he would
break them and say,
"It is as if they are the altars of the Jews."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text: ُّ وَّ رَّإ َّى عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ مَّ سْ ح ِ ذإً ن ِالْكُّوق َّه ِ ق َّذْ س ُّ زِّف َّ ق َّالَّ «كَّا َّن َّهُّ ن ِي عَّه إ ِن َّ إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذَّ لأَّ ي ًس َّ ز َّف ُّ ي ُّن ْن َّى ج ُّ م ا .
english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} saw a mosque in Kufa that had been decorated or
elevated and said:
"It is as if it is a church. Mosques are not to be adorned; they should be built plain
(simple)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 236 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 320 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 253 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 493 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 215 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 352

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إ َّن ُّو إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلْأ َّو َّ لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِعَّن ِ إَّلطِّ ي ن ِ ق ِي هِ إَّلي ِّن ْن ُّ ي ُّطَّ ي َّن ُّ ن ِهِ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذُّ إ َّوِ إَّلْن َّي ْث ُّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي ُّصَّ ل َّى ق ِي ه
َّق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal, Imam Musa Al-Kadhim {a.s}, was asked about using
clay mixed with straw to plaster the mosque or the house where prayers are offered.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
english_text:
Imam {a.s} was asked about using plaster that had been prepared with dung for
plastering a mosque. Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّو َّسُّ ن ِلَّ: عَّن ْ ن َّي ْث ٍ ق َّذْ كَّان َّ جَّ س اً ر َّمَّ ان اً هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّح ْ عَّلَّ مَّ سْ ح ِ ذإً ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ن ُّط ِّ ف َّ وَّ إ ُّصْ لِحَّ ق َّلا
َّن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} was asked about
a house that had been used as a latrine for a period of time and whether it would be
suitable to make it into a mosque.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it is cleaned and repaired, then there is no harm."
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 229 • Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 289 • Man La Yahduruhu Al- Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 236 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 211 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 358

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عُّن َّي ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ عَّلِى ٍّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ْ ق ِى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذٍ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى إَّلذ َّإرِ ق َّي َّن ْذُّو لِأ َّهْلِهِ إ َّن
ْي َّي َّوَّ س َّ عُّوإ ن ِطَّ ان ِق َّه ٍ مِن ْهُّ إ َّوْ ي ُّحَّ وِّ لُّوةُّ عَّن ْ مَّ كَّان ِهِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِذ َّلِك َّ » ق َّالَّ ق َّق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّي َّصْ لُّحُّ إَّل ًمَّكَّان ُّ إَّل َّذ ِى كَّان َّ جَّ س اً ر َّمَّ ان ا
َّإ َّن ْ ي ُّن َّط َّ ف َّ وَّ ي ُّي َّح َّ ذ َّ م ُّسْ ح ِ ذإً، ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ إ ِذ َّإ إ ُّلْق ِى َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ مِن َّ إَّلي ُّزَّإب ِ مَّ ا ي ُّوَّ إرِي هِ ق َّا ِن َّ ذ َّلِك َّ ي ُّن َّط ِّ ق ُّهُّ وَّ ي ُّطَّ هِّ زُّة .
english_text:
Ubaidullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi asked Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a mosque within a
house, where the owners might wish to expand part of it or move it from its original
location. Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
Ubaydullah then asked: "Would it be suitable for a place that was previously used as
a latrine for a period of time to be cleaned and made into a mosque?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if soil is placed over it to cover it, as this cleanses and purifies it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
- وَّ كَّان َّ إ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّق ُّولُّ: «مَّ ن ِ إِج ْ ي َّلَّف َّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ إ َّصَّ اب َّ إ ِجْ ذَّى إَّلي َّمَّا ن ِ إ َّج اً مُّ سْ ي َّق َّاذإً ق ِى
ًإَّلل َّهِ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ إ َّوْ عِ لْما ُّمُّسْ ي َّطْ زَّق اً إ َّوْ إ ي َّه ً مُّحْ كَّمَّه ً إ َّوْ رَّجْ مَّه ً مُّن ْي َّط َّ زَّة ً إ َّوْ كَّلِمَّه ً ي َّزُّذ ُّةُّ عَّن ْ رَّذًى إ َّوْ ي َّسْ مَّغُّ كَّلِمَّه ً ي َّذ ل ُّهُّ عَّلَّى
ًهُّذًى إ َّوْ ي َّي ْزُّك ُّ ذ َّن ْن اً ج َّ س ْ ي َّه ً إ َّوْ جَّ ي َّاء .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} used to say:
"Whoever frequently visits the mosques will attain one of eight benefits: a brother
(friend) beneficial in the cause of Allah {SWT}, newly acquired knowledge, a definitive
verse (of guidance), a mercy awaited, a word that turns him away from misguidance,
hearing a word that leads him to guidance, abandoning a sin out of fear (of Allah {SWT})
or out of shame”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 237 • Thawāb al-Aʿmāl wa ʿIqāb al-Aʿmāl, Part 1, p. 27 • Al-Khisal, Part 2, p. 409 • Al-Amali (by Al-Saduq) Vol. 1, p. 389 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 248 • Amali (by Al-Tusi) Vol. 1, p. 432 • Al-Wa'ezin School, Vol. 2, p. 338 • Falah Al-Sael, Part 1, p. 90 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 1, p. 407 • Al-Masbah (Lalkafami) Vol. 1, p. 13

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سَّ مِغَّ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ رَّج ُّ لاً ي ُّن ْس ِ ذُّ ص َّ ال َّه ً ق ِى إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ ق َّق َّالَّ «ق ُّولُّوإ لَّهُّ لأ َّ رَّذ َّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ ص َّ ال َّي َّك
ْ ق َّا ِن َّهَّا لِع َّي ْ زِ هَّذ َّإ ن ُّن ِي َّث .
english_text:
The Prophet {saws}, heard a man searching for a lost item in the mosque and
said:
"Say to him, 'May Allah {SWT} not return your lost item to you,' for the mosque was not
built for this purpose."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 237 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 235 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 362

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «ج َّ ن ِّن ُّوإ مَّ سَّ اج ِ ذَّكُّمْ صِ ن ْي َّان َّكُّمْ وَّ مَّ ح َّ ان ِي ن َّكُّمْ وَّ رَّق ْغَّ إ َّصْ وَّ إي ِكُّمْ و َّ س ِ زَّإءَّكُّمْ وَّ ن َّي ْعَّكُّمْ وَّ إَّلص َّ ال َّه
َّوَّ إَّلْحُّ ذُّوذَّ وَّ إَّلْأ َّجْ كَّام .
. وي ن ن ع ى إ ن ي ح ن ث إلمساج ذ إ ن س اذ إلس عز ق ي ها وج لوس إلمعلم للي ا ذي ث ق ي ها، وج لوس إلح ي اط ق ي ها للح ي اطه
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said: "Keep your children, the insane, raising of voices, buying and
selling, seeking lost items, and administering legal punishments and rulings away
from your mosques”.
commentary:
It is also recommended to avoid reciting poetry, having teachers sit for disciplining,
and tailors sitting for sewing in the mosques.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 237 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 234

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه :
َّ«مَّ ن ْ إ َّسْ زَّح َّ ق ِى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذٍ مِن ْ مَّ سَّ اج ِ ذِ إَّلل َّهِ سِ زَّإج اً لَّمْ ي َّز َّلِ إَّلْمَّلاَّن ِكَّه ُّ و
ِ جَّ مَّلَّه ُّ إَّلْعَّزْس ِ ي َّسْ ي َّع ْ ق ِزُّون َّ لَّهُّ مَّ ا ذَّإمَّ ق ِى ذ َّلِك َّ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ ص َّ وْ ء مِن َّ إَّلسِّ زَّإح.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"Whoever lights a lamp in one of the mosques of Allah {SWT}, the angels and the bearers
of the Throne will continue to seek forgiveness for them as long as there remains any
light from that lamp in the mosque."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 237 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 29 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 261 • Jami’ al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 71 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 1, p. 351 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 509 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 241 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 15

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ٍ«إ ِذ َّإ إ َّج ْ زَّح َّ إ َّجَّ ذُّكُّمُّ إَّلْحَّ صَّ اة َّ مِن َّ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ ق َّلْي َّزُّذ َّهَّا ق ِى مَّ كَّان ِهَّا إ َّوْ ق ِى مَّ سْ ح ِ ذ
ُّإ ج َّ زَّ ق َّا ِن َّهَّا ي ُّسَّ ن ِّح .
ولأ ي ح ور للحان ض وإلح ن ث إ ن ي ذج لا إلمسح ذ إ لأ مح ي ار ي ن .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"If any of you takes a pebble from the mosque, let them return it to its place or to
another mosque, for it glorifies Allah {SWT}”.
commentary:
Additionally, it is not permissible for a menstruating woman or someone in a state of
major ritual impurity (janabah) to enter the mosque, except by passing through.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 237 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 320 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 256 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 503 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 232 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 7

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ «ج َّ ي ْ زُّ مَّ سَّ اج ِ ذِ ن ِسَّ ان ِكُّمُّ إَّلْن ُّي ُّوب .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The best mosques for your women are their homes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 238 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 252 • Al-Wa'ezin School, Vol. 2, p. 338 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 514 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 237 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 237 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 371

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text: ِوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ: عَّن ِ إَّلْوُّق ُّوف ِ عَّلَّى إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي َّح ُّ ور ُّ ق َّا ِن َّ إَّلْمَّح ُّ وسَّ إ َّوْ ق َّق ُّوإ عَّلَّى ن ُّي ُّوب ِ إَّلن َّار .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} was asked about endowing property to mosques, and He said:
"It is not permissible, for the Magians endowed property for their fire temples”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّ ق ِى إَّلي َّوْ رَّإة ِ مَّ كْي ُّون اً إ َّن َّ ن ُّي ُّوي ِى ق ِى إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذُّ ق َّطُّ ون َّى لِعَّن ْذٍ ي َّطَّ ه َّزَّ ق ِى ن َّ ي ْي ِهِ ي ُّم ر َّإرَّن ِى ق ِى
ِ ن َّي ْي ِى إ َّلأَّ إ ِن َّ عَّلَّى إَّلْمَّز ُّورِ كَّزَّإمَّ ه َّ إَّلز َّإن ِزِ إ َّلأَّ ن َّس ِّ زِ إَّلْمَّس َّ اءِ ي ن َّ ق ِى إَّلط ُّ لُّمَّاب ِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْمَّسَّ اج ِ ذِ ن ِالن ُّورِ إَّلس َّ اطِ غِ ي َّوْ مَّ إَّلْق ِي َّامَّ ه .
english_text:
It is narrated "In the Torah, it is written that 'My houses on earth are the
mosques. Glad tidings to the servant who purifies themselves in their home and then
visits Me in My house. Surely, it is incumbent upon the host to honor their guest. Give
glad tidings to those who walk in the darkness to the mosques of a radiant light on the
Day of Judgment.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 239 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 26 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 512 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 244 • Kulliyat Hadith Qudsi, Vol. 1, p. 126 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 373 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Part 1, p. 298

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّ إَّلْن ُّي ُّوب َّ إَّل َّي ِى ي ُّصَّ ل َّى ق ِي هَّا ن ِالل َّي ْ لِ ي ُّص ِ ى ءُّ ن ُّورُّهَّا لِأ َّهْلِ إَّلس َّ مَّاءِ كَّمَّا ي ُّص ِ ى ءُّ ن ُّور ِإَّلْكَّوَّ إكِث ِ لِأ َّهْل
ِ إَّلْأ َّرْض .
english_text:
It is narrated: "The houses in which prayers are offered at night shine with light
for the inhabitants of the heavens just as the stars shine with light for the inhabitants
of the earth."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE VIRTUE OF MOSQUES, THEIR SANCTITY AND THE REWARD FOR THOSE WHO PRAY IN THEM
english_text:
It is narrated that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}, passed by a tall minaret and
ordered it to be demolished.
He then said: "The minaret should not be raised higher than the roof of the mosque”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 239 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 256 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 494 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 230

english_text:
"And indeed, Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, intends to bring punishment
upon all the people of the earth without exception. But when He looks at the elderly,
who move their feet to the prayers and the children learning the Qur'an, He has mercy
on them and withholds that punishment”.
commentary:
One who wishes to enter the mosque should do so with calmness and dignity, for
mosques are the houses of Allah {SWT} and the most beloved places to Him. The people
most beloved to Allah {SWT}, the Almighty, are those who enter first and leave last.
When entering the mosque, one should step in with the right foot before the left and say;
"In the name of Allah {SWT}, and by Allah {SWT}, peace be upon you, O’ Prophet, and the
mercy and blessings of Allah {SWT}. O’ Allah {SWT}, bless Muhammad and the family of
Muhammad. Open for us the doors of Your mercy, and make us among those who
maintain Your mosques. Exalted is Your praise, O’ Lord {AZJ}."
When leaving, one should step out with the left foot before the right and say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and open for us the
door of Your mercy”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 239 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 512 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 198

ً«إ ُّعْ طِ ي ث ُّ ج َّ مْ ساً لَّمْ ي ُّعْ طَّ هَّا إ َّجَّ ذ ق َّن ْلِى ج ُّ عِلَّث ْ لِى َّ إَّلْأ َّرْ ض ُّ مَّ سْ ح ِ ذإً وَّ طَّ هُّورإ

english_text:
The Prophet, said:
"I was given five things that no one was given before me: The entire earth was made a
place of prayer and a means of purification for me, I was aided with fear (cast into the
hearts of my enemies), war booty was made lawful for me, I was given concise speech
(Jawaami' al-Kalim), and I was granted intercession."
commentary:
It is permissible to pray on the entire earth except in places specifically designated as
prohibited for prayer.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 240 • Al-Khisal, Part 1, p. 292 • Al-Amali (by Al-Saduq) Vol. 1, p. 216 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 573 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 350 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 117 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 8, p. 38 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 16, p. 313 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 16, p. 323 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 276

ُّ «عَّس َّ زَّة ُّ مَّ وَّ إص ِ غَّ لأَّ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى ق ِي هَّا إَّلطِّ ي ن ُّ وَّ إَّلْمَّاءُّ وَّ إَّلْحَّ م َّامُّ وَّ إَّلْق ُّن ُّورُّ وَّ مَّ سَّ ان
ُّ إَّلط َّ زِي ق ِ وَّ ق ُّزَّى إَّلن َّمْ لِ وَّ مَّ عَّاطِ ن ُّ إَّلْأ ِن ِلِ وَّ مَّ ح ْ زَّى إَّلْمَّاءِ، وَّ إَّلس َّ ن َّح َّ ه ُّ وَّ إَّلي َّلْح .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"There are ten places where prayer should not be performed: mud, water, baths,
graves, paths frequently used by travelers, ant hills, camel resting places,
watercourses, salty land (sabkha), and snow”.
references: Al Mahasin, Part 1, p. 13 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 366 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 390 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 241 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 394 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 445 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 305

ق ا ذ إ جصل إلزج ل ق ى إلطي ن إ و إلماء وق ذ ذج ل وق ث إلصلاة ولم ي مكن ه إلح زوح من ه صلى إ ي ماء وي كون سح وذة إ ج ق ض من
ركوعه ولأ ن ا س ن الصلاة ق ى مسلح إلحمام وإ ن ما. ي كزة ق ى إلحمام لأ ن ه ما وى إلس ي اطي ن
english_text:
It is narrated that prayer should not be performed in al-Bayda', Dhat al-Salasil,
the valley of al-Shaqra, or the valley of Dajnan.
commentary:
If a person finds themselves in mud or water and the time for prayer has entered, and
they are unable to leave, they should pray by making gestures, ensuring that their
prostration is lower than their bowing. There is no harm in praying in a bathhouse
changing area, but it is disliked to pray in the main bath area because it is a dwelling
place for devils.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 242 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 469 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p.

ق ا ما على
إلط وإهز إلي ى ن ي ن إلح وإذ ق لا ن ا س.
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about
praying in the bathhouse.
Imam {a.s} said: "If the place is clean, then there is no harm in praying” (referring
specifically to the changing area (maslakh)).”
commentary:
As for graves, it is not permissible to use them as a direction of prayer or to turn them
into mosques. However, there is no harm in praying between graves, as long as none
of them are taken as a direction of prayer. It is recommended that there be a distance
of ten cubits between the person praying and the graves on all sides.
Regarding paths, it is not permissible to pray in the main pathways or on roads, but
there is no harm in praying on areas adjacent to the roads.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} said:
"Any path that is trodden and commonly used, whether it has a main road or not,
should not be used for prayer."
He was asked: "Then where should one pray?"
Imam {a.s} said: "To the right or to the left (of the path)."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 389 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 243 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 220 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 448 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 147

english_text:
And Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about praying in
sheep pens, and Imam {a.s} said:
"Pray there, but do not pray in camel enclosures unless you fear for the safety of your
belongings; in that case, sweep it and sprinkle it with water, then pray there."
He also said: "Prayer in a salty land (sabkha) is disliked unless it is a soft, level place
where the forehead can rest properly."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

ا لَّمْ ي َّزُّس َّ إَّلْمَّكَّا ن َّ إَّل َّذ ِى
ي َّزَّى إ َّن َّهُّ ن َّط ِ ي ف .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about praying in the houses
of the Magians (Zoroastrians) if they are sprinkled with water, and He said:
"There is no harm in it."
He then mentioned that he sometimes saw someone on the road to Makkah sprinkling
water on the spot where they placed their forehead before prostrating, while at other
times, they did not sprinkle water if they deemed the place to be clean.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:

«۝
ًق ُّلْ كُّل ي َّعْ مَّلُّ عَّلىٰ س ٰ اكِلَّي ِهِ ق َّزَّن ُّكُّمْ إ َّعْ لَّمُّ ن ِمَّن ْ هُّوَّ إ َّهْذىٰ سَّ ن ِي لا
۝»
ْصَّ لِّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ وَّ ذَّعْ هُّم .
english_text:
Saleh ibn Al-Hakam reported that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was
asked about praying in synagogues and churches. Imam {a.s} said: "Pray in them."
Salih then asked: "Even if they (non-Muslims) are praying there?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes. Do you not recite the Qur'an: 'Say, each acts according to their
manner, but your Lord {AZJ} knows best who is rightly guided' (Surah Al-Isra, 17:84)?
Pray facing the Qibla and leave them (to their practices)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلْن َّوْ لِ ي َّكُّون ُّ عَّلَّى إَّلس َّ طْ حِ إ َّوْ ق ِى إَّلْمَّكَّان ِ إَّل َّذ ِى ي ُّصَّ ل َّى ق ِي هِ ق َّق َّال
«إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ ق َّق َّي ْهُّ إَّلس َّ مْ سُّ ق َّصَّ لِّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّهُّوَّ طَّ اهِز.
english_text:
Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about urine that is present
on a rooftop or in a place where one prays.
Imam {a.s} said: "If the sun dries it, then you may pray on it, for it is purified”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 244 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 59

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّامِزُّ ن ْن ُّ ن ُّعَّي ْمٍ إَّلْق ُّمِّى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلْمَّن َّار ِلِ إَّل َّي ِى ي َّن ْز ِلُّهَّا إَّلن َّاسُّ ق ِي هَّا إ َّن ْوَّ إلُّ إَّلذ َّوَّ إب ِّ و
َّ إَّلسِّ زْج ِ ي ن ُّ وَّ ي َّذْ ج ُّ لُّهَّا إَّلْي َّهُّوذُّ وَّ إَّلن َّصَّ ارَّى كَّي ْف َّ ن َّصْ ن َّغُّ ن ِالص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِي هَّا ق َّق َّالَّ «صَّ لِّ عَّلَّى ي َّوْ ن ِك .
english_text:
Amir ibn Nuaym al-Qummi asked Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} about places where
people stay that contain the urine of animals, manure, and are frequented by Jews and
Christians.
He asked: "What should we do about praying in such places?"
Abu 'Abdillah replied: "Pray on your garment."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ مَّ هْ ز ِي َّارَّ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلي َّالِث َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّصِ ي زُّ ق ِى إَّلْن َّي ْذَّإءِ ق َّي ُّذْ رِكُّهُّ صَّ لاَّة ق َّزِي ص َّ ه
َّ ق َّلاَّ ي َّح ْ زُّح ُّ مِن َّ إَّلْن َّي ْذَّإءِ جَّ ي َّى ي َّح ْ زُّح َّ وَّ ق ْي ُّهَّا كَّي ْف َّ ي َّصْ ن َّغُّ ن ِالص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ ق َّذْ ن ُّهِى َّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ ن ِالْن َّي ْ ذَّإءِ ق َّق َّالَّ «ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِي هَّا و
َّ ي َّي َّح َّ ن َّث ُّ ق َّارِعَّه ِ إَّلط َّ زِي ق .
english_text:
Ali ibn Mahziyar asked Abu Al-Hasan the Third, Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-
Hadi {a.s}, about a man who finds himself in the desert (al-Bayda') when the time for an
obligatory prayer comes and does not leave the desert until the prayer's time has
passed.
He asked: "What should he do about the prayer, given that it is prohibited to pray in al-
Bayda'?"
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray there, but he should avoid the main path (road)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 244 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 156

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
english_text:
It was narrated from Imam {a.s} said, by Ayyub ibn Nuh that He said:
"One should move away from the main roads to the right or to the left and pray."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 244 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 156

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلْن َّي ْث ِ وَّ إَّلذ َّإرِ لأَّ ي ُّصِ ي ن ُّهُّمَّا إَّلس َّ مْ سُّ و
َّي ُّصِ ي ن ُّهُّمَّا إَّلْن َّوْ لُّ وَّ ي ُّع ْ ي َّسَّ لُّ ق ِي هِمَّا مِن َّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّان َّه ِ إ َّ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى ق ِي هِمَّا إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ ق َّا ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ » ق َّالَّ وَّ س ِا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْق ُّن ُّور
هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ل ِأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a
house or room that does not receive sunlight and in which urine might be present and
where one bathes after major ritual impurity (janabah). He asked if it is permissible to
pray there once it has dried?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
Ali ibn Ja'far also asked about praying between graves?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّم َّارُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّوسَّ ى إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْن َّارِي َّه ِ ي ُّن َّل ُّ ق َّصَّ ن ُّهَّا ن ِمَّاءٍ ق َّذ ِرٍ هَّلْ ي َّح ُّ ور
إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ج ُّ ق ِّق َّث ْ ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِالص َّ لاَّة ِ عَّلَّي ْهَّا .
english_text:
Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
about a mat made of reeds that had been wetted with impure water, and whether it is
permissible to pray on it.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it has dried, then there is no harm in praying on it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّإ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلس َّ اذ َّكُّون َّه ِ ي َّكُّون ُّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إَّلْح َّ ن َّان َّه ُّ إ َّ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى عَّلَّي ْهَّا ق ِى إَّلْمَّحْ مِلِ ق َّق َّال
«لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِالص َّ لاَّة ِ عَّلَّي ْهَّا .
english_text:
Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a cushion
(shadhakunah) that may have come into contact with major ritual impurity (janabah)
and whether it is permissible to pray on it while it is in a carriage (mahmil).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in praying on it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There is no harm in praying on any images (representations) if you place them
beneath you."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 245 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 363 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 464 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 439 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 171

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ لَّي ْث إَّلْمُّزَّإذِى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّه ُّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ْعَّن ِ إَّلْوَّ سَّ ان ِذِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى إَّلْن َّي ْث ِ ق ِي هَّا إَّلي َّمَّاي ِي لُّ عَّن ْ ي َّمِي ن ٍ إ َّو
َّ عَّن ْ س ِ مَّالٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِهِ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّكُّن ْ ي ُّح َّ اةَّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ س َّ ى ْ ء مِن ْهَّا ن َّي ْ ن َّ ي َّذَّ ي ْك َّ مِم ِّا ي َّلِى إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه َّ ق َّع َّطِّ هِ وَّ صَّ ل .
english_text:
Laith al-Muradi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about cushions
in the house that have images on them, whether they are to the right or to the left.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it as long as they are not facing the Qibla. If any of
them are in front of you, facing the Qibla, then cover them and pray."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
وَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ: عَّن ِ إَّلي َّمَّاي ِي لِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى إَّلْن ِسَّ اطِ لَّهَّا عَّي ْن َّان ِ وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لَّهَّا عَّي ْن وَّ إجِ ذَّة ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ و
َّإ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لَّهَّا عَّي ْن َّان ِ وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّلا.
english_text:
He, Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, was asked about images on a
carpet that have two eyes while you are praying.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it has one eye, then there is no harm, but if it has two eyes and you
are praying, then it is not permissible."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 245 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 363 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 438 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 245

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال ْ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِالص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ ي َّن ْط ُّ زُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلي َّصَّ اوِي زِ إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّث ٍ ن ِعَّي ْن ٍ وَّ إجِ ذَّة .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"There is no harm in praying while looking at images if they have only one eye."
references: Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 620 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 246 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 465 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 172 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 173 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 76, p. 288 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 293

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ«لأَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّ ق ِى ذَّإرٍ ق ِي هَّا كَّلْث إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّكُّون َّ كَّلْث َّ صَّ ي ْ ذٍ وَّ إ َّع ْ لَّق ْث َّ ذُّون َّهُّ ن َّان اً ق َّلا
ن َّا ْسَّ وَّ إ ِن َّ إَّلْمَّلاَّن ِكَّه َّ لأَّ ي َّذْ ج ُّ لُّ ن َّي ْي اً ق ِي هِ كَّلْث وَّ لأَّ ن َّي ْي اً ق ِي هِ ي َّمَّاي ِي لُّ وَّ لأَّ ن َّي ْي اً ق ِي هِ ن َّوْ ل
ٍ مَّ ح ْ مُّوع ق ِى إ ن ِي َّه.
. ولأ ي ح ور إلصلاة ق ى ن ي ث ق ي ه ج مز محصورة ق ى إ ن ي ه
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Do not pray in a house where there is a dog, except if it is a hunting dog and you have
closed a door between you and it, then there is no harm. Indeed, the angels do not
enter a house where there is a dog, nor a house with images, nor a house with urine
collected in a container."
commentary:
Additionally, it is not permissible to pray in a house where there is wine stored in
containers.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 246 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 459 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 175 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 62, p. 53

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي زٍ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّال-
ً«مَّ ن ْ كَّان َّ ق ِى مَّ وْ ص ِ غٍ لأَّ ي َّق ْذِرُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ ق َّلْي ُّومِ إ ِي مَّاء
ٍ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ق ِى إ َّرْض ٍ مُّن ْق َّطِ عَّه .
english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"Whoever is in a place where they cannot reach the ground should make gestures (for
prayer), even if they are in a remote area”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 246 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 441

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ سَّ مَّاعَّه ُّ ن ْن ُّ مِهْ زَّإن:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلْأ َّسِ ي زِ ي َّا ْسِ زُّةُّ إَّلْمُّس ْ زِكُّون َّ ق َّي َّحْ ص ُّ زُّةُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ ق َّي َّمْ ن َّعُّهُّ إَّل َّذ ِى إ َّسَّ زَّةُّ مِن ْهَّا ق َّق َّال
ً«ي ُّومِى ُّ إ ِي مَّاء .
english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Him about a captive taken by the polytheists who is
prevented from performing prayer by his captor.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should make gestures (for prayer)."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 411 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 457 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 246 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 175 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 299 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1071 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 448

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ مُّ عَّاوِي َّه ُّ ن ْن ُّ وَّ هْث ٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم :
عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ وَّ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ ي ُّصَّ لِّي َّان ِ ق ِى ن َّي ْث ٍ وَّ إجِ ذٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ
َّكَّان َّ ن َّي ْن َّهُّمَّا ق َّذْ رُّ س ِ ن ْزٍ صَّ ل َّث ْ ن ِحِ ذ َّإةُّ وَّ جْ ذَّهَّا وَّ هُّوَّ وَّ جْ ذَّةُّ لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Muawiya ibn Wahb asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
and a woman praying in the same room.
Imam {a.s} said: "If there is a space of about a handspan (shibr) between them, She may
pray beside him alone and he alone; there is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 247 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 125

Chapter Title: PLACES WHERE PRAYER IS PERMISSABLE AND WHERE IT IS NOT
arabic_text:

english_text:
In the narration of Zurarah from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}, said:
"If there is a distance between her and him that is about the length of a step or about
the length of a cubit or more, then there is no harm if She prays beside him alone."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Jamil narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} in which He said:
"There is no harm if a woman prays beside a man while he is praying. Indeed, The
Prophet {saws} would pray while Aisha was lying down in front of him, even though She
was menstruating. When he wanted to prostrate, he would touch her legs, and She
would move them so that he could prostrate."
commentary:
There is also no harm if there is a small object, such as an armrest or something
similar, in front of a man and woman while they are praying.

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}
that he asked him about wearing the skin of a dead animal (carrion) during prayer if it
has been tanned.
Imam {a.s} said: "No, even if it has been tanned seventy times."

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about the verse in which
Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Musa {a.s}:
"Remove your sandals, for you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa" (Surah Taha 20:12).
Imam {a.s} said: "They were made from the skin of a dead donkey."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 248 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 417 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 343 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 3, p. 374

english_text:
Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} and Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} were asked:
"We buy clothes that may have come into contact with wine or the fat of a pig during
their tailoring. Should we pray in them before washing them?"
They replied: "Yes, there is no harm. Allah {SWT} has only forbidden eating and drinking
it (pork and wine) but has not forbidden wearing it, touching it, or praying in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 248 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 220 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p.

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who
has only one garment, and it has urine on it, but he is unable to wash it.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
He was asked by Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah about a man who becomes
ritually impure (junub) in a garment and has no other garment and is unable to wash it.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 248 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 224 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 169 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 58 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 440 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 485

In another narration, Imam {a.s} said:
"He should pray in it, and when he finds water, he should wash it and repeat the
prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man
who is without clothing and the time for prayer arrives, and he finds a garment that is
half covered in blood or entirely covered in blood. Should he pray in it, or should he
pray without clothing?
Imam {a.s} said: "If he finds water, he should wash it; if he does not find water, he should
pray in it and should not pray without clothing”.
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 219 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 248

english_text:
Safwan ibn Yahya wrote to Abu Al-Hasan, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}
asking about a man who has two garments, one of which has been contaminated with
urine, but he does not know which one. When the time for prayer arrives and he fears
missing it, and he has no water available, what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in both of them."
commentary:
The compiler of this book (may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him) clarified that this means
praying in each of them separately.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 249 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 225 • Awaali al- La’aali, Part 3, p. 55 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 442 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 505

presence of blood on a garment while in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you see it and have another garment with you, remove it and pray in
the other garment. If you do not have another garment, continue your prayer, and you
do not have to repeat it, provided that the blood does not exceed the size of a dirham.
If it is less than a dirham, it is of no consequence whether you see it or not. But if you
saw it and it was more than a dirham's size and neglected to wash it, and you prayed
multiple prayers in that state, then repeat all prayers you performed in that garment.
However, this is not the same ruling as for semen or urine."
Imam {a.s} then emphasized that the impurity of semen is more severe than urine and
said: "If you see semen before or after, you must repeat the prayer. If you inspected
your garment and did not find it and prayed, there is no need for repetition, and the
same applies for urine”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّ إ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن ِصَّ لَّوَّ إب ُّ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ ه :
ُّ«إَّلس َّ ي ْف ُّ ن ِمَّن ْز ِلَّه ِ إَّلزِّذَّإءِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِي هِ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّزَّ ق ِي هِ ذَّماً وَّ إَّلْق َّوْ س
ِن ِمَّن ْز ِلَّه ِ إَّلزِّذَّإء.
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"A sword is like a garment; you may pray with it as long as you do not see any blood on
it. A bow is also like a garment."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 249 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 371 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 529 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 458 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 189 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 261

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّ«إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن َّهُّ لأ ْ ي َّح ُّ ور ُّ لِلز َّج ُّ لِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ وَّ ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّذَّ ي ْ هِ سَّ ي ْف لِأ َّن َّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه َّ إ َّمْ ن » رُّوِى َّ ذ َّلِك َّ عَّن ْ إ َّمِي زِ إَّلْمُّو ِمِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم.
english_text:
"It is not permissible for a man to pray while there is a sword in front of him,
because the Qibla is a place of security."
This was narrated from The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ْ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّ وسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ُّي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ وَّ إ َّمَّ امَّ ه
َّمِس ْ ح َّ ث عَّلَّي ْ هِ ي ِي َّاب ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about
whether it is permissible for a man to pray while there is a rack with clothes hanging
on it in front of him.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 222 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 250

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja'far) asked him (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}) about a man
praying while there is garlic or onion in front of him.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja'far) asked him (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}) about
whether it is permissible for a man to pray on growing vegetation (fresh grass).
Imam {a.s} said: "If he places his forehead on the ground, then there is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text: وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ: عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ عَّلَّى َّإَّلْحَّ س ِ ي س ِ إَّلن َّان ِث ِ إ َّوِ إَّلي َّي ِّلِ وَّ هُّوَّ ي ُّصِ ي ث ُّ إ َّرْ ص اً ج َّ ذَّذإً ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja'far) asked him (Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}) about praying
on growing grass or lush greenery that covers fresh ground.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ و َّإَّلسِّ زَّإح ُّ مَّ وْ ص ُّ وع ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّذَّ ي ْ هِ ق ِى إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّسْ ي َّق ْ ن ِل
َّإَّلن َّار.
.هذ إ هو إلأ صل إلذ ى ي ح ث إ ن ي عمل ن ه
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja'far) asked about whether it is permissible for a man to pray with
a lamp (or flame) placed in front of him in the direction of the Qibla.
Imam {a.s} said: "It is not permissible for him to face the fire."
commentary: This is the principle that should be adhered to.
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 226 • Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 187 • Man La Yahduruhu Al- Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 250 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 225 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 396 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 461 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 166

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّ ق َّا َّم َّا إَّلْحَّ ذِي ث ُّ إَّل َّذ ِى رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ُّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ وَّ إَّلن َّارُّ وَّ إَّلسِّ زَّإح
ِوَّ إَّلص ُّ ورَّة ُّ ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّذَّي ْ ه ِلِأ َّن َّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي ُّصَّ لِّى لَّهُّ إ َّق ْزَّب ُّ إ ِلَّي ْ هِ مِن َّ إَّل َّذ ِى ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّذَّ ي ْ ه.
ق هو جذي ث ي زوى عن ي لاي ه من إلمح هولي ن ن اسن اذ من ق طغ ي زوي ه إلحسن ن ن على إلكوق ى وهو معزوف ، عن إلحسي ن ن ن
عمزو، عن إ ن ي ه، عن عمزو ن ن إ ن زإهي م إلهمذإن ى وهم مح هولون ي زق غ إلحذي ث ق ال: ق ال إ ن و عن ذ إلله علي ه إلسلام ذ لك ، ولكن ها
رج صه إق ي زن ث ن ها عله
صذرب عن ي ق اب ي م إي صلث ن المح هولي ن وإلأن ق طاع ق من إ ج ذ ن ها لم ي كن مح طن ا، ن عذ إ ن ي علم إ ن
. إلأ صل هو إلن هى ، وإ ن إلأطلاق هو رج صه ، وإلزج صه رجمه
english_text:
As for the narration reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
stating: "There is no harm if a man prays while the fire, the lamp, or an image is in front
of him, for the One to whom he is praying is closer to him than that which is in front of
him,"
commentary:
It is a narration transmitted through three unknown individuals with an interrupted
chain. It is narrated by Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Hussain ibn Amr, from his father,
from Amr ibn Ibrahim al-Hamdani, all of whom are unknown.
The narration is attributed to Abu 'Abdillah {a.s}. However, it is considered a concession
accompanied by a justification given by trustworthy sources but later connected
through unknown and interrupted chains. Thus, whoever acts upon it is not mistaken,
knowing that the default rule is to avoid it, while the permissibility is a concession, and
the concession is a mercy.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 250 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 342 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 226 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 396 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 461 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 167 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 296

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِعَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِى إَّلْق َّلَّن ْسُّ وَّ ة ِ إَّلس َّ وْ ذَّإءِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّ ق ِي هَّا ق َّا ِن َّهَّا لِن َّاسُّ إ َّهْلِ إَّلن َّار.
english_text:
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about praying while wearing a black cap.
Imam {a.s} said: "Do not pray in it, for it is the attire of the people of the Fire”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال إ َّمِي زُّ إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق ِي مَّا عَّل َّمَّ إ َّصْ حَّ ان َّهُّ: «لأَّ ي َّلْن َّسُّ وإ َّ إَّلس َّ وَّ إذَّ ق َّا ِن َّهُّ لِن َّاسُّ ق ِزْعَّوْ ن .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said in what he taught
his companions: "Do not wear black, for it is the clothing of Pharaoh."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 251 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 346 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 383 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 248

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text: ُّ وَّ كَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ي َّكْزَّةُّ إَّلس َّ وَّ إذَّ إ ِلأ َّ ق ِى ي َّلاَّي َّه ٍ إَّلْعِمَّامَّ ه ِ وَّ إَّلْح ِف ِّ وَّ إَّلْكِسَّ اء .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} disliked wearing black except in three cases: the
turban, the shoes, and the cloak.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 251 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 347 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 249

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
وَّ رُّوِى َّ: إ َّن َّهُّ هَّن َّظَّ ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّلَّى رَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق ِى ق َّن َّا ءٍ إ َّسْ وَّ ذَّ وَّ مِن ْطَّ ق َّه ٍ ق ِي هَّا
ج َّ ن ْح َّ ز ق َّق َّالَّ صَّ ل َّى ْ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ «ي َّا ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ مَّ ا هَّذ َّإ إَّلز ِّى ُّ » ق َّق َّالَّ ر ِى ُّ وُّلْذِ عَّمِّك َّ إَّلْعَّن َّاسِ ي َّا مُّحَّ م َّذُّ وَّ ي ْ ل لِوُّلْذِك َّ مِن
« َّوُّلْذِ عَّمِّك َّ إَّلْعَّن َّاسِ ق َّح َّ زَّح َّ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْعَّن َّاسِ ق َّق َّال ي َّا عَّمِّ وَّ ي ْل لِوُّلْذِى مِن ْ وُّلْذِك َّ» ق َّق َّالَّ ي َّا
ِرَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ إ َّ ق َّا َّج ُّ ث ُّ ن َّق ْسِ ى ، ق َّالَّ «ج َّ زَّى إَّلْق َّلَّمُّ ن ِمَّا ق ِي ه .
english_text:
It is narrated that Archangel Jibril, descended upon the Messenger of Allah {saws}
wearing a black cloak and a belt with a dagger.
The Prophet {saws} asked: "O’ Archangel Jibril {a.s}, what is this attire?"
Archangel Jibril {a.s} replied: "It is the attire of your uncle's descendants, O’ Muhammad.
Woe to your progeny from the progeny of your uncle al-Abbas." Prophet {saws} then went
out to al-Abbas and said: "O’ uncle, woe to my progeny from your progeny."
Al-Abbas asked: "O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, should I end myself (to prevent this)?"
The Prophet replied: "The Pen has decreed what is to come."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 252 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 348 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 712 • Ithbāt al-Hudāt, Part 1, p. 276 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 22, p. 291 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 28, p. 48

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ ِسْ مَّاعِ ي لُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّال-
ِ«إ َّوْ جَّ ى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ إ ِلَّى ن َّن ِى ٍّ مِن ْ إ َّن ْن ِي َّان ِه
َّ «ق ُّلْ لِلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ لأَّ ي َّلْن َّسُّ وإ لِن َّاسَّ إ َّعْ ذَّإن ِى وَّ لأَّ ي َّطْ عَّمُّوإ مَّ طَّ اعِ مَّ إ َّعْ ذَّإن ِى وَّ لأَّ ي َّسْ لُّكُّوإ مَّ سَّ الِك َّ إ عْ ذَّإن ِى ق َّي َّكُّون ُّوإ إ َّعْ ذَّإن ِى
» كَّمَّا هُّمْ إ َّعْ ذَّإن ِى.
.ق ا ما لن س إلسوإذ للي ق ي ه ق لا إ ي م ق ي ه
english_text:
Ismail ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said: "Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to one of His prophets, saying:
'Tell the believers not to wear the attire of My enemies, not to eat the foods of My
enemies, and not to follow the paths of My enemies, lest they become My enemies as
they are My enemies.'".
commentary: However, wearing black for the sake of dissimulation (taqiyya) carries no sin.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 252 • Kulliyat Hadith Qudsi, Vol. 1, p. 671 • Awalim al- Ulum, Vol. 20, p. 746

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ق َّق َّذْ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ جُّ ذ َّ ي ْق َّه َّ ن ْن ِ مَّ ن ْصُّ ورٍ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: كُّن ْث ُّ عِ ن ْذَّ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ن ِالْحِ ي زَّة ِ ق َّا َّي َّاةُّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إ َّن ِى
إَّلْعَّن َّاسِ إَّلْح َّ لِي ق َّه ِ ي َّذْ عُّوةُّ ق َّذَّعَّا ن ِمِمْ طَّ زٍ إ َّجَّ ذُّ وَّ ج ْ هَّي ْ هِ إ َّسْ وَّ ذُّ وَّ إَّلْأ ج َّ زُّ إ َّن ْي َّض ُّ ق َّلَّن ِسَّ هُّ ي ُّم َّ ق َّا ُّلَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «إ َّمَّ ا إ ِن ِّى إ َّلْن َّسُّ ه
ِوَّ إ َّن َّا إ َّعْ لَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ لِن َّاسُّ إ َّهْلِ إَّلن َّار .
english_text:
It has been reported from Hudhayfa ibn Mansur that He said:
"I was with Abu 'Abdillah {a.s} in Al-Hirah when a messenger from Abu al-Abbas, the
Caliph, came to invite him. So he (Imam {a.s}) called for a cloak, one side of which was
black and the other white. He wore it and then said: 'Indeed, I wear it knowing that it
is the clothing of the people of the Fire.'"
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 6, p. 449 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 252 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 347 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 712 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 384 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 47, p. 45 • Awalim al- Ulum, Vol. 20, p. 153 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 20, p. 398

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ٍ«لأَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ وَّ ق ِى ي َّذِةِ ج َّ اي َّمُّ جَّ ذِي ذ .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said: "A man should not pray while wearing an iron
ring."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 253 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 227 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 428 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 417 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 420

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال ٍعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «مَّ ا طَّ ه َّزَّ إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّذإً ق ِي هَّا جَّ لْق َّه ُّ جَّ ذِي ذ .
english_text: He {a.s} said: "Allah {SWT} has not purified a hand that wears an iron ring."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 253 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 428

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:

ِي َّي َّح َّ ي َّمُّ ن ِهِ لِأ َّن َّهُّ مِن ْ لِن َّاسِ إ َّهْلِ إَّلن َّار .
english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
regarding a man who prays while wearing an iron ring.
Imam {a.s} said: "No, and he should not wear it, for it is the attire of the people of the
Fire."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

ْي َّل ِن َّسِ إَّلْق ِزْمِز َّ ق َّا ِن َّهُّ مِن ْ إ َّرْ ذِي َّه ِ إ ِن ْلِي سَّ ، وَّ لأَّ ي َّزْكَّث ْ ن ِمِي ي َّزَّة ٍ جَّ مْ زَّإءَّ ق َّا ِن َّهَّا مِن ْ مَّ زَّإكِث ِ إ ِن ْل َّ ي سَّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّلْن َّسِ إَّلْحَّ زِي زَّ ق َّي ُّحْ زِق
»ُّإَّلل َّهُّ ج ِ لْذَّك َّ ي َّوْ مَّ ي َّلْق َّاة.
ولم ي طلق إلن ن ى صلى إلله علي ه وإ له لن س إلحزي ز لأجذ من إلزج ال إ لأ لعن ذ إلزجمن ن ن عوف وذ لك إ ن ه كان رج لا ق ملا.
english_text:
Abu al-Jaroud narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that the
Prophet said to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}:
"Indeed, I love for you what I love for myself, and I dislike for you what I dislike for
myself.
Do not wear a gold ring, for it is your adornment in the Hereafter.
Do not wear crimson, for it is among the garments of Iblis,
Do not ride on a red saddlecloth, for it is among the mounts of Iblis.
And do not wear silk, for Allah {SWT} will burn your skin on the Day you meet Him."
commentary:
The Prophet, only permitted the wearing of silk for any man in the case of 'Abd al-
Rahman ibn 'Awf, as he was afflicted with severe lice.

ًعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ إ َّمَّ امَّ هُّ جِ مَّار وَّ إق ِف ق َّالَّ «ي َّص َّ غُّ ن َّي ْن َّهُّ وَّ ن َّي ْ ن َّهُّ ق َّصَّ ن َّه ً إ َّوْ عُّوذإً إ َّوْ س َّ ي ْ ن ا
ِي ُّق ِي مُّهُّ ن َّي ْ ن َّهُّمَّا ي ُّم َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ » وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ مَّ عَّهُّ ذَّن َّه م َّ ن ْ ج ِ لْذِ جِ مَّارٍ إ َّوْ ن َّع ْ لٍ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى
َّ وَّ هِى َّ مَّ عَّهُّ إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّي َّح َّ و َّ ف َّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا ذ َّهَّان َّهَّا ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ وَّ هِى َّ مَّ عَّهُّ » وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّحَّ ز َّك َّ ن َّعْ ض ُّ إ َّسْ ن َّان ِهِ وَّ هُّو
ُّق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ هَّلْ ي َّن ْز ِعُّه ق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لأَّ ي ُّذْ مِي هِ ق َّلْي َّن ْز ِعْ هُّ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ي ُّذْ مِى ق َّلْي َّن ْصَّ زِف ْ » وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ ق ِى
ْكُّمِّهِ طَّ ي ْ ز ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ ج َّ اف َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ذ َّهَّان اً ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْسَّ » وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ن ِهِ إَّلي َّالُّولُّ إ َّوِ إَّلْح ُّ ز ْحُّ هَّل َّي َّصْ لُّحُّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّق ْطَّ غ
َّ إَّلي َّالُّولَّ وَّ هُّوَّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ إ َّوْ ي َّن ْي ِف َّ ن َّعْ ض َّ لَّحْ مِهِ مِن ْ ذ َّلِك َّ إَّلْح ُّ زْحِ وَّ ي َّطْ زَّجَّ هُّ ق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّي َّح َّو َّف ْ إ َّن ْ ي َّسِ ي لَّ إَّلذ َّمُّ ق َّلا
َّن َّا ْسَّ وَّ إ ِن ْ ي َّح َّ و َّف َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّسِ ي لَّ إَّلذ َّمُّ ق َّلاَّ ي َّق ْعَّلْهُّ» وَّ ع ُّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ ق َّزَّمَّ اةُّ رَّج ُّ ل ق َّس َّ ح َّ هُّ ق َّسَّ الَّ إَّلذ َّم
َّق َّان ْصَّ زَّف َّ وَّ ع َّسَّ لَّهُّ وَّ لَّمْ ي َّي َّكَّل َّمْ جَّ ي َّى رَّج َّ غَّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ هَّلْ ي َّعْ ي َّذ ُّ ن ِمَّا صَّ ل َّى إ َّوْ ي َّسْ ي َّق ْن ِلُّ إ َّ لص َّ لاَّة َّ ق َّالَّ «ي َّسْ ي َّق ْ ن ِلُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة
َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّعْ ي َّذ ُّ ن ِس َّ ى ْ ءٍ مِم َّا صَّ ل َّى» وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّزَّى ق ِى ي َّوْ ن ِهِ ج ُّ زْءَّ إَّلط َّ ي ْ زِ إ َّوْ ع َّي ْ زِةِ هَّلْ ي َّحُّ ك ُّهُّ وَّ هُّو
َّق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ ق َّالَّ «لأ
» َّن َّا ْس َّوَّ ق َّال «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ إ َّن ْ ي َّزْق َّغَّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ طَّ زْق َّهُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلس َّ مَّاءِ وَّ هُّوَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} regarding a
man praying while a bird is in front of him.
Imam {a.s} said: ‘There is no harm’.
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man praying while there is a date palm tree with fruit
in front of him’
Imam {a.s} said: ‘There is no harm’
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man praying in a vineyard with grapes’
Imam {a.s} said: ‘There is no harm’
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man praying with a donkey standing in front of him’
Imam {a.s} said: "He should place a stick or a rod or something as a barrier between
himself and the donkey, then pray, and there is no harm.
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man praying while having a leather pouch made of
donkey or mule hide with him’
Imam {a.s} said: “It is not suitable for him to pray while it is with him unless he fears it
will be lost, then there is no harm if he prays while it is with him.”
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man who has a loose tooth while in prayer, should
he remove it’
Imam {a.s} said: "If it does not bleed, he may remove it; but if it bleeds, he should stop.
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man praying with a bird in his sleeve’
Imam {a.s} said: “If he fears it may escape, there is no harm”.
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man with a wart or wound, can he cut it or remove a
piece of flesh from it during prayer’
Imam {a.s} said: "If he does not fear that it will bleed, there is no harm; but if he fears it
will bleed, he should not do it."
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man struck by someone during prayer, causing a
wound and bleeding, who leaves to wash the blood without speaking until returning to
the mosque’
Imam {a.s} said: "He must restart the prayer and cannot count what he prayed before."
(Ali ibn Ja’far asked): ‘Regarding a man who sees bird droppings or other filth on his
clothing during prayer, can he scrape it off’
Imam {a.s} said: ‘There is no harm’
And Imam {a.s} also said: "There is no harm if a man raises his gaze to the sky while
praying."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT

َّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ: عَّن ِ إَّلْح َّ لاَّج ِ لِ هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لُّن ْسُّ هَّا لِلن ِّسَّ اءِ وَّ إَّلصِّ ن ْي َّان ِ ق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كُّن َّ صَّ م َّاءَّ ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْس وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لَّهَّا صَّ وْ ب
َّق َّلا ُّي َّصْ لُّح .
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja’far ) asked Him, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}, about
whether it is permissible for women and children to wear anklets.
Imam {a.s} said: "If they are silent (do not make noise), there is no harm, but if they
produce sound, it is not appropriate”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text: َّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ عَّن ْ ق َّا ْرَّة ِ إَّلْمِسْ ك ِ ي َّكُّون ُّ مَّ غَّ مَّ ن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى و َّ هِى َّ ق ِى ج َّ ي ْ ن ِهِ إ َّوْ ي ِي َّان ِهِ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِذ َّلِك .
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja’far ) asked Him, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}, about a musk
pouch being with someone while they are praying, either in their pocket or clothing.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 219 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 254 • Wasail Al- Shia, Vol. 4, p. 433

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
He (Ali ibn Ja’far ) asked Him, Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about
whether it is permissible for a man to pray with beads or pearls in his mouth.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it prevents him from reciting (properly), then no; but if it does not
prevent him, there is no harm."
references: Masa’il Ali ibn Ja’far, Part 1, p. 238 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 254 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 432 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 461 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 173
