ُّ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ » ق ُّلْث ُّ ي صَّ لِّى وَّ ن َّي ْن َّ ي َّذَّ ي ْ هِ مِح ْ مَّزَّة ُّ س َّ ن َّهٍ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ » ق َّالَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّا ِن ْ كَّان َّ ق ِي هَّا ن َّار ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى جَّ ي َّى
ِي ُّن َّحِّ ي َّهَّا عَّن ْ ق ِن ْلَّي ِهِ » وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِى ي َّوْ ب ٍ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى عَّلَّمِهِ مِي َّالُّ طَّ ي ْ زٍ إ َّوْ ع َّي ْ ز ُّذ َّلِك َّ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ» وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّلْن َّس
ِإَّلْح َّ اي َّمَّ ق ِي هِ ن َّق ْ س ُّ مِي َّالِ إَّلط َّ ي ْ زِ إ َّوْ ع َّي ْ زِ ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي َّح ُّ ور ُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ ق ِي ه.
english_text:
Ammar ibn Musa asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about whether
it is permissible for a man to pray with an open Qur'an in front of him facing the qibla.
Imam {a.s} said: ‘No’
I (Ammar ibn Musa) asked: "What if it is in its cover?"
Imam {a.s} said: ‘Yes’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) then asked about praying with a bowl containing perfume in front
of him.
Imam {a.s} said: ‘Yes’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked: "What if there is a censer made of brass in front of him?"
Imam {a.s} said: ‘Yes’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked: "What if it has fire in it?"
Imam {a.s} said: ‘He should not pray until it is moved away from his qibla.’
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked about praying in a garment with the image of a bird or other
figures on its design.
Imam {a.s} said: ‘No’.
(Ammar ibn Musa) asked about wearing a ring with an engraved image of a bird or other
figures while praying.
Imam {a.s} said: ‘Prayer is not valid with it.’
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ جَّ ن ِي ث ُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْمُّعَّل َّى إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهُّ: إ ِن ِّى رَّج ُّ ل كَّي ِي زُّ إَّلس َّ هْ و
ق َّمَّا َّ إ َّجْ ق َّظ ُّ صَّ لاَّي ِى إ ِلأ
ِن ِح َّ اي َّمِى إ ُّجَّ وِّ لُّهُّ مِن ْ مَّ كَّان ٍ إ ِلَّى مَّ كَّان ٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Habib ibn al-Mu'alla asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, saying:
"I am a man who experiences frequent forgetfulness, so I can only maintain focus in
my prayer by moving my ring from one finger to another."
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}:
"Can a man pray while covering his mouth (muffling)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "While on an animal, yes; but on the ground, no”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّن ْذ ُّإَّلز َّجْ مَّن ِ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْحَّ ح َّ اح ِ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
عَّن ِ إَّلذ َّرَّإهِمِ إَّلس ُّ وذِ ي َّكُّون ُّ مَّ غَّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ وَّ هُّوَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى
َّ مَّ زْن ُّوطَّ ه ً إ َّوْ ع َّي ْ زَّ مَّ زْن ُّوطَّ ه ٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «مَّ ا إ َّس ْ ي َّهِى إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ وَّ مَّ عَّهُّ هَّذ ِةِ إَّلذ َّرَّإهِمُّ إَّل َّي ِى ق ِي هَّا إَّلي ِمَّاي ِي لُّ» ي ُّم َّ ق َّالَّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
ِإَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «مَّ ا لِلن َّاس ُّن ُّذ مِن ْ جِ ق ْظ ِ ن َّص َّ ان ِعِهِمْ ق َّا ِن ْ صَّ ل َّى وَّ هِى َّ مَّ عَّهُّ ق َّلْي َّكُّن ْ مِن ْ ج َّ لْق ِهِ وَّ لأَّ ي َّح ْ عَّلْ س َّ ي ْن اً مِن ْهَّا ن َّي ْن َّه َّ وَّ ن َّي ْ ن
ِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه.
english_text:
Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
about black dirhams (coins) with images on them being with a man while he prays,
whether tied or untied.
Imam {a.s} said: "I do not desire that he prays while having these dirhams with images
on them."
Then Imam {a.s} said: "People have no choice but to safeguard their belongings, so if he
prays while having them, let them be behind him, and he should not place anything
between himself and the qibla”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 256 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 437

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
:ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن ُّ عُّمَّزَّ ن ْن ِ ن َّز ِي غٍ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّه إ َّس ُّ ذ ُّ إَّلْأ ِر َّإرَّ وَّ إَّلْمِن ْذِي لَّ ق َّوْ ق َّ ق َّمِي صِ ى
َّق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Musa ibn Umar ibn Buzai' asked Abu Al-Hasan, Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha
{a.s}:
"I tie a waist wrap and a scarf over my shirt during prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 256 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 214 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 388 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 388 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 397

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إَّلْعِي ضُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْق َّاسِ مِ ، إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى ي َّوْ ب ِ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ إ َّوْ إ ِر َّإرِهَّا وَّ ي َّعْ ي َّم
ً ن ِح ِ مَّارِهَّا ق َّق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّث ْ مَّ ا ْمُّون َّه.
english_text:
Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man praying in a woman's garment or her waist wrap, or wrapping himself with her
headcover.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if it is clean (from any impurity)”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ِوَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ عَّن ْذ
إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ِ سِ ن َّان ٍ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: سُّ ن ِلَّ إ َّن ُّو عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ رَّج ُّ لٍ لَّي ْسَّ مَّ عَّهُّ إ ِلأ َّ سَّ زَّإ َّوِي لُّ ق َّق َّال
ْ«ي َّحُّ ل ُّ إَّلي ِّك َّه َّ مِن ْهُّ ق َّي َّص َّ عُّهَّا عَّلَّى عَّاي ِق ِهِ وَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ مَّ عَّهُّ سَّ ي ْف وَّ لَّي ْسَّ مَّ عَّهُّ ي َّو ب ق َّلْي َّي َّق َّل َّذِ إَّلس َّ ي ْف َّ وَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى
ًق َّان ِما .
english_text:
It was narrated by Abdullah ibn Sinan from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-
Sadiq {a.s}, was asked about a man who has nothing but trousers (for covering).
Imam {a.s} said: "He should untie the waistband and place it over his shoulder and pray.
If he has a sword but no garment, he should hang the sword around himself and pray
standing”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 256 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 366 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 380 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 452 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 191

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّال -
«إ َّذْ ن َّى مَّ ا ي ُّح ْ ز ِي ك َّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ ق ِي هِ ن ِق َّذْ رِ مَّ ا ي َّكُّون ُّ عَّلَّى
ِ مَّ ن ْكِن َّي ْك َّ مِي ْلَّ ج َّ ن َّاجَّ ى ِ إَّلْح ُّ ط َّ اف .
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that Imam {a.s}
said:
"The minimum acceptable covering for you to pray in is to have something on your
shoulders, like the wings of a swallow”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 256 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 380 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 453 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 191

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي زٍ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ مَّ ا ي ُّح ْ ز ِى إَّلز َّج ُّ لَّ مِن َّ إَّلي ِّي َّاب ِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّصَّ لِّى َّ ق ِي هِ ق َّق َّالَّ «صَّ ل َّى إَّلْحُّ سَّ ي ْ ن
ْ ن ْن ُّ عَّلِى ٍّ صَّ لَّوَّ إب ُُّّ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق ِى ي َّوْ ب ٍ ق َّذْ ق َّلَّضَّ عَّن ْ ن ِصْ ف ِ سَّ اق ِهِ وَّ ق َّارَّب َّ رُّكْن َّي َّي ْ هِ لَّي ْ سَّ عَّلَّى مَّ ن ُّكِن َّي ْ هِ مِن ْهُّ إ ِلأ َّ ق َّذْ ر
ِ ج َّ ن َّاجَّ ى
ِ إَّلْح ُّ ط َّ اف
َّ وَّ كَّان َّ إ ِذ َّإ رَّكَّغَّ سَّ ق َّظَّ عَّن ْ مَّ ن ْكِن َّي ْ هِ وَّ كُّل َّمَّا سَّ ح َّ ذَّ ي َّن َّالُّهُّ عُّن ُّق ُّهُّ ق َّزَّذ َّةُّ عَّلَّى مَّ ن ْكِن َّي ْ هِ ن ِي َّذِةِ ق َّ لَّمْ ي َّز َّلْ ذ َّلِك
َّ ذَّإ ْن َّهُّ وَّ ذَّإ ْن َّهُّ مُّس ْ ي َّع ِلاً ن ِهِ جَّ ي َّى إِن ْصَّ زَّف .
english_text:
Abu Basir asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about what is
sufficient clothing for a man to pray in.
Imam {a.s} said: "Hussain ibn Ali {a.s} prayed in a garment that reached up to half his shin
and was close to his knees, with only as much covering on his shoulders as the wings
of a swallow.
When he would bow (in ruku'), it would slip off his shoulders, and whenever he
prostrated (Sujood), it would touch his neck, so he would pull it back over his
shoulders with his hand, and this remained his practice until he completed the
prayer”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 257 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 381 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إَّلْق ُّص َّ ي ْلُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّال-
«صَّ ل َّث ْ ق َّاطِ مَّه ُّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق ِى ذِرْعٍ وَّ ج ِ مَّارُّهَّا عَّلَّى
رَّإ ْسِ هَّا لَّي ْسَّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إ َّكْي َّزُّ مِم َّا وَّ إرَّب ْ ن ِهِ س َّ عْ زَّهَّا وَّ إ ُّذ ُّن َّي ْهَّا .
english_text:
Al-Fudayl narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A} prayed in a tunic with a headscarf covering her head,
and She did not have more on than what concealed her hair and her ears”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 257 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 381 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
Zurarah narrated that a man asked him (Abu Ja'far {a.s}):
"If a person sees a scorpion, a snake, or a serpent while he is praying, should he kill
it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if he wishes to do so."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 257 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 905

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ سُّ لَّي ْمَّان ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إَّلْح َّ عْ ق َّزِى ُّ إَّلْعَّن ْذَّ إَّلص َّ الِحَّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّم:

» َّ إَّلذِّ ي ن َّ إ َّوْ سَّ غُّ مِن ْ ذ َّلِك.
english_text:
Suleiman ibn Jaafar al-Ja'fari asked the righteous servant Imam Musa ibn Jafar
Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man who goes to the market and buys a fur garment without
knowing if it is from a properly slaughtered (halal) animal or not. Can he pray in it?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, you are not obligated to inquire about that. Abu Ja'far {a.s} used to
say, 'The Khawarij (a group known for extreme practices) imposed restrictions upon
themselves out of ignorance; indeed, religion is more accommodating than that.'".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 257 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 368 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 419 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 491 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 455 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 2, p. 281

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT

ٍ عَّن ِ إَّلْح ُّ لُّوذِ وَّ إَّلْق ِزَّإءِ ي َّس ْ ي َّزِي هِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ق ِى سُّ وق

ِرَّإ َّي ْي ُّمُّ إَّلْمُّس ْ ز ُّكِي ن َّ ي َّن ِي عُّون َّ ذ َّلِك َّ وَّ إ ِذ َّإ رَّإ َّي ْي ُّمُّوهُّمْ ي ُّصَّ ل ُّون َّ ق َّلاَّ ي َّسْ ا َّلُّوإ عَّن ْه .
english_text:
Ismail ibn Isa asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Ridha about leather and fur items
purchased from a market in the mountain regions: Should a person inquire about their
source of slaughter (i.e., whether it was properly done) if the seller is a Muslim but not
a known believer?
He {a.s} replied: "You should inquire if you see that the sellers are polytheists selling
those items. But if you see them performing prayer, then you do not need to ask”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 258 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 371 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 420 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 492

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
It was narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus that his father wrote to
Imam Abu Al-Hasan {a.s} asking about wearing fur or leather socks (khuff) and praying
in them without knowing if they were from a properly slaughtered (halal) animal.
He {a.s} replied: "There is no harm in it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 258 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 456

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
It was narrated from Hashim Al Hannat that he heard Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-
Kadhim {a.s} say: "Anything that eats leaves and plants, there is no problem in praying
while wearing it (its leather or fur), but anything that eats carrion, do not pray in it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 404 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 354 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 76

english_text:
Zurarah said that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said: "The Commander
of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} came out to a group of people and saw them
praying in the mosque with their cloaks draped (over their shoulders), and Imam {a.s}
said to them:
'What is the matter with you that you drape your garments as if you are Jews coming
out of their synagogues?' Meaning, beware of draping your garments (while praying)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 386 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

english_text:
Zurarah narrated that Abu Ja'far, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Beware of the 'wrapped shroud' (al-samma')."
I asked: "And what is the 'wrapped shroud'?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is when you take your garment under your arm and place it over one
shoulder”.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 394 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Ma’ani al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 390 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 214 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 388 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 387 • Wasail Al- Shia, Vol. 4, p. 399 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 201

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT

ًصَّ ل َّى ج َّ الِسا .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} stated regarding a man who finds
himself outside without clothing and the time for prayer arrives, that he should pray
standing while uncovered if no one can see him. However, if he is in view of others, he
should pray sitting.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 365 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 438 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 449 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 449 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 213

english_text:
Abu Jamila narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that he
asked him about wearing the garment of a Magian (Zoroastrian) and praying in it.
Abu Abdullah {a.s} replied: "Yes." Then he asked: "But they drink wine."
He {a.s} said: "Yes, we buy Sabiriyyah garments (a type of fabric) and wear them without
washing."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 210 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p.

وعن إ ن ى ج عق ز إلي ان ى علي ه إلسلام ون ها إ ج ذ وإ ق ي ى .
english_text:
Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that a man, while in his
presence, asked about a person who exits the bathhouse or performs a ritual bath,
then wraps himself and wears a shirt over his lower garment and prays in this manner.
Imam {a.s} said: "This is from the actions of the people of Lot."
I (Ziyad) said: "He wraps the cloth over his shirt."
Imam {a.s} said: "This is an act of arrogance."
I said: "The shirt is thin, and he covers himself with it."
Imam {a.s} responded: "This, along with unfastening the buttons during prayer, flicking
pebbles, and chewing gum (frankincense) in gatherings or while on the street, are
among the practices of the people of Lot."
commentary:
It has also been narrated that there is leniency in wrapping the garment over the shirt
from the Righteous Servant (of Allah {SWT}), from Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith, Imam Ali ibn
Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}, and from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad {a.s} and they
accepted it in certain cases.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 260 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 371 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 385 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 396 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, vol. 4, p. 312

english_text:
Abdullah ibn Bukayr asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man praying while letting the sides of his garment hang loose.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue with it”.
commentary:
Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Jaroud al-Hamdani, was a blind Kufi follower of the Zaydi
sect. Al-Kashi narrated some reports criticizing him, some of which included claims
that he was a liar and an infidel.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
Abu Basir asked Imam {a.s} about a man praying in extreme heat and fearing for
his forehead due to the hot ground.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should place his garment beneath his forehead”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:
وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ذَّإوُّذُّ إَّلص َّ زْمِى ُّ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ عَّلِى َّ ن ْن َّ مُّ حَّ م َّذٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّق َّالَّ لَّهُّ: إ ِن ِّى ْإ َّج ْ زُّح ُّ ق ِى هَّذ َّإ إَّلْوَّ ج ْ هِ وَّ رُّن َّمَّا لَّم

english_text:
Dawud Al-Sarmi asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}
about going on a journey where there may be no place to pray except on snow. How
should he pray in such a case?
Imam {a.s} replied: "If you can avoid prostrating on the snow, then do not prostrate on
it. But if it is not possible, then level it and prostrate on it."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 390 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 261 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 310 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 336 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 452 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1051 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 164

Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmoud said to Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} about a man
who prays on a bed made of teakwood and prostrates on the teakwood itself.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, there is no issue”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 261 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 310 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 744 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 178 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 364

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There is no issue with praying on mats made from reeds or on palm-leaf mats, and on
any plant-based material, except for fruit”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 261 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 311 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 744 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 345

english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} regarding
eating the meat of wild animals, including birds and other beasts.
Imam responded, "As for eating their meat, we dislike it, but as for their skins, you may
use them to ride on but do not wear anything made from them for prayer."
commentary:
My father, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:
"There is no issue with praying in clothing made from the hair or fur of any animal
whose meat is permissible to eat. However, if you have garments of squirrel, sable, or
marten fur, remove them before prayer, though concessions have been narrated for
this.
Be cautious not to pray wearing fox skins or clothing directly touching such skins."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
It has been narrated from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari that He said: "I saw
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} praying in a silk cloak (jubbah made of khazz)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 262 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 359

Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated: "I saw Abu Ja'far al-Thani (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali
Al-Jawad {a.s}) praying both the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers in a cloak made
of fine silk fabric (khazz taruni). He gave me a cloak made of khazz, informed me that
he had worn it on his body and prayed in it, and instructed me to pray in it as well."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 262 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 411 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 359 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 387 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 521

english_text:
It was narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Imran that He said: ‘I wrote to Abu Ja'far al-
Thani (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad {a.s}) concerning clothing made from squirrel
(sanjab), mink (fanak), and silk (khazz), and I said: 'May I be your ransom, I would like
you not to respond with dissimulation (taqiyya) regarding this matter.'
The Imam {a.s} wrote back in his own handwriting, 'Pray in them.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 262 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 411 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 349 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 337 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 386 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 521

english_text:
It was narrated from Dawud al-Sarmi that a man asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith
(Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}), about praying in silk (khazz) that is mixed with
rabbit fur.
The Imam wrote in response: "That is permissible."
commentary:
This is a leniency for which the one who acts upon it will be rewarded, and the one who
rejects it will be blameworthy. The original ruling as mentioned by (the narrator's)
father in his letter states: "Pray in silk (khazz) as long as it is not mixed with rabbit fur."
He also stated: "Do not pray in brocade, pure silk, or embroidered silk, except if it is a
garment with silk warp and cotton or linen weft."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 262 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 213

english_text:
Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali {a.s}, asking
about praying in garments dyed with crimson (qirmaz), saying, "Our companions avoid
praying in it."
The Imam wrote back: "There is no problem with it at all, and all praise is due to Allah
{SWT}."
commentary:
The author of this book commented:
This ruling applies if the crimson-dyed garment is not made of pure silk. The prohibition
pertains only to garments made from pure silk.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
He (Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar) wrote to Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan {a.s} asking
about a man who replaces cotton in his cloak with qazz (a type of silk): "Can he pray in
it?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, there is no problem with it."
commentary:
The explanation is that it refers to qazz from goats, not pure silk qazz.
The narrations have prohibited wearing brocade (dibaj), silk, and pure silk (ibrisim) and
praying in them for men.
However, there is an allowance for women to wear such materials, though it does not
extend to praying in them. The prohibition on praying in pure silk applies generally to
both men and women, unless a specific exception has been made for women
regarding prayer as there has been for wearing it. For men, wearing silk and brocade is
only permitted in times of war. It is also permissible even if it contains images.
This was narrated by Sama’a ibn Mehran from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated from the Imam {a.s} that He said:
"There is no issue if a garment's warp, buttons, or trim is made of silk; what is disliked
for men is pure silk (mubham)”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 264 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 208 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 386 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 726 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 375 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 240

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
It was narrated from Mus'ab ibn Abdul Malik al-Basri that He said:
"There is no issue in taking (a piece) from the silk covering of the Ka’ba and using it as
a cover for a Quran or making it into a prayer mat to pray upon."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 264 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 734 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 378 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 13, p. 258

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-
Ridha {a.s}, about praying in a garment with patterns (decorations), and the Imam
disliked it if it contained images (representations).
commentary:
Praying in a belt (headband) with a silk end is not permitted. There is no issue with
praying in garments made from Khwarazmian furs or those tanned in the land of Hijaz.
Also, there is no issue with praying in the wool of a dead animal because wool does
not have a soul.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 264 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 437

english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
wearing a sword during prayer that has glue or leather (adhesive substances, such as
glue made from animal parts) on it.
Imam {a.s} replied: "There is no problem as long as you do not know that it is from a dead
(non-slaughtered) animal”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 265 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 56

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT

english_text:
Ali ibn al-Rayan ibn al-Salt asked Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s} about a
man who cuts his hair or trims his nails and then goes to pray without shaking the
remnants off his clothes.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue (no problem)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 265 • The Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 66 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 123

. ولأ ي ح ور للمعي م إ ن ي صلى إ لأ وهو مي حن ك
english_text:
Yunus ibn Ya'qub asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
praying while wearing a burṭulah (a type of hat or head covering).
The Imam said: "It does not harm him (there is no issue)."
commentary:
And I heard our esteemed scholars say that it is not permissible to pray in a ṭabaqiyyah
(a specific type of head covering), and a person wearing a turban (muʿtamim) must
have it wrapped (with a part of the turban under the chin).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text:

english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati narrated from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said: "Whoever goes
out on a journey without wrapping the turban under his chin and suffers from an
ailment for which there is no remedy, let him blame none but himself”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 245 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 398 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 745 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 402

english_text:
The truthful one, Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said: "I guarantee that whoever leaves his
house with his turban wrapped under his chin will return to it safely."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:

لَّأ َّعْ ح َّ ث ُّ مِم َّن ْ ي َّا ْج ُّ ذ ُّ ق ِى ُّجَّ اج َّ ه ٍ وَّ هُّوَّ مُّ عْ ي َّم ي َّحْ ث َّ جَّ ن َّكِهِ كَّي ْف َّ لأَّ ي ُّق ْص َّ ى جَّ اج َّ ي ُّه.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said:
"I am amazed by one who goes about seeking to fulfil a need while in a state of ritual
purity (wudu) - how is it that his need is not met?
And I am amazed by one who seeks to fulfil a need while wearing his turban wrapped
under his chin - how is it that his need is not met?"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 165

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:

ِ«إَّلْق َّزْق ُّ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْمُّسْ لِمِي ن َّ وَّ إَّلْمُّس ْ زِكِي ن َّ إَّلي َّلَّحِّ ى ن ِالْعَّمَّان ِم .
.وذ لك ق ى إ ول إلأسلام وإن ي ذإن ه
english_text:
The Prophet, said: "The distinction between the Muslims and the polytheists
is the wearing of turbans."
commentary: This was during the early period of Islam and its establishment.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 745 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 403

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text: ِوَّ ق َّذْ ن َّق َّلَّ عَّن ْهُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه ِإ َّهْلُّ إَّلْح ِ لاَّف ِ إ َّي ْص اً: إ َّن َّهُّ إ َّمَّ زَّ ن ِالي َّلَّحِّ ى وَّ ن َّهَّى عَّن ِ إَّلأِق ْي ِعَّاط .
english_text:
It has also been reported from the Messenger, by those outside the Shi'a
tradition that he commanded the wearing of turbans (tallaḥḥi) and forbade wrapping
without a tail (iqti'āṭ).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 165 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 165 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 403

ِهَّلْ ي َّق ْ زَّإ ُّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ وَّ ي َّوْ ن ُّهُّ عَّلَّى ق ِي ه
َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِذ َّلِك.
ِّ وَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى :
َّ «إ ِذ َّإ سَّ مِغَّ إَّلْهَّمْ هَّمَّه .
english_text:
Al-Halabi and Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} whether a man may recite during prayer with his garment covering his mouth.
The Imam said: "There is no issue with that."
In another narration by Al-Halabi, it is added: "As long as he can hear his murmuring
(sound of his recitation)”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
arabic_text:

ِعَّن ِ إَّلْمُّح ْ ي َّص ِ ث ِ إ ِذ َّإ ي َّمَّك َّن َّ مِن َّ إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذ

َّهِى َّ مُّ ح ْ ي َّص ِ ن َّه وَّ ي َّذَّإهَّا مَّ زْن ُّوط ِ ي َّان.
روى ذ لك عمار إلسان اطى عن إلصاذق علي ه إلسلام.
english_text:
Rifa'ah ibn Musa asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}
about a person who is dyed (with henna or similar) and whether they can pray while in
this state if they are able to perform prostration and recitation.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, as long as their cloth (used during the process) is pure and they
are in a state of wudu (ritual purity). There is also no issue if a woman prays while She
is dyed and her hands are bound (covered)."
commentary: This was narrated by 'Ammar al-Sabati from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT

إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ وَّ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ ي َّح ْ ي َّص ِ ن َّان ِ إ َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّي َّان ِ وَّ هُّمَّا مُّ ح ْ ي َّص ِ ن َّان ِ ن ِالْحِ ن َّاءِ وَّ إَّلْوَّ سِ مَّه ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ َّإ َّن ْزَّر ُّوإ إَّلْق َّمَّ وَّ إَّلْمَّن ْح ِ زَّ ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far and Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-
Kadhim {a.s} about whether a man and a woman may pray while dyed with henna or
wasmah (a type of dye).
Imam {a.s} said: "If they expose the mouth and nostrils, there is no problem."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 267 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 356 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 391 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 396 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 429

Chapter Title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a
man praying without taking his hands out of his garment.
The Imam said: "If he takes his hands out, it is good, but if he does not, there is no issue
(no problem)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 267 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 356 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 391 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 398 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 431 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 202

english_text:
Ziyad ibn Suqah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He
said: "There is no issue if one of you prays in a single garment with its buttons undone.
Indeed, the religion of Muhammad {saws} is upright (easy and straightforward)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 267 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 2, p. 216 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 357 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 392 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 374 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 393 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 185

arabic_text:

ق ال إلصاذق علي ه إلسلام: " إلسح وذ على إلأ رض ق زي ص ه وعلى ع ي ز ذ لك سن ه .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Prostration (Sujood) on the earth is obligatory (fardh), while prostrating on other than
that is a recommended practice (sunnah)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذُّ عَّلَّى ِ طِ ي ن ِ ق َّن ْزِ إَّلْحُّ سَّ ي ْن ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي ُّن َّوِّ رُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ إَّلس َّ ان ِعَّه.
ومن كان معه سن حه من طي ن ق ن ز إلحسي ن علي ه إلسلام كي ث مسن حا وإ ن لم ي سن ح ن ها. وإلي سن ي ح ن الأ صان غ إ ق ص ل من ه
ن ع ي زها لأ ن ها مسو ولأب ي وم إلق ي امه .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said: "Prostrating on the clay from the grave of Imam Hussain ibn Ali
{a.s} illuminates to the seventh layer of the earth."
commentary:
Whoever possesses a prayer bead (subha) made from the clay of the grave of Imam
Hussain ibn Ali {a.s}, is considered as having performed tasbih (glorification) even if they
do not actively recite.
Additionally, performing tasbih with one's fingers is superior to using anything else
because the fingers will be questioned (held accountable) on the Day of Judgment.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 268 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 731

Chapter Title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR
arabic_text: ْ وَّ رَّوَّ ى جَّ م َّاذُّ ن ْن ُّ عُّي ْ مَّان َّ عَّن َّإ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذُّ عَّلَّى مَّ ا إ َّن ْن َّي َّث ِ إَّلْأ َّرْض ُّ إ ِلأ َّ مَّ ا إ ُّكِلَّ إ َّوْ لُّن ِس .
english_text:
Hamad ibn Uthman narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said:
"Prostration is to be done on what the earth produces, except for that which is eaten
or worn."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 268 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 341 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 234 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 313 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 729 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 344 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 82, p. 148

english_text:
It was narrated from the Yasir al-Khadim that He said:
"Abu al-Hasan {a.s} passed by me while I was praying on a piece of ṭabarī (a mat) upon
which I had placed something.
Imam {a.s} said: 'Why do you not prostrate on it? Is it not from what the earth produces?'"
commentary:
My father further explained in his letter: "Prostrate on the earth or on what grows from
the earth. Do not prostrate on the ḥuṣur (reed mats) of Medina because their bindings
are made of leather. Do not prostrate on hair, wool, leather, silk, glass, iron, brass,
bronze, lead, copper, feathers, or ashes. If the earth is hot and you fear burning your
forehead, or if it is a dark night and you fear scorpions or thorns that might harm you,
there is no issue with prostrating on your sleeve if it is made of cotton or linen.
If there is a swelling on your forehead, dig a small hole so that when you prostrate, the
swelling can fit inside.
If you have an ailment on your forehead that prevents you from prostrating, prostrate
on the right side of your forehead. If that is not possible, then prostrate on the left side
of your forehead. If you cannot do that, prostrate on the back of your hand. If even that
is not possible, then prostrate on your chin, for Allah {SWT}, says: 'Those who were given
knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down prostrating on their chins..
and it increases them in humility' (Surah Al-Isra, 17:107-109).
There is no issue with standing and placing your palms, knees, and big toes on
surfaces other than earth. You should bring your nose close to the ground, and for
placing the forehead, the amount from the hairline to the eyebrows equivalent to a
dirham suffices. Your prostration should be like a thin, gaunt camel lowering itself,
such that no part of your body rests on another."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 268 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 341 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 235 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 308 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 331 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 79 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 743 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 348

english_text:
Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
praying on qufr (bare ground or desert soil) and qīr (a type of tar or pitch).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue with it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
english_text:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Imam Abu al-Hasan {a.s} about gypsum (plaster)
that was fired using dung and the bones of the dead, and whether it would be
permissible to prostrate on it if a mosque was plastered with it.
The Imam wrote back in his own handwriting: "Fire and water have purified it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Dawud ibn Abi Zayd asked Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s} about prostrating
on papers and documents with writing on them.
The Imam wrote back: "It is permissible."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 270 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 235 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 355

english_text:
Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} about a man prostrating
on a misḥ (a type of mat or rug) and on a carpet.
The Imam said: "There is no issue if it is in a situation of taqiyya (precautionary
dissimulation to protect oneself)."
commentary: It is no issue with prostrating on clothing in situations of taqiyya.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Muawiya ibn Ammar asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
praying on qār (bitumen or tar).
The Imam said: "There is no issue with it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Zurarah narrated from one of the Imams {a.s} that He said:
"I asked him about a man prostrating while wearing a cap or a turban.
Imam {a.s} said: 'If any part of his forehead touches the ground, between his eyebrows
and his hairline, then it suffices.'"

Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:
"I saw Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} leveling the pebbles at the place of his
prostration between the two prostrations."

It was narrated from Ali ibn Bajil that He said:
"I saw Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, every time he prostrated and then
raised his head, he would take the pebbles from his forehead and place them back on
the ground."

. وروى ر رإرة عن ه علي ه إلسلام مي ل ذ لك
english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati narrate from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He
said:
"The area between the hairline and the tip of the nose is considered a place of
prostration (masjid), so whatever part of it touches the ground suffices."
commentary: And Zurarah also narrated a similar statement from Imam {a.s}.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 271 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 298 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 327 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 716 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 356

. وق ى رساله إ ن ى رص ى إلله عن ه إ لى : ولأ ي ن ق ح ق ى موص غ سح وذك ق ا ذ إ إ رذب إلن ق ح ق لي كن ق ن ل ذج ولك ق ى إلصلاة
english_text:
A man asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} bout a place with dust
where he wanted to blow it away before prostrating.
The Imam said: "There is no issue”.
commentary:
The narrator's father further explained in his letter:
"Do not blow on your place of prostration during the prayer. If you wish to blow, do so
before entering the prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION

وَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِن َّمَّا ِي ُّكْزَّةُّ ذ َّلِك َّ ج َّ س ْ ي َّه َّ إ َّن ْ ي ُّو ْ ذ َّى مَّ ن ْ إ ِلَّى ج َّ ان ِن ِه .
وي كزة إ ن ي مسح إلزج ل إلي زإب عن ج ن هي ه وهو ق ى إلصلاة ، وي كزة إ ن ي ي زكه ن عذ ما صلى ق ا ن مسح إلي زإب من ج ن هي ه وهو
.ق ى إلصلاة ق لا س ى علي ه لوروذ إلزج صه ق ي ه
english_text:
It was narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"It is disliked (makruh) because it may cause harm to the person next to him."
commentary:
It is disliked for a man to wipe the dust from his forehead while in prayer, and it is also
disliked to leave it there after the prayer. However, if a person wipes the dust from his
forehead while in prayer, there is no issue, as leniency has been reported regarding
this matter.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Hisham ibn al-Hakam said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"Tell me about what is permissible to prostrate on and what is not."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Prostration is only permissible on the earth or what grows from the
earth, except for what is eaten or worn."
Hisham then asked: "May I be your ransom, what is the reason for that?"
The Imam said: "Prostration is an act of humility before Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic, and it should not be on what is eaten or worn because the people of the world
are slaves to what they eat and wear.
The one who prostrates in worship of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, should not
place his forehead on what is worshipped by the people of the world who are deceived
by its allure. Prostration on the earth is superior because it is more effective in
demonstrating humility and submission to Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 272 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 341 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 82, p. 147

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said :
"Indeed, Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, made the Ka’ba the Qiblah (direction of
prayer) for the people of the mosque (Masjid al-Haram), and He made the mosque the
Qiblah for the people of the sanctuary (Haram), and He made the sanctuary the Qiblah
for the people of the world."

english_text:
Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
the deviation of some of our companions to the left from the Qiblah and the reason for
it.
Imam {a.s} replied: "When the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad) was brought down from
Paradise and placed in its position, the boundaries of the Haram (sanctuary) were
determined by the reach of the light emanating from the Stone. It is four miles to the
right of the Ka’ba and eight miles to the left, making a total of twelve miles.
Thus, if a person deviates to the right, they leave the boundary of the Qiblah due to the
lesser extent of the Haram's boundary, but if they deviate to the left, they do not leave
the boundary of the Qiblah."
commentary:
For those within Masjid al-Haram, it is permissible to face any side of the Ka’ba during
prayer. One praying inside the Ka’ba may also face any of its walls. However, the best
position is to stand between the two columns on the red tile and face the corner
containing the Black Stone. If someone is above the Ka’ba and it is time for prayer, they
should lie down and incline their head toward the Bayt al-Ma'mur (Heavenly House).
Similarly, anyone praying on Mount Abu Qubays should face the Ka’ba, as the Qiblah
extends upward to the sky.
The Prophet {saws} prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for thirteen years in
Makkah after receiving prophethood and for nineteen months in Madinah.
The Jews mocked him, saying that he was following their Qiblah, causing him great
distress. One night, he turned his face toward the heavens in anticipation, and in the
morning, after completing two units (rak'ahs) of the Dhuhr prayer, Archangel Jibril {a.s}
came to him and said:
"We have seen you turning your face toward the sky, so We shall turn you to a Qiblah
that pleases you. Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144)."
Archangel Jibril {a.s} then took the Prophet’s hand and turned him toward the Ka’ba, and
those behind him also turned, so that men and women changed their positions.
Thus, his initial prayer was toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and the remainder was toward the
Ka’ba.
The news reached a mosque in Madinah where people had already prayed two rak'ahs
of 'Asr. They turned toward the Ka’ba, and so their initial prayer direction was toward
Bayt al-Maqdis and its completion was toward the Ka’ba. This mosque became known
as Masjid al-Qiblatayn (the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs).
The Muslims then asked:
"O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, what happens to our prayers toward Bayt al-Maqdis?"
Allah {SWT} revealed: "Allah {SWT} would not make your faith to be in vain (Surah Al-
Baqarah 2:143)," meaning that their prayers toward Bayt al-Maqdis were accepted.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 272 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 44

english_text:
It was narrated from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah that he asked Imam Jafar
Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a blind man who prayed facing a direction other than the Qiblah.
Imam {a.s} replied: "If it is still within the prayer time, he should repeat the prayer. If the
time has passed, he does not need to repeat it."
He further asked about a man who prayed during cloudy weather and afterward, when
the clouds cleared, realized he had prayed in the wrong direction.
The Imam said: "If it is still within the prayer time, he should repeat the prayer. If the
time has passed, he does not need to repeat it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol 1, p. 276 • Al-Wafi, V. 7, p. 551 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 4, p. 318

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
english_text:
Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that He
said: "For one who is confused (about the direction of the Qiblah), it suffices for him to
pray in whichever direction he faces if he does not know where the Qiblah is."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V 1, p. 276 • Al-Wafi, V. 7, p. 548 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 4, p. 311

english_text:
Muawiya ibn Ammar asked Him about a man who stands for prayer and, after
finishing, realizes that he had deviated to the right or the left of the Qiblah.
Imam {a.s} replied: "His prayer is valid, for the area between the east and the west is
(considered) the Qiblah."
commentary:
And this was revealed concerning those who are confused about the direction:
"To Allah {SWT} belongs the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the face of
Allah {SWT}" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:115)
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Volume 1, p. 276 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 48 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 297 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 554 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 314

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s}
that He said:
"If a seepage (liquid or discharge) appears behind a latrine (toilet) and it is in the
direction of the Qiblah, one should cover it with something."
commentary:
Nothing that passes in front of a Muslim while he is praying - whether it be a dog, a
woman, a donkey, or anything else - invalidates the prayer.

english_text: The Messenger of Allah {saws} forbade spitting in the direction of the Qiblah.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Volume 1, p. 277 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 500 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 319

ِعَّلَّى صَّ لاَّي ِه َّوَّ ق َّال ً إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «وَّ هَّذ َّإ ي َّق ْي َّحُّ مِن َّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ إ َّن ْوَّ إن اً كَّي ِي زَّة.
english_text:
The Prophet {saws} saw phlegm (or a spittle) in the mosque. He walked over to it
with a palm branch from the branches of Ibn Tab and scraped it off, then returned
backward and continued his prayer.
And Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "This opens many doors regarding
(permissible) actions during prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Volume 1, p. 277 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 500

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:

ٍع َّان ِظ .
english_text:
The Prophet, forbade engaging in sexual intercourse while facing or with one's
back to the Qiblah.
He also forbade facing the Qiblah when urinating or defecating.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال إ َّن ُّو ُّج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ«لأَّ ي َّن ْز ُّق َّن َّ إ َّجَّ ذُّكُّمْ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِن َّلَّ وَّ ج ْ هِهِ وَّ لأَّ عَّن ْ ي َّمِي ن ِهِ وَّ لْي َّن ْز ُّق ْ عَّن ْ ي َّسَّ ارِة
وَّ ي َّحْ ث ِ ق َّذَّمِهِ إَّلْي ُّسْ زَّى .
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"None of you should spit in front of themselves or to their right while praying. Instead,
they should spit to their left or beneath their left foot."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Volume 1, p. 277 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 257 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 501 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 319 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 222 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 365 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 201

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:
ُّق َّالَّ إَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
«مَّ ن ْ جَّ ن َّسَّ رِي ق َّهُّ إ ِج ْ لاَّلأً لِل َّهِ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ إ َّوْ رَّي َّهُّ إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّعَّالَّى صِ ح َّ ه ً جَّ ي َّى
ِ إَّلْمَّمَّاب.
وق ذ روى ق ي من لأ ي هي ذى إ لى إلق ن له ق ى مق ار ة إ ن ه ي صلى إ لى إ رن غ ج وإن ث .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever holds back their saliva out of reverence for Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic, during prayer, Allah {SWT} will grant them health until their death."
commentary:
It has also been narrated regarding someone who cannot determine the Qiblah in a
desert or wilderness that they should pray in all four directions.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 278 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 29 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 319 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 265 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 239

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «لأَّ صَّ لاَّة َّ إ ِلأ َّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ » ق َّالَّ ق ُّل َّث ُّ و َّإ َّي ْن َّ جَّ ذ ُّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ ق َّال
َّ «مَّ ا ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْمَّس ْ زِق ِ وَّ إَّلْمَّع ْ زِب ِ ق ِن ْلَّه كُّل ُّهُّ» ق َّالَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّمَّن ْ صَّ ل َّى لِع َّي ْ زِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ إ َّوْ ق ِى ي َّوْ مِ ع ُّي ْمٍ ق ِى ع َّي ْ زِ إَّلْوَّ ق ْث ِ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّعِي ذ .
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There is no prayer except toward the Qiblah."
Zurarah asked: "And where is the boundary of the Qiblah?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "The entire area between the east and the west is the Qiblah."
Zurarah then asked: "What if someone prays facing a direction other than the Qiblah,
or on a cloudy day when they miss the correct time?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They must repeat the prayer”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 278 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 540 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 312 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 137 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 2, p. 186

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:

ْق َّا ِن َّ إَّلل َّهَّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ ي َّق ُّولُّ لِن َّن ِي ِّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق ِى إَّلْق َّزِي ص َّ ه ِ «ق َّوَّ لِّ وَّ ج ْ هَّك َّ س َّ ط َّزَّ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ إ لْحَّ زٰ إمِ وَّ جَّ ي ْث ُّ مٰ ا
»ُّكُّن ْي ُّمْ ق َّوَّ ل ُّوإ وُّج ُّ وهَّكُّمْ س َّ طْ زَّة
َّق َّق ُّمْ مُّ ن ْي َّصِ ن اً» ق َّا ِن َّ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق َّالَّ «مَّ ن ْ لَّمْ ي ُّق ِمْ صُّ لْن َّهُّ ق َّلا
ْصَّ لاَّة َّ لَّهُّ وَّ إِج ْ س َّ غْ ن ِن َّصَّ زِك َّ لِل َّهِ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّزْق َّع َّ هُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلس َّ مَّاءِ وَّ لْي َّكُّن ْ جِ ذ َّإءَّ وَّ ج ْ هِك َّ ق ِى مَّ وْ ص ِ غِ سُّ ح ُّ وذِك .
english_text:
In another narration, the Imam said :
"Then turn your face toward the Qiblah and do not turn your face away from the Qiblah,
lest your prayer become invalid. Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His
Prophet in the obligatory prayer:
'Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144); and wherever
you are, turn your faces toward it.' Stand upright."
Prophet {saws} said: "Whoever does not straighten their spine (while standing) has no
prayer."
And lower your gaze in humility before Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic; do not raise
it to the sky. Let your gaze be directed in front of you toward your place of prostration”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 278 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 312

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ لِز ُّرَّإرَّة:
ِ«لأَّ ي ُّعَّاذُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ إ ِلأ َّ مِن ْ ج َّ مْ سَّ ه ٍ إَّلط َّ هُّورِ وَّ إَّلْوَّ ق ْث ِ وَّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ وَّ إَّلز ُّكُّوعِ وَّ إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذ .

. على إلأ رض وق ال ق ي ها:
إ ذ إ ي عزض لك سن غ وج ق ث ق وب إلصلاة ق اسي ق ن ل إلق ن له وصل صلاي ك ن الأي ماء، وإ ن ج س ي ث إلسن غ
.وي عزض لك ق ذر معه كي ف ذإر وصل ن الأي ماء
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said to Zurarah:
"The prayer is not to be repeated except for five things: purification (taharah), time
(observing the prayer time), facing the Qiblah, bowing (ruku'), and prostration
(Sujood)”.
commentary:
My father, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:
"If you want to perform a supererogatory (nafl) prayer while riding, pray and turn the
head of your mount in whatever direction it faces, whether toward the Qiblah or
otherwise, right or left. If you pray a mandatory (fardh) prayer while on the back of your
mount, face the Qiblah, say the opening takbir (Allahu Akbar), and then proceed in
whichever direction your mount takes you, reciting. When you wish to bow and
prostrate, bow and prostrate on something you have with you that is permissible to
prostrate upon. Do not pray a mandatory prayer in this manner unless there is a severe
necessity. If you are walking, follow the same procedure, but when you wish to
prostrate, you must prostrate on the ground."
The letter also stated : "If a wild animal approaches and you fear missing the prayer,
face the Qiblah and pray using gestures. If you fear the animal and it continues to circle
you, move with it as it moves and pray using gestures."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 279 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 1, p. 371 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 312 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 313 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 389 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 89 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 101 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 236

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:

ِ إَّلس َّ ق ِي ن َّه.
english_text:
It is narrated that "If the wind blows strongly upon someone on a ship, and they
are unable to turn toward the Qiblah, they should pray facing the front of the ship”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 280 • Al-Wafi, V. 7, p. 528 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 4, p. 321

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِإَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ِ «كُّل ُّ وَّ إعِ ظ ٍ ق ِن ْلَّه وَّ كُّل ُّ مَّ وْ عُّوط ٍ ق ِن ْلَّه لِلْوَّ إعِ ظ .
.ي عن ى ق ى إلح معه وإلعي ذي ن وصلاة إلأسي سق اء ق ى إلح طن ه ي سي ق ن لهم إلأمام و ي سي ق ن لون ه جي ى ي ق زع من ج طن ي ه
english_text:
The Prophet {saws}, said:
"Every preacher is a Qiblah, and every one being preached to is a Qiblah for the
preacher."
commentary:
This means that during the Jumu’ah sermon (Khutbah), the Eid prayers, and the prayer
for rain (Salat al-Istisqa), the Imam (preacher) faces the people, and they face him until
he completes his sermon.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّرَّج ُّ ل لِلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:

َّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي ُّق َّالُّ لَّهُّ إَّلْح َّ ذْ ى َّ» ق ُّلْث ُّ ن َّعَّمْ ق َّالَّ «ق َّاج ْ عَّلْهُّ عَّلَّى ي َّمِي ن ِك َّ وَّ إ ِذ َّإ كُّن ْث َّ عَّلَّى طَّ زِي ق ِ إَّلْحَّ ح ِّ ق َّاج ْ عَّلْهُّ ن َّي ْن َّ ك َّ ي ِق َّي ْك .
english_text:
A man said to Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"I am sometimes traveling and cannot determine the Qiblah at night."
The Imam asked: "Do you know the star that is called 'al-Jady' (the North Star)?"
The man replied: "Yes."
The Imam said: "Place it to your right, and if you are on the pilgrimage route, place it
between your shoulders”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 280 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 547 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 306

ي ِسْ غِ سِ ن ِي ن َّ مَّ ا إ َّطَّ اق ُّوةُّ مِن ْ صِ ي َّامِ إَّلْي َّوْ مِ ق َّا ِذ َّإ ع َّلَّن َّهُّمُّ إَّلْعَّطَّ س ُّ إ َّق ْطَّ زُّوإ .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"We command our children to pray when they are five years old, so you should instruct
your children to pray when they are seven years old.
We also command our children to fast when they are seven years old, as much as they
can bear of fasting for the day - whether it is until midday, more, or less. If thirst or
hunger overwhelms them, they may break their fast so that they can gradually get
accustomed to fasting and be able to bear it. So, instruct your children to fast when
they are nine years old, as much as they are capable of fasting for the day. If thirst
overwhelms them, they may break their fast."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE AGE AT WHICH CHILDREN ARE REQUIRED TO
english_text:
It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Qarin that He said:
"I asked Imam al-Ridha {a.s}, or he was asked while I was listening, about a man who
circumcises his son, and the boy does not pray for a day or two."
Imam {a.s} asked: "How old is the boy?"
The response was, "Eight years old."
Imam {a.s} said: "Glory be to Allah {SWT}! He leaves prayer?"
The narrator replied: "He is in pain."
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray to the extent that he is able."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 280 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 195 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p.

Chapter Title: THE AGE AT WHICH CHILDREN ARE REQUIRED TO PRAY
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Fadalah narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
and Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"When a boy reaches the age of three, he should be instructed to say 'la illaha illa Allah
{SWT}' seven times.
Then he is left until he completes three years, seven months, and twenty days, at
which point he is instructed to say 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah {saws}' seven
times.
He is then left until he reaches four years of age, after which he is instructed to say
seven times, 'May Allah {SWT} bless Muhammad and his family.'
He is then left until he turns five years old and is asked: 'Which hand is your right and
which is your left?' When he recognizes this, his face is turned toward the Qiblah, and
he is told to prostrate.
He is then left until he turns seven years old, at which point he is told to wash his face
and hands. When he washes them, he is told to pray.
He is then left until he reaches the age of nine. At nine, he is taught the proper way of
performing ablution (wudu) and is disciplined for neglecting it. He is also instructed to
perform prayer and disciplined for neglecting it.
When he has learned wudu and prayer, Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, forgives
him and his parents, if Allah {SWT} wills."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 281 • Al-Amali (by Al-Saduq) Vol. 1, p. 391 • Amali (by Al-Tusi) Vol. 1, p. 433 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 222 • Majmu’at Warram, Part 2, p. 21 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 195 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 21, p. 474 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 101, p.

ُّمَّ ن ِ إِي َّن َّعَّه .
english_text:
Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrate from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} :
"When the Messenger of Allah {saws} was taken on the night journey (Isra'), the time for
prayer arrived, and Archangel Jibril {a.s} called the adhan (call to prayer).
When He said 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar' (Allah {SWT} is the Greatest, Allah {SWT} is the
Greatest), the angels said 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.'
When He said 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah {SWT}' (I bear witness that there is no god but
Allah {SWT}), the angels said: 'He has renounced rivals (associating others with Allah
{SWT}).'
When He said 'Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah' (I bear witness that
Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah {saws}), the angels said: 'A Prophet has been sent.'
When He said 'Hayya 'ala as-Salah' (Come to prayer), the angels said: 'He calls to the
worship of his Lord {AZJ}.'
When He said 'Hayya 'ala al-Falah' (Come to success), the angels said: 'Success is for
the one who follows him.'".
references: Tafsir al-Ayashi, vol. 2, p. 278 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 281 • Ma’ani al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 387 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 557 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 417 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, vol. 3, p. 492 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 18, p. 344 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 143

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى مَّ ن ْصُّ ورُّ ن ْن ُّ جَّ ار ِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «هَّن َّظ ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ن ِالْأ َّذ َّإن ِ عَّلَّى

»ُّق َّالَّ «إُّذْ عُّ ن ِلاَّلأً ق َّعَّلِّمْ هُّ ق َّذَّعَّا ن ِلاَّلأً ق َّعَّل َّمَّه.
english_text:
Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said: "Archangel Jibril {a.s} descended with the adhan (call to prayer) upon
Messenger of Allah {saws} while his head was resting in the lap of Imam Ali {a.s}. Archangel
Jibril {a.s} pronounced the adhan and the iqamah (second call to prayer).
When the Messenger of Allah {saws} awoke, He said: 'O’ Ali, did you hear?'
Imam {a.s} replied: 'Yes, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}.'
He {saws} said: 'Did you memorize it?'
Imam {a.s} replied: 'Yes.'
The Prophet {saws} then said: 'Call Bilal and teach him,'
So Imam Ali {a.s} called Bilal and taught him."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 302 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 282 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 277 • Al-Waezin, Vol. 2, p. 313 • Al-Manaqib, Part 2, p. 238 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 558 • Wasail Al- Shia, Vol. 5, p. 369 • Ithbāt al-Hudāt, Part 1, p. 186 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 40, p. 62

english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"You may give the adhan (call to prayer) without being in a state of wudu (ritual purity),
wearing a single garment, whether standing or sitting, and in any direction you face.
However, when you perform the iqamah (second call to prayer), you must be in a state
of wudu, prepared for the prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 282 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 594 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 391 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 401

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated from Imam al-Ridha
{a.s} that He said: "A man may give the adhan (call to prayer) while sitting or while riding."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 282 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 593 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p.

Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"There is no issue if you give the adhan (call to prayer) while riding, walking, or without
wudu (ritual purity). However, do not perform the iqamah (second call to prayer) while
riding or sitting, unless there is an excuse, or if you are on slippery ground”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ِ«لِلْمُّو َّ ذ ِّن ِ ق ِي مَّا ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ وَّ إَّلْأ ِق َّامَّ ه ِ مِي ْلُّ إ َّج ْ زِ إَّلس َّ هِي ذِ إَّلْمُّي َّس َّ حِّ ظ
ِ ن ِذَّمِهِ ق ِى سَّ ن ِي لِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ» ق َّق َّالَّ عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «إ ِن َّهُّمْ ي َّح ْ ي َّلِذُّون َّ عَّلَّى إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ْ » ق َّق َّالَّ «كَّلا َّ إ ِن َّهُّ ي َّا ي ِى عَّلَّى
ِإَّلن َّاسِ ر َّمَّ ان ي َّطْ زَّجُّ ون َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن َّ عَّلَّى ص ُّ عَّق َّان ِهِمْ ق َّي ِلْك َّ لُّحُّ وم جَّ ز َّمَّ هَّا إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّى إَّلن َّار.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"The mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) has a reward between the adhan and the iqamah
equal to that of a martyr who is drenched in his blood in the way of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty
and Majestic."
Imam Ali {a.s} said: "People will compete over the adhan."
The Prophet replied: "No, there will come a time when people will leave the adhan to
their weak ones. These (mu'adhdhins) are people whose flesh Allah {SWT} has forbidden
for the Fire”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 283 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 32 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 283 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 565 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 372 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 147

arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّعَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
«إ ج ِ زُّ مَّ ا ق َّارَّق ْث ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ جَّ ن ِي ث َّ ق َّلْن ِى صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ «ي َّا عَّلِى ُّ إ ِذ َّإ
»ًصَّ ل َّي ْث َّ ق َّصَّ لِّ صَّ لاَّة َّ إ َّص ْ عَّف ِ مَّ ن ْ ج َّ لْق َّك َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّي َّح ِ ذ َّن َّ مُّو َّ ذ ِّن اً ي َّا ْج ُّ ذ ُّ عَّلَّى إ َّذ َّإن ِهِ إ َّج ْ زإ.
english_text:
Imam Ali {a.s} said:
"The last thing my beloved (the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his
family) said to me before parting was:
'O’ Ali, when you lead the prayer, lead it considering the weakest among those behind
you. And do not appoint a mu'adhdhin who takes payment for his adhan.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 283 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 283 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 592 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 447

arabic_text: ِ وَّ رَّوَّ ى ج َّ الِذُّ ن ْن ُّ ن َّح ِ ي حٍ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّلي َّكْن ِي زُّ ج َّ ز ْم ق ِى إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ مَّ غَّ إَّلْأ ِق ْصَّ احِ ن ِالْهَّاءِ وَّ إَّلْأ َّلِف .
english_text:
Khalid ibn Najih narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He
said: "The takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') in the adhan must be pronounced firmly, with
clear articulation of the 'ha' and 'alif'“.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 283 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 58 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 576 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 408

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي زٍ عَّن ْ إ َّجَّ ذِهِمَّا عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِن َّ ن ِلاَّلأً كَّان َّ عَّن ْذإً صَّ الِحاً ق َّق َّال
َّلأَّ إ ُّو َّ ذ ِّن ُّ لِأ َّجَّ ذٍ ن َّعْ ذ
ِرَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ق َّي ُّزِك َّ ي َّوْ مَّ ن ِذ ٍ جَّ ى َّ عَّلَّى ج َّ ي ْ زِ إَّلْعَّمَّل .
english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from one of the Imams {a.s} that He said:
"Bilal was a righteous servant who said:
'I will not call the adhan for anyone after the Messenger of Allah {saws}.'
Therefore, on that day, 'Hayya 'ala khayr al-'Amal' (Hasten to the best of deeds) was
left out."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 283 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 583 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 417 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 22, p. 142

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلس َّ زِى ِّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّه َّق َّالَّ: «مِن َّ إَّلس ُّ ن َّه ِ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّذ َّن َّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّص َّ غ
ِإ ِصْ ن َّعَّي ْ هِ ق ِى إ ُّذ ُّن َّي ْ ه .
english_text:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Sari reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said:
"It is part of the Sunnah (tradition) for a person giving the adhan (call to prayer) to place
his fingers in his ears."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 284 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 411

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text: َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى ج َّ الِذُّ ن ْن ُّ ن َّح ِ ي حٍ عَّن ْهُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ُّ و ِ إَّلْأ ِق َّامَّ ه ُّ مَّ ح ْ ز ُّومَّ ان ِ » وَّ ق ِى ج َّ ن َّزٍ إ ج َّ زَّ «مَّ وْ ق ُّوق َّان .
english_text:
Khalid ibn Najih narrated from Imam {a.s} that He said:
"The adhan and the iqamah must be recited with firmness."
In another narration, it states, "They must be delivered with a pause."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 284 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 577

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «لأَّ ي ُّح ْ ز ِي ك َّ مِن َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ إ ِلأ َّ مَّ ا إ َّسْ مَّع ْث َّ ن َّق ْسَّ ك َّ إ َّو ُّق َّهِمْ ي َّه
َّ وَّ إ َّق ْصِ حْ ن ِالْأ َّلِف ِ وَّ إَّلْهَّاءِ وَّ صَّ لِّ عَّلَّى إَّلن َّن ِى ِّ وَّ إ لِهِ صَّ لَّوَّ إب ُّ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْهِمْ كُّل َّمَّا ذ َّكَّزْ ي َّهُّ إ ْوْ ذ َّكَّزَّةُّ ذ َّإكِز عِ ن ْذَّك َّ ق ِى إ َّذ َّإن ٍ إ َّو
َّ ع َّي ْ زِةِ وَّ كُّل َّمَّا إِس ْ ي َّذ َّ صَّ وْ ي ُّك َّ مِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ إ َّن ْ ي ُّح ْ هِذَّ ن َّق ْ سَّ ك َّ كَّان َّ مَّ ن ْ ي َّسْ مَّغُّ إ َّكْي َّزَّ وَّ كَّان َّ إ َّج ْ زُّك َّ ق ِى ذ َّلِك َّ إ َّعْ ط َّ م .
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"The adhan is not sufficient for you unless you hear it yourself or understand it. Clearly
articulate the 'alif' and 'ha'."
Send blessings upon the Prophet and his family {a.s} whenever you mention him or hear
someone mention him, whether during the adhan or outside of it. The louder your
voice, without straining yourself, the more people will hear, and your reward will be
greater."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 284 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 574

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ مُّ عَّاوِي َّه ُّ ن ْن ُّ وَّ هْث ٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إِج ْ هَّزْ وَّ إِرْق َّغْ ن ِهِ صَّ وْ ي َّك َّ ق َّا ِذ َّإ إ َّق َّمْ ث
ًق َّذُّون َّ ذ َّلِك َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّن ْي َّط ِ زْ ن ِا َّذ َّإن ِك َّ وَّ إ ِق َّامَّ ي ِك َّ إ ِلأ َّ ذُّج ُّ ولَّ وَّ ق ْث ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ إُّجْ ذُّرْ إ ِق َّامَّ ي َّك َّ جَّ ذْ رإ .
english_text:
Muawiya ibn Wahb asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the
adhan (call to prayer).
The Imam said: "Raise your voice and speak loudly when giving the adhan. When
performing the iqamah (second call to prayer), use a slightly lower voice.
Do not delay your adhan and iqamah except until the time for prayer has arrived, and
recite the iqamah quickly (with fluidity)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْهُّ عَّ عَّم َّار إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى ُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ ق ُّمْ ث َّ إ ِلَّى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْق َّزِي ص َّ ه ِ ق َّا َّذ ِّن ْ وَّ إ َّق ِم َّوَّ إِق ْصِ لْ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ و
» ٍإَّلْأ ِق َّامَّ ه ِ ن ِق ُّعُّوذٍ إ َّوْ ن ِكَّلاَّمٍ إ َّوْ ي َّسْ ن ِي ح َّوَّ ق َّال ِسَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ كَّمِ إَّل َّذ ِى ي ُّح ْ ز ِى ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ وَّ إَّلْأ ِق َّامَّ ه ِ مِن َّ إَّلْق َّوْ لِ ق َّالَّ «إَّلْحَّ مْ ذُّ لِل َّه .
english_text:
It is narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} by 'Ammar al-Sabati
that He said: "When you stand for a mandatory prayer, give the adhan and the iqamah,
and separate between the adhan and the iqamah with sitting, speaking, or tasbih
(glorification of Allah {SWT})."
He (Ammar) asked: "What is the minimum that suffices between the adhan and the
iqamah in terms of speech?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Saying 'Alhamdulillah' (All praise belongs to Allah {SWT})."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 285 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 588

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a
man who gives the adhan (call to prayer) while walking, while not in a state of ritual
purity, or while riding an animal.
The Imam said: "Yes, it is permissible if the one giving the testimony of faith (in the
adhan) faces the Qiblah; there is no issue."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 285 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 56 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 598 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 403

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
وَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ ِإ ُّق ِي مَّث ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ جَّ زُّمَّ إَّلْكَّلاَّمُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْأ ِمَّ امِ وَّ عَّلَّى إ َّهْلِ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذ
» ٍإ ِلأ َّ ق ِى ي َّق ْذِي مِ إ ِمَّ ام
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Abu Ja'far {a.s} that He said:
"When the iqamah (second call to prayer) is pronounced, speaking becomes
prohibited for the Imam and the people of the mosque, except in the case of
appointing an Imam."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 285 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 385 • Al- Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 596 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 393

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِعَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
«ي َّو ُّم ُّكُّمْ إ َّق ْزَّو ُّكُّمْ وَّ ي ُّو َّ ذ ِّن ُّ لَّكُّمْ ج ِ ي َّارُّكُّمْ وَّ ق ِى
ْجَّ ذِي ث ٍ إ ج َّ زَّ إ َّق ْصَّ حُّ كُّم .
english_text:
Imam Ali {a.s} said that the Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"The one who leads you in prayer should be the one who has the most knowledge of
the Qur'an among you, and the one who calls the adhan (mu'adhdhin) should be the
best among you."
In another narration, it is said: "the most articulate among you."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 285 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 591

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ِرَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ُّ «مَّ ن ْ إ َّذ َّن َّ ق ِى مِصْ زٍ مِن ْ إ َّمْ صَّ ارِ إَّلْمُّسْ لِمِي ن َّ سَّ ن َّه ً وَّ ج َّ ن َّث ْ لَّهُّ إَّلْح َّ ن َّه .
english_text:
The Messenger, and his family, said:
"Whoever calls the adhan (call to prayer) in one of the cities of the Muslims for a year,
Paradise becomes obligatory for him."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 285 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 31 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 283 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 567 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 371 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 146

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"For the mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer), Allah {SWT} forgives him as far as his sight and
voice reach into the sky. Every moist and dry thing that hears him bears witness to his
truth. For every person who prays with him in his mosque, he receives a share, and for
every person who prays due to hearing his call, he earns a good deed."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق َّال ِعَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «مَّ ن ْ إ َّذ َّن َّ سَّ ن ْغَّ سِ ن ِي ن َّ مُّحْ ي َّسِ ن اً ج َّ اءَّ ي َّوْ مَّ إَّلْق ِي َّامَّ ه ِ لأَّ ذ َّن ْث َّ لَّه.
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said:
"Whoever calls the adhan (call to prayer) for seven years with the intention of seeking
Allah’s {SWT} reward will come on the Day of Judgment without any sins."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 286 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 31 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 283 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 567 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 371 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 374 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 146 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 149

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن ُّإَّلْمَّلاَّن ِكَّه َّ إ ِذ َّإ سَّ مِعَّث ِ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن َّ مِن ْ إ َّهْلِ إَّلْأ َّرْ ض ِ ق َّالَّث ْ هَّذ ِةِ إ َّصْ وَّ إب ُّ إ ُّم َّ ه ِ مُّحَّ م َّذٍ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّه َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ و
ْ إ لِهِ ن ِي َّوْ جِ ي ذِ إَّلل َّهِ ق َّي َّسْ ي َّع ْ ق ِزُّون َّ إَّلل َّهَّ لِأ ُّم َّ ه ِ مُّحَّ م َّذٍ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ جَّ ي َّى ي َّق ِ زُّع ُّوإ مِن ْ ي ِلْك َّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة .
english_text:
It is narrated: "When the angels hear the adhan (call to prayer) from the people
of the earth, they say,
'These are the voices of the nation of Muhammad {saws} declaring oneness of Allah {SWT}.'
They then seek forgiveness from Allah {SWT} for the nation of Muhammad until the prayer
is completed."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 286 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 376

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
َّو ْ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِن َّ إ َّذْ ن َّى مَّ ا ي ُّح ْ ز ِى مِن َّ إَّلْأ َّذ َّإن ِ إ َّن ْ ي َّق َّي َّي ِحَّ إَّلل َّي ْ لَّ ن ِا َّذ َّإن ٍ و
َّ إ ِق َّامَّ ه ٍ وَّ ي َّق ْي َّي ِحَّ إَّلن َّهَّارَّ ن ِا َّذ َّإن ٍ وَّ إ ِق َّامَّ ه ٍ وَّ ي ُّح ْ ز ِي ك َّ ق ِى سَّ ان ِزِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ إ ِق ٍ امَّ ه ن ِع َّي ْ زِ إ َّذ َّإن.
وج مغ رسول إلله صلى إلله علي ه وإ له ن ي ن إلط هز وإلعصز ن عزق ه ن ا ذ إن وإجذ وإ ق امي ي ن ، وج مغ ن ي ن إلمع زب وإلعس اء ن ح مغ
. ن ا ذ إن وإجذ وإ ق امي ي ن
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"The minimum that suffices for the adhan is to begin the night with an adhan and
iqamah and to begin the day with an adhan and iqamah. For the other prayers during
the day, an iqamah without an adhan suffices."
commentary:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} combined the Dhuhr (noon) and 'Asr (afternoon) prayers
at 'Arafat with one adhan and two iqamah, and he combined the Maghrib (sunset) and
'Isha (night) prayers at Muzdalifah with one adhan and two iqamah.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 286 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 80 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 4, p. 16 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 605 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 386

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ سِ ن َّان ٍ عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ اذِق ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ«إ َّن َّ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ج َّ مَّغَّ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلط ُّ هْ ز

english_text:
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} combined the Dhuhr (noon) and 'Asr (afternoon) prayers
with one adhan and two iqamah, and he combined the Maghrib (sunset) and 'Isha
(night) prayers in the same setting without any particular reason, using one adhan and
two iqamah”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 287 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 282 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p.

Chapter Title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS

ْ وَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّ مَّ ن َّ صَّ ل َّى ن ِا َّذ َّإن ٍ وَّ إ ِق َّامَّ ه ٍ صَّ ل َّى ج َّ لْق َّهُّ صَّ ق َّان ِ مِن َّ إَّلْمَّلاَّن ِكَّه ِ وَّ مَّ ن ْ صَّ ل َّى ن ِا ِق َّامَّ ه ٍ ن ِع َّي ْ زِ إ َّذ َّإن ٍ صَّ ل ى
