arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى إَّلْعَّلاَّءُّ عَّن ْ مُّ حَّ م َّذِ ن ْن ِ مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن ْ رَّج ًلٍ صَّ ل َّى إَّلط ُّ هْ زَّ ج َّ مْ سا
ْق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لأَّ ي َّذْ رِى ج َّ لَّسَّ ق ِى إَّلز َّإن ِعَّه ِ إ َّمْ لَّمْ ي َّح ْ لِس َّ ق َّلْي َّح ْ عَّلْ إ َّرْن َّغَّ رَّكَّعَّاب ٍ مِن ْهَّا إَّلط ُّ هْ زَّ وَّ ي َّح ْ لِسُّ وَّ ي َّي َّس َّ ه َّذُّ ي ُّم
ً ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ هُّوَّ ج َّ الِس رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ إ َّرْن َّغَّ سَّ ح َّ ذَّإب ٍ ق َّي ُّص ِ ي ق ُّهُّمَّا إ ِلَّى إَّلْح َّ امِسَّ ه ِ ق َّي َّكُّون ُّ ن َّاق ِلَّه .
english_text:
Al-Ala reported from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"I asked him about a man who prayed Dhuhr five rak'ahs. He said: 'If he does not know
whether he sat in the fourth rak'ah or not, let him treat it as four rak'ahs for the Dhuhr
prayer, then he should sit, perform the tashahhud, and then pray two rak'ahs while
sitting and perform four sajdahs. He should then add these to the fifth rak'ah, and it
will be considered a nafl (voluntary) prayer.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 349 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 965 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 233 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 202

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إَّلْق ُّص َّ ي ْلُّ ن ْن ُّ ي َّسَّ ارٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِعَّن ِ إَّلس َّ هْ وِ ق َّق َّالَّ «مَّ ن ْ ي َّحْ ق َّظ ْ سَّ هْ وَّ ةُّ ق َّا َّي َّم َّهُّ ق َّلَّي ْ سَّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
سَّ ح ْ ذَّي َّا إَّلس َّ هْ وِ وَّ إ ِن َّمَّا إَّلس َّ هْ وُّ عَّلَّى مَّ ن ْ لَّمْ ي َّذْ رِ إ َّ ر َّإذَّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ إ َّمْ ن َّق َّضَّ مِن ْهَّا .
english_text:
Al-Fudail ibn Yasar asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
forgetfulness in prayer.
Imam said: "Whoever remembers his forgetfulness and corrects it, there is no need for
him to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (Sajdatay al-Sahw). However,
forgetfulness applies to the one who does not know whether he has added to or
missed part of his prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ عَّن ْهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ لَّمْ ي َّذْ رِ إ َّرْن َّعاً صَّ ل َّي ْ ث َّ إ َّوْ ج َّ مْ ساً إ َّم ْر ِذْ ب َّ إ َّمْ ن َّق َّصْ ث َّ ق َّي َّس َّ ه َّذ
ًوَّ سَّ لِّمْ وَّ إُّسْ ح ُّ ذْ سَّ ح ْ ذَّ ي َّى ِ إَّلس َّ هْ وِ ن ِع َّي ْ زِ رُّكُّوعٍ وَّ لأَّ ق ِزَّإءَّة ٍ ي َّي َّس َّ ه َّذُّ ق ِي هِمَّا ي َّس َّ ه ُّذإً ج َّ ق ِي ق ا .
english_text:
Al-Halabi narrated from him (the Prophet {a.s}) that He said:
“If you are unsure whether you prayed four or five rak'ahs, or whether you added or
omitted something, then perform the tashahhud (testification of faith), say salaam
(greeting of peace), and prostrate two prostrations of forgetfulness without bowing or
reciting (in them), and you will make a brief tashahhud in both of them.”
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 350 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 196 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 380 • Nuzhat al-Nāẓir, Part 1, p. 40 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 105 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 988 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 224 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 234 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 206 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 226

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}
was asked about a man who entered the prayer with the Imam and was already behind
by one rak'ah.
When the Imam completed the prayer and left with the congregation, the man
remembered that he had missed one rak'ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should repeat one rak'ah."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 350 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 405 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 346 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 367 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 198 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 8, p. 202

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذُّ إَّلز َّجْ مَّن ِ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْحَّ ح َّ اح ِ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: ق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل ،ُّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم
َّرَّج ُّ ل لأَّ ي َّذْ رِى إ َّ ي ِن ْي َّي ْن ِ صَّ ل َّى إ َّمْ ي َّلاَّي اً إ َّمْ إ َّرْن َّعاً ق َّق َّال
«ي ُّصَّ لِّى رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ مِن ْ ق ِي َّامٍ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّسَّ لِّمُّ ي ُّم َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ هُّوَّ ج َّ الِس .
english_text:
Abdurrahman ibn Al-Hajjaj narrated from Abu Ibrahim who said:
"I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who does not know
whether he prayed two, three, or four rak'ahs.
Imam {a.s} said: 'He should pray two rak'ahs standing, then make salaam (salutation),
then pray two more rak'ahs while sitting.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 350 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 981 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 8, p. 222 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 184

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ِوَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ عَّلِى ِّ ن ْن ِ إ َّن ِى جَّ مْ ز َّة َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْعَّن ْذِ إَّلص َّ الِحِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ ل
َّ ي َّس ُّ ك ُّ ق َّلاَّ ي َّذْ رِى إ
ُّوَّ إجِ ذَّة ً صَّ ل َّى إ َّوِ إِي ْن َّي َّي ْن ِ إ َّوْ ي َّلاَّي اً إ َّوْ إ َّرْن َّعاً ي َّلْي َّن ِسُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ صَّ لاَّي ُّهُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ك »ل ُّ ذ َّإ
َّ ق َّق ُّلْث ُّ ن َّعَّمْ ق َّالَّ «ق َّلْي َّمْ ض ِ ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ وَّ لْي َّي َّعَّو َّذ ْ ن ِالل َّهِ مِن ُّإَّلس َّ ي ْطَّ ان ِ إَّلز َّج ِ ي مِ ق َّا ِن َّهُّ ي ُّوس ِ ك ُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّذ ْ هَّث َّ عَّن ْه.
english_text:
It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamza that he asked the Righteous Servant
(Imam Musa al-Kadhim {a.s}) about a man who doubts and does not know whether he
has prayed one, two, three, or four units (rak'ahs) of prayer. His prayer becomes
confusing for him.
Imam said: "All of that [doubt] applies."
I said: "Yes."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Then let him continue with his prayer and seek refuge in Allah {SWT}
from the accursed Satan, for it is likely that this [state of doubt] will go away."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 350 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 188 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 374 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 228 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 273

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى سَّ هْ لُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْي َّسَّ غِ ق ِى ذ َّلِك َّ عَّن ِ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «ي َّن ْن ِى عَّلَّى ي َّق ِي ن ِهِ وَّ ي َّس ِ ح ُّ ذُّ سَّ ح ْ ذَّي َّى
ًإَّلس َّ هْ وِ ن َّعْ ذَّ إَّلي َّسْ لِي مِ وَّ ي َّي َّس َّ ه َّذُّ ي َّس َّ ه ُّذإً ج َّ ق ِي ق ا .
english_text:
Sahl ibn al-Yas'a narrated regarding this matter from Imam al-Ridha {a.s}, who
said:
"He should base his actions on certainty and perform the two prostrations of
forgetfulness after the Tasleem (salutation), and make a brief tashahhud in them."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ ق َّذْ رُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّهُّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى رَّكْعَّه ً مِن ْ ق ِي َّامٍ وَّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ مِن ْ ج ُّ لُّوس.
ولي سث هذ ة إلأ ج ن ار ن مح ي لق ه وصاجث إلسهو ن الح ي ار ن ا ى ج ن ز من ها إ ج ذ ق هو مصي ث.
english_text:
It has been narrated: "He should pray one rak'ah standing and two rak'ahs
sitting."
commentary:
These narrations are not contradictory, and the person with doubt has the choice to
follow any of these reports, and whichever one they follow, they are correct.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ إ ِسْ حَّ اق َّ ن ْن ِ عَّم َّارٍ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: ق َّالَّ لِى إ َّن ُّو إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلْأ َّو َّ لُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «إ ِذ َّإ س َّ ك كْث َّ ق َّان ْن ِ عَّلَّى
إَّلْي َّق ِي ن ِ » ق َّالَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ هَّذ َّإ ْإ َّصْ ل ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّم.
english_text:
It is narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
"Abul Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} said to me: 'When you are in doubt, rely on what you are
certain of.'
I said: 'Is this a principle?'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Yes.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 351 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 987

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّن ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ إ َّن ِى ي َّعْ ق ُّورٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم :
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ مِن َّ إَّلْمَّكْي ُّون َّه ِ ق َّلا
ْي َّح ْ لِسُّ ق ِي هِمَّا ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ ذ َّكَّزَّ وَّ هُّوَّ ق َّان ِم ق ِى إَّلي َّالِي َّه ِ ق َّلْي َّح ْ لِسْ وَّ إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّذ ْ كُّزْ جَّ ي َّى رَّكَّغَّ ق َّل ُّي ُّي ِم َّ صَّ لاَّي َّهُّ ي ُّم َّ ي َّسْ ح ُّ ذ
َّ سَّ ح ْ ذَّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ هُّوَّ ج َّ الِس ق َّن ْلَّ إ َّن ْ ي َّي َّكَّل َّم .
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
a man who prays two rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer but does not sit in them.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he remembers while standing in the third rak'ah, he should sit. If he
does not remember until he has already bowed, he should complete his prayer, then
prostrate two prostrations while sitting before speaking."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 351 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 159 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 941

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّ حَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِن ْ س َّ ك َّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ن َّعْ ذَّ مَّ ا صَّ ل َّى ق َّلَّم
ي َّذْ رِ إ َّ ي َّلاَّي اً صَّ ل َّى
َّإ َّمْ إ َّرْن َّعاً وَّ كَّان َّ ي َّق ِي ن ُّهُّ جِ ي ن َّ إِن ْصَّ زَّف َّ إ َّن َّهُّ كَّان َّ ق َّذْ إ َّي َّم َّ لَّمْ ي ُّعِذِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ و
َّكَّان َّ جِ ي ن َّ إِن ْصَّ زَّف َّ إ َّق ْزَّب َّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْحَّ ق ِّ مِن ْهُّ ن َّعْ ذ
َّ ذ َّلِك .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrates from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s}:
"If a man is uncertain after he has prayed and does not know whether he prayed three
or four rak'ahs, and when he finishes, he is certain that he has completed it, he does
not need to repeat the prayer. At the time of his departure (after the prayer), his
certainty is closer to the truth than it was afterward."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 352 • Al-Wafi, V. 8, p. 999 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p.

Chapter Title: THE RULES OF FORGETFULNESS (SAHW) IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ ق ِى ن َّوَّ إذِرِ إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مَّ ن ْن ِ هَّاس ِ م:

english_text:
In the Nawaadir of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, it is narrated that Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about an Imam leading a prayer with four or five
people, and two of them testify that they prayed three rak'ahs, while three testify that
they prayed four rak'ahs. Some say, "Stand up," and others say, "Sit down," and the
Imam is unsure, either leaning towards one or being uncertain. What should be done?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no fault on the Imam if those behind him agree that he made
a mistake. There is no fault on those behind the Imam if the Imam has not erred. There
is no confusion in the Maghrib prayer, nor in Fajr, nor in the first two rak'ahs of any
prayer.
If there is disagreement among those behind the Imam, then both the Imam and the
congregation should take precaution and repeat the prayer, acting decisively."
commentary:
And if you forget which prayer you prayed and do not know if it was two, three, or four
rak'ahs, then pray two rak'ahs, three rak'ahs, or four rak'ahs. If it was Dhuhr, Asr, or
Isha, you have prayed four. If it was Maghrib, you have prayed three. If it was Fajr, you
have prayed two.And if you spoke during your prayer by mistake, such as saying,
"Straighten the rows," then complete your prayer and perform two prostrations of
forgetfulness.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 352 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 241 • Mustadrak Al- Wasail, Vol. 6, p. 419

english_text:
It is narrated: "If someone speaks during their prayer out of forgetfulness,
they should make additional takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar'). But if someone speaks
during their prayer intentionally, they must repeat the prayer. If someone makes an
utterance during their prayer, they have indeed spoken”.
If you forget the Dhuhr (noon) prayer until the sun sets and you have already prayed
Asr (afternoon) prayer, then if it is possible to perform Dhuhr before missing Maghrib
(sunset) prayer, you should start with Dhuhr. Otherwise, pray Maghrib first and then
perform Dhuhr afterward. If you remember Dhuhr while you are performing Asr, then
consider the prayer you are performing as Dhuhr - unless you fear that the time for Asr
will expire. Then perform Asr after that. If you fear that the time for Asr will expire,
perform Asr first.
If you forget both Dhuhr and Asr prayers and remember them at sunset, then perform
Dhuhr first and then Asr, provided that you do not fear missing one of them. If you fear
missing one, perform Asr first, so that neither of them is completely missed. Then,
afterward, perform the Dhuhr prayer immediately after. Whenever you miss a prayer,
perform it as soon as you remember. If you remember it while you are in the time of
another obligatory prayer, perform the current prayer first, then perform the missed
prayer afterward.
If a person misses both Dhuhr and Asr prayers and remembers them with enough time
left in the day to perform both, they should start with Dhuhr and then perform Asr. If
there is only enough time to perform one of the two prayers, they should begin with
Asr. If there is enough daylight left to perform six units of prayer, they should begin with
Dhuhr.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 354 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 877 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 281 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 206

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"No one misses a prayer who truly desires to pray. The prayer of the day does not miss
until the sun sets, and the prayer of the night does not miss until dawn breaks."
commentary:
This applies to the person who is forced, ill, or forgetful.
If you forget to pray Maghrib and Isha, and remember them before dawn, pray both if
there is still time. If you fear one of them will be missed, begin with Isha. If you
remember them after Fajr, pray Fajr first, then Maghrib, then Isha before sunrise. If you
miss Fajr until the sun rises, pray two rak'ahs for the missed prayer, then perform Fajr.
If you forget the tashahhud (testification) in the second rak'ah and remember it in the
third, pause and sit for the tashahhud as long as you have not yet bowed. If you
remember after bowing, continue the prayer, and when you finish, perform two
prostrations of forgetfulness and recite the missed tashahhud during them.
If you raise your head from the second sajdah in the fourth rak'ah and then break your
wudu, if you have said the shahada (testification), your prayer is complete. If you have
not yet said it, your prayer is invalid; you must perform wudu again and return to your
place, then perform the tashahhud.
If you forget the tashahhud or the Tasleem (salutation) and realize it after you have
moved from your prayer mat, face the Qiblah whether standing or sitting, then recite
the tashahhud and Tasleem.
If someone is certain that they prayed six rak'ahs, they should repeat the prayer. If
someone is unsure how many rak'ahs they prayed, and their doubt does not settle on
any particular number, they should repeat the prayer.
If a man prays next to another and mistakenly stands on his left, but later realizes while
in prayer, he should turn to his right. If someone needs to perform prostrations of
forgetfulness but forgets to do so, they should perform them whenever they
remember.
If a person joins a group in prayer thinking it is the first rak'ah, but it is Asr, they should
make it the first rak'ah and complete Asr after. Similarly, if someone stands in a prayer
mistakenly thinking it is a voluntary prayer but later realizes it is obligatory, their prayer
is valid as it began. It is permissible for someone to pray Dhuhr behind someone
praying Asr, but it is not permissible to pray Asr behind someone praying Dhuhr unless
they mistakenly think it is Asr, then they pray Asr with him. This will count as their Asr
prayer.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 355 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 256 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 260 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 273 • Al-Sarayer, Part 3, p. 602 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 289 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 159 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 363

english_text:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Rabati, from Saeed Al-A'raj who said:
"I heard Abu Abdullah {a.s} (Imam Ja'far Al-Sadiq {a.s}) say:
'Indeed, Allah {SWT}, the Blessed and Exalted, caused His Messenger {saws} to sleep
through the Fajr prayer until the sun had risen. Then he stood up and prayed the two
rak'ahs before Fajr, followed by the Fajr prayer. He forgot during his prayer, so he made
a mistake and gave the salutation in two rak'ahs. Then he described what Dhul-
Shimalayn said (who pointed out the mistake).
He did this out of mercy for this ummah, so that no Muslim man would be reproached
if he sleeps through his prayer or makes a mistake in it, and so that it would be said:
'This happened to the Messenger of Allah {saws}.'".
commentary:
The compiler of this book (may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him) said:
The extremists and those who deny the Imamate, may Allah {SWT} curse them, deny the
possibility of the Prophet forgetting in prayer. They claim that if it was possible for him
to forget in prayer, it would also be possible for him to forget in delivering the message,
just as prayer is an obligatory act upon him, so too is the message (tabligh).
This claim does not apply to us because all circumstances common to others also
apply to the Prophet {saws} in matters like prayer. He was bound by the same obligations
in prayer as anyone who is not a Prophet, though the exception for him is his
Prophethood and the duty of delivering the message (tabligh). There is no reason to
assume that the Prophet would forget in delivering the message as he does in prayer,
since prayer is a specific form of worship, whereas delivering the message is a
different task.
It should be noted that the Prophet’s forgetfulness or mistakes are not like our
mistakes. His forgetfulness is willed by Allah {SWT}, and He made the Prophet forget to
show that he is a human being, so that people would not make him an object of
worship. Allah {SWT} alone is the one who does not sleep or forget. And the forgetfulness
of the Prophet is meant to teach the people the rulings of forgetfulness, as it is not
from the devil, who has no power over the Prophet {a.s} or the Imams {a.s}. His power is
only over those who follow him and commit shirk with him.
Some opponents have claimed that there was no person called Dhul-Yadayn (the man
who pointed out the mistake). They deny his existence and the reports about him. But
this is false. Dhul-Yadayn is known, and he was Abu Muhammad ibn Umayr ibn Abd
Amr, and he has been reported about by both opponents and supporters.
Our teacher, Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah {SWT} have
mercy on him), used to say: 'The first degree of extremism is to deny the Prophet’s
forgetfulness. If such reports were to be rejected, all reports would have to be
rejected, which would invalidate the entire religion and its law. I intend to write a
separate book to establish the forgetfulness of Prophet {saws} and refute those who deny
it, Insha’Allah {SWT}.'
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 358 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1019 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 17, p. 106

english_text:
Hammad ibn Uthman asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} a person
who missed part of their prayers and then remembered it at sunrise or sunset.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should pray as soon as he remembers”.

ْ «ي ُّصَّ لِّى إَّلْمَّزِي ض ُّ ق َّان ِماً ق َّا ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّق ْ ذِرْ عَّلَّى ذ َّلِك َّ صَّ ل َّى ج َّ الِساً ق َّا ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّق ْذِرْ إ َّن

ُّ عَّي ْن َّي ْ هِ رَّق ْغَّ رَّإ ْسِ هِ مِن َّ إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذِ ي ُّم َّ ي َّي َّس َّ ه َّذُّ وَّ ي َّن ْصَّ زِف .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The sick person should pray standing. If they are unable to do so, they should pray
sitting. If they cannot pray sitting, they should pray lying down.
They should say the Takbir, then recite.
When they want to bow, they should close their eyes and then say the Tasbih
(SubhanAllah {SWT}). When they say Tasbih, they should open their eyes.
The opening of the eyes represents the raising of their head from the bowing position.
When they want to prostrate, they should close their eyes and then say the Tasbih.
When they say Tasbih, they should open their eyes, and the opening of the eyes
represents raising their head from the prostration position. Then they should recite the
testimony of faith (Tashahhud) and end the prayer”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK
english_text:
It was asked about a sick person who is unable to sit - whether they can pray
while lying down and placing something on their forehead.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, Allah {SWT} has not burdened them beyond their capacity."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 361 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 485

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS

english_text:
Samahat ibn Mehran asked about a man who has an eye condition (cataracts
or similar) and undergoes a procedure to remove the issue, requiring him to lie on his
back for many days - forty days, or possibly fewer or more. As a result, he can only
perform his prayers by gestures due to his condition.
The response was: "There is no harm in that."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Bazi' the Muezzin asked Imam {a.s}: "I intend to undergo a procedure on my
eye."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Do it."
Bazi' then said: "But they claim that I will be made to lie on my back for several days
and will not be able to perform prayer while sitting."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Do it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 361 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 484

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS

ْ وَّ ج ِهَّهُّ ن َّحْ وَّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ وَّ ج َّ عَّلَّ سُّ ح ُّ وذَّةُّ إ َّج ْ ق َّض َّ مِن ْ رُّكُّوعِ ه .
وي ح ور للمزي ض إ ن ي صلى إلق زي ص ه على إلذإن ه ي سي ق ن ل ن ه إلق ن له وي ح ز ي ه ق اي حه إلكي اب ، وي ص غ ج ن هي ه ق ى إلق زي ص ه على ما
إ مكن ه من س ى ، وي و مى ق ى إلن اق له إ ي ماء.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"A sick person should pray standing, and if he cannot, he should pray sitting. If he
cannot do that, he should pray on his right side. If he cannot do that, he should pray
on his left side. If he cannot do even that, he should lie down, face the Qibla, and make
gestures for his prayers, with his prostration lower than his bowing."
commentary:
It is permissible for a sick person to perform the obligatory prayer while riding an
animal, as long as they face the Qibla. It is sufficient for them to recite Surah Al-Fatiha
and to place their forehead on whatever is possible for prostration. In supererogatory
(non-obligatory) prayers, they may gesture instead.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 362 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1040 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 485 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 545 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 3, p. 529

ُّعِ ن ْذَّةُّ وَّ إ َّسْ مِعُّوة .
english_text:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} visited a man from the Ansar who was struck by a strong
wind. The man asked:
'O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, how should I pray?'
The Prophet {a.s} replied: 'If you are able to, seat him. If not, direct him towards the
Qibla, and command him to gesture with his head (for prayer). Make his prostration
lower than his bowing. If he is unable to recite (the Quran), then recite for him and
make him listen.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 362 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1042 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 485

arabic_text:
ِ وَّ رَّوَّ ى عُّمَّزُّ ن ْن ُّ إ ُّذ َّي ْن َّه َّ عَّن ْ ر ُّرَّإرَّة َّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن َّإَّلْمَّزِي ض ِ كَّي ْف َّ ي َّسْ ح ُّ ذُّ ق َّق َّال
َّ«عَّلَّى ج ُّ مْ زَّة ٍ إ َّوْ عَّلَّى مِزْوَّ جَّ ه ٍ إ َّوْ عَّلَّى سِ وَّ إك ٍ ي ُّزْق َّغُّ إ ِلَّي ْ هِ وَّ هُّوَّ إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ مِن َّ إَّلْأ ِي مَّاءِ إ ِن َّمَّا كَّز َّة مَّ ن ْ كَّز َّةَّ إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذَّ عَّلَّى
ْإَّلْمِزْوَّ جَّ ه ِ مِن ْ إ َّج ْ لِ إَّلْأ َّوْ ي َّان ِ إَّل َّي ِى كَّان َّث ْ ي ُّع َّن َّذُّ مِن ْ ذُّون ِ إَّلل َّهِ وَّ إ ِن َّا لَّمْ ن َّعْ ن ُّذْ ع َّي ْ زَّ إَّلل َّهِ ق َّظ ُّ ق َّاسْ ح ُّ ذُّوإ عَّلَّى إَّلْمِزْوَّ جَّ ه ِ و
ٍعَّلَّى إَّلسِّ وَّ إك ِ وَّ عَّلَّى عُّوذ .
english_text:
Umar ibn Udhaynah narrated from Zurarah from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-
Baqir {a.s} that he asked about how a sick person should perform prostration (Sujood).
Abu Ja'far said: "On a small mat (Khumrah), a fan (Miroohah), or a stick (Miswak) that
is raised to them, and this is better than mere gesturing. The disapproval from some
for prostrating on a fan was due to the idols that were worshiped besides Allah {SWT}.
However, we have never worshiped anything besides Allah {SWT}, so prostrate on the
fan, on the Miswak, or on a piece of wood."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 362 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 364

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمَّزِي ض ِ هَّلْ ي َّق ْص ِ ى إَّلص َّ لَّوَّ إب ِ إ ِذ َّإ إ ُّع ْ مِى َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ إ ِلأ
إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ إَّل َّي ِى إ َّق َّاق َّ ق ِي هَّا.
english_text:
The Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-about a sick person who
faints. Does he need to make up the prayers he missed during his fainting?
Imam {a.s} replied: "No, except for the prayer in which he regained consciousness”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ كَّي َّث َّ إ َّي ُّوب ُّ ن ْن ُّ ن ُّوحٍ إ ِلَّى إ َّن ِى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلي َّالِث ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم :
ْي َّسْ ا َّلُّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمُّع ْ مَّى عَّلَّي ْ هِ ي َّوْ ماً إ َّوْ إ َّكْي َّزَّ هَّل
َّ ي َّق ْص ِ ى مَّ ا ق َّاي َّهُّ مِن َّ إَّلص َّ لَّوَّ إب ِ إ َّمْ لأَّ ق َّكَّي َّث َّ «لأَّ ي َّق ْص ِ ى إَّلص َّ وْ مَّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّق ْص ِ ى إَّلص َّ لاَّة.
english_text:
Ayoub ibn Noah wrote to Abu Al-Hasan al-Third (Imam Musa al-Kadhim) {a.s}
asking whether a person who is unconscious for a day or more needs to make up the
prayers (salat) they missed.
The Imam wrote in response, "He does not have to make up the fasting (sawm) or the
prayers (salat)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ مَّ هْ ز ِي َّار :
ِعَّن ْ هَّذ ِةِ إَّلْمَّسْ ا َّلَّه ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ي َّق ْص ِ ى إَّلص َّ وْ مَّ وَّ لأَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ وَّ كُّل ُّ مَّ ا ع َّلَّث َّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
ِق َّالل َّهُّ إ َّوْ لَّى ن ِالْعُّذ ْ ر .
ق ا ما إلأج ن ار إلي ى روي ث ق ى إلمع مى علي ه إ ن ه ي ق ص ى ج مي غ ما ق اي ه، وما روى إ ن ه ي ق ص ى صلاة س هز، وما روى إ ن ه ي ق ص ى
صلاة ي لاي ه إ ي ام ، ق هى صحي حه ولكن ها على إلأسي حن اب لأ على إلأي ح اب وإلأ صل إ ن ه لأ ق ص اء علي ه.
english_text:
Ali ibn Mahziyar asked about this issue, and Imam {a.s} replied:
"He does not have to make up the fasting (sawm) or the prayers (salat), and everything
that overwhelms a person due to God's will, God is more deserving of granting the
excuse."
commentary:
As for the narrations that mention the unconscious person making up all the missed
prayers, or that they must make up the prayers for a month, or for three days, these
are correct but are understood to be recommended (mustahabb) and not obligatory
(wajib). The principle is that there is no obligation to make up the missed prayers or
fasts.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}:
"The person who has a frequent (or overpowering) stomach condition should perform
ablution (wudu) and continue with their prayer (salat)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 363 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 26 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p.

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّ مُّ زَّإر ِمُّ ن ْن ُّ جَّ كِي مٍ إَّلْأ َّر ْذِى:
ُّمَّ زِص ْ ث ُّ إ َّرْن َّعَّه َّ إ َّس ْ هُّزٍ لَّمْ إ َّي َّن َّق َّلْ ق ِي هَّا ق َّق ُّلْث ُّ ذ َّلِك َّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم
ُّق َّق َّالَّ «لَّي ْسَّ عَّلَّي ْ ك َّ ق َّص َّ اء إ ِن َّ إَّلْمَّزِي ض َّ لَّي ْسَّ كَّالص َّ حِ ي حِ كُّل ُّ مَّ ا ع َّلَّث َّ إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّعَّالَّى عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّالل َّه ْ إ َّوْ لَّى ن ِالْعُّذ ِر.
english_text:
Murazim ibn Hakim al-Azdi said:
"I was ill for four months and did not perform any voluntary prayers (nawafil) during
that time.
I mentioned this to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s},
Imam {a.s} said:
'There is no obligation upon you for making up those prayers. Indeed, the sick person
is not like the healthy one. Whatever Allah {SWT} has made overpowering upon him, Allah
{SWT} is more entitled to excuse him.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 364 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 80

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّسْ ي َّن ِذَّ إ ِلَّى
ٍ جَّ ان ِظِ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ وَّ هُّوَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إ َّوْ ي َّص َّ غَّ ي َّذَّةُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْحَّ ان ِظِ وَّ هُّوَّ ق َّان ِم مِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ مَّ زَّض ٍ وَّ لأَّ عِ ل َّه ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ » وَّ عَّن
َّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّة ٍ ق َّزِي ص َّ ه ٍ ق َّي َّ ق ُّومُّ ق ِى إَّلز َّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ إَّلْأ َّو َّلَّي َّي ْن ِ هَّلْ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لَّهُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّي َّن َّاوَّ لَّ ج َّ ان ِث َّ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذِ ق َّي َّن ْهَّض
ِي َّسْ ي َّعِي ن ُّ ن ِهِ عَّلَّى إَّلْق ِي َّامِ مِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ ص َّ عْ ف ٍ وَّ لأَّ عِ ل َّه ٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} on whether
it is permissible for a man to lean against the wall of the mosque while he is praying,
or to place his hand on the wall while standing, without any illness or condition?"
He {a.s} replied: "There is no harm in that."
He also asked: "What about a man who is praying the obligatory prayer, and in the first
two rak'ahs, he stands up and leans on the side of the mosque to help him rise, without
any weakness or condition?"
He {a.s} replied: "There is no harm in that either."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 364 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 326 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 899 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 499

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّ جَّ م َّاذُّ ن ْن ُّ عُّي ْ مَّان:
َّ ق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّذِ إِس ْ ي َّذ َّ عَّلَّى َّ إَّلْق ِي َّامُّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ إ َّرَّذْ ب
إ َّن ْ ي ُّذْ رِك َّ صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلْق َّان ِمِ ق َّاق ْزَّإ ْ وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ ج َّ الِس ق َّا ِذ َّإ ن َّق ِى َّ مِن َّ إَّلس ُّ ورَّة ِ إ ي َّي َّان ِ ق َّق ُّمْ وَّ إ َّي ِم َّ مَّ ا ِ ن َّق َّ ى َّ وَّ إِرْكَّغْ وَّ إُّسْ ح ُّ ذْ ق َّذ َّإك
ِصَّ لاَّة ُّ إَّلْق َّان ِم .
english_text:
Hamad ibn Othman said: I said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
'The standing in prayer has become very difficult for me.'
He {a.s} replied: 'When you want to catch the prayer of the one standing, recite while
sitting. When there remain two verses of the surah, then stand up and complete the
remaining part, and bow and prostrate. That is the prayer of the one standing.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 364 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 295 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 113 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 498

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ سَّ هْ لُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْي َّسَّ غِ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلْأ َّو َّلَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إَّلن َّاق ِلَّه َّ ق َّاعِ ذإً وَّ لَّي ْسَّ ن ِهِ عِ ل َّه ق ِى
ِسَّ ق َّزٍ إ َّوْ جَّ ص َّ زٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِه.
english_text:
Sahl ibn al-Yas'a asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} about a man who prays a
voluntary prayer sitting while he does not have any illness, whether in travel or while
at home.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال إ َّن ُّو ٍن َّصِ ي ز:
ٍ ق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِن َّا ن َّي َّحَّ ذ َّب ُّ وَّ ن َّق ُّولُّ مَّ ن ْ صَّ ل َّى وَّ هُّوَّ ج َّ الِس مِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ عِ ل َّه
ْكَّان َّث ْ صَّ لاَّي ُّهُّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ن ِزَّكْعَّه ٍ وَّ سَّ ح ْ ذَّي َّي ْن ِ ن ِسَّ ح ْ ذَّة ٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «لَّي ْسَّ هُّوَّ هَّكَّذ َّإ هِى َّ ي َّام َّ ه لَّكُّم .
english_text:
Abu Basir said: I said to Abu Ja'far {a.s},
"We talk and say that whoever prays while sitting without any illness, his prayer
consists of two rak'ahs in place of one, and two prostrations in place of one."
Imam {a.s} said: "It is not as you say. It is complete for you."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 410 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 365 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 170 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 294 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 111 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 492

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ِ وَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ جُّ مْ زَّإن َّ ن ْن َّإ َّعْ ي َّن َّ عَّن ْ إ َّجَّ ذِهِمَّا عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «كَّان َّ إ َّن ِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِذ َّإ صَّ ل َّى ج َّ الِساً ي َّزَّن َّغ
ِق َّا ِذ َّإ رَّكَّغَّ ي َّن َّى رِج ْ لَّي ْ ه .
english_text:
It was narrated from Humran ibn A'yan, from one of the Imams {a.s}, who said:
"My father {a.s} when he prayed while sitting, he would sit cross-legged, and when he
went into ruku' (bowing), he would fold his legs."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 365 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 171 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 114 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 502

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
english_text:
Muawiya ibn Maysara narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"Can a person pray while sitting in the position of tawarruk (cross-legged) or with his
legs spread out?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 365 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 502

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِى إَّلْمَّحْ مِلِ «صَّ لِّ مُّي َّزَّن ِّعاً وَّ مَّ مْ ذُّوذَّ إَّلزِّج ْ لَّي ْن ِ وَّ كَّي ْف َّ مَّ ا إ َّمْ كَّن َّك .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said regarding prayer in a carriage
(mahmil),
"Pray sitting cross-legged (tawarruk), with your legs extended, or in whatever manner
is possible for you."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 365 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 228 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 520 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 330 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 502

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مَّ ن ْن ِ إ َّن ِى ر ِي َّاذٍ إَّلْكَّزْج ِ ى ِّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: ق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لا َّمُّ رَّج ُّ ل س َّ ي ْ ح كَّن ِي ز لأ
َّ ي َّسْ ي َّطِ ي غُّ إَّلْق ِي َّامَّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْح َّ لاَّءِ لِص َّ عْ ق ِهِ وَّ لأَّ ي ُّمْ كِن ُّهُّ إَّلز ُّكُّوعُّ وَّ إَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذُّ ق َّق ُّالَّ «لِي ُّومِ ن ِزَّإ ْسِ هِ إ ِي مَّاءً وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لَّهُّ مَّ ن ْ ي َّزْق َّغ
َّ إ ِلَّي ْ هِ إَّلْح ُّ مْ زَّة َّ ق َّلْي َّسْ ح ُّ ذْ ق َّا ِن ْ لَّمْ ي ُّمْ كِن ْهُّ ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّلْي ُّومِ ن ِزَّإ ْسِ هِ ن َّحْ وَّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ إ ِي مَّاءً» ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّ الصِّ ي َّامُّ ق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ ق ِى ذ َّلِك
ْإَّلْحَّ ذِّ ق َّق َّذ ِ وَّ ص َّ غَّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّن ْهُّ ق َّا ِن ْ كَّان َّ لَّهُّ مَّ ق ْذُّرَّة ق َّصَّ ذَّق َّه ُّ مُّذٍّ مِن َّ إَّلط َّ عَّامِ ن َّذَّلَّ كُّلِّ ي َّوْ مٍ إ َّجَّ ث ُّ إ ِلَّى َّ ق َّا ُّن ْ لَّمْ ي َّكُّن ْ لَّهُّ ي َّسَّ ار
ِذ َّلِك َّ ق َّلاَّ س َّ ى ْ ءَّ عَّلَّي ْ ه.
english_text:
Ibrahim ibn Abi Ziyad al-Karkhi narrated:
I asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about an elderly man who could not
stand up due to weakness and was unable to perform ruku‘ (bowing) or sujood
(prostration).
Imam {a.s} said: "He should perform his prayer with gestures (īmā’), directing his head
towards the Qiblah. If he has someone to raise the ṣaḥfa (a mat or a piece of cloth,
typically used for prostration) for him, then he should prostrate. If he is unable to do
so, he should perform his prayer with gestures (īmā’) facing the Qiblah."
I asked: "What about fasting?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If he has reached such a state, then Allah {SWT} has excused him from
fasting. If he is able, he should give a ṣadaqa (charity) of a mud (a portion of food) for
each day, which is preferable. If he is not able to do this, then there is nothing required
of him."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 365 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 307

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّن ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ سُّ لَّي ْ مَّان َّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّا ْج ُّ ذ ُّةُّ إَّلز ُّعَّاف ُّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ لأَّ ي َّز ِي ذ
ْعَّلَّى إ َّن ْ ي َّسْ ي َّن ْس ِ ق َّهُّ إ َّ ي َّح ُّ ور ُّ ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّم .
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Sulayman asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
a person who experiences nosebleed during prayer and is only able to stop it by
sniffing. Is this permissible?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
english_text:
Bukayr ibn Ayyan narrated that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} saw a
man who had a nosebleed during prayer. The man put his hand into his nose, took out
blood, and the Imam gestured to him with his hand, saying,
"Wipe it with your hand and continue praying."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 366 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 871 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p.

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ لَّي ْث إَّلْمُّزَّإذِى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم :
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّزْعُّف ُّ ر َّوَّ إلَّ إَّلس َّ مْ سِ جَّ ي َّى ي َّذ ْ هَّث َّ إَّلل َّي ْلُّ ق َّال
ٍ «ي ُّومِى ُّ إ ِي مَّاءً ن ِزَّإ ْسِ هِ عَّن ْ كُّلِّ صَّ لاَّة .
english_text:
Layth al-Muradi asked Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who suffers from
continuous nosebleeds from the time of the sun's zenith until nightfall.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should gesture with his head for each prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
وَّ رَّوَّ ى ُّعُّمَّزُّ ن ْن ُّ إ ُّذ َّي ْ ن َّه َّ عَّن ْهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ إ َّن َّهُّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّزْعُّف ُّ وَّ هُّوَّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ ق َّذْ صَّ ل َّى ن َّعْ ض
ْ صَّ لاَّي ِهِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ إَّلْمَّاءُّ عَّن ْ ي َّمِي ن ِهِ إ َّوْ عَّن ْ س ِ مَّالِهِ إ َّوْ عَّن ْ ج َّ لْق ِهِ ق َّلْي َّع ْ سِ لْهُّ مِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ إ َّن
ِي َّلْي َّق ِث َّ وَّ لْي َّن ْن ِ عَّلَّى صَّ لاَّي ِه
َّ ق َّ ا ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّح ِ ذِ إَّلْمَّاءَّ جَّ ي َّى ي َّلْي َّق ِث َّ ق َّلْي ُّعِذِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ» ق َّالَّ «وَّ إَّلْق َّى ْ ءُّ مِي ْ لُّ ذ َّلِك .
english_text:
Umar ibn Uthayna reported from him {a.s} that he was asked about a man who
experiences a nosebleed while in prayer and has already prayed part of it.
Imam {a.s} replied: "If the blood is on his right, left, or behind him, he should wash it
without turning and continue with his prayer. If he cannot find water without turning,
then he should repeat the prayer." He also said: "Vomiting is similar to that."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 366 • Al-Wafi, V. 8, p. 869 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 7, p. 238

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
ِوَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ إ َّن ِى ن َّصِ ي زٍ عَّن ْهُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ «إ ِن ْ ي َّكَّل َّمْ ث َّ إ َّوْ صَّ زَّق ْث َّ وَّ ج ْ هَّك َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ ق َّا َّعِ ذِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة .
english_text:
In the narration of Abu Basir from Imam {a.s}, He {a.s} said: "If you speak or turn
your face away from the qibla, then you should repeat the prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 366 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 869 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 313 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 245 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 281

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ٍلَّهُّ إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي ز:
ِ إ َّسْ مَّغُّ إَّلْعَّطْ سَّ ه َّ ق َّا َّجْ مَّذُّ إَّلل َّهَّ ي َّعَّالَّى وَّ إ ُّصَّ لِّى عَّلَّى إَّلن َّن ِى ِّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ وَّ إ َّن َّا ق ى
ُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ن َّي ْ ن َّك َّ وَّ ن َّي ْ ن َّ صَّ اجِ ن ِك َّ إَّلْي َّم .
english_text:
Abu Basir said to him: "I hear someone sneeze, and I praise Allah {SWT} and
send blessings upon the Prophet {saws} while I am in prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, even if there is a sea between you and your companion."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 367 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, P 2, p. 332 • Wasail Al-Shia, P 7, p. 272

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «إَّلْأ َّعْ مَّى إ ِذ َّإ صَّ ل َّى لِع َّي ْ زِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ ق َّا ِن ْ كَّان َّ ق ِى وَّ ق ْث ٍ ق َّلْي ُّعِذْ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ق َّذْ م ُّ ص َّ ى إَّلْوَّ ق ْث
»ُّق َّلاَّ ي ُّعِي ذ
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said:
"If a blind person prays facing the wrong direction, and if it is during the time of the
prayer, then he should repeat it. But if the time has passed, he does not need to repeat
it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 367 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 554 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
وَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْق ُّص َّ ي ْلِ ن ْن ِ ي َّسَّ ارٍ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: ق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّكُّون ُّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّا َّج ِ ذُّ ع َّمْ ز إً ق ِى
ُّ ن َّطْ ن ِى إ َّوْ إ َّر إً إ َّوْ ص َّ زَّن َّان اً ق َّق َّالَّ «إِن ْصَّ زِف ْ وَّ ي َّوَّ ص َّ ا ْ وَّ إِن ْن ِ عَّلَّى مَّ ا مَّ ص َّ ى مِن ْ صَّ لاَّي ِك َّ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّن ْق ِض ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ ن ِالْكَّلاَّم
َّمُّي َّعَّمِّذإً ق َّا ِن ْ ي َّكَّل َّمْ ث َّ ن َّاسِ ي اً ق َّلاَّ س َّ ى ْ ءَّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ وَّ هُّو
ِ ن ِمَّن ْز ِلَّه ِ مَّ ن ْ ي َّكَّل َّمَّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ن َّاسِ ي اً» ق ُّلْث ُّ وَّ إ ِن ْ ق َّلَّث َّ وَّ ج ْ هَّهُّ عَّن
ِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ وَّ إ ِن ْ ق َّلَّث َّ وَّ ج ْ هَّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه .
english_text:
It is narrated from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar that He said:
"I said to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}: 'I am praying and I feel a pain in my
stomach, or a rumbling, or a sensation of something moving.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Turn away (from prayer) and perform ablution, and then continue the
prayer you have already performed, as long as you have not invalidated the prayer by
deliberately speaking. If you spoke by mistake, there is no harm, and it is like the one
who speaks in prayer by mistake.'
I asked: 'What if he turns his face away from the qibla?'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Yes, even if he turns his face away from the qibla.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 367 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 332 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 401 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 865 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 235

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
arabic_text:
وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّن ْذُّ إَّلز َّجْ مَّن ِ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْحَّ ح َّ اح ِ إ َّن َّا ُّإَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّعَّن ِ إَّلْع َّمْ ز ِ ي ُّصِ ي ث ُّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لَّ ق ِى ن َّطْ ن ِهِ وَّ هُّوَّ ي َّسْ ي َّطِ ي غ
َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّصْ ن ِزَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إ َّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى عَّلَّى ي ِلْك َّ إَّلْحَّ الَّه ِ إ َّمْ لأَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ِ إِجْ ي َّمَّلَّ إَّلص َّ ن ْزَّ وَّ لَّمْ ي َّح ِّف ْ إ ِعْ ح َّ الأً عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّلْي ُّصَّ ل
ْوَّ لْي َّصْ ن ِز.
english_text:
Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s} about a man who feels
discomfort in his stomach but is able to bear it. He asked whether the man should
continue praying in that situation or not.
Imam {a.s} replied: "If he can tolerate the pain and does not fear it causing him to rush
the prayer, then he should pray and be patient."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER OF THE SICK, THE UNCONCIOUS, THE WEAK AND THE INFIRM, THE ELDERLY AND OTHERS
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Smiling does not invalidate the prayer, but loud laughter does. And smiling does not
break the wudu (ablution)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 367 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 891 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 1, p. 264 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 251

Chapter Title: GREETING THE WORSHIPPER
arabic_text:
ب اب-
الي سلي م علي المصلي
ُّسَّ ا َّلَّ مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّسْ لِمٍ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّسَّ لِّمُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْق َّوْ مِ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ سَّ ل َّم
َّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ مُّ سْ لِم وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّسَّ لِّمْ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ي َّق ُّولُّ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ وَّ إ َّس ِ زْ ن ِا ِصْ ن َّعِك .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a
person who greets others while in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If a Muslim greets you while you are in prayer, respond to him by saying,
‘As-salamu ‘alayka,' and gesture with your finger."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 367 • Al-Sara’ir, Part 3, p. 604 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 888 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 268 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 303

Chapter Title: GREETING THE WORSHIPPER
arabic_text:

english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
greeting someone while in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If a man from the Muslims greets you while you are in prayer, respond
to him within yourself and do not raise your voice”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 368 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 331 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 888 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 268 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol. 2, p. 143

Chapter Title: GREETING THE WORSHIPPER
english_text:
Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Imam {a.s} that He said:
"If someone greets a man while he is praying, he should respond to him quietly, as He
(the greeter) said."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 368 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 332 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 888 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 268 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol. 2, p. 143

Chapter Title: GREETING THE WORSHIPPER

english_text:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Ammar greeted the Messenger of Allah {saws} while he was in prayer, and he responded
to him."
Then Abu Ja'far {a.s} said: "Indeed, Salam (greeting) is one of the names of Allah {SWT}, the
Mighty and Majestic."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 368 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 889 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 269 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 306

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a
person who is harmed by an animal while he is praying.
He {a.s} replied: "He should throw it away from him if he wishes, or bury it in the
pebbles."
references: Da‘ā’im al-Islām, Part 1, p. 174 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 368 • Mustadrak Al- Wasail, Vol. 5, p. 425

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING ENCOUNTERS PREDATORY

ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:

english_text:
Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a person who
scratches himself while in prayer. He {a.s} replied: "There is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING ENCOUNTERS PREDATORY ANIMALS AND HARMFUL CREATURES AND HE KILLS THEM 488
english_text:
He asked him about a person who kills a louse, a flea, a mosquito, or a fly
while in prayer. Does this invalidate his prayer and wudu?
Imam {a.s} said: "No."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 367 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 368 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 330 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 905 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 1, p. 293

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING ENCOUNTERS PREDATORY ANIMALS AND HARMFUL CREATURES AND HE KILLS THEM 488
arabic_text:

english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked him about a man who is performing the obligatory
prayer while standing and forgets his bag or belongings, fearing they might be lost or
damaged.
Imam {a.s} said: "He may cut his prayer and secure his belongings."
Sama’a then said: "What if his animal breaks loose and he fears it might run away or
cause harm?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is no problem for him to cut his prayer, secure his animal, and then
return to his prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING ENCOUNTERS PREDATORY ANIMALS AND HARMFUL CREATURES AND HE KILLS THEM 488
arabic_text:

english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati asked him about a man who is in prayer and sees a snake
in front of him. Is it permissible for him to step forward and kill it?
Imam {a.s} said: "If there is just one step between him and the snake, then he may step
forward and kill it; otherwise, he should not."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 369 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 289

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING ENCOUNTERS PREDATORY ANIMALS AND HARMFUL CREATURES AND HE KILLS THEM 489
arabic_text:
ِ وَّ رَّوَّ ى جَّ زِي ز عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ كُّن ْث َّ ق ِى صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلْق َّزِي ص َّ ه ِ ق َّزَّإ َّي ْث َّ ع ُّلاَّماً لَّك َّ ق َّذْ إ َّن َّق
ْإ َّوْ ع َّزِي ماً لَّك َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ مَّ ال إ َّوْ جَّ ي َّه ً ي َّي َّح َّ و َّ ق ُّهَّا عَّلَّى ن َّق ْسِ ك َّ ق َّاق ْطَّ غِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ وَّ إِي ْن َّغْ ع ُّلاَّمَّ ك َّ إ َّو

english_text:
Hariz narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If you are in the obligatory prayer and you see one of your servants who has run away,
or a debtor to whom you owe money, or a snake that you fear for your life, then break
your prayer, follow your servant or debtor, and kill the snake."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 367 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 369 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 331 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 903 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 276 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 289

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF

english_text:
Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
regarding a person who wishes to attend to a need while in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should gesture with his head and signal with his hand. As for a
woman, when She wants to attend to a need, She should clap."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 370 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 254

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF
english_text:
Al-Halabi asked him about a man who wishes to attend to a need while
praying.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should gesture with his head, signal with his hand, and glorify
(SubhanAllah {SWT}). As for a woman, when She wants to attend to a need while praying,
She should clap her hands”.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 365 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 370 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 895

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ جَّ ن َّان ُّ ن ْن ُّ سَّ ذِي ز:

ِمَّ سْ ح ِ ذٍ مِن ْ مَّ سَّ اج ِ ذِ إَّلْأ َّن ْصَّ ارِ ن ِمِحْ ح َّ ن ٍ كَّان َّ مَّ عَّهُّ » ق َّالَّ جَّ ن َّان وَّ لأَّ إ َّعْ لَّمُّهُّ إ ِلأ َّ مَّ سْ ح ِ ذَّ ن َّن ِى عَّن ْذ ِإَّلْأ َّس ْ هَّل .
english_text:
Hanan ibn Sadeer asked him: "Can a man gesture while praying?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, the Prophet {saws} gestured in one of the mosques of the Ansar with
a Muḥjan that he had with him."
Hanan said: "And I do not know except that it was the mosque of the Banu Abd al-
Ashhal."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 370 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 896 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p.

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF

english_text:
Ammar ibn Musa asked him about a man who hears a sound at the door while
he is in prayer and clears his throat to make his servant or family member hear, so that
they come and look to see who is at the door. Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
He also asked about a man and a woman who are in prayer and want something,
whether it is permissible for them to say "SubhanAllah {SWT}."
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, and they can gesture to what they want. And a woman, when She
wants something, can strike her thighs while in prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 370 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 895 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p.

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF
arabic_text:
ِّوَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ ن َّح ِ ي لٍ إ َّج ُّ و عَّلِى ِّ ن ْن ِ ن َّح ِ ي لٍ ق َّالَّ: رَّإ َّي ْ ث ُّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي ُّصَّ ل َّى ق َّمَّز َّ ن ِهِ رَّج ُّ ل و
ِهُّوَّ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلس َّ ح ْ ذَّي َّي ْن ِ ق َّزَّمَّ اةُّ إ َّن ُّو عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ ن ِحَّ صَّ اة ٍ ق َّا َّق ْن َّلَّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ إ ِلَّي ْ ه.
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Bajil, the brother of Ali ibn Bajil, narrated:
"I saw Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} praying, and a man passed by him while
he was between the two prostrations. Abu Abdullah {a.s} threw a small stone at him, and
the man came towards him."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 371 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 327 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 897 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 7, p. 258

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF
arabic_text:
- وَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ر َّكَّزِي َّا إَّلْأ َّعْ وَّ رِ ق َّالَّ: رَّإ َّي ْث ُّ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّان ِماً وَّ إ ِلَّى
ج َّ ان ِن ِهِ رَّج ُّ ل كَّن ِي ز
ُّي ُّزِي ذُّ إ َّن ْ ي َّق ُّومَّ وَّ مَّ عَّهُّ عَّصً ا لَّهُّ ق َّا َّرَّإذَّ إ َّن ْ ي َّي َّن َّاوَّ لَّهَّا ق َّان ْحَّ ظ َّ إ َّن ُّو إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ وَّ ه َّوَّ ق َّان ِم ق ِى صَّ لاَّي ِهِ ق َّن َّاوَّ ل
ِإَّلز َّج ُّ لَّ إَّلْعَّصَّ ا ي ُّم َّ عَّاذَّ إ ِلَّى مَّ وْ ص ِ عِهِ إ ِلَّى صَّ لاَّي ِه .
english_text:
It was narrated by Abu Zakariya al-Awra :
"I saw Abu al-Hasan {a.s} praying while standing, and beside him was an elderly man
who wanted to stand up and had a stick with him. The man wanted to take the stick,
so Abu al-Hasan {a.s}, while still standing in his prayer, bent down and handed the man
the stick. Then he returned to his place and resumed his prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 371 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 332 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 901 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 503 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 304

Chapter Title: THE ONE PRAYING WHO NEEDS TO RELIEVE HIMSELF
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإ َّن ُّو جَّ ن ِي ث ٍ ن َّاج ِ ي َّه ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّإ ِن َّ لِى رَّجً ى إ َّطْ حَّ ن ُّ ق ِي هَّا إَّلسِّ مْ سِ مَّ ق َّا َّق ُّومُّ وَّ إ ُّصَّ لِّى و
َّ إ َّعْ لَّمُّ إ َّن َّ إَّلْع ُّلاَّمَّ ن َّان ِم ق َّا َّص ْ زِب ُّ إَّلْحَّ ان ِظَّ لِأ ُّوق ِط َّ هُّ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ إ َّن ْث َّ ق ِى طَّ اعَّه ِ رَّن ِّك َّ ي َّطْ لُّث ُّ رِر ْق َّك َّ لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Abu Habib Najiyah said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"I have a mill where I grind sesame seeds, and I stand to pray, knowing that the servant
is asleep. I strike the wall to wake him up."
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, you are in the obedience of your Lord {AZJ}, seeking your
sustenance. There is no harm in that."
commentary:
There is no call to prayer (adhan) or iqama for a woman, nor is there a Jumu’ah prayer
(Jumu'ah) or congregational prayer (Jama'ah) for her.
When a woman stands in prayer, She gathers her feet together and does not spread
them apart, placing her hands on her chest at the location of her breasts.
When She bows, She places her hands on her knees, on her thighs, so as not to bend
too much and cause her back to rise.
When She goes to prostrate, She sits first and then prostrates, pressing her face to the
ground and placing her arms on the ground.
When She rises to stand, She lifts her head from the prostration and sits on her
buttocks, not in the way a man would sit. Then, She rises to stand without raising her
back and hips, moving smoothly.
When She sits for the tashahhud (testification), She raises her legs and brings her
thighs together. A free woman (Hura) does not pray except with a veil (niqab), while a
slave woman (ama) prays without a veil.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}
who said:
"A woman prays in a dress (dir'aa) and a head covering (miqna'a) if it is thick, meaning
it is concealing."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 372 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 376 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ي ُّون ُّسُّ ن ْن ُّ ي َّعْ ق ُّوب َّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى ي َّوْ ب ٍ وَّ إجِ ذٍ ق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ » ق َّال
ُّق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّالْمَّزْإ َّة ُّ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّصْ لُّحُّ لِلْحُّ ز َّة ِ إ ِذ َّإ جَّ اص َّ ث ْ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلْح ِ مَّارُّ إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْ لأَّ ي َّح ِ ذَّة.
english_text:
Yunus ibn Ya'qub asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
who prays in one garment.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
He then asked: "What about a woman?"
Imam {a.s} said: "No, and it is not proper for a free woman (Hurr) to pray when she
menstruates except with a khimar (headscarf), unless She does not find it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 373 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 405

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ ، إ َّج َّ اةُّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ لَّي ْسَّ لَّهَّا إ ِلأ َّ مِلْحَّ ق َّه وَّ إجِ ذَّة كَّي ْف
ِي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّالَّ «ي َّلْي َّف ُّ ق ِي هَّا وَّ ي ُّع َّطِّ ى رَّإ ْسَّ هَّا وَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّا ِن ْ ج َّ زَّج َّ ث ْ رِج ْ لَّي ْهَّا وَّ لَّي ْ سَّ ي َّق ْ ذِرُّ عَّلَّى ع َّي ْ ز َّ ذ َّلِك َّ ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a
woman who has only one cover (milhafa). How should She pray?
Imam {a.s} said: "She should wrap herself in it and cover her head, and then pray. If her
legs are exposed and She is unable to cover them in any other way, then there is no
harm."
references: Questions of Ali bin Jaafar, Part 1, p. 172 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 373 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 177

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ِوَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ إَّلْمُّعَّل َّى ن ْن ِ ج ُّ ن َّي ْ سٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذ َّإَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن ِ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى ذِرْعٍ و
َّمِلْحَّ ق َّه ٍ لَّي ْ سَّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إ ِر َّإر وَّ لأَّ مِق ْن َّعَّه ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ إ ِذ َّإ إِلْي َّق َّث ْ ن ِهَّا وَّ إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّكُّن ْ ي َّكْق ِي ه ًا عَّزْص اً ج َّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا طُّ ولأ .
english_text:
In a narration from Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, he asked Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a woman praying in a shirt (dir') and a cover (milhafa)
without a waistcloth (izar) or headcover (miqna'a).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm if She wraps herself in it, and if it is not wide enough
to cover her, She should make it long."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 373 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 379 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «لَّي ْ سَّ عَّلَّى إَّلْأ َّمَّ ه ِ ق ِن َّاع ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ لأَّ عَّلَّى
َّ إَّلْمُّذَّن َّزَّة ِ ق ِن َّاع ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ لأَّ عَّلَّى إَّلْمُّكَّاي َّن َّه ِ إ ِذ َّإ إِس ْ ي َّزَّطَّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا مَّ وْ لأَّهَّا ق ِن َّاع ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ هِى َّ مَّ مْ لُّوكَّه جَّ ي َّى ي ُّو َّ ذِّى
ج َّ مِي غَّ مُّكَّاي َّن َّي ِهَّا وَّ ي َّح ْ زِى عَّلَّي ْهَّا مَّ ا ي َّح ْ زِى عَّلَّى إَّلْمَّمْ لُّوك ِ ق ِى إَّلْحُّ ذُّوذِ كُّلِّهَّا .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"There is no obligation for a slave woman (amā) to wear a headcover (qina'ah) in
prayer, nor for a woman who is 'mukātabah' (a slave who has entered into a contract
to pay for her freedom) if her master has not required it as part of the terms of her
contract, until She has fulfilled all the terms of her contract. The same rules that apply
to a slave in all legal matters apply to her as well."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 5, p. 525 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 373 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 346 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 377 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 20, p. 207 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 182

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ِ ق َّالَّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ: عَّن َّإَّلْأ َّمَّ ه ِ إ ِذ َّإ وَّ لَّذَّب ْ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إَّلْح ِ مَّارُّ ق َّالَّ «لَّوْ كَّان َّ عَّلَّي ْ هَّا لَّكَّان َّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إ ِذ َّإ هِى َّ جَّ اص َّ ث ْ وَّ لَّي ْ س
ِ عَّلَّي ْهَّا إَّلي َّق َّن ُّغُّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة.
english_text:
I asked him about a slave woman (amā) who gave birth, and whether the
headcover (khimar) would be required for her.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it were required for her, She would have to wear it when She
menstruates, but there is no requirement for her to wear a headcover in prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 373 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 377

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى عِ ي ضُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْق َّاسِ مِ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّق ِى إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى إ ِر َّإرِ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ وَّ ق ِى ي َّوْ ن ِهَّا و
َّي َّعْ ي َّم ُّ ن ِح ِ مَّارِهَّا ق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّث ْ مَّ ا ْمُّون َّه ً ق َّلاَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Iyas ibn al-Qasim narrated from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who prays in
a woman's izar (waistcloth), in her garment, and uses her khimar (headcover) as a
turban.
Imam {a.s} said: "If She is trustworthy (māʾmūnah), there is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 374 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 447

Chapter Title: THE ETIQUETTE OF WOMEN IN PRAYER
arabic_text:
َّو ُّرُّوِى َّ: «إ َّن َّ ج َّ ي ْ زَّ مَّ سَّ اج ِ ذِ إَّلن ِّسَّ اءِ إَّلْن ُّي ُّوب ُّ وَّ صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ ق ِى ن َّي ْي ِهَّا إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ مِن ْ صَّ لاَّي ِهَّا ق ِى ص ق َّي ِهَّا وَّ صَّ لاَّي َّهَّا
ْ ق ِى صُّ ق َّي ِهَّا إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ مِن ْ صَّ لاَّي ِهَّا ق ِى صَّ حْ ن ِ ذَّإرِهَّا وَّ صَّ لاَّي َّهَّا ق ِى صَّ حْ ن ِ ذَّإرِهَّا إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ مِن َّصَّ لاَّي ِهَّا ق ِى سَّ طْ حِ ن َّي ْي ِهَّا و
ٍي ُّكْزَّةُّ لِلْمَّزْإ َّة ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ ق ِى سَّ طْ حٍ ع َّي ْ زِ مُّ حَّ ح َّ ز .
english_text:
It is narrated:
"The best places for women to pray are their homes. A woman's prayer in her house is
better than her prayer in a public prayer area (ṣuffah), and her prayer in the public
prayer area is better than her prayer in the courtyard of her house. Her prayer in the
courtyard is better than her prayer on the roof of her house. And it is disliked for a
woman to pray on a roof that is not enclosed (muḥajjar)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 374 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 514

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Do not place women in upper rooms (ghuraf), nor teach them writing, nor teach them
Surah Yusuf. Teach them spinning (al-mighzal) and Surah al-Nur."
commentary:
And when a woman makes the tasbih (glorification of God), She should knot her
fingers, for they will be questioned on the Day of Judgment.

arabic_text:

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}
who said: "When you finish your prayer, turn to your right as you leave."
commentary:
Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, says:
"And establish the prayer and give the zakah and bow with those who bow."
(Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:43).
Allah {SWT} has commanded the congregation as He commanded the prayer. Allah {SWT},
Blessed and Exalted, has made it obligatory upon the people to pray five times a day,
from Jumu’ah to Jumu’ah, totaling thirty-five prayers. Among them, one prayer is
obligatory in congregation, which is the Jumu’ah prayer.
As for the other prayers, it is not obligatory to pray in congregation, but it is a
recommended practice (Sunnah).
Whoever neglects it without a valid excuse has no prayer. Whoever neglects three
consecutive Jumu’ah prayers without a valid excuse is considered a hypocrite.
A man's prayer in congregation is worth twenty-five degrees more than his prayer alone
in Paradise. The prayer in congregation is worth twenty-four prayers more than the
individual prayer, making a total of twenty-five prayers.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 338 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 375 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 317 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 782 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 421 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 422 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 500 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 500 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 82, p. 303 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 82, p. 326 Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}
said:
"There is no prayer for the one who does not attend the congregational prayer from
among the neighbors of the mosque, except for someone who is ill or preoccupied."

Chapter Title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said to a group of people:
"You must attend the mosque, or I will burn down your houses."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 376 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 291

He {a.s} said: "Whoever prays the five daily prayers in congregation, assume
every good about him."

english_text:
Al-Hasan al-Sayqal asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the
minimum number for a congregation.
Imam {a.s} said: "A man and a woman."
commentary:
And if no one else attends the mosque, a believer praying alone is still a congregation
because when he gives the call to prayer (adhan) and the iqamah, two rows of angels
pray behind him.
If he performs the iqamah but not the adhan, one row of angels prays behind him.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 376 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 26 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1171 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 298

Chapter Title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
english_text:
The Prophet {saws} said:
"A believer alone is a proof (Hujjah), and a believer alone is a congregation."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 376 • Al-Khasal, Part 2, p. 584 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1172 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 297 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 1, p. 592 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 28, p. 3

english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} prayed the Fajr (dawn) prayer one day, and after
finishing, he turned his face towards his companions and asked about certain people
by name, asking if they were present for the prayer.
They replied: "No, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}."
He {saws} then said: "Are they absent?"
They said: "No, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}."
He {saws} said: "Indeed, there is no prayer heavier on the hypocrites than this prayer
(Fajr) and the 'Isha' (night) prayer. If they knew the reward that is in them, they would
come to them, even if crawling."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever prays the morning (Fajr) and the evening ('Isha') prayers in congregation is
under the protection of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic. Whoever wrongs him,
wrongs Allah {SWT}, and whoever belittles him, belittles Allah {SWT}, the Majestic."
commentary:
And when there is rain or severe cold, it is permissible for a man to pray in his dwelling
and not attend the mosque.
references: Al Mahasin, P1, p. 52 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V1, p.377 • Awaali al-La’aali, P1, p. 342 • Al-Wafi, V8, p.1169 • Wasail Al-Shia, V8, p.295 • Bihar Al Anwar, V85, p.12 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, V6, p. 453

english_text:
The Prophet {saws} said:
"If the sandals are wet, then pray in your dwellings."
commentary:
My father (may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him) said in his letter to me:
"Know, my son, that the one most deserving to lead the congregation is the one most
proficient in reciting the Qur'an.
If they are equal in recitation, then the one who has the most understanding of
jurisprudence (Fiqh).
If they are equal in Fiqh, then the one who has migrated (performed Hijrah) the earliest.
If they are equal in migration, then the oldest in age.
If they are equal in age, then the one with the most pleasing appearance.
The owner of the mosque has more right to lead in his mosque. Let those who stand
closest to the Imam be people of sound judgment and piety so that if the Imam forgets
or becomes confused, they can correct him. The best rows are the front rows, and the
best part of the front row is that which is closest to the Imam."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 377 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1278 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 195 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 292

english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"The Imam of the people is their representative, so choose the best among you to
lead."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 377 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1174 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 347 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 206

Imam {a.s} said:
"If it pleases you to purify and perfect your prayers, then choose the best among you
(to lead)."
