ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّح ْ زُّح ُّ مَّ غَّ إَّلْق َّوْ مِ ق ِى سَّ ق َّزٍ ي ُّزِي ذُّةُّ ق َّذَّج َّ لَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلْوَّ ق ْث ُّ و
ُّق َّذْ ج َّ زَّح َّ مِن َّ إَّلْق َّزْ ي َّه ِ عَّلَّى ق َّزْسَّ ح َّ ي ْن ِ ق َّصَّ ل َّوْ إ وَّ إِن ْصَّ زَّف َّ ن َّعْ ص ُّ هُّمْ ق ِى جَّ اج َّ ه ٍ ق َّلَّمْ ي ُّق ْ ض َّ لَّهُّمُّ إَّلْح ُّ ز ِ وح ُّ مَّ ا ي َّصْ ن َّغُّ ن ِالص َّ لاَّة
َّ إَّل ُّي ِى كَّان َّ صَّ لا َّهَّا رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ق َّالَّ «ي َّم َّث ْ صَّ لاَّي ُّهُّ وَّ لأَّ ي ُّعِي ذ .
english_text:
Zurarah asked Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who sets out with a group of
people for a journey that he intends to complete. The time for prayer enters while they
have already departed from the village by a distance of two farsakhs (approximately
six miles) and they perform their prayers (as two units). Some of them then turn back
for a specific need, and they are unable to continue their journey. What should be done
about the prayer that was performed as two units?
Imam {a.s} said: "His prayer is complete and he does not need to repeat it”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 438 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 521

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّرَّسُّ ول ِإَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
«مَّ ن ْ صَّ ل َّى ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ إ َّرْن َّعاً ق َّا َّن َّا إ ِلَّى إَّلل َّهِ مِن ْهُّ ن َّزِى ء . ي عن ى : مي عمذإ .
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said: "Whoever performs four units of prayer
during travel, I disassociate myself from him in front of Allah {SWT}”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ«إَّلْمُّي َّمِّمُّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ كَّالْمُّق َّصِّ زِ ق ِى إَّلْحَّ ص َّ ز.
english_text:
Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "One who prays in full (without shortening) while
traveling is like the one who shortens (prayer) while residing (at home)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 438 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 39 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p.

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ٍوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي ز:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ إ َّرْن َّغَّ رَّكَّعَّاب ٍ ن َّاسِ ي اً ق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ ذ َّكَّزَّ ق ِى ذ َّلِك َّ إَّلْي َّوْ مِ ق َّلْي ُّعِذْ و
ِإ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّذ ْ كُّزْ جَّ ي َّى ي َّمْ ص ِ ى َّ ذ َّلِك َّ إَّلْي َّوْ مُّ ق َّلاَّ إ ِعَّاذَّة َّ عَّلَّي ْ ه .
english_text:
Abu Basir asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who,
while traveling, prays four rak'ahs (instead of two) out of forgetfulness.
Imam said: "If he remembers it on that same day, he should repeat (the prayer). If he
does not remember until the day has passed, then there is no need for him to repeat”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
وَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ َّرْن َّعَّه ي َّح ِ ث ُّ عَّلَّي ْهِمُّ إَّلي َّمَّامُّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ كَّان ُّوإ إ َّوْ ق ِى
ْإَّلْحَّ ص َّ زِ إَّلْمُّكَّارِى وَّ إَّلْكَّزِى ُّ وَّ إَّلز َّإعِ ى وَّ إَّلْأ َّس ْ ي َّق َّان ُّ لِأ َّن َّهُّ عَّمَّلُّهُّم.
ُّوَّ رُّوِى َّ: «إَّلْمَّلا َّحُّ وَّ إَّلْأ َّس ْ ي َّق َّان ُّ إَّلْن َّزِي ذ .
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There are four categories of people who are required to offer the full (complete) prayer
whether they are traveling or at home: the mule driver (al-Mukari), the camel driver (al-
Karri), the shepherd, and al-Ashtaqan (those who constantly travel as part of their
work). This is because it is their work (which involves constant travel)."
It was also narrated: "The sailor (al-Mallah) and al-Ashtaqan (a type of courier or mail
carrier) are also included."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 436 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 439

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
وَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّجَّ ذِهِمَّا عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «لَّي ْ سَّ عَّلَّى َّإَّلْمَّلا َّجِ ي ن َّ ق ِى سُّ ق ُّن ِهِمْ ي َّق ْصِ ي ز و
ِلأَّ عَّلَّى إَّلْمُّكَّارِى وَّ إَّلْح َّ م َّال .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of the Imams {a.s} that He said:
"There is no shortening of the prayer for sailors on their ships, nor for the mule drivers
(al-Mukari) and camel drivers (al-Jammal)."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 437 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 439 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 167 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 485

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ْسِ ن َّان ٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّلْمُّكَّارِى إ ِذ َّإ لَّمْ ي َّسْ ي َّق ِز َّ ق ِى مَّ ن ْز ِلِهِ إ ِلأ َّ ج َّ م َّ سَّ ه
َّ إ َّي َّامٍ إ َّوْ إ َّق َّل َّ ق َّص َّ زَّ ق ِى سَّ ق َّزِةِ ن ِالن َّهَّارِ وَّ إ َّي َّم َّ صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلل َّي ْلِ ، وَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ صَّ وْ مُّ س َّ هْ زِ رَّمَّ ص َّ ان َّ ق ا ِن ْ كَّان َّ لَّهُّ مُّق َّام ق ِى إَّلْن َّلَّذِ إَّل َّذ ِى
َّ ي َّذ ْ هَّث ُّ عَّس َّ زَّة َّ إ َّي َّامٍ إ َّوْ إ َّكْي َّزَّ وَّ ي َّن ْصَّ زِف ُّ إ ِلَّى مَّ ن ْز ِلِهِ وَّ ي َّكُّون ُّ لَّهُّ مُّق َّامُّ عَّس َّ زَّة ِ إ َّي َّامٍ إ َّوْ إ َّكْي َّزَّ ق َّص َّ زَّ ق ِى سَّ ق َّزِةِ وَّ إ َّق ْطَّ ز .
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
who said:
"If a mule driver (al-Mukari) does not stay in his home for more than five days or less,
he should shorten his prayer while traveling during the day but offer the complete
prayer at night. He is also required to observe the fast of the month of Ramadan. If he
has a stay of ten days or more in the town he goes to and then returns to his home with
another stay of ten days or more, then he should shorten the prayer while traveling and
break his fast."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 439 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 111 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 170 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 489

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
«إَّلْح َّ م َّالُّ وَّ إَّلْمُّكَّارِى إ ِذ َّإ ج َّ ذ َّ ن ِهِمَّا إَّلس َّ ي ْ زُّ ق َّص َّ زَّإ ق ِي مَّا ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْمَّن ْز ِلَّي ْن ِ وَّ إ َّي َّم َّا ق ِى
ِ إَّلْمَّن ْز ِلَّي ْن.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The camel driver (al-Jammal) and the mule driver (al-Mukari) should shorten their
prayers while traveling between their stopping places, but when they reach their
stopping places, they should offer the complete prayers”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذ َّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّن ْ مُّحَّ م َّذِ ن ْن ِ ج َّ ز َّك ٍ ق َّالَّ: كَّي َّن ْث ُّ إ ِلَّى إ َّن ِى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلي َّالِث ِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ن َّ لِى
ج ِ مَّالأً وَّ لِى ق ُّو َّإم عَّلَّي ْهَّا وَّ لَّسْ ث ُّ إ َّج ْ زُّح ُّ ق ِي هَّا إ ِلأ َّ ق ِى طَّ زِي ق ِ مَّ ك َّه َّ لِزَّع ْ ن َّي ِى ق ِى إَّلْحَّ ح ِّ إ َّوْ ق ِى ِإَّلن َّذْ رَّة ِ إ ِلَّى ن َّعْ ض ِ إَّلْمَّوَّ إص ِ غ
ق َّمَّا ي َّح ِ ث ُّ عَّلَّى َّ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّن َّا ج َّ زَّج ْ ث ُّ مَّ عَّهَّا إ َّن ْ إ َّعْ مَّلَّ إ َّ ي َّح ِ ث ُّ إَّلي َّق ْصِ ي زُّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ إَّلص َّ وْ مِ ق ِى إَّل ِس َّ ق َّزِ إ َّوِ إَّلي َّمَّامُّ ق َّوَّ ق َّغَّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
َّإَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «إ ِذ َّإ كُّن ْث َّ لأَّ ي َّلْز َّمُّهَّا وَّ لأ ي َّح ْ زُّح ُّ مَّ عَّهَّا ق ِى كُّلِّ سَّ ق َّزٍ إ ِلأ َّ إ ِلَّى مَّ ك َّه َّ ق َّعَّلَّي ْك َّ ي َّق ْصِ ي ز وَّ ق ُّطُّ ور .
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated from Muhammad ibn Jazk who said:
‘I wrote to Imam Al-Hassan Al-Askari {a.s} saying,
"I own camels and have people managing them, but I do not travel with them except
when going to Mecca due to my desire for pilgrimage or rarely to some other places.
What is required of me when I travel with them? Should I shorten my prayers and break
my fast during travel, or should I perform them fully?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "If you do not always accompany them and only travel with them to
Mecca, then you must shorten your prayers and break your fast."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّن ْذُّ إَّلز َّجْ مَّن ِ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْحَّ ح َّ اح ِ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ٍ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ لَّهُّ إَّلص ِّ ي َّاعُّ ن َّعْ ص ُّ هَّا ق َّزِي ث مِن ْ ن َّعْ ض
ُّ ق َّي َّح ْ زُّح ُّ ق َّي َّطُّ وف ُّ ق ِي هَّا إ َّ ي ُّي ِم ُّ إ َّوْ ي ُّق َّصِّ زُّ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّي ِم .
english_text:
Abd al-Rahman bin al-Hajjaj asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
about a man who owns lands that are close to one another and he travels between
them. Should he complete his prayers or shorten them?
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should complete [his prayers]."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى إ ِسْ مَّاعِ ي لُّ ن ْن إ َّن ِى ر ِي َّاذٍ عَّن ْ ج َّ عْ ق َّزِ ن ْن ِ مُّحَّ م َّذٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِي هِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «سَّ ن ْعَّه لأَّ ي ُّق َّصِّ زُّون َّ ق ِى
َّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْح َّ ان ِى إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّذُّورُّ ق ِى ج ِ ن َّاي َّي ِهِ ، وَّ إَّلْأ َّمِي زُّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّذُّورُّ ق ِى إ ِمَّ ارَّي ِهِ وَّ إَّلي َّاج ِ زُّ إَّل ذ ِى ي َّذُّورُّ ق ِى
ٍ ي ِح َّ ارَّي ِهِ مِن ْ سُّ وق
ْإ ِلَّى سُّ وق ٍ وَّ إَّلز َّإعِ ى وَّ إَّلْن َّذَّوِى ُّ وَّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّطْ لُّث ُّ مَّ وَّ إص ِ غَّ إَّلْق َّطْ زِ وَّ مَّ ن ْن ِث َّ إَّلس َّ ح َّ زِ وَّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ ي َّط َّلُّث ُّ إَّلص َّ ي ْذَّ ي ُّزِي ذُّ ن ِهِ لَّهْ و
َّإَّلذ ُّن ْي َّا وَّ إَّلْمُّحَّ ارِب ُّ إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّق ْطَّ غُّ إَّلس َّ ن ِي ل .
english_text:
Isma'il bin Abi Ziyad narrated from Ja'far bin Muhammad {a.s} from his father
{a.s} who said:
"There are seven who do not shorten their prayers: the tax collector who travels for the
purpose of collecting taxes, the leader who moves around within his jurisdiction, the
trader who travels between markets for commerce, the shepherd, the Bedouin, the
one who seeks places of rainfall and vegetation growth, and the man who hunts for the
purpose of worldly amusement, and the bandit who blocks roads."
Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be
upon them, who said:
"Seven do not fall short in prayer: the tax collector who goes about his collection, the
prince who manages his rule, the merchant who moves from market to market, the
shepherd, the Bedouin, the one who seeks places of rain and the growth of trees, the
man who hunts for the sake of worldly enjoyment, and the warrior who roams the
paths."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 441 • Al-Khisal, Part 2, p. 403 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 214 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 232 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 110 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 166 • Wasail Al- Shia, Vol. 8, p. 486

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن ُّ ن َّكْزٍ عَّن ْ ر ُّرَّإرَّة َّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ ن َّسِ ى َّ إَّلز َّج ُّ لُّ صَّ لاَّة ً إ ِوْ صَّ لا َّهَّا ن ِع َّي ْ ز
َّطَّ هُّورٍ و ْ هُّوَّ مُّق ِي م إ َّوْ مُّسَّ اق ِز ق َّذ َّكَّزَّهَّا ق َّلْي َّق ْض ِ إَّل َّذ ِى وَّ ج َّ ث َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ لأَّ ي َّز ِي ذُّ عَّلَّى ذ َّلِك َّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّن ْق ُّضُّ وَّ مَّ ن ًن َّسِ ى َّ إ َّرْن َّعا
ِق َّص َّ ى إ َّرْن َّعاً جِ ي ن َّ ي َّذ ْ كُّزُّهَّا مُّسَّ اق ِزإً كَّان َّ إ َّوْ مُّق ِي ماً وَّ إ ِن ْ ن َّسِ ى َّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ صَّ ل َّى رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ج ْي ن َّ ي َّذ ْ كُّزُّهَّا مُّ سَّ اق ِزإً كَّان َّ إ َّو
ًمُّق ِي ما .
english_text:
Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Zurarah from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir
{a.s} who said:
"If a man forgets a prayer or prays it without purification, whether he is at home or
traveling, and then remembers it, he must make up the prayer that is due, neither
adding to it nor subtracting from it. If he forgot four rak'ahs (units of prayer), he should
make up four rak'ahs when he remembers, regardless of whether he is traveling or at
home. And if he forgot two rak'ahs, he should perform two rak'ahs when he
remembers, whether traveling or at home."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 441 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 225 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1010 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 269 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 118

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"From the reserved rulings is the completion of the prayer in four locations: Mecca,
Medina, the Mosque of Kufa, and the Shrine (Haa'ir) of Imam Hussain {a.s}."
commentary:
The author of this book, may Allah {SWT} have mercy upon him, commented: This means
that one should resolve to stay for ten days in these locations in order to complete (the
prayer), as confirmed by the following: (continues in the next hadith)
references: Kamil al-Ziyarat, Part 1, p. 249 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 442 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 187 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 531 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 532 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 77

ٍإَّلْمَّذِي ن َّه ِ ي ُّق َّص َّ زُّ إ َّوْ ي ُّي َّم ُّ ق َّالَّ «ق َّصِّ زْ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّعْ ز ِمْ عَّلَّى مُّق َّامِ عَّس َّ زَّة ِ إ َّي َّام .
english_text:
It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Imam al-Ridha {a.s}
that He said: I asked Imam {a.s} about the prayer in Mecca and Medina, whether it
should be shortened or completed.
Imam {a.s} said: "Shorten it unless you intend to stay for ten days”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ مَّ ا رَّوَّ إةُّ مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ الِذٍ إَّلْن َّزْق ِى ُّ عَّن ْ جَّ مْ ز َّة َّ ن ْن ِ عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ إَّلْح َّ عْ ق َّزِى ِّ ق َّالَّ: لَّم َّا إ َّن ْ ن َّق َّزْب ُّ مِن ْ مِن ًى ن َّوَّ ي ْث ُّ إَّلْمُّق َّام
َّن ِمَّك َّه َّ ق َّا َّي ْمَّمْ ث ُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ ي ُّم َّ ج َّ اءَّن ِى ج َّ ن َّز مِن َّ إَّلْمَّن ْز ِلِ ق َّلَّمْ إ َّج ِ ذْ ن ُّذ إً مِن َّ إَّلْمَّصِ ي زِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْم ن ْز ِلِ ق َّلَّمْ إ َّذْ رِ إ ُّي ِم ُّ إ َّمْ إ ُّق َّصِّ زُّ وَّ إ َّن ُّو

english_text:
It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from Hamza ibn Abdullah
al-Ja'fari who said: “When I departed from Mina, I intended to stay in Mecca, so I
completed the prayer. Then news came from my home, and that I had no choice but
to return. I was uncertain whether to continue completing my prayers or to shorten
them. At that time, Abu al-Hasan {a.s} was in Mecca, so I approached him and explained
the situation.”
Imam {a.s} said to me: "Return to shortening [your prayers]”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 443 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 221 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 239 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 153 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 509

Al-Fudhayl ibn Yasaar reported from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"There is no Jumu'ah (Jumu’ah prayer), nor Eid al-Adha, nor Eid al-Fitr for the traveler”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
- وَّ رَّوَّ ى إ ِسْ مَّاعِ ي لُّ ن ْن ُّ ج َّ ان ِزٍ ق َّالَّ: ق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّذْ ج ُّ لُّ عَّلَّى َّ وَّ ق ْث ُّ إَّلص َّ ل ِاَّة ِ وَّ إ َّن َّا ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّز
َّ ق َّلاَّ إ ُّصَّ لِّى جَّ ي َّى إ َّذْ ج ُّ لَّ إ َّهْلِى ق َّق َّالَّ «صَّ لِّ وَّ إ َّي ِم َّإَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ» ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّي َّذْ ج ُّ لُّ عَّلَّى َّ وَّ ق ْث ُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ وَّ إ َّن َّا ق ِى إ َّهْلِى إ ُّرِي ذُّ إَّلس َّ ق َّز
ُّق َّلاَّ إ ُّصَّ لِّى جَّ ي َّى إ َّج ْ زُّح َّ ق َّالَّ «صَّ لِّ وَّ ق َّصِّ زْ ق َّا ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّق ْ عَّلْ ق َّق َّذْ ج َّ الَّق ْث َّ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّه
ِعَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه.
english_text:
Ismail ibn Jabir reported: “I said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"The time for prayer enters while I am traveling, so I do not pray until I return home."
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray and complete the prayer."
I said: "The time for prayer enters while I am at home and I intend to travel, so I do not
pray until I have departed."
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray and shorten the prayer, for if you do not, you have opposed
Messenger of Allah {saws}”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 443 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 13 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 3, p. 163 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 222 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 240 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 111 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 146 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 512 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 46

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ْ وَّ إ َّم َّا ج َّ ن َّزُّ جَّ زِي ز ٍ عَّن ْ مُّ حَّ م َّذِ ن ْن ِ مُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ عَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ ي َّذْ ج ُّ لُّ مِن

ُّ إ ِلَّى سَّ ق َّزِةِ وَّ ق َّذْ ذَّج َّ لَّ وَّ ق ْث
ًإَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّلْي ُّصَّ لِّ إ َّرْن َّعا .
ق ا ن ه ي عن ى ن ه إ ذ إ كان لأ ي ح اف ق وإب ج زوح إلوق ث إ ي م وإ ن ج اف ج زوح إلوق ث ق صز، وي صذي ق ذ لك:
english_text:
Regarding the report of Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Imam Jafar
ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, who said:
"I asked him about a man who returns from his journey while the time for prayer has
entered, and he is still on the road."
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray two rak'ahs (units of prayer). If he sets out on a journey
and the time for prayer has already entered, then he should pray four rak'ahs."
commentary:
Indeed, it means that if there is no fear of the time passing, he should complete it. But
if there is fear of the time passing, he should shorten it. And the proof for this is: (in the
next hadith)
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 434 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 443 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 13 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 222 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 239 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 145 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 513 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 516 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 47

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّق ِى كِي َّاب ِ إَّلْحَّ كَّمِ ن ْن ِ مِسْ كِي ن ٍ ق َّالَّ ق َّالَّ إ َّن ُّو عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِ ق ِى إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّق ْذَّمُّ مِن ْ سَّ ق َّزِةِ ق ِى وَّ ق ْث
ْصَّ لاَّة ٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ لأَّ ي َّح َّ اف ُّ ج ُّ زُّوح َّ إَّلْوَّ ق ْث ِ ق َّلْي ُّي ِم َّ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ي َّح َّ اف ُّ ج ُّ زُّوح َّ إَّلْوَّ ق ْث ِ ق َّلْي ُّق َّصِّ ز .
وهذ إ موإق ق لحذي ث إ سماعي ل ن ن ج ان ز.
english_text:
In the book of Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, it is reported that Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who arrives from his journey during
the time for a prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he does not fear that the time for the prayer will expire, he should
complete it (in full). But if he fears that the time will expire, he should shorten it”.
commentary: This is in accordance with the hadith of Ismail ibn Jabir.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 444 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 223 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 3, p. 223 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 240 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 241 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 147 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 514 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 49

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إ ِسْ حَّ اق ُّ ن ْن ُّ عَّم َّارٍ إ َّن َّا إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مَّ مُّوسَّ ى ن ْن َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّم:

ِإ ِلَّى إ َّهْلِه .
english_text:
Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Abu Ibrahim Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}
about a man who is traveling and then arrives, entering the boundaries of Kufa.
He asked: "Should he perform the full prayer or continue to shorten it until he enters
his home?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Rather, he should continue to shorten it until he enters his home”.
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 434 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 444 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 222 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 242 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 142 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 474

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
وَّ رَّوَّ ى َّسَّ ي ْف إَّلي َّم َّارُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: ق َّالَّ لَّهُّ ن َّعْ ض ُّ إ َّصْ حَّ ان ِن َّا كُّن َّا ن َّق ْص ِ ى صَّ لا ة َّ إَّلن َّهَّارِ إ ِذ َّإ
َّ ن َّز َّلْن َّا ن َّي ْن َّ إَّلْمَّع ْ زِب ِ وَّ إَّلْعِس َّ اءِ إَّلْأ ج ِ زَّة ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ إَّلل َّهُّ إ َّعْ لَّمُّ ن ِعِن َّاذِةِ جِ ي ن َّ رَّج ِضَّ إ ِن َّمَّا ق َّزَّض َّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ عَّلَّى إَّلْمُّسَّ اق ِز
َّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ لأَّ ق َّن ْلَّهُّمَّا وَّ لأَّ ن َّعْ ذَّهُّمَّا س َّ ى ْ ء إ ِلأ َّ صَّ لاَّة ُّ إَّلل َّي ْلِ عَّلَّى ن َّعِي زِك َّ جَّ ي ْث ُّ ي َّوَّ ج َّ هَّ ن ِك .
english_text:
Saif al-Tammar narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
one of our companions said to him:
"We used to make up the daytime prayers when we would stop between Maghrib
(evening prayer) and Isha (night prayer)."
He {a.s} replied: "No, Allah {SWT} knows His servants best when He granted the
concession. Allah {SWT} the Mighty and Majestic has prescribed for the traveler two
rak'ahs (units of prayer); there is nothing before or after them except for the night
prayer while you are on your mount, wherever it may take you”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 445 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 16 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 120 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 84

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سُّ ن ِلَّ إ َّن ُّو عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِعَّن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلن َّاق ِلَّه ِ ن ِالن َّهَّارِ ق ِى سَّ ق َّزٍ ق َّق َّالَّ «لَّوْ صَّ لَّحَّ ث ِ إَّلن َّاق ِلَّه ُّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّز
ُّ ي َّم َّث ِ إَّلْق َّزِي ص َّ ه.
ولأ ن ا س ن ق ص اء صلاة إللي ل ن الن هار ق ى إلسق ز.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about performing the
supererogatory (nafilah) prayers during the day while traveling.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it were appropriate to perform the nafilah (supererogatory) prayers
during travel, then the obligatory (fardh) prayers would have been completed (in full)”.
commentary:
However, there is no harm in making up the night prayers during the day while
traveling.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text: ٍوَّ كَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى عَّلَّى رَّإجِ لَّي ِهِ إَّلْق َّزِي ص َّ ه َّ ق ِى ي َّوْ مٍ مَّ طِ ي ز.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} would perform the obligatory prayer on his mount
on a rainy day.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 445 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 523

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّ إ ِن ْزَّإهِي مُّ إَّلْكَّزْج ِ ى:
ِق ُّلْث ُّ لِأ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِن ِّى إ َّق ْذِرُّ إ َّن ْ إ َّي َّوَّ ج َّ هَّ ن َّحْ وَّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ ق ِى إَّلْمَّحْ مِل
ق َّق َّالَّ «هَّذ َّإ إَّلص ِّ ي ق ُّ إ َّ مَّ ا لَّكُّمْ ق ِى رَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ ُّسْ وَّ ة.
english_text:
Ibrahim al-Karkhi said:
"I said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}: "I am able to face the Qiblah
(direction of prayer) while in the mahmil (a covered mount or carrier)."
He {a.s} replied: "Is this restriction (truly necessary) ? Do you not have in the Messenger
of Allah {saws} an example to follow?"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
english_text:
Sa'd ibn Sa'd asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s} about a man who is with a
menstruating woman in a mahmil (covered mount or carrier).
He asked: "Should he pray while She is with him?"
He {a.s} replied: "Yes”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ سَّ عِي ذُّ ن ْن ُّي َّسَّ ارٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ْ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلل َّي ْلِ وَّ هُّوَّ عَّلَّى ذَّإن َّي ِهِ إ َّ لَّهُّ إ َّن
َّ ي ُّع َّطِّ ى َّ وَّ ج ْ هَّهُّ وَّ هُّوَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّالَّ «إ َّم َّا إ ِذ َّإ ق َّزَّإ َّ ق َّن َّعَّمْ وَّ إ َّم َّا إ ِذ َّإ إ َّوْ مَّ ا َّ ن ِوَّ ج ْ هِهِ لِلس ُّ ح ُّ وذِ ق َّلْي ِكْس ِ ق ْ هُّ جَّ ي ْث ُّ مَّ ا إ َّوْ مَّ ا َّب ْ ن ِه
ُّ إَّلذ َّإن َّه.
english_text:
Sa'id ibn Yasarasked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
performing the night prayer while on his mount.
He asked: "Is it permissible for him to cover his face while praying?"
He {a.s} replied: "Yes, when he is reciting (the Qur'an). However, when he gestures with
his face for prostration, he should uncover it wherever the mount takes him”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 446 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 329 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 422

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّن ْذُّ إَّلز َّجْ مَّن ِ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْحَّ ح َّ اح ِ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إَّلن َّوَّ إق ِلَّ ق ِى إَّلْأ َّمْ صَّ ارِ وَّ هُّو
َّعَّلَّى ذَّإن َّي ِهِ جَّ ي ْي ُّمَّا ي َّوَّ ج َّ هَّث ْ ن ِهِ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْس .
english_text:
Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
about a man performing supererogatory (nafilah) prayers in towns and cities while on
his mount, wherever it faces.
He {a.s} replied: "There is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ي َّق ْطِ ي ن ٍ ، إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّح ْ زُّح ُّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ ي ُّم َّ ي َّن ْذُّو لَّهُّ ق ِى إَّلْأ ِق َّامَّ ه ِ و
َّهُّوَّ ق ِى إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّي ِم ُّ إ ِذ َّإ ن َّذَّب ْ لَّهُّ إَّلْأ ِق َّامَّ ه ُّ» وَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّس َّ ي ِّغُّ إ َّج َّ اةُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْمَّكَّان ِ إ ُّل َّذ ِى ي َّح ِ ث ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق ِي هِ إَّلي َّق ْصِ ي ز
ْوَّ إَّل َّ أ ِق ْطَّ ارُّ ق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ ن ِذ َّلِك .
. ولأ ن ا س ن الح مغ ن ي ن إلصلاي ي ن ق ى إلسق ز وإلحص ز من عله وع ي ز عله . ولأ ن ا س ن ي ا ج ي ز إلمع زب ق ى إلسق ز جي ى ي ع ي ث إلس ق ق
.ولأ ن ا س ن ي ا ج ي ز إلمع زب للمساق ز إ ذ إ كان ق ى طلث إلمن ز ل إ لى رن غ إللي ل
english_text:
Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu al-Hasan {a.s} about a man who sets out on a journey
and then decides to stay (reside) while he is in the midst of prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should complete (the full prayer) when he decides to stay."
He also asked about a man who accompanies his brother to the point where
shortening prayers and breaking the fast becomes obligatory.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in that."
commentary:
There is also no harm in combining two prayers during travel or when at home, whether
due to a reason or without a reason. There is no harm in delaying the Maghrib prayer
during travel until the twilight has disappeared. There is no harm in a traveler delaying
Maghrib prayer until one-quarter of the night if he is seeking a place to rest.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
:َّوَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ إ َّن ِى ن َّصِ ي زٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّال «إ َّن ْث َّ ق ِى وَّ ق ْث ِ إَّلْمَّع ْ زِب ِ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ إ ِلَّى
ِج َّ مْ سَّ ه ِ إ َّمْ ي َّالٍ مِن ْ ن َّعْ ذِ ع ُّزُّوب ِ إَّلس َّ مْ س .
ولأ ن ا س ن ي عح ي ل إلعي مه ق ى إلسق ز ق ن ل مع ي ث إلس ق ق.
english_text:
In a narration from Abu Basir, Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "You are in the time of
Maghrib (evening prayer) while traveling up to a distance of five miles after sunset”.
commentary:
There is no harm in hastening Isha prayer during travel before the disappearance of
twilight.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 447 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 234 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 291 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 194

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّم َّار إَّلس َّ ان َّاطِ ى ُّ ، إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم :
ُّعَّن ْ جَّ ذِّ إَّلطِّ ي ن ِ إَّل َّذ ِى لأَّ ي ُّسْ ح َّ ذُّ ق ِي هِ مَّ ا ه َّوَّ ق َّال «إ ِذ َّإ
ِ ع َّزِق َّث ْ ق ِي هِ إَّلْح َّ ن ْهَّه ُّ وَّ لَّمْ ي َّي ْن ُّث ْ عَّلَّى إَّلْأ َّرْض .
english_text:
Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the
extent of wetness or mud that makes it unsuitable for prostration.
Imam {a.s} said: "When the forehead sinks into it and does not remain firm on the
ground”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 447 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 312 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 2, p. 376 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 143 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 306

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
english_text:
Muawiya ibn Ammar said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}: "The
people of Mecca complete (perform in full) their prayers at Arafat."
He {a.s} replied: "Woe to them! (Or, Alas for them!) What journey is more significant than
this? No, it should not be completed”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 447 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 433 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 487

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ«إ ِن َّ رَّسُّ ولَّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ لَّم َّا ن َّز َّلَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ج َّ ن ْزَّن ِي لُّ ن ِالي َّق ْصِ ي زِ ق َّالَّ لَّه
ْ إَّلن َّن ِى ُّ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ «ق ِى كَّمْ ذ َّلِك َّ » ق َّق َّالَّ ق ِى ن َّزِي ذٍ ق َّالَّ «وَّ كَّمِ إَّلْن َّزِي ذُّ» ق َّالَّ مَّ ا ن َّي َّن َّ ط ِ لِّ ع ٍي ْ زٍ إ ِلَّى ق َّى ْ ءِ وُّعَّي ْ ز
ق َّذ َّرَّعَّي ْهُّ ن َّن ُّو إ ُّمَّ ي َّه َّ ي ُّم َّ ج َّ ز َّءُّوةُّ عَّلَّى إِي ْن َّى ْ عَّس َّ زَّ مِي لاً ق َّكَّان َّ كُّل ُّ مِي لٍ إ َّلْق اً وَّ ج َّ مْ سَّ مِان َّه ِ ذ ِرَّإ َّ عٍ وَّ هُّوَّ إ َّرْن َّعَّه ُّ ق َّزَّإسِ ح .
ي عن ى إ ن ه إ ذ إ كان إلسق ز إ رن عه ق زإسح وإ رإذ إلزج وع من ي ومه ق الي ق صي ز علي ه وإج ث ، ومي ى لم ي زذ إلزج وع من ي ومه ق هو
ن الح ي ار إ ن س اء إ ي م وإ ن س اء ق صز وي صذي ق ما ق سزب من ذ لك:
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"When Archangel Jibril {a.s} descended upon the Messenger of Allah {saws} with the ruling
of shortening (the prayer), the Prophet {saws} asked him, 'For how long (a distance) is this
required?'
Archangel Jibril {a.s} replied: 'For a barid.'
The Prophet {saws} asked: 'And what is a barid?'
Jibril said: 'The distance between the shadow of 'Ayr to the shade of Wu'ayr.'
The Banu Umayyah measured it, divided it into twelve miles, with each mile being one
thousand five hundred cubits, equating to four farsakhs (parasangs).'"
commentary:
It means that if the journey is four farsakhs (a unit of distance) and he intends to return
on the same day, shortening (the prayer) is obligatory for him. However, if he does not
intend to return on the same day, he has the choice - whether to complete the prayer
or to shorten it. The proof for this explanation is: (in the following hadith).
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 447 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 125 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p.

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِج َّ ن َّزُّ ج َّ مِي لِ ن ْن ِ ذَّر َّإح ٍ عَّن ْ ر ُّرَّإرَّة َّ ن ْن ِ إ َّعْ ي َّن َّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْث ُّ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ ه إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلي َّق ْصِ ي زِ ق َّق َّالَّ «ن َّزِي ذ
َّذ َّإهِث وَّ ن َّزِي ذ ج َّ ان ِى وَّ كَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ ِذ َّإ إ َّي َّى ذ ُّن َّان اً ق َّص َّ ز.
وذ ن اب على ن زي ذ وإ ن ما ق عل ذ لك لأ ن ه إ ذ إ رج غ كان سق زة ن زي ذ ن ن ي مان ي ه ق زإسح.
english_text:
Jamil ibn Darraj reported from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far {a.s} about the ruling for shortening the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "A barid going and a barid returning. The Messenger of Allah {saws} would
shorten his prayers when he reached Dhu'bāb."
commentary:
Dhu'bāb was at a distance of a barid (approximately 12 miles), and the reason for this
was that upon his return, his total journey would amount to two barids, which equals
eight farsakhs.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ر َّكَّزِي َّا ن ْن ُّ إ ذَّمَّ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ عَّن ِ إَّلي َّق ْصِ ي زِ ق ِى كَّمْ ي ُّق َّصِّ زُّ إَّلز َّج ِلُّ إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ ق ِى ص ِ ي َّاع
إ َّهْلِ ن َّي ْي ِهِ وَّ إ َّمْ زُّةُّ ج َّ ان ِز ق ِي هَّا ي َّسِ ي زُّ ق ِى ِ إَّلص ِّ ي َّاعِ ي َّوْ مَّ ي ْن ِ وَّ لَّي ْلَّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ ي َّلاَّي َّه َّ إ َّي َّامٍ وَّ لَّي َّالِي َّهُّن َّ ق َّكَّي َّث َّ «إَّلي َّق ْصِ ي زُّ ق ِى مَّ سِ ي زَّة
ٍ ي َّوْ مٍ وَّ لَّي ْلَّه .
english_text:
Zakariyya ibn Adam asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s} about the distance for
shortening prayers when a man is in the lands belonging to his family and has control
over them, traveling through these lands for two days and two nights or three days and
their nights.
Abu al-Hasan {a.s} wrote in response;
"Shortening is applicable for the journey of one day and one night."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 450 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 140

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِ وَّ رَّوَّ ى مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ إ َّن ِى عُّمَّي ْ زٍ عَّن ْ مُّحَّ م َّذِ ن ْن ِ إ ِسْ حَّ اق َّ ن ْن ٍ عَّم َّارٍ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْث ُّ إ َّن َّا إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّ عَّن ِ إِمْ زَّإ َّة
كَّان َّث ْ ق ِى طَّ زِي ق ِ مَّ ك َّه َّ ق َّصَّ ل َّث ْ ذ َّإهِن َّه ً وَّ ج َّ ان ِي َّه ً إَّلْمَّع ْ زِب َّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لَّي ْسَّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا
إ ِعَّاذَّة.
ِ وَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه
إَّلْحُّ سَّ ي ْن ِ ن ْن ِ سَّ عِي ذٍ عَّن ِ إِن ْن ِ إ َّن ِى عُّمَّي ْ زٍ عَّن ْ مُّحَّ م َّذِ ن ْن ِ إ ِسْ حَّ اق َّ ن ْن ِ عَّم َّارٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ عَّ ق َّا لَّ: «لَّي ْسَّ عَّلَّي ْهَّا ق َّص َّ اء.
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr reported from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar,
who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s} about a woman who was on the way to
Mecca and performed the Maghrib prayer two rak'ahs going and two rak'ahs returning.
Imam {a.s} said: "She does not need to repeat it."
In another narration from al-Hussain ibn Sa'id, from ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad
ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan {a.s},
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no obligation to make it up."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 450 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 969

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِ وَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ إَّلْعَّلاَّءِ عَّن ْ مُّحَّ م َّذِ ن ْن ٍمُّسْ لِمٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ صَّ ل َّى إَّلْمُّسَّ اق ِزُّ ج َّ لْف َّ ق َّوْ م
جُّ ص ُّ ورٍ ق َّلْي ُّي ِم َّ صَّ لاَّي َّهُّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ ي ُّسَّ لِّمُّ وَّ إ ِن ْ صَّ ل َّى مَّ عَّهُّمُّ إَّلط ُّ هْ زَّ ق َّلْي َّح ْ عَّلِ إَّلْأ َّو َّ لَّي َّي ْن ِ إَّل ْط ُّ هْ زَّ وَّ إَّلْأ َّج ِ ي زَّي َّي ْن ِ إَّل َّعَّصْ ز.
english_text:
In a narration from Al-‘Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Imam
Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}, He said:
"If a traveler prays behind residents (those who are not traveling), he should complete
his prayer as two rak'ahs and then give the salutation (end the prayer).
If he prays with them at Dhuhr (noon prayer), he should make the first two rak'ahs for
Dhuhr and the last two for Asr (afternoon prayer)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V1, p.451 • Wasail Al-Shia, V8, p.329 • Wasail Al-Shia, V 8, p. 400

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ إ ِسْ مَّاعِ ي لُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْق َّص ْ لِ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّعَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ ي ُّسَّ اق ِزُّ مِن ْ إ َّرْض ٍ إ ِلَّى إ َّرْ ض ٍ وَّ إ ِن َّمَّا ي َّن ْز ِل
َّ ق ُّزَّإةُّ وَّ ص َّ ي ْعَّي َّهُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ ن َّز َّلْث َّ ق ُّزَّإك َّ وَّ إ َّرْص َّ ك َّ ق َّا َّي ِم َّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ وَّ إ ِذ َّإ كُّن ْث َّ ق ِى ع َّي ْ زِ إ َّرْص ِ ك َّ ق ْق َّصِّ ز.
ق ال مصن ف هذ إ إلكي اب رجمه إلله : ي عن ى ن ذ لك إ ذ إ إ رإذ إلمق ام ق ى ق زإة وإ رص ه عس زة إ ي ام ومي ى لم ي زذ إلمق ام ن ها عس زة
إ ي ام ق صز إ لأ إ ن ي كون لها ن ه من ز ل ي كون ق ي ه ق ى إلسن ه سي ه إ س هز، ق ا ن كان كذ لك إ ي م مي ى ذج لها، وي صذي ق ذ لك:
english_text:
Ismail ibn al-Fadl asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
who travels from one land to another but resides in his own villages and properties.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you stay in your own village or land, then complete the prayer; if you
are in land that is not yours, then shorten the prayer."
commentary:
The compiler of this book, may Allah {SWT} have mercy upon him, added: This applies if
he intends to stay in his village or land for ten days. If he does not intend to stay for ten
days, he should shorten the prayer unless he has a residence there where he stays for
six months of the year; in that case, he should complete the prayer whenever he enters
it.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 451 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 213 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 231 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 36

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّمَّ ا رَّوَّ إةُّ مُّحَّ م َّذُّ ن ْن ُّ إ ِسْ مَّاعِ ي لَّ ن ْن ِ ن َّز ِي غٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلزِّص َّ ا عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ ع ُّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّق َّصِّ ز
َّق ِى ص َّ ي ْ عَّي ِهِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لأَّ ن َّا ْسَّ مَّ ا لَّمْ ي َّن ْوِ مُّق َّامَّ عَّس َّ زَّة ِ إ َّي َّامٍ إ ِلأ َّ إ َّن ْ ي َّكُّون َّ لَّهُّ ن ِه ا مَّ ن ْز ِل ي َّسْ ي َّوْ طِ ن ُّهُّ» ق َّالَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ لَّهُّ مَّ ا
َّإَّلأِسْ ي ِي طَّ ان ُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ َّن ْ ي َّكُّون َّ لَّهُّ ن ِهَّا مَّ ن ْز ِل ي ُّق ِي مُّ ق ِي هِ سِ ي َّه َّ إ َّس ْ هُّزٍ ق َّا ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ كَّذ َّلِك َّ ي ُّي ِم ُّ ق ِي ه
ا مَّ ي َّى ذَّج َّ لَّهَّا .
english_text:
Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' reported from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s} that
he asked about a man shortening his prayers at his property.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm as long as he does not intend to stay for ten days,
unless he has a house there where he resides."
I asked him, "What is meant by 'resides'?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It means he has a house where he stays for six months. If that is the
case, he should complete (his prayers) whenever he enters it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 451 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 213 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 231 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 36

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
وَّ مَّ ا َّ رَّوَّ إةُّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ ي َّق ْطِ ي ن ٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن ِ إَّلْأ َّو َّلِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «كُّل ُّ مَّ ن ْز ِلٍ مِن ْ مَّ ن ُّار ِلِك َّ لأَّ ي َّسْ ي َّوْ طِ ن ُّه
ُّق َّعَّلَّي ْك َّ ق ِي هِ إَّلي َّق ْصِ ي ز.
english_text:
Ali ibn Yaqtin reported from Abu al-Hasan the First {a.s} who said:
"For every dwelling of yours that you do not consider a permanent residence, you must
shorten your prayers there."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 451 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 161 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 492 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 125

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ُّ ق ِى إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّح ْ زُّح ُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلص َّ ي ْذِ مَّ سِ ي زَّة َّ ي َّوْ مٍ إ َّوْ ي َّوْ مَّ ي ْن ِ إ َّوْ ي َّلاَّي َّه ً إ َّ ي ُّق َّصِّ زُّ إ َّوْ ي ُّي ِم
َّق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ ج َّ زَّح َّ لِق ُّوي ِهِ وَّ ق ُّوب ِ عِ ي َّالِهِ ق َّلْي ُّق َّصِّ زْ وَّ لْي ُّق ْطِ زْ وَّ إ ِن ْ ج َّ زَّح َّ لِطَّ لَّث ِ إَّلْق ُّص ُّ ولِ ق َّلاَّ وَّ لأ َّ كَّزَّإمَّ ه.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked regarding a man who goes
out for hunting for a journey of one day, two days, or three days:
"Should he shorten his prayers or complete them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If he goes out for his sustenance and the sustenance of his family, he
should shorten his prayers and break his fast. But if he goes out seeking leisure or
excess (unnecessary pursuit), then no, and it is not permissible."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 438 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 452 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 217 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 236 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 174 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 480

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِ وَّ رَّوَّ ى إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي زٍ إ َّن َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «لَّي ْ سَّ عَّلَّى صَّ اجِ ث ِ إَّلص َّ ي ْذِ ي َّق ْصِ ي ز ي َّلاَّي َّه َّ إ َّي َّامٍ ق َّا َّ ذ َّإ ج َّ اوَّ ر َّ إَّلي َّلاَّي َّه
ُّلَّز ِمَّ ه.
.ي عن ى إلصي ذ للق ص ول
english_text:
Abu Basir reported that Imam {a.s} said:
"A hunter is not required to shorten his prayers for three days; however, if he goes
beyond three days, then it becomes obligatory upon him to do so."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 452 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 218 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 236 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 177 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 479

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رَّوَّ ى عِ ي ضُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْق َّاسِ مِ عَّن ْهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّإ َّن َّهُّ سُّ ن ِلَّ عَّن ِ إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي َّي َّصَّ ي َّذُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ي َّذُّورُّ جَّ وْ لَّهُّ ق َّلا
ْي ُّق َّصِّ زْ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ ي َّح َّ اوَّ ر َّ إَّلْوَّ ق ْث َّ ق َّلْي ُّق َّصِّ ز.
ولو إ ن مساق زإ ممن ي ح ث علي ه إلي ق صي ز مال عن طزي ق ه إ لى صي ذ
لوج ث علي ه إلي مام لطلث إلصي ذ، ق ا ن رج غ من صي ذة إ لى
إلطزي ق ق علي ه ق ى رج وعه إلي ق صي ز.
english_text:
Ays ibn al-Qasim reported that He {a.s} was asked about a man who goes
hunting.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he is moving around within his vicinity (local area), then he should
not shorten his prayer. But if he goes beyond (a specified distance), he should
shorten."
commentary:
If a traveler who is obligated to shorten his prayers diverts from his path for the
purpose of hunting, he must then complete his prayers due to the pursuit of hunting.
However, if he returns to his path, he should revert to shortening his prayers.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 452 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 481

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِن ْ ج َّ س ِ ي ث َّ إ َّن ْ لأَّ ي َّق ُّومَّ ق ِى إ ج ِ زِ إَّلل َّي ْلِ إ َّوْ كَّان َّث ْ ن ِك
ِعِ ل َّه إ َّوْ إ َّصَّ ان َّك َّ ن َّزْذ ق َّصَّ لِّ وَّ إ َّوْ ي ِزْ ق ِى إ َّو َّلِ إَّلل َّي ْلِ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّز .
english_text:
Al-Halabi reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If you fear that you will not be able to wake up at the end of the night, or if you have an
ailment or are afflicted by cold, then pray and perform the Witr prayer at the beginning
of the night while traveling."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 453 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 227 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 250

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:
ِوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ سَّ عِي ذٍ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ ه ُّإَّلس َّ لاَّم:
َّعَّن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلل َّي ْلِ وَّ إَّلْوَّ ي ْزِ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ ق ِى إ َّو َّلِ إَّلل َّي ْلِ ق َّال
ْ«ن َّعَّم .
english_text:
Ali ibn Sa'id asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about performing
the night prayer and Witr prayer during travel at the beginning of the night.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER DURING TRAVEL
arabic_text:

english_text:
Sama'a ibn Mehran asked Abu al-Hasan the First {a.s} about the timing of the
night prayer during travel.
Imam {a.s} said: "From the time you perform the 'Atamah (Isha, the night prayer) until
the break of dawn (Fajr)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Hariz reported from someone who narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali
Al-Baqir {a.s} that he did not see any problem with praying while walking, as long as he
was not driving the camels.

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked:
"Why is the Maghrib prayer three rak'ahs with an additional four rak'ahs
(supererogatory) afterward, and why is there no shortening of it during residence or
travel?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Indeed, Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to His Prophet {saws}
every prayer as two rak'ahs. The Messenger of Allah {saws} added two rak'ahs to each
prayer in residence and shortened them during travel, except for the Maghrib and Fajr
(morning) prayers. When the Prophet {saws} performed the Maghrib prayer, he was
informed of the birth of Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}, so he added a rak'ah out of
gratitude to Allah {SWT}, Mighty and Majestic. When Hasan {a.s} was born, he added two
more rak'ahs out of gratitude to Allah {SWT}, and when Hussain {a.s} was born, he added
two more rak'ahs out of gratitude to Allah {SWT}.
He then said: 'For a male, the share is twice that of a female,' and thus he left the
prayer in its current form during residence and travel."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 454 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 324 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 113 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 192 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 88 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 37, p. 38 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 262 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 543 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 3, p. 201 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 3, p. 524

english_text:
Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Naysaburi, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him,
mentioned among the reasons he heard from al-Ridha {a.s} regarding why prayers are
shortened during travel.
He (Imam {a.s}) said: "The initially prescribed obligatory prayer was ten rak'ahs. The
seven additional rak'ahs were later added, and Allah {SWT}, the Blessed and Exalted,
lightened this addition for the servant due to the burden, fatigue, and preoccupation
of travel. This relief was granted so that the servant would not become distracted from
the essential needs of their livelihood during travel. However, the Maghrib prayer is not
shortened because it was originally set as a shortened prayer.
The obligation to shorten applies to eight farsakhs (a day's journey) and no less. The
reason for this is that eight farsakhs is a day’s journey for the common people,
caravans, and baggage carriers, necessitating shortening for such a journey.
If the obligation were not established for a day’s journey, it would not be required for a
journey of a thousand years, as every day after this day is similar to it ; if it were not
obligatory for this day, it would not be obligatory for its equivalent.
Voluntary prayers during the day are omitted while traveling, but not voluntary prayers
at night, because every prayer that is not shortened also maintains its voluntary
aspect. Thus, the Maghrib prayer is not shortened, so neither are the voluntary prayers
that follow it.
Similarly, the Fajr prayer is not shortened, so neither are the voluntary prayers
preceding it. The Isha prayer (Atamah) is considered shortened, but its two rak'ahs are
not omitted because they are not part of the fifty obligatory rak'ahs; rather, they are
additional voluntary rak'ahs to complete the fifty.
These extra rak'ahs serve as compensation, with two voluntary rak'ahs taking the
place of every rak'ah of obligation. The traveler and the sick are permitted to perform
the night prayer at the beginning of the night due to their preoccupation, weakness, or
to ensure they fulfil their prayers and gain rest or focus on their travel."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 454 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 191

إ ِلَّى إَّلس َّ مَّاءِ وَّ لِي َّعْ ح ِ ي لِ ن ُّز ُّولِ مَّ لاَّن ِكَّه ِ إَّلن َّهَّارِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْأ َّرْض ِ ق َّكَّان َّث ْ مَّ لاَّن ِكَّه ُّ إَّلن َّهَّارِ وَّ مَّ ل ِاَّن ِكَّه ُّ إَّلل َّي ْلِ ي َّس ْ هَّذُّون َّ مَّ غَّ رَّسُّ ول
َّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلْق َّح ْ زِ ق َّلِذ َّلِك َّ ق َّالَّ إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّن َّارَّك وي َّعَّالَّى ً«وَّ ق ُّزْإ ن َّ إَّلْق َّح ْ زِ إ ِن َّ ق ُّزْإ ن َّ إَّلْق َّح ْ زِ كٰان َّ مَّ س ْ هُّوذإ
َّي َّس ْ هَّذُّةُّ إَّلْمُّسْ لِمُّون َّ وَّ ي َّس ْ ه ِذُّةُّ مَّ لاَّن ِكَّه ُّ إَّلن َّهَّارِ وَّ مَّ لاَّن ِكَّه ُّ إَّلل َّي ْل .
english_text:
Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib asked Ali ibn al-Hussain {a.s},
"When was the prayer made obligatory upon the Muslims in the form it is today?"
He {a.s} replied: "In Medina, when the call (to Islam) became manifest, Islam was
strengthened, and Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, prescribed jihad upon the
Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah {saws} added seven rak'ahs to the prayers: two to Dhuhr, two to
Asr, one to Maghrib, and two to the Isha prayer, while leaving the Fajr prayer as it had
been prescribed in Mecca.
This was to hasten the ascent of the night’s angels to the heavens and the descent of
the day’s angels to the earth. Thus, the angels of the night and the angels of the day
would witness the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah {saws}.
This is why Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Recite the Qur'an at dawn. Indeed,
the recitation of the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed' (Qur'an 17:78) - witnessed by
the Muslims and by the angels of the night and the angels of the day."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 455 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 324 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 65 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 51 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 79, p. 263 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 3, p. 202 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 7, p. 476

english_text:
Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about praying on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: "Face the Qiblah and place your feet firmly.
If the ship turns and you are able to adjust to face the Qiblah, then do so. If not, then
pray in whatever direction it turns you.
If you can stand, then pray standing; otherwise, sit and pray”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER ON A SHIP
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ٍ لَّهُّ ج َّ مِي لُّ ن ْن ُّ ذَّر َّإح:
ي َّكُّون ُّ إَّلس َّ ق ِي ن َّه ُّ ق َّزِي ن َّه ً مِن َّ إَّلْح ُّ ذِّ، ق َّا َّج ْ زُّح ُّ وَّ إ ُّصَّ لِّى ق َّالَّ «صَّ لِّ ق ِي هَّا إ َّ مَّ ا ي َّزْص َّ ى
ُّن ِصَّ لاَّة ِ ن ُّوحٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم.
english_text:
Jamil ibn Darraj asked him (Abu Abdullah {a.s}):
"The ship is close to the shore ; should I disembark and pray?"
He {a.s} replied: "Pray on it (the ship). Are you not content with the prayer of Noah {a.s}?"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER ON A SHIP

» ن َّح ْ زُّح ُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْأ َّهْوَّ إر ِ ق ِى إَّلس ُّ ق ُّن ِ ق َّن ُّح َّ مِّغُّ ق ِي هَّا إَّلص َّ لاَّة َّ ق َّق َّالَّ «ن َّعَّمْ لَّي ْسَّ ن ِهِ ن َّا ْس

english_text:
Ibrahim ibn Maymun said to him (Abu Abdullah {a.s}):
"We travel to Ahwaz in ships, and we combine the prayers on board."
He {a.s} replied: "Yes, there is no harm in that."
He further asked: "And we prostrate on what is in the ship and on the pitch (tar)?"
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 457 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 298 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 530 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 320

arabic_text: ِ وَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْهُّ مَّ ن ْصُّ ورُّ ن ْن ُّ جَّ ار ِمٍ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّلْق ِي زُّ مِن ْ ن َّن َّاب ِ إَّلْأ َّرْ ض .
english_text:
Mansur ibn Hazim reported from him (Abu Abdullah {a.s}) that He said: "Pitch
(tar) is from the vegetation of the earth."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 457 • Al-Wafi, V. 8, p. 736 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 355

Chapter Title: PRAYER ON A SHIP
arabic_text: ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ إ َّن َّا ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم: ق ِى إَّلز َّج ُّ لِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إَّلن َّوَّ إق ِلَّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق ِي ن َّه ِ ق َّالَّ «ي ُّصَّ لِّى ن َّحْ وَّ رَّإ ْسِ هَّا .
english_text:
Zurarah asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man performing
supererogatory (nafilah) prayers on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray in the direction of its front (bow)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text:
ُّوَّ سَّ ا َّلَّ ي ُّون ُّسُّ ن ْن ُّ ي َّعْ ق ُّوب َّ إ َّن َّا عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ِعَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق ِى إَّلْق ُّزَّإب ِ وَّ مَّ ا هُّوَّ إ َّصْ ع َّزُّ مِن ْهُّ مِن َّ إَّلْأ َّن ْهَّار

english_text:
Yunus ibn Ya'qub asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
praying in the Euphrates or smaller rivers while on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: "If you pray (on the ship), it is good (acceptable), and if you disembark
to pray, it is also good (acceptable)."
He further asked about praying on a ship that moves eastward and westward.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Face the Qiblah, say the takbir (opening declaration of prayer), and
then turn with the ship wherever it turns."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: PRAYER ON A SHIP
arabic_text:

ًي َّي َّحَّ ز َّك ْ ق َّصَّ لِّ ق َّان ِماً وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّث ْ ج َّ ق ِي ق َّه ً ي َّكَّق َّا ُّ ق َّصَّ لِّ ق َّاعِ ذإ .
english_text:
Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi asked Imam {a.s} about praying on a ship.
Imam {a.s} said: "If it is heavily loaded and does not move when you stand, then pray
standing. But if it is light and unstable, then pray seated."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 442 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 458 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 171 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 455 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 527

english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a
man on a ship: Is it permissible for him to place a mat over goods, straw, wheat, barley,
or other items and then pray on it?
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm."
references: Questions of Ali bin Jaafar, Part 1, p. 224 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 458 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 183

Chapter Title: PRAYER ON A SHIP
arabic_text:

وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ ق َّان ِم .
english_text:
Imam Ali {a.s} said:
"When you are on a ship and it is moving, then pray while seated. If it is stationary, then
pray standing."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 459 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 505

english_text:
Abu Ja'far {a.s} said to some of his companions:
"When Allah {SWT} grants you the opportunity to embark on the sea, recite what Allah
{SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, said:
'In the Name of Allah {SWT} shall be its sailing and its anchoring; indeed, my Lord {AZJ} is
All-Forgiving, Most Merciful' (Qur'an 11:41).
If the sea becomes turbulent for you, lean on your right side and say:
'In the Name of Allah {SWT}, be calm with the tranquility of Allah {SWT}, be settled with the
settling of Allah {SWT}, and be at peace by the permission of Allah {SWT}, and there is no
power nor strength except by Allah {SWT}.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 459 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 17, p. 416 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 11, p. 455

Muhammad ibn Muslim reported from one of the Imams {a.s} who said:
"My father {a.s} disliked traveling by sea for trade."

Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
traveling by sea when it is turbulent.
He {a.s} replied: "Why would a person endanger his life and his religion?".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Imam {a.s} said:
"How commendable is the effort of the one who travels by sea to seek [livelihood or

english_text:
Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah reported from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He
said:
"The Prophet {saws} prayed with his companions during the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa'. He
divided his companions into two groups: one group faced the enemy, while the other
stood behind him (for prayer). He commenced the prayer with them by saying the
takbir, and they all said the takbir. He recited, and they listened silently. He bowed,
and they bowed. He prostrated, and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah {saws} remained standing while they prayed an additional
rak'ah for themselves and then exchanged positions. The first group took their place
facing the enemy, and the other group came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah
{saws}. He then repeated the takbir, and they followed. He recited, and they listened
silently. He bowed, and they bowed. He prostrated, and they prostrated.
Then the Messenger of Allah {saws} sat for the tashahhud and offered the salutation
(ending the prayer). Afterward, this group completed another rak'ah for themselves,
and then they exchanged greetings with one another."
commentary:
Allah {SWT} Almighty revealed to His Prophet {saws} :
"When you ˹O’ Prophet˺ are ˹campaigning˺ with them and you lead them in prayer, let
one group of them pray with you - while armed. When they prostrate themselves, let
the other group stand guard behind them. Then the group that has not yet prayed will
then join you in prayer - and let them be vigilant and armed. The disbelievers would
wish to see you neglect your weapons and belongings, so they could launch a
sweeping assault on you. But there is no blame if you lay aside your weapons when
overcome by heavy rain or illness - but take precaution. Indeed, Allah {SWT} has prepared
a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers. When the prayers are over, remember
Allah {SWT} - whether you are standing, sitting, or lying down. But when you are secure,
establish regular prayers. Indeed, performing prayers is a duty on the believers at the
appointed times." (Surah An-Nisa 4:102-103).
This is the prayer of fear that Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, commanded His Prophet {saws} to
perform.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 460 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol. 2, p. 164

ذإر ولي صل ن الأي ماء.
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said :
"Whoever prays the Maghrib prayer during a situation of fear with a group, he prays one
rak'ah with the first group and two rak'ahs with the second group."
commentary:
And if someone encounters a wild animal and fears missing the prayer, he should face
the Qiblah and perform his prayer using gestures. If the wild animal approaches and
poses a threat, he should move with it as it moves and continue his prayer using
gestures.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 463 • Al-Wafi, V. 8, p. 1065 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, V. 2, p. 165

english_text:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a
man who encounters a wild beast, and the time for prayer has arrived, but he is unable
to walk due to fear of the beast.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should face the lion, perform the prayer, and gesture with his head
while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the Qibla."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 463 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 119

Sama'a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man who encounters a wild beast, and the time for prayer has arrived, but he cannot
walk due to fear of the lion.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should face the lion and perform the prayer, gesturing with his head
while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the Qibla."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Sama'a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man who is captured by polytheists, and the time for prayer arrives, but he fears that
they will prevent him from praying.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray by gesturing."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text:

Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}:
I asked him about the prayer of fear and the prayer of travel - are both to be shortened?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, and the prayer of fear is more deserving of being shortened than
the prayer of travel because it involves fear”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 464 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 433

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION

english_text:
I heard our teacher, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, say: It was narrated that Imam
Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about the words of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic:
"And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening
the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you" (Surah An-Nisa 4:101).
Imam {a.s} said: "This refers to a second form of shortening, where a man reduces two
rak'ahs to one."
commentary: This was narrated by Hariz from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 464 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1066

» ًإَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ: «ق َّا ِن ْ ج ِ ق ْي ُّمْ ق َّزِج ٰ الأً إ َّوْ رُّكْن ٰان ا .
english_text:
Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad
Al-Sadiq {a.s} regarding the prayer during advancing troops (battle or combat).
Imam {a.s} said: "You say the takbir (proclaiming 'Allahu Akbar') and tahleel (proclaiming
'La ilaha illallah).
Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'But if you fear [an enemy], then [pray] on foot
or while riding' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:239)”.
references: Tafsir al-Ayashi, vol. 1, p. 129 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 465 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1069 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 443 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 447 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol. 1, p. 499 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 117 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 239 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 2, p. 370

english_text:
It was narrated from Abu Basir that He said: I heard Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} say,
"If you are in a place of danger and fear a thief or a wild beast, then perform the
obligatory prayer while riding your mount."
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 456 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 465 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 172 • Tafsir al-Safi, Part 1, p. 269 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 442 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 239 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 2, p. 370

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION
arabic_text: َّوَّ ق ِى رِوَّ إي َّه ِ ر ُّرَّإرَّة َّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّح َّ اف ُّ إَّلل ُّصُّ وضَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى إ ِي مَّاءً ع ِلَّى ذَّإن َّي ِه.
english_text:
In the narration from Zurarah from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} who said: "One who
fears robbers should perform their prayer by gesturing while on their mount”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 466 • Al-Wafi, V. 8, p. 1074 • Tafsir al-Safi, Part 1, p. 270 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 8, p. 441 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Pt 1, p. 240 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 2, p. 370

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION

english_text:
t has been permitted, in the case of the prayer of fear from a wild beast when
a person fears for their life, to simply say the takbir (proclaiming "Allahu Akbar")
without making gestures.
This was narrated by Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams {a.s}.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 466 • Al-Wafi, V8, p. 1075 • Wasail Al-Shia, V8, p. 441

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION

ِّوَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إَّل َّذ ِى ي َّح َّ اف ُّ إَّلل ُّصُّ وضَّ وَّ إَّلس َّ ن ُّغَّ ي ُّصَّ ل ِ ى صَّ لاَّة َّ إَّلْمُّوَّ إق َّق َّه
َّ إ ِي مَّاءً عَّلَّى ذَّإن َّي ِهِ » ق َّالَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ إ َّ رَّإ َّي ْث َّ إ ِن ْ لَّمْ ي َّكُّن ِ إَّلْمُّوَّ إق ِف ُّ عَّلَّى وُّص ُّ وءٍ كَّي ْ ف َّي َّصْ ن َّغُّ وَّ لأَّ ي َّق ْ ذِرُّ عَّلَّى إَّلن ُّز ُّولِ ق َّال
ُّ«ي َّي َّي َّم َّمُّ مِن ْ لِن ْذِ ذَّإن َّي ِهِ إ َّوْ سَّ زْج ِ هِ إ َّوْ مَّ عْ زَّق َّه ِ ذَّإن َّي ِهِ ق َّا ِن َّ ق ِي هَّا ع ُّن َّارإً وَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ ي َّح ْ عَّل َّإَّلس ُّ ح ُّ وذَّ إ َّج ْ ق َّض َّ مِن َّ إَّلز ُّكُّوعِ و
َّلأَّ ي َّذُّورُّ إ ِلَّى إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه ِ و ُّلَّكِن ْ إ َّي ْن َّمَّا ذَّإرَّب ْ ذَّإن َّي ُّهُّ ع َّي ْ زَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ي َّسْ ي َّق ْ ن ِلُّ إَّلْق ِن ْلَّه َّ ن ِا َّو َّ لِ ي َّكْن ِي زَّة ٍ جِ ي ن َّ ي َّي َّوَّ ج َّ ه .
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"One who fears robbers or a wild beast should perform the prayer of a stopped traveler
using gestures while on their mount."
I (Zurarah) asked: "What if the person does not have wudu (ablution) and cannot
dismount? What should they do?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They should perform tayammum (dry ablution) using the saddlecloth,
saddle, or the cover of their mount, as it contains dust, and then pray, making the
gesture for prostration lower than that of bowing. They do not need to turn to face the
Qiblah; rather, they should face the Qiblah for the initial takbir (opening declaration)
and then continue as the mount moves."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 466 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 173 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 441

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION
arabic_text:
ْوَّ رَّوَّ ى عُّن َّي ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ عَّلِى ٍّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «صَّ لاَّة ُّ إَّلز َّج ف ِ عَّلَّى إَّلط َّ هْ زِ إ ِي مَّاء
ُّ ن ِزَّإ ْسِ ك َّ وَّ ي َّكْن ِي ز وَّ إَّلْمُّسَّ اي َّق َّه ِ ي َّكْن ِي ز ن ِع َّي ْ زِ إ ِي مَّاءٍ وَّ إَّلْمُّطَّ ارَّذَّة ِ إ ِي مَّاء ي ِصَّ لِّى كُّل ُّ رَّج ُّ لٍ عَّلَّى جِ ي َّالِه .
english_text:
Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-
Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"The prayer during advancing combat (al-zahf) is performed on one's back with
gestures of the head and the takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar'). During close
fighting (al-musayafa), it involves takbir without gestures. During pursuit (al-
mutarada), it is performed with gestures, and each person prays individually as per
their situation."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 466 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 174 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1069 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 443 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 86, p. 110

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ: «ق َّاب َّ إَّلن َّاسَّ مَّ غَّ عَّلِى ٍّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّوْ مَّ صِ ق ِّي ن َّ صَّ لاَّة ُّ إَّلط ُّ هْ زِ وَّ إَّلْعَّصْ زِ و َّإَّلْمَّع ْ زِب ِ و
إَّلْعِس َّ اءِ ق َّا َّمَّ زَّهُّمْ ق َّكَّن َّزُّوإ وَّ هَّل َّلُّوإ وَّ سَّ ن َّحُّ وإ ًرِج َّ الأً وَّ رُّكْن َّان ا .
english_text:
Imam {a.s} said:
"The people missed the Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha prayers with Ali {a.s} on the day of
Siffin. He instructed them to make the takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar'), tahleel (saying 'La
ilaha illAllah {SWT}'), and tasbih (glorifying Allah {SWT}) while standing and while mounted."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 467 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1069 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 444

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION
arabic_text:
ِ وَّ ق ِى كِي َّاب ِ عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن َّ إَّلْمُّع ِي زَّة ِ إ َّن َّ إَّلص َّ اذِق َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ َّق َّل ُّ مَّ ا ي ُّح ْ ز ِى ق ِى جَّ ذِّ إَّلْمُّسَّ اي َّق َّه ِ مِن
ِإَّلي َّكْن ِي زِ ي َّكْن ِي زَّي َّان ِ لِكُّلِّ صَّ لاَّة ٍ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلْمَّع ْ زِب َّ ق َّا ِن َّ لَّهَّا ي َّلاَّي اً مِن َّ إَّلي َّكْن ِي ز .
english_text:
In the book of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, it is reported that Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The minimum that suffices for the prayer during close combat (al-musayafa) is two
takbirs (proclamations of 'Allahu Akbar') for each prayer, except for the Maghrib
prayer, for which there are three takbirs."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 467 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 174 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 444

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF FEAR, PURSUIT, ENCOUNTER, AND COMPETITION
arabic_text:
َّ وَّ سَّ ا َّلَّهُّ سَّ مَّاعَّه ُّ ن ْن ُّ مِهْ زَّإن:
عَّن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْق ِي َّالِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ إِلْي َّق َّوْ إ ق َّاق ْي َّي َّلُّوإ ق َّا ِن َّمَّا إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ جِ ي ن َّن ِذ ٍ ي َّكْن ِي ز وَّ إ ِذ َّإ
كَّان ُّوإ وُّق ُّوق اً لأَّ ي َّق ْذِرُّون َّ عَّلَّى إَّلْح َّ مَّاعَّه ِ ق َّالص َّ لاَّة ُّ إ ِي مَّاء .
وإلعزي ان ي صلى ق اعذإ وي ص غ ي ذة على عوري ه، وإ ن كان ث إمزإ ة وص عث ي ذها على ق زج ها، ي م ي و مي ان إ ي ماء وي كون سح وذهما
إ ج ق ض من ركوعهما، ولأ ي زكعان ولأ ي سح ذإن ق ي ن ذو ما ج لق هما ولكن إ ي ماء ن زو وسهما.
وإ ن كان وإ ج ماعه صلوإ وجذإن ا.
وق ى إلماء وإلطي ن ي كون إلصلاة ن الأي ماء وإلزكوع إ ج ق ض من إلسح وذ.
english_text:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked him (Abu Abdullah {a.s}) about the prayer during
battle.
Imam {a.s} said: "When they meet and engage in fighting, the prayer at that time is
performed with takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar'). If they are standing and unable
to form a congregation, then the prayer is performed with gestures."
commentary:
Regarding one who is unclothed, they should pray while seated and cover their private
parts with their hands. If it is a woman, She should cover herself in a similar manner.
They should perform gestures for the movements of the prayer, making their
prostration lower than their bowing, and they should not bow or prostrate fully to avoid
exposing themselves, instead using gestures with their heads.
If they are a group, they should pray individually. When praying in water or mud, the
prayer is performed using gestures, with the bowing made less deep than the
prostration.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 458 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 468 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1067 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 444

Chapter Title: WHAT A PERSON SHOULD SAY WHEN THEY LIE DOWN
arabic_text:

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever purifies themselves (performs wudu) and then goes to their bed, their bed
will be like their mosque (place of prayer). If they remember that they are not in a state
of wudu, they should perform tayammum (dry ablution) using the fabric of their
covering, whatever it may be, and as long as they remember Allah {SWT}, they will remain
in a state of prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 469 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 116 • Makarem al- Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 288 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1581 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 1, p. 378 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 182 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 77, p. 308 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 78, p. 157

Chapter Title: WHAT A PERSON SHOULD SAY WHEN THEY LIE DOWN
arabic_text:

ُّ ن ِسْ مِ إَّلل َّهِ إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ ِن ِّى إ َّسْ لَّمْ ث ُّ ن َّق ْسِ ى إ ِلَّي ْك َّ وَّ وَّ ج َّ هْ ث ُّ وَّ ج ْ هِى إ ِلَّي ْك َّ وَّ ق َّو َّ ص ْ ث َّ إ َّمْ زِى إ ِلَّي ْك َّ وَّ إ َّلْح َّ ا ْب ُّ ط َّ هْ زِى إ ِلَّي ْك َّ و
ِ ي َّوَّ ك َّلْث ُّ عَّلَّي ْك َّ رَّهْن َّه ً مِن ْك َّ وَّ رَّع ْ ن َّه ً إ ِلَّي ْك َّ لأَّ مَّ لْح َّ ا َّ وَّ لأَّ مَّ ن ْح َّ ى مِن ْك َّ إ ِلأ َّ إ ِلَّي ْك َّ إ مَّ ن ْث ُّ ن ِكِي َّان ك َّ إَّل َّذ ِى إ َّن ْز َّلْث َّ وَّ ن ِزَّسُّ ولِك َّ إَّل َّذ ِى

ِّ إَّلْمُّعَّوِّ ذ َّي َّي ْن ِ وَّ إ ي َّه َّ إَّلْكُّزْسِ ى.
english_text:
Al-'Ala reports from Muhammad ibn Muslim that Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} said to
me: "When a man places his right side (for sleep), he should say:
'In the Name of Allah {SWT}. O’ Allah {SWT}, I have submitted my soul to You, turned my
face towards You, entrusted my affairs to You, and placed my reliance upon You, in
fear of You and in hope of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to
You. I believe in Your Book, which You have revealed, and in Your Messenger, whom
You have sent.'
Then he should recite the Tasbih of Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}.
If someone experiences fear at bedtime, they should recite the two protective
chapters (al-Mu'awwidhatayn) and Ayat al-Kursi (The Verse of the Throne)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 469 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 116 • Makarem al- Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 288

english_text:
Al-'Ala' reported from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams {a.s},
who said: "A man should not neglect to say at bedtime:
'I seek protection for myself, my descendants, my family, and my wealth with the
complete words of Allah {SWT} from every devil, harmful creature, and every envious
eye.' This is what Archangel Jibril {a.s} used to protect Hasan and Hussain {a.s}."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 470 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 116 • Makarem al- Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 288 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1583 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 447 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 196 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 84, p. 174

Abdullah ibn Sinan reports from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"Recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya-ayyuhal kaafirun’ (Surah
al-Kafirun) before you sleep, for they are a declaration of freedom from shirk
(associating partners with Allah {SWT}), and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
affirms the nature of the Lord {AZJ}, Mighty and Majestic."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 470 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 116 • Makarem al- Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 288 • Al-Wafi, V. 9, p. 1585 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 6, p. 450 • Bihar Al-Anwar, V. 73, p. 195 • Bihar Al Anwar, V. 84, p. 174 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Pt 5, p. 688 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 14, p. 472

Chapter Title: WHAT A PERSON SHOULD SAY WHEN THEY LIE DOWN TO SLEEP
english_text:
Bakr ibn Muhammad reported that Imam {a.s} said:
"Whoever says the following three times when taking their place to sleep:
'All praise is due to Allah {SWT}, Who is exalted and dominates. All praise is due to Allah
{SWT}, Who is hidden yet knows. All praise is due to Allah {SWT}, Who rules and controls
with power. All praise is due to Allah {SWT}, Who gives life to dead and causes living to
die, and is over all things capable,' will be free of sins as on the day their mother gave
birth to them."
references: Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 35 • Al-Kafi, Volume 2, p. 535 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 470 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 153 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 117 • Makarem al- Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 289 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 282 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1577 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 448 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 196

english_text:
The Prophet {saws} said: "Whoever recites this verse before sleeping:
'Say, I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is One God'
(Surah al-Kahf 18:110) until the end of the verse, a light will shine for him to the Sacred
Mosque (Masjid al-Haram), filled with angels who seek forgiveness for him until he
awakens”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 470 • Uddat al-Da’i, Part 1, p. 301 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1585 • Tafsir al-Safi, Part 3, p. 270 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, vol. 3, p. 609 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 3, p. 316 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 8, p. 183

Amir ibn Abdullah ibn Juza'ah narrated from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"There is no servant who recites the end of Surah al-Kahf before sleeping except that
they will wake up at the hour they desire."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 471 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 175 • Meftah al- Falah, Part 1, p. 283 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 229 • Tafsir Al-Burhan, Vol. 3, p. 610

Sa'd al-Iskaf reported from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"Whoever recites these words, I guarantee that no scorpion or harmful creature will
harm them until morning: 'I seek refuge with the complete words of Allah {SWT}, which
neither the righteous nor the wicked can surpass, from the evil of what He created,
from the evil of what He brought forth, and from the evil of every creature over which
He holds control. Truly, my Lord {AZJ} is on a straight path.'"

Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
who said:
"If you fear experiencing a state of janabah (ritual impurity) during sleep, say in your
bed:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, I seek refuge with You from experiencing a wet dream, from evil dreams,
and from being manipulated by Shaytan (the devil) in wakefulness and in sleep.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 471 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 290 • Meftah al- Falah, Part 1, p. 284 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1578 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 448

»ًع َّق ُّورإ
ُّ ق َّسَّ ق َّظَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلْن َّي ْث .
english_text:
Al-‘Abbas ibn Hilal reported from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha {a.s}, from his father
{a.s} who said:
"No one has ever recited, when intending to sleep :
'Indeed, Allah {SWT} holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and if they should
cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and
Forgiving' (Qur'an 35:41) without being protected, such that even if a house were to
collapse upon him, he would be safe."

english_text:
Archangel Jibril {a.s} descended upon the Prophet {saws} and said to Him {saws}:
"O’ Muhammad {saws+, live as long as you wish, for you will surely die; love whomever
you wish, for you will be separated from them; and do whatever you wish, for you will
be recompensed for it. The honor of a believer lies in their night prayer, and their dignity
is in refraining from harming people”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 471 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 4, p. 399 • Al- Waezin, Vol. 2, p. 321 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 101

english_text:
Bahr al-Saqqa' reported from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} Ali who said:
"Indeed, among the blessings and comfort from Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic,
are three things: praying in the late hours of the night (Tahajjud), breaking the fast (iftar)
of a fasting person, and meeting with one's brothers (fellow believers)."
references: Da‘ā’im al-Islām, Part 1, p. 271 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 472 • Amali (by Al- Tusi) Vol. 1, p. 172 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 102 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 153 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 14, p. 587 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 71, p. 353 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 84, p. 143 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 93, p. 258 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 6, p. 327
