english_text:
When a yellow, red, or black wind would blow, the Prophet {saws} would
become visibly changed - his face would turn pale, and his color would change as if he
were fearful and anxious.
He would remain in this state until a drop of rain fell from the sky, at which point his
color would return, and he would say,
'It has come to you with mercy.'

Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim reported from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali
Al-Baqir {a.s} that they asked him, "What do you say about these winds and darkness
that occur? Should one pray because of them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "For every fear-inducing phenomenon from the sky, be it darkness,
wind, or dread, pray the prayer of the eclipse (Salat al-Kusuf) until it subsides."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Muawiya narrated from Imam
Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} and Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"When an eclipse or any of these celestial signs occurs, perform the prayer (Salat al-
Kusuf) as long as you do not fear missing the time of an obligatory prayer. If you fear
that the time of the obligatory prayer will pass, then begin with the obligatory prayer
and interrupt your Salat al-Kusuf. Once you have completed the obligatory prayer,
return to where you left off in the Salat al-Kusuf and continue from there, counting
what you have already performed."

It is reported from Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti that He said:
"I wrote to Imam al-Ridha {a.s} asking about what to do if the sun or moon eclipses while
I am riding and unable to dismount.
He {a.s} wrote back to me saying, 'Pray on your mount, whatever you are on.'".

english_text:
It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim and al-Fudhayl ibn Yasar that they
said:
"We asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s}: Should one make up the prayer for
an eclipse if he becomes aware of it in the morning or evening after it has occurred?
He {a.s} replied: 'If both discs (the sun and the moon) were completely eclipsed, you
must make it up. However, if only a part of either of them was eclipsed, then you are
not required to make it up.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 549 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1379 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 499

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER FOR ECLIPSES, EARTHQUAKES, WINDS, AND OPPRESSION AND THEIR CAUSES

ي هَّا .
english_text:
Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the prayer for
the eclipse (Salat al-Kusuf) of the sun and moon.
Imam {a.s} said: "It consists of ten rak'ahs (units of prayer) and four prostrations
(Sujood). You perform five bowings (ruku) and then prostrate (Sujood) in the fifth. Then
you perform another five bowings and prostrate in the tenth.
If you wish, you can recite a chapter (Surah) in each rak'ah, or if you prefer, you may
recite half of a chapter in each rak'ah. If you recite a chapter in each rak'ah, then recite
the opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha). If you choose to recite half a chapter, it suffices to
recite Al-Fatiha only in the first rak'ah until you start another chapter. And you should
not say 'Sami' Allahu liman hamidah' (Allah {SWT} hears the one who praises Him) when
rising from ruku except in the rak'ah where you intend to prostrate."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 549 • Al-Wafi, V. 9, p. 1374 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 7, p. 495

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER FOR ECLIPSES, EARTHQUAKES, WINDS, AND OPPRESSION AND THEIR CAUSES

َّ وَّ رَّوَّ ى عُّمَّزُّ ن ْن ُّ إ ُّذ َّي ْن َّه:
ِ «إ َّن َّ إَّلْق ُّن ُّوب َّ ق ِى إَّلز َّكْعَّه ِ إَّلي َّان ِي َّه ِ ق َّن ْلَّ إَّلز ُّكُّوعِ ي ُّم َّ ق ِى إَّلز َّإن ِعَّه ِ ي ُّم َّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ اذِسَّ ه ِ ي ُّم َّ ق ى
ِ إَّلي َّامِن َّه ِ ي ُّم َّ ق ِى إَّلْعَّاس ِ زَّة.
وإ ن لم ي ق ن ث إ لأ ق ى إلح امسه وإلعاس زة ق هو ج ان ز لوروذ إلح ن ز ن ه. وإ ذ إ ق زع إلزج ل من صلاة إلكسوف ولم ي كن إن ح لث ق لي عذ
إلصلاة وإ ن س اء ق عذ ومح ذ إلله عز وج ل جي ى ي ن ح لى . ولأ ي ح ور إ ن ي صلي هما ق ى وق ث ق زي ص ه جي ى ي صلى إلق زي ص ه . وإ ذ إ
كان ق ى صلاة إلكسوف وذج ل علي ه وق ث إلق زي ص ه ق. لي ق طعها ولي صل إلق زي ص ه ي م ي ن ن ى على ما صلى من صلاة إلكسوف
english_text:
Umar ibn Udhaynah narrates: "The Qunoot (supplication) is to be recited in
the second rak'ah before bowing (ruku), then in the fourth, sixth, eighth, and tenth
rak'ahs."
commentary:
However, if one only performs Qunoot in the fifth and tenth rak'ahs, it is still
permissible as there is a narration supporting this practice. If a person finishes the
Salat al-Kusuf (prayer during an eclipse) and the eclipse has not yet ended, they
should repeat the prayer. Alternatively, if they wish, they may sit and glorify Allah {SWT}
the Almighty until the eclipse clears.
It is not permissible to perform Salat al-Kusuf during the time of a prescribed
(obligatory) prayer until the obligatory prayer is completed. If one is engaged in Salat
al-Kusuf and the time for an obligatory prayer begins, they should interrupt the eclipse
prayer, perform the obligatory prayer, and then continue from where they left off in
Salat al-Kusuf.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 549 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1374 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 495

english_text:
Hammad ibn Uthman narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
that during a discussion about the eclipse of the moon and the hardship that people
endure because of it,
He (Imam Al-Sadiq) said: "If a part of it (the moon) has cleared, then it has cleared”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

َّ سَّ ن ْعُّون َّ مَّ ز َّة ً ق ِى كُّلِّ رَّكْعَّه ٍ ي َّلاَّي ُّمِان َّه ِ ي َّسْ ن ِي حَّ ه ٍ ي َّكُّون ُّ ي َّلاَّي ُّمِان َّه ِ مَّ ز َّة ٍ ق ِى إَّلْأ َّرْن َّغِ رَّكَّعَّاب ٍ إ لْف وَّ مِان َّي َّا ي َّسْ ن ِي حَّ ه ٍ ي ُّص َّ اعِ ق ُّهَّا
ٍإَّلل َّهُّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ وَّ ي َّكْي ُّث ُّ لَّك َّ ن ِهَّا إِي ْن َّي َّى ْ عَّس ْ زَّة َّ إ َّلْف َّ جَّ سَّ ن َّه ٍ إَّلْحَّ سَّ ن َّه ُّ مِن ْهَّا مِي ْ لُّ ج َّ ن َّلِ إ ُّجُّ ذ ُّوَّ إ َّعْ ط َّ م .
english_text:
Abu Hamza al-Thumali reported from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} said to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib; 'O’ Ja'far, shall I bestow upon
you, give you, honor you, or teach you a prayer that if you perform it, even if you were
to have fled from the battlefield and had sins equivalent to the sand of ‘Alij or the foam
of the sea, they would be forgiven for you?'
Ja'far replied: 'Yes, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}.'
He {saws} said: 'You should pray four units (rak'ahs) whenever you wish: if you wish, every
night; if you wish, every day; if you wish, from Jumu’ah to Jumu’ah; if you wish, from
month to month; or if you wish, from year to year. You begin the prayer, then say fifteen
times, "Allahu Akbar, SubhanAllah {SWT}, Alhamdulillah, and La ilaha illAllah {SWT}."
Then recite Surah al-Fatiha and a surah, and in your bowing (ruku'), you say them ten
times.
You raise your head from ruku' and say them ten times.
Then you prostrate (sujud) and say them ten times.
You raise your head from prostration and say them ten times.
Then you prostrate again and say them ten times.
You raise your head and say them ten times.
Then you stand up and say them fifteen times.
Then recite Surah al-Fatiha and a surah, then bow and say them ten times, then raise
your head from bowing and say them ten times, then prostrate and say them ten times,
then raise your head from prostration and say them ten times, then prostrate again
and say them ten times, and then raise your head and say them ten times.
Then you perform the tashahhud (testimony of faith) and Tasleem (concluding
salutations) and stand to pray two more units in the same manner and then conclude
with Tasleem.'
Abu Ja'far {a.s} said: 'That makes seventy-five (tasbihs) in each rak'ah, totaling three
hundred glorifications in four rak'ahs, which is one thousand two hundred tasbihs.
Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, multiplies it and writes for you twelve thousand
good deeds, each one like the size of Mount Uhud or even greater.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 552 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1386 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 51

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF SITTING AND GLORIFICATION, WHICH IS THE PRAYER OF JA'FAR IBN ABI TALIB
arabic_text:

َّلأَّ إ ِلَّهَّ إ ِلأ َّ إَّلل َّهُّ و ُّإَّلل َّهُّ إ َّكْن َّز .
.ق ن ا ى إلحذي ي ي ن إ ج ذ إلمصلى ق هو مصي ث وج ان ز له
وإلق ن وب ق ى كل ركعي ي ن من هما ق ن ل إلزكوع، وإلق زإءة ق ى إلزكعه إلأ ولى
إلحمذ وإ ذ إ ر لز لث ، وق ى إلي ان ي ه إلحمذ وإلعاذي اب ، وق ى إلي الي ه إلحمذ وإ ذ إ ج اء ن صز إلله، و ق ى إلزإن عه إلحمذ وق ل هو إلله
.إ جذ ، وإ ن س ن ث صلي ي ها كلها ن الحمذ وق ل هو إلله إ جذ
english_text:
It has been narrated that in the Tasbih (glorifications) of the Salat (prayer) of
Ja'far, the order of the Tasbih following the recitation (of the chapters from the Qur'an)
is "SubhanAllah {SWT} (Glory be to God), Alhamdulillah (All praise is due to God), La ilaha
illAllah {SWT} (There is no god but Allah {SWT}), and Allahu Akbar (God is the Greatest)”.
commentary:
Whichever narration the worshiper follows, he is correct and it is permissible for him.
In this prayer, Qunoot (supplication) is performed in every two units before bowing
(ruku'). The chapters to be recited in each unit are as follows: In the first unit, recite Al-
Fatiha (the Opening) and "If the Earth is Shaken" (Surat al-Zalzalah). In the second unit,
recite Al-Fatiha and "Those Who Run" (Surat al-Adiyat). In the third unit, recite Al-
Fatiha and "When the Victory of Allah {SWT} has come" (Surat al-Nasr). In the fourth unit,
recite Al-Fatiha and "Say, He is Allah {SWT}, [who is] One" (Surat al-Ikhlas).
If you wish, you may perform the entire prayer with Al-Fatiha and Surat al-Ikhlas.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 553 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 52

english_text:
In a narration from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s},
Imam {a.s} said: "Recite in the Salat of Ja'far {a.s} 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas)
and ‘Qul ya-ayyuhal kaafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun)."

» ِوَّ «إ ِذ ٰ إ ج ٰ اءَّ ن َّصْ زُّ إَّللّٰه
ِوَّ إ ِن ّٰا إ َّن ْز َّلْن ٰاةُّ ق ِى لَّي ْلَّه ِ إَّلْق َّذْ ر

english_text:
It is narrated from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan
Imam Al-Kadhim {a.s}: "What is the reward for one who prays the Salat of Ja'far?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If they have sins equal in quantity to the sand of 'Alij and the foam of
the sea, Allah {SWT} would forgive them."
I asked: "Is this exclusively for us?"
Imam {a.s} said: "For whom else would it be if not for you specifically?"
I then asked: "Which chapters (of the Qur'an) should be recited in it?"
Imam {a.s} answered: "Recite 'When the Earth is Shaken' (Surat al-Zalzalah), 'When the
Victory of Allah {SWT} has Come' (Surat al-Nasr), 'Indeed, We sent it down during the
Night of Decree' (Surat al-Qadr), and 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas)."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 553 • Thawab al-A’mal wa Iqab al-A’mal, Part 1, p. 40 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 186 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1388 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 54 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 88, p. 204

english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about someone who
performs the Salat of Ja'far. Would they receive the same reward as that which the
Messenger of Allah {saws} mentioned to Ja'far?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, by Allah {SWT}."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 554 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1389

ْوَّ إجِ ذٍ ق َّكَّي َّث َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «ن َّلَّى إ ِن ْ ق َّطَّ عَّهُّ عَّن ْ ذ َّلِك َّ إ َّمْ ز لأَّ ن ُّذ َّ لَّهُّ مِن ْهُّ ق َّلْي َّق ْطَّ غْ ي ُّم َّ لْي َّز ْ ج ِ غْ ق َّلْي َّن ْن ِ عَّلَّى مَّ ا ن َّق ِى َّ مِن ْهَّا إ ِن
س َّ اءَّ إَّل ُّل َّه .
english_text:
It is narrated from Ali ibn al-Rayan that He said:
I wrote to the Last Imam {a.s} asking about a man who prayed two rak'ahs of the Salat of
Ja'far but was forced to interrupt before completing the final two rak'ahs due to a need
or an event that occurred. Would it be permissible for him to complete the remaining
rak'ahs once his need was met, even if he had left his original place of prayer, or must
he start the prayer again and pray all four rak'ahs together without interruption?
He {a.s} replied: "Yes, if he was interrupted by a matter of necessity, then let him stop
and afterward return to complete what remains, if Allah {SWT} wills."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 554 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 309 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1391 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 59 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 88, p. 213

english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"Pray the Salat of Ja'far whenever you wish, be it during the day or night. If you wish,
you may count it as part of the supererogatory prayers of the night, and if you wish, you
may count it as part of the supererogatory prayers of the day. It will be counted as part
of your supererogatory prayers and as the Salat of Ja'far {a.s}."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 554 • Al-Wafi, V. 9, p. 1388 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 8, p. 58

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF SITTING AND GLORIFICATION, WHICH IS THE PRAYER OF JA'FAR IBN ABI TALIB
arabic_text: ِوَّ رَّوَّ ى إ َّن ُّو ن َّصِ ي زٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذ َّإَّلل َّهِ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ كُّن ْث َّ مُّ سْ ي َّعْ ح ِ لاً ق َّصَّ لِّ صَّ لاَّة َّ ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ مُّ ح َّ ز َّذَّة ً ي ُّم َّ إِق ْض ِ إَّلي َّسْ ن ِي ح .
english_text:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If you are in a hurry, pray the Salat of Ja'far in a simplified form, and then complete the
Tasbih (glorification) afterwards."

english_text:
In a narration from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, it is reported that one should say in
the final prostration of the Salat of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib {a.s}:
"O’ One who is clothed in might and dignity, O’ One who adorns Himself with majesty
and nobility, O’ One for whom glorification is befitting and belongs to none but Him, O’
One whose knowledge encompasses all things, O’ Possessor of bounty and grace, O’
Bestower of favors and blessings, O’ One with power and generosity, I ask You by the
pillars of might from Your Throne and by the ultimate mercy from Your Book and by
Your greatest and highest Name and by Your perfect words to send blessings upon
Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and to fulfil for me such and such
(mentioning one’s needs)."

english_text:
Murazim narrated from the pious servant Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s},
who said:
"If you are afflicted with a grave matter, give charity during the day to sixty needy
people, with each receiving half a sa' of the Prophet’s {saws} measure from dates, wheat,
or barley. At night, during the last third of the night, perform a ritual bath (ghusl), then
wear the simplest clothing that one in your care wears, but ensure you have a waist
wrapper on.
Pray two units of prayer (rak'ahs) in which you recite Surah Al-Ikhlas (the Unity) and
‘Qul ya-ayyuhal kaafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun).
When you place your forehead on the ground in the last rak’as prostration, glorify,
sanctify, and praise Allah {SWT}, then remember your sins, confessing by name what you
know and generally admitting what you do not know. Raise your head, and when you
place your forehead on the second prostration, seek Allah’s {SWT} guidance 100 times,
saying, 'O’ Allah {SWT}, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge.' Then invoke Allah {SWT}
with whatever of His names you wish, saying, 'O’ One who existed before all things, O’
Creator of all things, O’ One who remains after all things, do for me such-and-such.'
In every prostration, lower your knees to the ground and lift your waist wrapper,
exposing them. Place the wrapper behind you between your buttocks and thighs. I
hope that your need will be fulfilled, Allah {SWT} willing. Begin with prayers upon the
Prophet and his household, may Allah’s {SWT} blessings be upon them all."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 555 • The Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 326 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1424 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 88, p. 352

Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad
ibn Sahl, from their elders, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If you have an important need from Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, then fast for
three consecutive days - Wednesday, Thursday, and Jumu’ah. On Jumu’ah, if Allah {SWT}
wills, perform a ritual bath (ghusl), wear a new garment, and go to the highest part of
your house. Pray two units (rak'ahs) there, and then raise your hands toward the sky
and say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, I have come to Your court because of my recognition of Your Oneness
and Your Self-Sufficiency, and I know that no one can fulfil my need except You. O’ my
Lord {AZJ}, I have also realized that whenever Your bounty upon me increases, my
neediness towards You becomes more severe. A particular concern has befallen me
(mention your specific need here), and You, in Your knowledge, are fully aware of it
without being taught, capable of removing it without effort. I ask You by the Name that
You placed upon the mountains so that they crumbled, upon the heavens so that they
split, upon the stars so that they scattered, and upon the earth so that it spread forth.
I ask You by the truth that You have placed with Muhammad and the Imams {a.s}, and
by naming them up to the last one, to bless Muhammad and his family, and to fulfil my
need, make what is difficult for me easy, and relieve me of its burden. If You fulfil it,
then all praise is due to You. If You do not fulfil it, then all praise is due to You without
injustice in Your decree, without accusation in Your judgment, and without departure
from Your justice.'
Then, place your cheek upon the ground and say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, Yunus ibn Matta (Prophet Jonah), Your servant, called upon You from
within the belly of the whale, and You answered him. I am also Your servant, calling
upon You, so answer me.'
Abu Abdullah {a.s} then said: 'Whenever I had a need, I would recite this supplication,
and I would return with my need fulfilled.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 556 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 183 • Misbah al- Mutahjad, vol. 2, p. 530 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 325 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1426 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 132

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF NEED
arabic_text:
رَّوَّ ى سَّ مَّاعَّه ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِن َّ إ َّجَّ ذَّكُّمْ إ ِذ َّإ مَّ زِض َّ ذَّعَّا إَّلط َّ ن ِي ث َّ وَّ إ َّعْ طَّ اةُّ وَّ إ ِذ َّإ
َّكَّان َّث ْ لَّهُّ جَّ اج َّ ه إ ِلَّى سُّ لْطَّ ان ٍ رَّس َّ ا إَّلْن َّو َّإب َّ وَّ إ َّعْ طَّ اةُّ وَّ لَّوْ إ َّن َّ إ َّجَّ ذَّكُّمْ إ ِذ َّإ ق َّذَّج َّهُّ إ َّمْ ز ق َّز ِعَّ إ ِلَّى إَّلل َّهِ ي َّعَّالَّى ق َّي َّطَّ ه َّزَّ و
ْ ي َّصَّ ذ َّق َّ ن ِصَّ ذَّق َّه ٍ ق َّل َّث ْ إ َّوْ كَّي ُّزَّب ْ ي ُّم َّ ذَّج َّ لَّ إَّلْمَّسْ ح ِ ذَّ ق َّصَّ ل َّى رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ق َّحَّ مِذَّ إَّلل َّهَّ وَّ إ َّي ْن َّى عَّلَّي ِهِ وَّ صَّ ل َّى عَّلَّى إَّلن َّن ِى ِّ وَّ إ َّهْل
ُّ ن َّي ْي ِهِ عَّلَّي ْهِمُّ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي َّ م َّ ق َّالَّ إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ ِن ْ عَّاق َّي ْي َّن ِى مِن ْ مَّ زَّص ِ ى إ َّوْ رَّذَّذْ ي َّن ِى مِن ْ سَّ ق َّزِى إ َّوْ عَّاق َّي ْي َّن ِى مِم َّا إ َّج َّ اف ُّ مِن ْ كَّذ َّإ و
َّ كَّذ َّإ إ ِلأ َّ إ ي َّاةُّ إَّلل َّهُّ ذ َّلِك َّ وَّ هِى َّ إَّلْي َّمِي ن ُّ إَّلْوَّ إج ِ ن َّه ُّ وَّ مَّ ا ج َّ عَّلَّ إَّلل َّهُّ ي َّن َّارَّك وي َّعَّالَّى .»ِعَّلَّي ْ هِ ق ِى إَّلس ُّ كْز
english_text:
Sama’a narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"When one of you falls ill, he calls for the physician and pays him. When someone has
a need from a ruler, he bribes the gatekeeper and gives him.
However, if one of you is struck by an overwhelming concern and turns to Allah {SWT},
the Exalted, purifies himself (performs ablution), gives charity (whether small or large),
then enters the mosque, prays two units (rak'ahs) of prayer, praises and glorifies Allah
{SWT}, and invokes blessings upon the Prophet and his family {a.s}, then says: 'O’ Allah
{SWT}, if You cure me of my illness, or return me safely from my journey, or protect me
from what I fear of such and such (mentioning the specific concern),'
Allah {SWT} would grant him that.
This is the binding oath, and it is what Allah {SWT}, the Blessed and Exalted, has made
incumbent upon one as an expression of gratitude."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 557 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 182 • Misbah al- Mutahjad, vol. 2, p. 530 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 325 • The Safe Country, Part 1, p. 155 • Al-Masbah (Lalkafami) Vol. 1, p. 398 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1427 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 136 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 88, p. 351

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF NEED
arabic_text:
َّ كَّان َّ عَّلِى ُّ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْحُّ سَّ ي ْن ِ عَّلَّي ْهِمَّا إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ ِذ َّإ جَّ ز َّن َّهُّ إ َّمْ ز لَّن ِسَّ ي َّوْ ن َّي ْن ِ مِن ْ إ َّع ْ لَّظ ِ ي ِي َّان ِهِ وَّ إ ِج ْ س َّ ن ِهَّا ي ُّم َّ رَّكَّغَّ ق ِى إ ج ِ ز
إَّلل َّي ْلِ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ جَّ ي َّى إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ ق ِى إ ج ِ زِ سَّ ح ْ ذَّة ٍ مِن ْ سُّ ح ُّ وذِةِ سَّ ن َّحَّ إَّلل َّهَّ مِا َّن َّه َّ ي َّسْ ن ِي حَّ ه ٍ وَّ جَّ مِذَّ إَّلل َّهَّ مِان َّه َّ مَّ ز َّة ٍ وَّ هَّل َّلَّ إَّلل َّه
َّ مِان َّه َّ مَّ ز َّة ٍ وَّ كَّن َّزَّ إَّلل َّهَّ مِان َّه َّ مَّ ز َّة ٍ ي ُّم َّ ي َّعْ ي َّزِف ُّ ن ِذ ُّن ُّون ِهِ كُّلِّهَّا مَّ ا عَّزَّف َّ مِن ْهَّا إ َّق َّز َّ لَّهُّ ي َّن َّ ارَّك وي َّعَّالَّى ْن ِهِ ق ِى سُّ ح ُّ وذِةِ وَّ مَّ ا لَّم
ِي َّذ ْ كُّزْ م ِ ن ْهَّا إِعْ ي َّزَّف َّ ن ِهِ ج ُّ مْ لَّه ً ي ُّم َّ ي َّذْ عُّو إَّلل َّهَّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ وَّ ي ُّق ْص ِ ى ن ِزُّكْن َّي َّي ْ هِ إ ِلَّى إَّلْأ َّرْض .
english_text:
When Ali ibn al-Hussain {a.s} was troubled by a matter, he would wear two of
his roughest and coarsest garments, then stand for two units of prayer in the last part
of the night.
When he reached the last prostration (Sujood), he would glorify Allah {SWT} one hundred
times, praise Allah {SWT} one hundred times, declare the oneness of Allah {SWT} (La ilaha
illAllah {SWT}) one hundred times, and magnify Allah {SWT} (Allahu Akbar) one hundred
times.
Then, he would acknowledge all of his sins - everything he remembered, he would
confess before Allah {SWT}, the Blessed and Exalted, during his prostration; what he
could not recall, he would acknowledge in general. Thereafter, he would supplicate to
Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, while placing his knees on the ground.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 558 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1428 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 136

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF NEED
arabic_text:
َّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ ي ُّون ُّسَّ ن ْن ِ عَّم َّارٍ ق َّالَّ: س َّ كَّوْ ب ُّ إ ِلَّى إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ رَّج ُّ لاً كَّان َّ ي ُّو ْ ذ ِي ن ِى ق » ِق َّالَّ «إ ُّذْ عُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
ِّق َّق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّذْ ذَّعَّوْ ب ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ ق َّق َّالَّ «لَّي ْ سَّ هَّكَّذ َّإ وَّ لَّكِن ْ إ َّق ْلِغْ عَّن ِ إَّلذ ُّن ُّوب ِ وَّ صُّ مْ وَّ صَّ ل ِ وَّ ي َّصَّ ذ َّق ْ ق َّا ِذ َّإ كَّان َّ إ ج ِ زُّ إَّلل َّي ْ لِ ق َّا َّسْ ن ِغ
إَّلْوُّص ُّ وءَّ ي ُّم َّ ق ُّمْ ق َّصَّ لِّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ي ُّم َّ ق ُّلْ وَّ إ َّن ْث َّ سَّ اج ِ ذ : إَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ ِن َّ ق ُّلاَّن َّ ن ْن َّ ق ُّلاَّن ٍ ق َّذْ إ ذ َّإن ِى
ْإَّلل َّهُّم َّ إ َّسْ ق ِمْ ن َّذَّن َّهُّ وَّ إِق ْطَّ غ
َّ إ َّي َّزَّةُّ وَّ إُّن ْق ُّضْ إ َّ ج َّ لَّهُّ وَّ عَّح ِّ لْ لَّهُّ ذ َّلِك َّ ق ِى عَّامِهِ هَّذ َّإ » ق َّالَّ ق َّق َّعَّلْث ُّ ق َّمَّا لَّن ِث َّ إ َّن ْ هَّلَّك .
english_text:
Yunus ibn Ammar reported:
I complained to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man who was harming
me.
Imam {a.s} said: "Pray against him."
I replied: "I have already prayed against him."
Imam {a.s} said: "Not like that. Instead, refrain from sins, fast, pray, and give charity.
Then, in the last part of the night, perform ablution thoroughly, stand up and pray two
units (rak'ahs). While in prostration, say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, so-and-so (mention his name) has harmed me. O’ Allah {SWT}, weaken his
body, cut off his influence, shorten his lifespan, and hasten this upon him this year.'"
He said: I did so, and it wasn't long before he perished.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 559 • Al-Muqni’ah, Part 1, p. 223 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 332 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1428 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 141 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 88, p. 358

ًج َّ طَّ زٍ عَّط ِ ي مٍ ق َّذَّج َّ لْث ُّ عَّلَّى إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّذ َّكَّزْب ُّ لَّهُّ ذ َّلِك َّ وَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ عَّلِّمْ ن ِى س َّ ي ْن ا لَّعَّل َّ إَّلل َّهَّ ي َّزُّذ ُّ عَّلَّى َّ مَّ ط ْ لِمَّي ِى
ْق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ إ َّرَّذْ ب َّ إَّلْعَّذُّو َّ ق َّصَّ لِّ ن َّي ْن َّ إَّل ْ ق َّن ْزِ وَّ إَّلْمِن ْن َّزِ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ إ َّوْ إ َّرْن َّغَّ رَّكَّعَّاب ٍ وَّ إ ِن ْ س ِ ن ْث َّ ق َّق ِى ن َّي ْي ِك َّ وَّ إِسْ ا َّلِ إَّلل َّهَّ إ َّن
ي ُّعِي ن َّك َّ وَّ ج ُّ ذ ْ س َّ ي ْن اً مِم َّا ي َّي َّس َّ زَّ ق َّي َّصَّ ذ َّق ْ ن ِهِ عَّلَّى إ َّو َّلِ مِسْ كِي ن ٍ ي َّلْق َّاةُّ» ق َّالَّ ق َّق َّعَّلْث ُّ مَّ ا إ َّمَّ زَّن ِى
َّق َّق َّص َّ ى لِى و َّ رَّذ َّ إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّى
إ َّرْص ِ ى .
english_text:
Umar ibn Udhaynah narrated from a man from the family of Sa'd who said:
I had a significant dispute with a man from Medina. I went to Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} and mentioned the matter to him and asked: "Teach me
something that might make Allah {SWT} return my right to me."
Imam {a.s} said: "If you want to deal with your enemy, then pray two or four rak'ahs
between the grave and the pulpit (of the Prophet {saws} in Medina), or if you wish, pray in
your house. Ask Allah {SWT} for assistance, and take whatever you can afford and give it
as charity to the first needy person you encounter."
He said: I did what he commanded, and Allah {SWT} resolved the matter in my favour and
returned my land to me.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 559 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1429

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF NEED
arabic_text:

english_text:
Ziyad al-Qandi narrated from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir who said: "I entered
Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} and said: 'May I be your ransom, I have composed a supplication.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Leave aside your composition; if a matter befalls you, then seek help
from the Messenger of Allah {saws} by praying two rak'ahs, dedicating them to the
Messenger of Allah {saws}.'
I asked: 'How should I do this?'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Perform ghusl (ritual purification), pray two rak'ahs, beginning them as
you would begin a prescribed prayer (with the opening takbir and intention), and recite
the tashahhud as you would in the obligatory prayer. When you finish the tashahhud
and say the salutation (Tasleem), say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, You are Peace, and from You comes peace, and to You returns peace.
O’ Allah {SWT}, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and
convey my greetings of peace to the soul of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
Peace be upon them, and the mercy and blessings of Allah {SWT}. O’ Allah {SWT}, these two
rak'ahs are a gift from me to Your Messenger {saws}. So reward me for them with what I
hope and expect from You through Your Messenger, O’ Guardian of the believers."
Then prostrate (sujud) and say:
"O’ Ever-Living, O’ Self-Sustaining, O’ Living One who does not die, O’ Living One, there
is no god but You, O’ Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O’ Most Merciful of the
merciful," forty times.
Then place your right cheek on the ground and say it forty times. Then place your left
cheek and say it forty times. Then raise your head, stretch out your hands, and say it
forty times. Then bring your hands to your neck and hold your index finger while saying
it forty times. Then take hold of your beard with your left hand, weep, or pretend to
weep, and say: "O’ Muhammad, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, I complain to Allah {SWT}
and to you about my need. I complain to your rightly guided family about my need.
Through you, I turn to Allah {SWT} in my need."
Then prostrate and say:
"O’ Allah {SWT}, O’ Allah {SWT}," until you are out of breath. Then say: "Send blessings upon
Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and do for me (such and such)."
Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: 'I guarantee by Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, that his need
will be fulfilled before he rises.'"
commentary:
My father (may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him) wrote to me:
"If you have a need from Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, fast for three days -
Wednesday, Thursday, and Jumu’ah. On Jumu’ah, go forth to Allah {SWT} before noon
while you are in a state of ritual purity (ghusl) and pray two rak'ahs. In each rak'ah,
recite Surah al-Fatiha and Surah al-Ikhlas fifteen times. When you bow, recite it ten
times. When you raise your head from bowing, recite it ten times.
When you prostrate, recite it ten times. When you raise your head from prostration,
recite it ten times. When you prostrate again, recite it ten times. When you raise your
head from the second prostration, recite it ten times. Then stand for the second rak'ah
without saying the takbir (additional opening) and pray it in the same manner as
described. Recite the Qunoot (supplication) in the second rak'ah before bowing and
after the recitation.
When Allah {SWT} favors you by fulfiling your need, pray two rak'ahs of gratitude. In the
first rak'ah, recite Surah al-Fatiha and Surah al-Ikhlas. In the second rak'ah, recite
Surah al-Fatiha and Surah al-Kafirun. In the first rak'ah, say in your bowing: 'All praise
belongs to Allah {SWT} in thanks,'
and in your prostration: 'Thanks to Allah {SWT} and praise.'
In the second rak'ah, say in bowing and prostration:
'All praise belongs to Allah {SWT} who fulfilled my need and granted my request.'".
references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 476 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 559 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1419 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 130 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 9, p. 229

english_text:
In the book of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, narrated
by Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, raised to Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} regarding a man troubled by a matter and in need of
something,
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray two rak'ahs and recite in one of them 'Qul Huwa Allahu
Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) a thousand times, and in the other rak'ah he should recite it
once, then ask for his need."
commentary:
I have compiled what I have narrated regarding the Prayers of Needs in a book
dedicated to prayers other than the (obligatory) fifty prayers.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 477 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 562 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1420 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 131

english_text:
Harun ibn Khurajah narrate from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If one of you intends to undertake a matter, let him not consult any person before first
consulting Allah {SWT}, the Blessed and Exalted."
I asked: "What is meant by consulting Allah {SWT}, may I be your ransom?"
Imam {a.s} said: "He should first seek guidance (istikhara) from Allah {SWT} regarding it,
then he may consult others about it. For if one begins by turning to Allah {SWT}, the
Blessed and Exalted, He will guide him to the best through the tongue of whomever He
wills from among His creation."
references: Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 598 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 562 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1414 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 74

english_text:
Murazim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If one of you intends to undertake something, let him pray two units of prayer
(rak'ahs). Then, let him praise Allah {SWT}, the Majestic, and glorify Him, and send
blessings upon the Prophet {saws}, and say:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, if this matter is good for me in my religion and worldly affairs, then make
it easy for me and decree it for me. But if it is otherwise, then turn it away from me.'"
Murazim asked: "What should be recited in these prayers?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Recite whatever you wish in them, and if you like, recite in them:
'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul ya-ayyuhal kaafirun’ (Surah al-
Kafirun)
Reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) is equivalent to one-third of the
Quran."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: THE PRAYER OF SEEKING GUIDANCE (ISTIKHARA)

english_text:
Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Qasri asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} about seeking divine guidance (istikhara).
Imam {a.s} said: "Seek guidance from Allah {SWT} in the last unit (rak'ah) of the night prayer
while you are in prostration, repeating it one hundred and one times."
Muhammad asked: "How should I say it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "You should say, 'I seek guidance from Allah {SWT} by His mercy, I seek
guidance from Allah {SWT} by His mercy.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 562 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1415

english_text:
Hammad ibn Uthman al-Naab narrated from Him {a.s} that He said:
"For istikhara (seeking divine guidance), a person should seek guidance from Allah {SWT}
during the last prostration (sajdah) of the two rak'ahs of Fajr prayer by repeating it one
hundred and one times, praising Allah {SWT}, and sending blessings upon the Prophet
and his family. Then, seek guidance from Allah {SWT} fifty times, praise Allah {SWT} again,
and send blessings upon the Prophet and his family until completing the count of one
hundred and one."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 563 • The Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 320 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1415

Hammad ibn Isa narrated from Najiyah, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-
Sadiq {a.s} that "Whenever He {a.s} intended to purchase a servant, an animal, or a light
matter, or something of little importance, he would perform istikhara (seek Allah’s {SWT}
guidance) seven times.
But if it was a serious matter, he would perform istikhara one hundred times”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 563 • Opening the Doors, Part 1, p. 253 • Al-Masbah (Lalkafami) Vol. 1, p. 392 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 9, p. 1415 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 74

english_text:
Mu'awiya ibn Maythara narrated that Imam {a.s} said:
"No servant who performs istikhara (seeks Allah’s {SWT} guidance) seventy times with
this istikhara will be left without Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, granting him
guidance."
The supplication is: "O’ the best of those who see, O’ the most hearing of the hearers,
O’ the swiftest of reckoners, O’ the most merciful of the merciful, O’ the wisest of
judges, send blessings upon Muhammad and his family and guide me in such and
such matter."
commentary:
My father, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him, advised in his letter:
"If you, my son, desire to undertake something, pray two rak'ahs (units of prayer), and
then perform istikhara one hundred and one times. Whatever is made firm in your
heart, proceed with it, and say in your supplication:
'There is no god but Allah {SWT}, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah
{SWT}, the Exalted, the Great. O’ Lord {AZJ}, by the right of Muhammad and his family, bless
Muhammad and his family and grant me guidance in such and such matter for this
world and the hereafter, as a choice in well-being.'"
It is well-known among the companions that it is the prayer of Amir al-Mu'minin {a.s},
as narrated in the tradition of al-Mufaddal.

Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"Whoever performs ablution and completes it thoroughly, then begins the prayer and
prays four units (rak'ahs), separating each two with a taslim (salutation), and recites
in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book (Surah al-Fatiha) once and 'Qul Huwa Allahu
Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) fifty times, he will finish his prayer with nothing between him
and Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Glorious, except that his sins will be forgiven."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 564 • Al-Wafi, V. 9, p. 1396 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 8, p. 112

Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ayyashi, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him,
narrated in his book from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn
al-Samak, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"Whoever prays four rak'ahs (units of prayer) and recites in each rak'ah 'Qul Huwa
Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) fifty times, it is the Prayer of Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra
{S.A}, and it is the prayer of those who turn to Allah {SWT} in repentance (al-Awwabin)."
commentary:
Our teacher, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, used to narrate this prayer and its
reward, but he would say: 'I do not recognize it as the Prayer of Sayyida Fatimah Al-
Zahra {S.A}.'
However, the people of Kufa know it as the Prayer of Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}.
This prayer and its reward is narrated by Abu Basir from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-
Sadiq {a.s}.

english_text:
In a narration from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Sadiq {a.s}, He said:
"Whoever prays two light (short) units of prayer (Rak'ahs), reciting 'Qul Huwa Allahu
Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas) sixty times in each Rak'ah, will finish the prayer without any
sins remaining between him and Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Exalted."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 • Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 468 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 564 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 310

Chapter Title: REWARD OF VOLUNTARY PRAYERS DURING THE TIME
arabic_text:
ب اب-
ت واب الي ن ق ل ف ي ساعة الغ ق لة
ِق َّالَّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِه:
ِ «ي َّن َّق َّلُّوإ ق ِى سَّ اعَّه ِ إَّلْع َّق ْلَّه ِ وَّ لَّوْ ن ِزَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ ج َّ ق ِي ق َّي َّي ْن ِ ق َّا ِن َّهُّمَّا ي ُّورِي َّان
ِ ذَّإرَّ إَّلْكَّزَّإمَّ ه.
english_text:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
"Perform supererogatory (extra) prayers during the time of heedlessness, even if it is
just two light rak'ahs (units of prayer), for they lead to the abode of honor."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 565 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 343

Chapter Title: REWARD OF VOLUNTARY PRAYERS DURING THE TIME
arabic_text:

. وهى إلح ن ه ، وساعه إلع ق له ن ي ن إلمع زب وإلعس اء إلأ ج زة
english_text: In another narration: "The Abode of Peace."
commentary:
It refers to Paradise, and the time of heedlessness is between Maghrib (sunset) and
the later Isha (night) prayer.
It appears that what is meant by "al-Nawadir" are uncommon reports that do not fall
under a specific chapter and are dispersed. The term may also refer to rare or unusual
narrations.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1 Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

english_text:
Bukayr ibn A'yan narrated from Imam Muhammad Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} never prayed the Duha prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 565 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 117 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذُّ إَّلْوَّ إجِ ذِ ن ْن ُّ إَّلْمُّح ْ ي َّارِ إَّلْأ َّن ْصَّ ارِى ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ق َّالَّ: سَّ ا َّلْي ُّهُّ ع َّن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلص ُّ حَّ ى ق َّق َّال

ِ«إ ِن َّ عَّلِي اً عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ مَّ ز َّ عَّلَّى رَّج ُّ لٍ وَّ هُّوَّ ي ُّصَّ لِّي هَّا ق َّق َّالَّ عَّلِى عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «مَّ ا هَّذ ِة َّإَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ» ق َّق َّالَّ إ َّذَّعُّهَّا ي َّا إ َّمِي ز
إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ِي ن َّ ق َّق َّالَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ «إ َّكُّون ُّ إ َّن ْهَّى «عَّن ْذإً إ ِذ ٰ إ صَّ لّٰى .
english_text:
Abdul Wahid ibn al-Mukhtar al-Ansari narrated from Abu Ja'far {a.s}, who said:
"I asked him about the Duha prayer”
Imam {a.s} said: ‘The first people to perform it were your people, for they were among
the heedless, so they performed it.
The Messenger of Allah {saws} did not perform it.'
He also said: 'Imam Ali {a.s} passed by a man who was performing it, and Imam Ali {a.s}
said: ‘What is this prayer?’
The man replied: ‘Should I leave it, O’ Commander of the Faithful?’
He (Imam Ali {a.s}) said: ‘Would I forbid a servant when he prays?’".
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 566 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 117 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 101 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 14, p. 348

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text:
ْ وَّ رَّوَّ ى ر ُّرَّإرَّة ُّ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى ج َّ عْ ق َّزٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «مَّ ا صَّ ل َّى رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إَّلص ُّ حَّ ى
َّ ق َّظ ُّ » ق َّالَّ ق َّق ُّلْث ُّ لَّهُّ إ َّ لَّمْ ي ُّح ْ ن ِزْن ِى إ َّن َّهُّ كَّان َّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّمُّ ي ُّصَّ لِّى ق ِى صَّ ذْ رِ إَّلن هَّارِ إ َّرْن َّغَّ رَّكَّعَّاب ٍ ق َّالَّ «ن َّلَّى إ ِن َّهُّ كَّان َّ ي َّح ْ عَّلُّهَّا
ِمِن َّ إَّلي َّمَّان ِ إَّل َّي ِى ن َّعْ ذَّ إَّلط ُّ هْ ز.
english_text:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"The Messenger of Allah {saws} never prayed the Duha prayer."
So I (Zurarah) said to him, "Did you not inform me that He {saws} used to pray four rak'ahs
in the forenoon?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, but he used to count it among the eight rak'ahs that are prayed
after Dhuhr."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 566 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 116 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 100 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 234

ِرَّكْعَّه ً مِن ْهَّا إَّلْوَّ ي ْزُّ وَّ رَّكْعَّي َّان ِ ق َّن ْلَّ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلْق َّح ْ زِ كَّذ َّلِك َّ كَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ ه
ًوَّ إ لِهِ ي ُّصَّ لِّى وَّ لَّوْ كَّان َّ ق َّص ْ لا
َّكَّان َّ رَّسُّ ولُّ إَّلل َّهِ ص َّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ إ َّعْ مَّلَّ ن ِهِ وَّ إ َّجَّ ق .
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about the
prayer during the month of Ramadan.
Imam {a.s} said: "Thirteen rak'ahs, including the Witr prayer and two rak'ahs before the
Fajr prayer. This is how the Messenger of Allah {saws} used to pray, and if there was any
greater virtue in adding more, the Messenger of Allah {saws} would have been the most
diligent and deserving of it."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 566 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2, p. 137 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 69 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 467 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 11, p. 436 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 43

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
english_text:
Uqbah ibn Khalid asked Him (Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}) about a man who was
praying and another man called out to him, causing him to become distracted and
respond to the person's request. What should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "He should continue with his prayer."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text: ِوَّ رَّوَّ ى عِ مْ زَّإن ُّ إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ عَّن ْهُّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «ي َّن ْن َّع ِى ي َّح ْ ق ِي ف ُّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ مِن ْ إ َّج ْ لِ إَّلس َّ هْ و.
english_text:
Imran Al-Halabi narrated from Imam {a.s} that He said:
"It is recommended to lighten (shorten) the prayer because of forgetfulness."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 567 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1002 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 236

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
english_text:
Sama’a bin Mehran narrated from Imam {a.s} that He said:
"The charity given by a boy, his emancipation (freeing a slave), and leading people in
prayer are permissible if he is ten years old."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 567 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1180 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 322

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text: وق ال إلصاذق علي ه إلسلام: " إ ذ إ صلي ث معهم ع ق ز لك ن عذذ من ج الق ك.
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"If you pray with them (in congregation), you will be forgiven according to the number
of those who oppose you."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

arabic_text:
ِوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْهُّ عَّن ْذُّ إَّلز َّجْ مَّن ِ ن ْن ُّ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّه َّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ صَّ ل َّي ْث َّ ق َّصَّ لِّ ق ِى ن َّعْ لَّي ْك َّ إ ِذ َّإ كَّان َّث ْ طَّ اهِزَّة ً ق َّا ِن
ِ ذ َّلِك َّ مِن َّ إَّلس ُّ ن َّه .
english_text:
It is narrated from Him (Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}) through Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi
Abdillah that Imam {a.s} said:
"If you pray, then pray in your sandals (shoes) if they are clean, for that is from the
Sunnah."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 568 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 233 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 424 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 426

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text: َّوَّ رَّوَّ ى إَّلْحَّ لَّن ِى ُّ عَّن ْهُّ عَّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: «إ ِذ َّإ صَّ ل َّي ْث َّ ق ِى إَّلس َّ ق َّزِ س َّ ي ْ ن اً مِن َّ إَّلص َّ لَّوَّ إب ِ ق ِى ع َّي ْ زِ وَّ ق ْي ِه َّ ا ق َّلاَّ ي َّص ُّ ز ُّك .
english_text:
It is narrated by Al-Halabi from Him (Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}) that He said: "If you
pray any of the prayers during travel outside of its (regular) time, it will not harm you."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 568 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 115

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text:
ُّوَّ رُّوِى َّ عَّن ْ عَّان ِذ ٍ إَّلْأ َّجْ مَّسِ ى ِّ إ َّن َّهُّ ق َّالَّ: ذَّج َّ لْث ُّ عَّلَّى إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذِ إَّلل َّهِ عَّ وَّ إ َّن َّا إ ُّرِي ذُّ إ َّن ْ إ َّسْ ا َّلَّه عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّان ْي َّذَّإ َّن ِى
ْمِن ْ ع َّي ْ زِ إ َّن ْ إ َّسْ ا َّلَّهُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِذ َّإ لَّق ِي ث َّ إَّلل َّهَّ عَّز َّ وَّ ج َّ ل َّ ن ِالص َّ لَّوَّ إب ِ إَّلْح َّ م َّ سِ إَّلْمَّق ْ زُّوص َّ اب ِ لَّمْ ي َّسْ ا َّلْك َّ عَّم َّا سِ وَّ ى ذ َّلِك .
english_text:
It is narrated from Aidh al-Ahmasi: "I entered upon Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} while I
intended to ask him about prayer. Without me asking, Imam {a.s} began (by saying):
'If you meet Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, with the five obligatory prayers, He will
not ask you about anything beyond that.'"
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 568 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 12 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 69 • Ithbāt al-Hudāt, Part 4, p. 190

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text:
َّوَّ ق َّال ُّإَّلص َّ اذِق ُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلس َّ لاَّم:
ٍ«إَّلْمُّو ْ مِن ُّ مُّعَّق ِّث مَّ ا ذَّإمَّ عَّلَّى وُّ ص ُّ وء .
english_text:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "A believer remains in a state of
spiritual reward (mu'aqqib) as long as they are in a state of ritual purity (wudhu)”.
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Chapter Title: RARE PRAYERS
arabic_text:
ِوَّ رَّوَّ ى عَّن ْذُّ إَّلل َّهِ ن ْن ُّ سِ ن َّان ٍ عَّن ْ إ َّن ِى عَّن ْذ إَّلل َّهِ عَّ ق َّالَّ: ق ُّلْث ُّ لَّهُّ إ َّج ْ ن ِزْن ِى عَّن ْ رَّج ُّ لٍ عَّلَّي ْ هِ مِن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلن َّوَّ إق ِلِ مَّ ا
َّ لأَّ ي َّذْ رِى مَّ ا هُّوَّ مِن ْ كَّي ْ زَّي ِهَّا كَّي ْف َّ ي َّصْ ن َّغُّ ق َّالَّ «ق َّلْي ُّصَّ لِّ جَّ ي َّى لأَّ ي َّذْ رِى َّ كَّمْ صَّ ل َّى مِن ْ كَّي ْ زَّي ِهَّا ق َّي كُّون َّ ق َّذْ ق َّص َّ ى ن ِق َّذْ رِ مَّ ا
َّعَّلِم َّهُّ مِن ْ ذ َّلِك َّ ، » ي ُّم َّ ق َّالَّ ق ُّلْث ُّ لَّهُّ ق َّا ِن َّهُّ لأَّ ي َّق ْ ذِرُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْق َّص َّ اءِ ق َّق َّالَّ «إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ س ُّ ع ُّلُّهُّ ق ِى طَّ لَّث ِ م ْعِي س َّ ه ٍ لأَّ ن ُّذ َّ مِن ْهَّا إ َّو
َّ جَّ اج َّ ه ٍ لِأ َّح ٍ مُّو ْ مِن ٍ ق َّلاَّ س َّ ى ْ ءَّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ ِن ْ كَّان َّ س ُّ ع ُّلُّهُّ لِح َّ مْ غِ إَّلذ ُّن ْي َّا وَّ إَّلي َّ س َّ اع ُّلِ ن ِهَّا عَّن ِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ِ ق َّعَّلَّي ْ هِ إَّلْق َّص َّ اءُّ وَّ إ ِلأ َّ لَّق ِى
ِ إَّلل َّهَّ وَّ هُّوَّ مُّسْ ي َّح ِ ف مُّي َّهَّاوِن مُّص َّ ي ِّغ لِحُّ زْمَّ ه ِ رَّسُّ ولِ إَّلل َّهِ صَّ ل َّى إَّلل َّهُّ عَّلَّي ْ هِ وَّ إ لِهِ » ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّا ْن َّهُّ لأَّ ي َّق ْ ذِرُّ عَّلَّى إَّلْق َّص َّ اءِ ق َّهَّل
َّ ي ُّح ْ ز ِى إ َّن ْ ي ْي َّصَّ ذ َّق َّ ق َّسَّ كَّث َّ مَّ لِي اً ي ُّم َّ ق َّالَّ «ق َّلْي َّي َّصَّ ذ َّق ْ ن ِصَّ ذَّق َّه ٍ » ق ُّلْث ُّ ق َّمَّا ي َّي َّصَّ ذ َّق ُّ ق َّالَّ «ن ِق َّذْ رِ طَّ وْ لِهِ وَّ إ َّذ ن َّى ذ َّلِك َّ مُّذ
ٍ لِكُّلِّ مِسْ كِي ن ٍ مَّ كَّان َّ كُّلِّ صَّ لاَّة ٍ» ق ُّلْث ُّ وَّ كَّمِ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ إَّل َّي ِى ي َّح ِ ث ُّ ق ِي هَّا مُّ ذ لِكُّلِّ مِسْ كِي ن ِ ق َّالَّ «لِكُّلِّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ مِن ْ صَّ لاَّة
َّ إَّلل َّي ْلِ مُّذ وَّ لِكُّلِّ رَّكْعَّي َّي ْن ِ مِن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلن َّهَّارِ مُّذ » ق َّق ُّلْث ُّ لأَّ ي َّق ْذِرُّ ق َّق َّالَّ «مُّ ذ إ ِذ إً لِكُّلِّ إ ُّ رْن َّغِ رَّكَّعَّاب ٍ مِن ْ صَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلن َّهَّارِ» ق ُّلْث
َّلأَّ ي َّق ْ ذِرُّ ق َّالَّ «ق َّمُّذ إ ِذ إً لِص ُّلاَّة ِ إَّلل َّي ْلِ وَّ مُّذ لِصَّ لاَّة ِ إَّلن َّهَّارِ وَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ وَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ إ َّق ْص َّ لُّ وَّ إَّلص َّ لاَّة ُّ إ َّق ْص َّ ل .
english_text:
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
said: I asked Imam {a.s} about a person who has so many missed (Qadha) prayers that
he cannot count them, what should he do?
Imam {a.s} said: "Let him pray until he no longer knows how many he has prayed due to
their abundance, and he would have compensated for the amount he is aware of."
I then asked: "What if he cannot complete all the Qadha prayers?"
Imam {a.s} said: "If his preoccupation is due to seeking a necessary livelihood or helping
a fellow believer in need, there is no obligation on him. But if his preoccupation is for
gathering worldly gain and being distracted from prayer, then he must make up for
them; otherwise, he will meet Allah {SWT} while being negligent, belittling, and neglecting
the sanctity of Messenger of Allah {saws}."
I asked: "What if he still cannot make up for them? Is charity sufficient?"
The Imam remained silent for a while and then said: "Let him give charity."
I asked: "How much charity?"
Imam {a.s} said: "As much as he can afford, with the minimum being a 'mud' (a specific
measure) of food for each missed prayer."
I asked: "How many prayers require a 'mudd' of charity?"
Imam {a.s} said: "A 'mud' for every two units (rak'ahs) of the night prayer and a 'mud' for
every two units of the day prayer."
I said: "What if he cannot do this?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Then one 'mudd' for every four units of the day prayer."
I said: "What if he cannot manage even this?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Then one 'mudd' for the entire night prayer and one 'mud' for the entire
day prayer. However, prayer is superior, and prayer is superior, and prayer is superior."
references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 568 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 4, p. 75
